)

var (
        verbosity int
        vmodule   string
        logFormat string
        logFile   string
)

func addLoggingFlags(root *cobra.Command) {
        f := root.PersistentFlags()
        f.IntVarP(&verbosity, "v", "v", 0, "log verbosity, 0 to 9, as in kubectl; see aiculator debug levels. A server defaults to 2")
        f.StringVar(&vmodule, "vmodule", "", "levels per component, such as engine=5,driver=3; wildcards work")
        f.StringVar(&logFormat, "log-format", "text", "log format: text or json")
        f.StringVar(&logFile, "log-file", "", "write logs to this file instead of stderr")
}

// setupLogging applies the flags. A flag beats the environment, which beats the default.
func setupLogging(cmd *cobra.Command) error {
        level := 0
        if cmd.Name() == "serve" {
                level = vlog.LevelSteady
        }
        if env := os.Getenv("AICULATOR_V"); env != "" {
                n, err := strconv.Atoi(env)
                if err != nil {
                        return fmt.Errorf("AICULATOR_V=%q: want a number from 0 to %d", env, vlog.MaxLevel)
                }
                level = n
        }
        if cmd.Flags().Changed("v") {
                level = verbosity
        }
        mod := vmodule
        if !cmd.Flags().Changed("vmodule") {
                mod = os.Getenv("AICULATOR_VMODULE")
        }
        verbosity, vmodule = level, mod
        opts := vlog.Options{Level: level, VModule: mod, Format: logFormat}
        if logFile != "" {
                f, err := os.OpenFile(logFile, os.O_APPEND|os.O_CREATE|os.O_WRONLY, 0o600)
                if err != nil {
                        return err
                }
                opts.Output = f
        }
        return vlog.Setup(opts)
}

// loggingArgs passes the choices on to a server started in the background. The server's
// own default applies unless a level was asked for.
func loggingArgs() []string {
        args := []string{"--log-format", logFormat}
        if verbosity > 0 {
                args = append(args, "--v", strconv.Itoa(verbosity))
        }
        if vmodule != "" {
                args = append(args, "--vmodule", vmodule)
        }
        return args
}

func debugCmd() *cobra.Command {
        cmd := &cobra.Command{
                Use:   "debug",
                Short: "Debugging tools: verbosity levels, and changing them on a running server",
        }
        cmd.AddCommand(&cobra.Command{
                Use:   "levels",
                Short: "Explain what each verbosity level shows",
                RunE: func(*cobra.Command, []string) error {
                        for i, d := range vlog.Descriptions {
                                fmt.Printf("%d  %s\n", i, d)
                        }
                        fmt.Println("\nComponents for --vmodule: engine, work, driver, swarm, sandbox, mcp, http, client, store.")
                        return nil
                },
        })
        var (
                mod string
                dur time.Duration
        )
        v := &cobra.Command{
                Use:   "verbosity [LEVEL]",
                Short: "Show or change a running server's verbosity, with no restart",
                Long: `Changes take effect at once. Use --for, so that a debugging session cannot leave
the server logging at a high level by accident. The previous level then comes back by itself.`,
                Example: `  aiculator debug verbosity                     show the current level
  aiculator debug verbosity 5 --for 10m         trace for ten minutes
  aiculator debug verbosity --vmodule engine=5 --for 5m
  aiculator debug verbosity 2                   set it for good`,
                Args: cobra.MaximumNArgs(1),
                RunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) error {
                        c, err := adminClient()
                        if err != nil {
                                return fmt.Errorf("%w; start it with: aiculator up", err)
                        }
                        var st api.VerbosityState
                        if len(args) == 0 && !cmd.Flags().Changed("vmodule") {
                                if err := c.Get(cmd.Context(), "/v1/debug/verbosity", &st); err != nil {
                                        return err
                                }
                                return printVerbosity(st)
                        }
                        q := api.VerbosityReq{ForSeconds: int64(dur.Seconds())}
                        if len(args) == 1 {
                                n, err := strconv.Atoi(args[0])
                                if err != nil {
                                        return fmt.Errorf("level %q: want a number from 0 to %d", args[0], vlog.MaxLevel)
                                }
                                q.Level = &n
                        }
                        if cmd.Flags().Changed("vmodule") {
                                q.VModule = &mod
                        }
                        if err := c.Do(cmd.Context(), http.MethodPut, "/v1/debug/verbosity", q, &st); err != nil {
                                return err
                        }
                        return printVerbosity(st)
                },
        }
        v.Flags().StringVar(&mod, "vmodule", "", "levels per component, such as engine=5")
        v.Flags().DurationVar(&dur, "for", 0, "go back to the previous level after this long")
        cmd.AddCommand(v)
        return cmd
}

func printVerbosity(st api.VerbosityState) error {
        fmt.Printf("level %d", st.Level)
        if st.VModule != "" {
                fmt.Printf("  vmodule %s", st.VModule)
        }
        if !st.RevertsAt.IsZero() {
                fmt.Printf("  until %s", st.RevertsAt.Local().Format(time.TimeOnly))
        }
        fmt.Println()
        return nil
}

func logsCmd() *cobra.Command {
        var (
                follow    bool
                tail      int
                component string
                grep      string
        )
        cmd := &cobra.Command{
                Use:   "logs",
                Short: "Show the logs of a server started with aiculator up",
                Example: `  aiculator logs --tail 50
  aiculator logs -f --component engine
  aiculator logs -f --grep ship-api-3`,
                RunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, _ []string) error {
                        path := filepath.Join(dataDir, "server.log")
                        f, err := os.Open(path)
                        if errors.Is(err, os.ErrNotExist) {
                                return fmt.Errorf("no log at %s; it exists only for a server started with aiculator up", path)
                        }
                        if err != nil {
                                return err
                        }
                        defer f.Close()
                        match := func(line string) bool {
                                if component != "" && !strings.Contains(line, "component="+component) && !strings.Contains(line, `"component":"`+component+`"`) {
                                        return false
                                }
                                return grep == "" || strings.Contains(line, grep)
                        }
                        var last []string
                        r := bufio.NewReader(f)
                        partial := ""
                        for {
                                chunk, err := r.ReadString('\n')
                                partial += chunk
                                if err != nil {
                                        break
                                }
                                if match(partial) {
                                        last = append(last, partial)
                                        if tail > 0 && len(last) > tail {
                                                last = last[1:]
                                        }
                                }
                                partial = ""
                        }
                        for _, l := range last {
                                fmt.Print(l)
                        }
                        for follow {
                                chunk, err := r.ReadString('\n')
                                partial += chunk
                                if errors.Is(err, io.EOF) {
                                        select {
                                        case <-cmd.Context().Done():
                                                return nil
                                        case <-time.After(200 * time.Millisecond):
                                        }
                                        continue
                                }
                                if err != nil {
                                        return err
                                }
                                if match(partial) {
                                        fmt.Print(partial)
                                }
                                partial = ""
                        }
                        return nil
                },
        }
        f := cmd.Flags()
        f.BoolVarP(&follow, "follow", "f", false, "keep printing new lines")
        f.IntVar(&tail, "tail", 0, "show only the last N matching lines")
        f.StringVar(&component, "component", "", "show only this component")
        f.StringVar(&grep, "grep", "", "show only lines containing this text")
        return cmd
}

package main

import (
        "errors"
        "fmt"
        "os"
        "path/filepath"
        "strconv"
        "strings"

        "github.com/spf13/cobra"

        "github.com/Grano22/aiculator/internal/swarm"
)

// fileChecks look at the data directory itself, so they work while the server is down,
// which is when they matter most.
func fileChecks(fix bool) []swarm.Finding {
        var out []swarm.Finding
        abs, err := filepath.Abs(dataDir)
        if err != nil {
                return out
        }
        if _, err := os.Stat(abs); err != nil {
                return append(out, swarm.Finding{Check: "data", OK: true, Detail: "no data directory here yet: aiculator join"})
        }
        _, running := serverURL()
        // The lock is the truth about whether a server runs here: the kernel drops it with the process.
        unlock, lockErr := lockDataDir(abs)
        held := lockErr != nil
        if unlock != nil {
                unlock()
        }
        out = append(out, swarm.Finding{Check: "server", OK: true, Detail: map[bool]string{true: "running", false: "not running"}[held]})
        if held && !running {
                out = append(out, swarm.Finding{Check: "server", OK: false, Detail: "a server holds the lock but does not answer: it may be starting, stuck, or another version"})
        }
        if pid, ok := readPid(abs); ok && !processAlive(pid) {
                f := swarm.Finding{Check: "pid file", OK: false, Fixable: true, Detail: fmt.Sprintf("names process %d, which is gone", pid)}
                if fix && !held {
                        if os.Remove(filepath.Join(abs, "pid")) == nil {
                                f.OK, f.Detail = true, f.Detail+"; removed"
                        }
                }
                out = append(out, f)
        }
        if _, err := os.Stat(filepath.Join(abs, "addr")); err == nil && !running {
                f := swarm.Finding{Check: "address file", OK: false, Fixable: true, Detail: "points at a server that does not answer, or is another project's"}
                if fix && !held {
                        if os.Remove(filepath.Join(abs, "addr")) == nil {
                                f.OK, f.Detail = true, f.Detail+"; removed"
                        }
                }
                out = append(out, f)
        }
        return out
}

func readPid(dir string) (int, bool) {
        b, err := os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(dir, "pid"))
        if err != nil {
                return 0, false
        }
        pid, err := strconv.Atoi(strings.TrimSpace(string(b)))
        return pid, err == nil && pid > 0
}

func doctorCmd() *cobra.Command {
        var fix, asJSON bool
        cmd := &cobra.Command{
                Use:   "doctor",
                Short: "Check this project's swarm for damage and leftovers, and fix them with --fix",
                Long: `Checks the data directory, even with the server down: a stale pid or address file, or a
server holding the lock without answering. With the server up, it also reports records repaired
at startup, records kept in quarantine, worktrees of finished tasks, and leases long past their
deadline.

Damaged task records are repaired when the server starts, with the originals kept. --fix removes
stale files and leftover worktrees. It never deletes a task or anything kept in quarantine.`,
                RunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, _ []string) error {
                        findings := fileChecks(fix)
                        var h swarm.Health
                        if c, err := adminClient(); err == nil {
                                if _, running := serverURL(); running {
                                        if err := c.Get(cmd.Context(), "/v1/doctor", &h); err != nil {
                                                return err
                                        }
                                        if fix && len(h.Orphans) > 0 {
                                                var res map[string]any
                                                if err := c.Post(cmd.Context(), "/v1/doctor/fix", nil, &res); err != nil {
                                                        return err
                                                }
                                                for i := range h.Findings {
                                                        if h.Findings[i].Check == "worktrees" {
                                                                h.Findings[i].OK, h.Findings[i].Detail = true, h.Findings[i].Detail+"; removed"
                                                        }
                                                }
                                        }
                                        findings = append(findings, h.Findings...)
                                }
                        }
                        h.Findings = findings
                        if asJSON {
                                return printJSON(h)
                        }
                        problems := 0
                        for _, f := range findings {
                                mark := "ok  "
                                if !f.OK {
                                        mark, problems = "FIX ", problems+1
                                        if !f.Fixable {
                                                mark = "LOOK"
                                        }
                                }
                                fmt.Printf("%s  %-13s %s\n", mark, f.Check, f.Detail)
                        }
                        for _, r := range h.Repairs {
                                fmt.Printf("      repaired %s: %s\n", r.TaskID, strings.Join(r.Did, "; "))
                        }
                        if len(h.Quarantined) > 0 {
                                fmt.Printf("      %d originals kept in quarantine: aiculator doctor --json shows them\n", len(h.Quarantined))
                        }
                        if problems > 0 && !fix {
                                fmt.Println("Run aiculator doctor --fix to fix what can be fixed.")
                                return errors.New("problems found")
                        }
                        return nil
                },
        }
        cmd.Flags().BoolVar(&fix, "fix", false, "fix what can be fixed safely")
        cmd.Flags().BoolVar(&asJSON, "json", false, "print as JSON")
        return cmd
}

package main

import (
        "fmt"
        "os"
        "os/signal"
        "syscall"
        "time"

        "github.com/knadh/koanf/parsers/yaml"
        "github.com/knadh/koanf/providers/file"
        "github.com/knadh/koanf/v2"
        "github.com/spf13/cobra"

        "github.com/Grano22/aiculator/internal/driver"
        "github.com/Grano22/aiculator/internal/sandbox"
        "github.com/Grano22/aiculator/internal/vlog"
)

func loadManifest(harness, path string) (driver.Manifest, error) {
        if path != "" {
                k := koanf.New(".")
                if err := k.Load(file.Provider(path), yaml.Parser()); err != nil {
                        return driver.Manifest{}, fmt.Errorf("manifest %s: %w", path, err)
                }
                var m driver.Manifest
                if err := k.Unmarshal("", &m); err != nil {
                        return driver.Manifest{}, fmt.Errorf("manifest %s: %w", path, err)
                }
                return m, nil
        }
        m, ok := driver.Preset(harness)
        if !ok {
                return m, fmt.Errorf("harness %q is unknown or has no ACP mode: see aiculator harness, or use --manifest", harness)
        }
        return m, nil
}

func driveCmd() *cobra.Command {
        var (
                harness, manifest, url, agent, sb string
                maxTasks                          int
                hold, heartbeat                   time.Duration
        )
        cmd := &cobra.Command{
                Use:   "drive",
                Short: "Launch an ACP harness and feed it tasks (token in SWARM_TOKEN)",
                RunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, _ []string) error {
                        token := os.Getenv("SWARM_TOKEN")
                        if token == "" {
                                return fmt.Errorf("SWARM_TOKEN is not set; create one with: swarm token --agent NAME --tier N")
                        }
                        m, err := loadManifest(harness, manifest)
                        if err != nil {
                                return err
                        }
                        s, err := sandbox.Open(sb)
                        if err != nil {
                                return err
                        }
                        self, err := os.Executable()
                        if err != nil {
                                return err
                        }
                        log := vlog.Slog("driver")
                        d, err := driver.New(driver.Options{
                                Manifest: m, URL: url, Token: token, AgentID: agent, Sandbox: s, SwarmBin: self, Hide: secretPaths(),
                                Hold: hold, Heartbeat: heartbeat, MaxTasks: maxTasks, Log: log, Stderr: os.Stderr,
                        })
                        if err != nil {
                                return err
                        }
                        ctx, stop := signal.NotifyContext(cmd.Context(), os.Interrupt, syscall.SIGTERM)
                        defer stop()
                        st, err := d.Run(ctx)
                        log.Info("driver finished", "tasks", st.Tasks, "submitted", st.Submitted, "failed", st.Failed, "reviews", st.Reviews, "waits", st.Waits, "exit", st.ExitReason)
                        return err
                },
        }
        f := cmd.Flags()
        f.StringVar(&harness, "harness", "", "harness id, from aiculator harness")
        f.StringVar(&manifest, "manifest", "", "YAML manifest file, instead of a preset")
        f.StringVar(&url, "url", "http://127.0.0.1:7777", "server URL")
        f.StringVar(&agent, "agent", "driver", "agent name, for review notes")
        f.StringVar(&sb, "sandbox", "auto", "sandbox: auto, seatbelt, bwrap, docker or none")
        f.IntVar(&maxTasks, "max-tasks", 0, "stop after this many tasks; 0 means no limit")
        f.DurationVar(&hold, "hold", 30*time.Second, "how long each wait call holds")
        f.DurationVar(&heartbeat, "heartbeat", 15*time.Second, "how often to save work and renew the lease")
        return cmd
}

package main

import (
        "bytes"
        "context"
        "encoding/json"
        "errors"
        "fmt"
        "os"
        "path/filepath"
        "slices"
        "strings"

        "github.com/spf13/cobra"
        "golang.org/x/term"

        "github.com/Grano22/aiculator/internal/core"
        "github.com/Grano22/aiculator/internal/export"
        "github.com/Grano22/aiculator/internal/meta"
        "github.com/Grano22/aiculator/internal/realm"
        "github.com/Grano22/aiculator/pkg/observe"
)

// The columns a table shows when none are asked for. JSON and YAML keep the whole record.
var exportColumns = map[string][]string{
        "tasks":  {"id", "title", "state", "tier", "priority", "owner", "attempt", "failures", "labels", "created_at", "updated_at"},
        "agents": {"id", "tier", "state", "task", "done", "failed", "tokens", "cost"},
        "usage":  nil,
        "flow":   nil,
        "realms": {"name", "state", "ready", "working", "review", "done", "parked", "agents", "path"},
}

func toRecords(v any) ([]export.Record, error) {
        b, err := json.Marshal(v)
        if err != nil {
                return nil, err
        }
        var out []export.Record
        if err := json.Unmarshal(b, &out); err != nil {
                return nil, err
        }
        return out, nil
}

func snapshotOf(ctx context.Context) (observe.Snapshot, error) {
        var s observe.Snapshot
        c, err := adminClient()
        if err != nil {
                return s, fmt.Errorf("%w; start it with: aiculator up", err)
        }
        return s, c.Get(ctx, "/v1/observe", &s)
}

// metaValue reduces a property to what fits a cell.
func metaValue(p meta.Prop) any {
        switch {
        case p.Blob != nil:
                return p.Blob.Name
        case p.Resource != nil:
                return p.Resource.URL
        }
        return p.Value
}

func exportTasks(ctx context.Context, all, withMeta bool) ([]export.Record, error) {
        if !all {
                c, err := adminClient()
                if err != nil {
                        return nil, fmt.Errorf("%w; start it with: aiculator up", err)
                }
                return fetchTasks(ctx, c, "", withMeta)
        }
        views, err := realm.Gather(ctx, nil)
        if err != nil {
                return nil, err
        }
        var out []export.Record
        for _, v := range views {
                if !v.Live {
                        continue
                }
                c, err := realm.Local(v.Realm)
                if err != nil {
                        continue
                }
                rows, err := fetchTasks(ctx, c, v.Realm.Name, withMeta)
                if err != nil {
                        fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "skipped realm %s: %v\n", v.Realm.Name, err)
                        continue
                }
                out = append(out, rows...)
        }
        return out, nil
}

type taskGetter interface {
        Get(ctx context.Context, path string, out any) error
}

func fetchTasks(ctx context.Context, c taskGetter, realmName string, withMeta bool) ([]export.Record, error) {
        var ts []core.Task
        if err := c.Get(ctx, "/v1/tasks", &ts); err != nil {
                return nil, err
        }
        rows, err := toRecords(ts)
        if err != nil {
                return nil, err
        }
        for i, r := range rows {
                if realmName != "" {
                        r["realm"] = realmName
                }
                if withMeta {
                        var m meta.Meta
                        if err := c.Get(ctx, "/v1/tasks/"+ts[i].ID+"/meta", &m); err != nil {
                                return nil, err
                        }
                        props := make(map[string]any, len(m.Props))
                        for k, p := range m.Props {
                                props[k] = metaValue(p)
                        }
                        r["meta"] = props
                }
        }
        return rows, nil
}

func exportRealms(ctx context.Context) ([]export.Record, error) {
        views, err := realm.Gather(ctx, nil)
        if err != nil {
                return nil, err
        }
        out := make([]export.Record, 0, len(views))
        for _, v := range views {
                r := export.Record{"name": v.Realm.Name, "path": v.Realm.Path, "state": "stopped"}
                switch {
                case v.Missing:
                        r["state"] = "missing"
                case v.Live:
                        r["state"] = "running"
                        st := v.Snapshot.States
                        r["ready"], r["working"] = float64(st["ready"]), float64(st["claimed"]+st["running"])
                        r["review"], r["done"] = float64(st["review"]+st["merging"]), float64(st["done"])
                        r["parked"], r["agents"] = float64(st["parked"]), float64(len(v.Snapshot.Agents))
                }
                out = append(out, r)
        }
        return out, nil
}

func exportCmd() *cobra.Command {
        var (
                output, format, sortBy string
                fields, states, labels []string
                where                  []string
                limit                  int
                withMeta, all, list    bool
        )
        cmd := &cobra.Command{
                Use:   "export [tasks|agents|usage|flow|realms]",
                Short: "Write tasks or other data to a file: JSON, YAML, CSV, TSV, Excel, HTML or Markdown",
                Long: `Exports what you choose, in the format you choose. Tasks are the default, and JSON is the
default format, unless the file name in -o says otherwise.

Values are always treated as text: HTML is escaped, Excel cells are stored as strings, and in
CSV a value that a spreadsheet would run as a formula starts with a quote.`,
                Example: `  aiculator export                                   # All tasks, as JSON
  aiculator export -o tasks.xlsx                     # The file name picks the format
  aiculator export --format html -o report.html --state running,review
  aiculator export --fields id,title,labels.team,owner --format csv
  aiculator export --label team=core --sort priority -o core.yaml
  aiculator export --with-meta --fields id,meta.points -o points.csv
  aiculator export --all -o everything.xlsx          # Tasks from every realm
  aiculator export --list-fields                     # What can be selected
  aiculator export realms --format md`,
                Args: cobra.MaximumNArgs(1),
                RunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) error {
                        what := "tasks"
                        if len(args) == 1 {
                                what = args[0]
                        }
                        defaults, known := exportColumns[what]
                        if !known {
                                return fmt.Errorf("cannot export %q: use tasks, agents, usage, flow or realms", what)
                        }
                        if format == "" {
                                format = export.FormatFor(output)
                        }
                        if format == "" {
                                if output != "" && output != "-" {
                                        return fmt.Errorf("the file name %s does not say the format: use --format %s", output, strings.Join(export.Formats, ", "))
                                }
                                format = "json"
                        }
                        if !slices.Contains(export.Formats, format) {
                                return fmt.Errorf("unknown format %q: use %s", format, strings.Join(export.Formats, ", "))
                        }
                        if format == "xlsx" && (output == "" || output == "-") && term.IsTerminal(int(os.Stdout.Fd())) {
                                return export.ErrNeedsFile
                        }
                        if (withMeta || all) && what != "tasks" {
                                return fmt.Errorf("--with-meta and --all work with tasks, not %s", what)
                        }
                        ctx := cmd.Context()
                        var records []export.Record
                        var err error
                        switch what {
                        case "tasks":
                                records, err = exportTasks(ctx, all, withMeta)
                        case "realms":
                                records, err = exportRealms(ctx)
                        default:
                                var s observe.Snapshot
                                if s, err = snapshotOf(ctx); err == nil {
                                        switch what {
                                        case "agents":
                                                records, err = toRecords(s.Agents)
                                        case "usage":
                                                records, err = toRecords(s.Usage.ByTier)
                                        default:
                                                records, err = toRecords(s.Flow)
                                        }
                                }
                        }
                        if err != nil {
                                return err
                        }
                        if list {
                                for _, f := range export.FieldNames(records) {
                                        fmt.Println(f)
                                }
                                return nil
                        }
                        if records, err = filterRecords(records, states, labels, where); err != nil {
                                return err
                        }
                        if sortBy != "" {
                                sortRecords(records, sortBy)
                        }
                        if limit > 0 && len(records) > limit {
                                records = records[:limit]
                        }
                        columns := defaults
                        if all && what == "tasks" {
                                columns = append([]string{"realm"}, columns...)
                        }
                        tabular := format != "json" && format != "yaml"
                        switch {
                        case len(fields) > 0:
                                known := export.FieldNames(records)
                                for _, f := range fields {
                                        if len(records) > 0 && !slices.Contains(known, f) {
                                                fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "warning: no record has a field named %s; see --list-fields\n", f)
                                        }
                                }
                                records, columns = export.Select(records, fields), fields
                        case tabular && len(columns) > 0:
                                records = export.Select(records, columns)
                        default:
                                columns = nil
                        }
                        var buf bytes.Buffer
                        if err := export.Write(&buf, records, export.Options{Format: format, Columns: columns, Title: "Aiculator " + what}); err != nil {
                                return err
                        }
                        if output == "" || output == "-" {
                                _, err = os.Stdout.Write(buf.Bytes())
                                return err
                        }
                        if err := writeFileAtomic(output, buf.Bytes()); err != nil {
                                return err
                        }
                        fmt.Printf("%d rows written to %s\n", len(records), output)
                        return nil
                },
        }
        f := cmd.Flags()
        f.StringVarP(&output, "output", "o", "", "file to write; standard output if empty")
        f.StringVar(&format, "format", "", "json, yaml, csv, tsv, xlsx, html or md; from the file name, or json")
        f.StringSliceVar(&fields, "fields", nil, "what to include, such as id,title,labels.team; see --list-fields")
        f.StringSliceVar(&states, "state", nil, "only these states, such as running,review")
        f.StringArrayVar(&labels, "label", nil, "only with this label, as name=value")
        f.StringArrayVar(&where, "where", nil, "only where a field has this value, as field=value")
        f.StringVar(&sortBy, "sort", "", "sort by this field; -field for descending")
        f.IntVar(&limit, "limit", 0, "stop after this many rows")
        f.BoolVar(&withMeta, "with-meta", false, "add each task's properties, as meta.NAME; costs one request per task")
        f.BoolVar(&all, "all", false, "tasks from every running realm, with a realm column")
        f.BoolVar(&list, "list-fields", false, "list what can be selected, and write nothing")
        return cmd
}

func filterRecords(records []export.Record, states, labels, where []string) ([]export.Record, error) {
        type test struct{ field, want string }
        var tests []test
        for _, l := range labels {
                k, v, ok := strings.Cut(l, "=")
                if !ok {
                        return nil, fmt.Errorf("--label %q: use name=value", l)
                }
                tests = append(tests, test{"labels." + k, v})
        }
        for _, w := range where {
                k, v, ok := strings.Cut(w, "=")
                if !ok {
                        return nil, fmt.Errorf("--where %q: use field=value", w)
                }
                tests = append(tests, test{k, v})
        }
        return slices.DeleteFunc(records, func(r export.Record) bool {
                if len(states) > 0 {
                        s, _ := export.Lookup(r, "state")
                        if !slices.Contains(states, export.Text(s)) {
                                return true
                        }
                }
                for _, t := range tests {
                        v, ok := export.Lookup(r, t.field)
                        if !ok || export.Text(v) != t.want {
                                return true
                        }
                }
                return false
        }), nil
}

func sortRecords(records []export.Record, by string) {
        desc := strings.HasPrefix(by, "-")
        by = strings.TrimPrefix(by, "-")
        slices.SortStableFunc(records, func(a, b export.Record) int {
                x, _ := export.Lookup(a, by)
                y, _ := export.Lookup(b, by)
                c := 0
                xn, xok := x.(float64)
                yn, yok := y.(float64)
                switch {
                case xok && yok && xn < yn:
                        c = -1
                case xok && yok && xn > yn:
                        c = 1
                case !xok || !yok:
                        c = strings.Compare(export.Text(x), export.Text(y))
                }
                if desc {
                        return -c
                }
                return c
        })
}

// writeFileAtomic means a failure leaves any earlier file whole.
func writeFileAtomic(path string, data []byte) error {
        tmp, err := os.CreateTemp(filepath.Dir(path), ".export-*")
        if err != nil {
                return err
        }
        defer os.Remove(tmp.Name())
        if _, err := tmp.Write(data); err != nil {
                tmp.Close()
                return errors.Join(err, errors.New("nothing was written"))
        }
        if err := tmp.Close(); err != nil {
                return err
        }
        if err := os.Chmod(tmp.Name(), 0o644); err != nil {
                return err
        }
        return os.Rename(tmp.Name(), path)
}

package main

import (
        "fmt"
        "os"
        "path/filepath"
        "strings"

        "github.com/spf13/cobra"

        "github.com/Grano22/aiculator/internal/harness"
        "github.com/Grano22/aiculator/internal/tmpl"
)

// genDocsCmd writes the reference pages from the code, so that they cannot drift.
// TestReferenceDocsAreCurrent fails if the committed pages are out of date.
func genDocsCmd() *cobra.Command {
        var out string
        cmd := &cobra.Command{
                Use:    "gen-docs",
                Short:  "Write the reference pages of the documentation",
                Hidden: true,
                RunE: func(*cobra.Command, []string) error {
                        if err := os.MkdirAll(out, 0o755); err != nil {
                                return err
                        }
                        if err := os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(out, "cli.md"), []byte(cliReference()), 0o644); err != nil {
                                return err
                        }
                        if err := os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(out, "harnesses.md"), []byte(harnessReference()), 0o644); err != nil {
                                return err
                        }
                        root := filepath.Join(filepath.Dir(filepath.Dir(out)))
                        for _, id := range demoHarnesses {
                                text, err := renderDemo(root, id)
                                if err != nil {
                                        return err
                                }
                                path := filepath.Join(root, "docs", "snippets", demoSnippetName(id))
                                if err := os.WriteFile(path, []byte(text), 0o644); err != nil {
                                        return err
                                }
                        }
                        return nil
                },
        }
        cmd.Flags().StringVar(&out, "out", "docs/reference", "output directory")
        return cmd
}

// demoHarnesses are the rendered forms the template demo page shows.
var demoHarnesses = []string{"", "claude", "opencode", "pi"}

func demoSnippetName(id string) string {
        if id == "" {
                id = "shared"
        }
        return "demo." + id + ".md"
}

// renderDemo produces what the docs show, from the real template in .agent/template.
func renderDemo(root, id string) (string, error) {
        s := tmpl.NewSet(root, nil)
        t, err := s.Get("demo")
        if err != nil {
                return "", err
        }
        c := tmpl.Context{Version: version}
        if id != "" {
                h, ok := harness.Get(id)
                if !ok {
                        return "", fmt.Errorf("unknown harness %q", id)
                }
                c.Harness = &h
        }
        return s.Render(t, c)
}

const generatedNote = "<!-- Generated by aiculator gen-docs. Do not edit by hand. -->\n\n"

func cliReference() string {
        var b strings.Builder
        b.WriteString(generatedNote + "# CLI reference\n\nEvery command, generated from the program itself. Run any command with `--help` to see the same text.\n")
        var walk func(c *cobra.Command)
        walk = func(c *cobra.Command) {
                for _, sub := range c.Commands() {
                        if sub.Hidden || !sub.IsAvailableCommand() || sub.Name() == "help" || sub.Name() == "completion" {
                                continue
                        }
                        fmt.Fprintf(&b, "\n## `%s`\n\n%s\n", sub.CommandPath(), sub.Short)
                        if sub.Long != "" {
                                fmt.Fprintf(&b, "\n%s\n", sub.Long)
                        }
                        fmt.Fprintf(&b, "\n```text\n%s\n```\n", sub.UseLine())
                        if sub.Example != "" {
                                fmt.Fprintf(&b, "\n**Examples**\n\n```text\n%s\n```\n", sub.Example)
                        }
                        if f := sub.LocalFlags().FlagUsages(); strings.TrimSpace(f) != "" {
                                fmt.Fprintf(&b, "\n**Flags**\n\n```text\n%s```\n", f)
                        }
                        walk(sub)
                }
        }
        walk(rootCmd())
        return b.String()
}

func harnessReference() string {
        var b strings.Builder
        b.WriteString(generatedNote + "# Harness reference\n\nGenerated from the registry in `internal/harness`.\n\n")
        b.WriteString("\"Docs\" means the skill and MCP facts come from that harness's own documentation. \"Table\" means the skill path comes from a community table and the ACP command from the ACP registry, so treat it as a starting point.\n\n")
        b.WriteString("| ID | Name | Skills | MCP config | ACP command | Facts from |\n|---|---|---|---|---|---|\n")
        for _, h := range harness.All() {
                skills := "`" + h.SkillsDir + "` (link)"
                if h.ReadsAgents {
                        skills = "`.agents/skills`"
                }
                mcp := "Shell route"
                if h.MCPFile != "" {
                        mcp = "`" + h.MCPFile + "`"
                }
                acp := "None"
                if len(h.ACP) > 0 {
                        acp = "`" + strings.Join(h.ACP, " ") + "`"
                }
                fmt.Fprintf(&b, "| `%s` | %s | %s | %s | %s | %s |\n", h.ID, h.Name, skills, mcp, acp, h.Source)
        }
        return b.String()
}

package main

import (
        "errors"
        "fmt"
        "os"
        "os/exec"
        "strings"

        "github.com/spf13/cobra"

        "github.com/Grano22/aiculator/internal/harness"
        "github.com/Grano22/aiculator/internal/prompt"
)

// gitState says what a directory needs before the swarm can work in it.
func gitState(dir string) (needsInit, needsCommit bool) {
        run := func(args ...string) error {
                c := exec.Command("git", args...)
                c.Dir = dir
                return c.Run()
        }
        if run("rev-parse", "--git-dir") != nil {
                return true, true
        }
        return false, run("rev-parse", "--verify", "HEAD") != nil
}

// prepareGit makes the first commit the swarm's worktrees need. It adds no files.
func prepareGit(dir string, needsInit bool) error {
        run := func(args ...string) error {
                c := exec.Command("git", args...)
                c.Dir = dir
                out, err := c.CombinedOutput()
                if err != nil {
                        return fmt.Errorf("git %s: %w: %s", args[0], err, strings.TrimSpace(string(out)))
                }
                return nil
        }
        if needsInit {
                if err := run("init", "-q"); err != nil {
                        return err
                }
        }
        return run("commit", "-q", "--allow-empty", "-m", "Initial commit")
}

// routeDetail says what a harness can use, for the list of choices.
func routeDetail(h harness.Harness) string {
        if h.MCP == harness.MCPNone {
                return "skills and shell"
        }
        return "skills, shell and MCP"
}

func initCmd() *cobra.Command {
        var (
                list, sb                 string
                tier                     int
                yes, dry, planner        bool
                noSkills, noMCP, noStart bool
                allHarnesses             bool
                scoped, withMCP          bool
        )
        cmd := &cobra.Command{
                Use:   "init",
                Short: "Set up this machine, step by step: harnesses, skills and MCP config",
                Long: `Asks what you want, then does it. By default this sets up the whole machine: the swarm's
skills go where each harness reads them for every project, so that afterwards aiculator join
only has to start a server in a project. This needs no git repository and starts no server.

With --scoped it sets up this project alone, which also offers to start the server, and to
create the git repository the swarm needs.

Nothing is written until the last question is answered, so backing out with Ctrl-C changes
nothing. Running it again is safe, and keeps what is already there.

For a script, --yes takes every default, and flags answer single questions.`,
                Args: cobra.NoArgs,
                RunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, _ []string) error {
                        err := runInit(cmd, initOptions{
                                list: list, sb: sb, tier: tier, yes: yes, dry: dry, planner: planner,
                                noSkills: noSkills, noMCP: noMCP, noStart: noStart, allHarnesses: allHarnesses,
                                scoped: scoped, withMCP: withMCP,
                        })
                        switch {
                        case errors.Is(err, prompt.ErrCanceled):
                                fmt.Println("Canceled. Nothing was changed.")
                                return nil
                        case errors.Is(err, prompt.ErrNoInput):
                                return errors.New("input ended before all the questions were answered, and nothing was changed: for a script, use --yes")
                        }
                        return err
                },
        }
        f := cmd.Flags()
        f.BoolVarP(&yes, "yes", "y", false, "take every default and ask nothing")
        f.StringVar(&list, "harness", "", "set these up without asking: installed, all, or comma-separated ids")
        f.BoolVar(&allHarnesses, "all-harnesses", false, "also offer harnesses that were not found on this machine")
        f.BoolVar(&scoped, "scoped", false, "set up this project only, rather than the whole machine")
        f.BoolVar(&noSkills, "no-skills", false, "do not install the skills")
        f.BoolVar(&noMCP, "no-mcp", false, "do not add MCP config")
        f.BoolVar(&withMCP, "mcp", false, "add MCP config without asking")
        f.BoolVar(&noStart, "no-start", false, "do not start the server, with --scoped")
        f.IntVar(&tier, "tier", 1, "tier for MCP sessions: 1 standard, 2 advanced, 3 ultra")
        f.BoolVar(&planner, "planner", false, "also allow these sessions to plan")
        f.BoolVar(&dry, "dry-run", false, "say what would be done, and do nothing")
        f.StringVar(&sb, "sandbox", "auto", "sandbox for the server: auto, seatbelt, bwrap, docker or none")
        return cmd
}

type initOptions struct {
        list, sb                 string
        tier                     int
        yes, dry, planner        bool
        noSkills, noMCP, noStart bool
        allHarnesses             bool
        scoped, withMCP          bool
}

// runInit collects every answer first, and acts only afterwards. That is the promise that
// backing out at any question changes nothing.
func runInit(cmd *cobra.Command, o initOptions) error {
        p := prompt.New(os.Stdin, os.Stdout)
        root := projectRoot()
        ask := func(question string, def bool) (bool, error) {
                if o.yes {
                        return def, nil
                }
                return p.Confirm(question, def)
        }
        if !o.yes {
                if o.scoped {
                        p.Say("This sets up %s for the swarm. Nothing is written until you have answered everything.\n", root)
                } else {
                        p.Say("This sets up the swarm for every project on this machine. For this project alone, use --scoped.")
                        p.Say("Nothing is written until you have answered everything.\n")
                }
        }

        // Only a project needs git, because its worktrees need a commit to start from.
        var needsInit, needsCommit, makeGit bool
        if o.scoped {
                needsInit, needsCommit = gitState(root)
        }
        if needsCommit {
                question := "This folder has no commits yet, and the swarm needs one. Make an empty first commit?"
                if needsInit {
                        question = "This folder is not a git repository, and the swarm needs one. Create it, with an empty first commit?"
                }
                // --yes must not turn some folder into a repository without anyone having asked.
                if !o.yes {
                        var err error
                        if makeGit, err = p.Confirm(question, true); err != nil {
                                return err
                        }
                }
                if !makeGit {
                        if !o.noStart {
                                p.Say("Without a commit the server cannot start, so that step will be skipped.")
                        }
                        o.noStart = true
                }
        }

        hs, err := chooseHarnesses(p, o)
        if err != nil {
                return err
        }
        if len(hs) == 0 {
                if !o.dry {
                        p.Say("No harness was chosen, so there is nothing to set up. To see what is supported: aiculator harness")
                }
                return nil
        }

        skills := !o.noSkills
        if skills {
                if skills, err = ask("Install the swarm's skills for these harnesses?", true); err != nil {
                        return err
                }
        }
        anyMCP := false
        for _, h := range hs {
                anyMCP = anyMCP || h.MCP != harness.MCPNone
        }
        mcp := !o.noMCP && anyMCP
        if mcp && !o.withMCP {
                // The tools of every MCP server take up room in a session's context. In one project
                // that is the point. In every session on the machine it is a cost for little gain,
                // since aiculator join adds them where they are wanted, and so the default differs.
                question, def := "Also add MCP config, so new sessions get the swarm's tools directly?", true
                if !o.scoped {
                        question, def = "Also add MCP config for every project? Its tools load in every session; aiculator join can add them per project instead.", false
                }
                if mcp, err = ask(question, def); err != nil {
                        return err
                }
        }
        tier := o.tier
        if mcp && !o.yes && !cmd.Flags().Changed("tier") {
                i, err := p.Select("Which tier are these sessions?", []prompt.Option{
                        {Label: "1 standard", Detail: "routine tasks; the usual choice"},
                        {Label: "2 advanced", Detail: "also takes harder tasks"},
                        {Label: "3 ultra", Detail: "takes the hardest tasks"},
                }, 0)
                if err != nil {
                        return err
                }
                tier = i + 1
        }
        start := o.scoped && !o.noStart
        if start {
                if start, err = ask("Start the server now?", true); err != nil {
                        return err
                }
        }

        plan := setupPlan{harnesses: hs, skills: skills, mcp: mcp, start: start, tier: tier, planner: o.planner, sandbox: o.sb, global: !o.scoped}
        if o.dry {
                printPlan(plan, needsInit && makeGit, needsCommit && makeGit)
                return nil
        }
        if !skills && !mcp && !start && !makeGit {
                p.Say("Nothing to do.")
                return nil
        }
        if makeGit {
                if err := prepareGit(root, needsInit); err != nil {
                        return fmt.Errorf("%w\nIf git does not know who you are, set user.name and user.email, and run this again", err)
                }
        }
        fmt.Println()
        if err := runSetup(plan); err != nil {
                return err
        }
        if needsCommit && !makeGit {
                fmt.Println("The swarm needs a git repository with at least one commit, so make one before aiculator up.")
        }
        return nil
}

func chooseHarnesses(p *prompt.Prompter, o initOptions) ([]harness.Harness, error) {
        if o.list != "" {
                return selectHarnesses(o.list)
        }
        found := harness.Detected()
        if o.yes {
                if len(found) == 0 {
                        return nil, errors.New("no known harness found on PATH; name one with --harness, or see aiculator harness")
                }
                return found, nil
        }
        choices := found
        if o.allHarnesses || len(found) == 0 {
                if len(found) == 0 {
                        p.Say("No known harness was found on PATH, so here are all of them.")
                }
                choices = harness.All()
        }
        options := make([]prompt.Option, len(choices))
        for i, h := range choices {
                detail := routeDetail(h)
                installed := h.Installed()
                if !installed {
                        detail += ", not found here"
                }
                options[i] = prompt.Option{Label: h.ID, Detail: detail, Selected: installed}
        }
        picked, err := p.MultiSelect("Which harnesses should use the swarm?", options)
        if err != nil {
                return nil, err
        }
        out := make([]harness.Harness, 0, len(picked))
        for _, i := range picked {
                out = append(out, choices[i])
        }
        return out, nil
}

func printPlan(s setupPlan, gitInit, gitCommit bool) {
        fmt.Println("This would:")
        if gitInit {
                fmt.Println("- Create a git repository")
        }
        if gitCommit {
                fmt.Println("- Make an empty first commit")
        }
        ids := make([]string, 0, len(s.harnesses))
        for _, h := range s.harnesses {
                ids = append(ids, h.ID)
        }
        if s.skills {
                where := ".agents/skills"
                if s.global {
                        where = "~/.agents/skills, for every project"
                }
                fmt.Printf("- Install the swarm's skills in %s, and link them for: %s\n", where, strings.Join(ids, ", "))
        }
        if s.mcp {
                for _, h := range s.harnesses {
                        file := h.MCPFile
                        if s.global {
                                file = h.GlobalMCPFile
                        }
                        if h.MCP != harness.MCPNone && file != "" {
                                fmt.Printf("- Add MCP config for %s to %s, at tier %d\n", h.ID, file, s.tier)
                        }
                }
        }
        if s.start {
                fmt.Println("- Start the server")
        }
        fmt.Println("Nothing was changed.")
}

package main

import (
        "context"
        "crypto/rand"
        "encoding/hex"
        "encoding/json"
        "errors"
        "fmt"
        "maps"
        "net"
        "net/http"
        "os"
        "os/exec"
        "path/filepath"
        "slices"
        "strconv"
        "strings"
        "sync"
        "text/tabwriter"
        "time"

        "github.com/modelcontextprotocol/go-sdk/mcp"
        "github.com/spf13/cobra"

        "github.com/Grano22/aiculator/internal/api"
        "github.com/Grano22/aiculator/internal/client"
        "github.com/Grano22/aiculator/internal/engine"
        "github.com/Grano22/aiculator/internal/harness"
        "github.com/Grano22/aiculator/internal/realm"
        "github.com/Grano22/aiculator/internal/skillpack"
        "github.com/Grano22/aiculator/internal/swarm"
)

// projectRoot is the git top level, or the working directory outside a repository.
func projectRoot() string {
        out, err := exec.Command("git", "rev-parse", "--show-toplevel").Output()
        if err == nil {
                // Inside a task's worktree this is the worktree. The project owns the data dir.
                root := strings.TrimSpace(string(out))
                if !strings.Contains(root, string(filepath.Separator)+".swarm"+string(filepath.Separator)) {
                        return root
                }
                if abs, err := filepath.Abs(dataDir); err == nil {
                        return filepath.Dir(abs)
                }
        }
        wd, err := os.Getwd()
        if err != nil {
                return "."
        }
        return wd
}

func healthy(url string) bool {
        ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), time.Second)
        defer cancel()
        return client.New(url, "").Get(ctx, "/v1/healthz", nil) == nil
}

func serverURL() (string, bool) {
        b, err := os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(dataDir, "addr"))
        if err != nil {
                return "", false
        }
        url := strings.TrimSpace(string(b))
        return url, ownServer(url)
}

// ownServer checks that the server answering there is this project's. After a crash, the
// address file can point at a port that another project's server has since taken.
func ownServer(url string) bool {
        ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), time.Second)
        defer cancel()
        var h map[string]string
        if client.New(url, "").Get(ctx, "/v1/healthz", &h) != nil {
                return false
        }
        abs, err := filepath.Abs(dataDir)
        if err != nil {
                return true
        }
        // A server from an older version does not say, and it is given the benefit of the doubt.
        return h["instance"] == "" || h["instance"] == realm.Instance(abs)
}

// excludeData keeps the data directory out of git without changing a tracked file.
func excludeData(root string) {
        cmd := exec.Command("git", "rev-parse", "--git-path", "info/exclude")
        cmd.Dir = root
        out, err := cmd.Output()
        if err != nil {
                return
        }
        path := strings.TrimSpace(string(out))
        if !filepath.IsAbs(path) {
                path = filepath.Join(root, path)
        }
        b, _ := os.ReadFile(path)
        for _, l := range strings.Split(string(b), "\n") {
                if strings.TrimSpace(l) == ".swarm/" {
                        return
                }
        }
        if err := os.MkdirAll(filepath.Dir(path), 0o755); err != nil {
                return
        }
        f, err := os.OpenFile(path, os.O_APPEND|os.O_CREATE|os.O_WRONLY, 0o644)
        if err != nil {
                return
        }
        defer f.Close()
        if len(b) > 0 && b[len(b)-1] != '\n' {
                _, _ = f.WriteString("\n")
        }
        _, _ = f.WriteString(".swarm/\n")
}

// startServer launches the server in the background unless one is already running.
// It reuses the previous address when it can, so open sessions can reconnect.
func startServer(sb string) (string, error) {
        if url, ok := serverURL(); ok {
                return url, nil
        }
        root := projectRoot()
        if dataDir == ".swarm" {
                dataDir = filepath.Join(root, ".swarm")
        }
        abs, err := filepath.Abs(dataDir)
        if err != nil {
                return "", err
        }
        if err := os.MkdirAll(abs, 0o700); err != nil {
                return "", err
        }
        excludeData(root)
        addr := "127.0.0.1:0"
        if b, err := os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(abs, "addr")); err == nil {
                // Reusing the port lets open sessions reconnect, but only if it is still free: another
                // project's server may have taken it since this one last ran.
                last := strings.TrimPrefix(strings.TrimSpace(string(b)), "http://")
                if ln, err := net.Listen("tcp", last); err == nil {
                        _ = ln.Close()
                        addr = last
                }
        }
        _ = os.Remove(filepath.Join(abs, "addr"))
        cmd, logPath, err := spawnServe(root, abs, addr, sb, false)
        if err != nil {
                return "", err
        }
        exited := make(chan error, 1)
        go func() { exited <- cmd.Wait() }()
        deadline := time.Now().Add(30 * time.Second)
        for time.Now().Before(deadline) {
                if url, ok := serverURL(); ok {
                        return url, nil
                }
                select {
                case <-exited:
                        tail, _ := os.ReadFile(logPath)
                        if len(tail) > 800 {
                                tail = tail[len(tail)-800:]
                        }
                        return "", fmt.Errorf("the server exited during startup:\n%s", tail)
                case <-time.After(50 * time.Millisecond):
                }
        }
        return "", fmt.Errorf("the server did not start in time; see %s", logPath)
}

// spawnServe starts a detached server writing to server.log.
func spawnServe(root, abs, addr, sb string, standby bool) (*exec.Cmd, string, error) {
        self, err := os.Executable()
        if err != nil {
                return nil, "", err
        }
        logPath := filepath.Join(abs, "server.log")
        logFile, err := os.OpenFile(logPath, os.O_APPEND|os.O_CREATE|os.O_WRONLY, 0o600)
        if err != nil {
                return nil, "", err
        }
        defer logFile.Close()
        args := append([]string{"serve", "--data", abs, "--addr", addr, "--repo", root, "--sandbox", sb}, loggingArgs()...)
        if len(upAging) > 0 {
                args = append(args, "--aging", strings.Join(upAging, ","))
        }
        if standby {
                args = append(args, "--standby")
        }
        cmd := exec.Command(self, args...)
        cmd.Dir = root
        cmd.Stdout, cmd.Stderr = logFile, logFile
        detach(cmd)
        if err := cmd.Start(); err != nil {
                return nil, "", err
        }
        return cmd, logPath, nil
}

// startStandby starts a server that waits on the data directory and takes over when the
// leader stops, on the leader's address so that sessions reconnect to the same place.
func startStandby(sb string) (int, error) {
        url, err := startServer(sb)
        if err != nil {
                return 0, err
        }
        pidPath := filepath.Join(dataDir, "standby.pid")
        if pid := pidFile(pidPath); pid != 0 && processAlive(pid) {
                return pid, nil
        }
        abs, err := filepath.Abs(dataDir)
        if err != nil {
                return 0, err
        }
        cmd, logPath, err := spawnServe(projectRoot(), abs, strings.TrimPrefix(url, "http://"), sb, true)
        if err != nil {
                return 0, err
        }
        exited := make(chan error, 1)
        go func() { exited <- cmd.Wait() }()
        for range 200 {
                if pidFile(pidPath) == cmd.Process.Pid {
                        return cmd.Process.Pid, nil
                }
                select {
                case <-exited:
                        return 0, fmt.Errorf("the standby exited during startup; see %s", logPath)
                case <-time.After(50 * time.Millisecond):
                }
        }
        return 0, fmt.Errorf("the standby did not start in time; see %s", logPath)
}

// stopPid stops a process and waits for it to exit.
func stopPid(pid int) (bool, error) {
        // A process that died just now needs no signal.
        if err := stopProcess(pid); err != nil && processAlive(pid) {
                return false, err
        }
        // The endpoint closes before the store finishes writing, so wait for the process
        // itself. Then a new up, or removing .swarm, cannot meet it.
        for range 400 {
                if !processAlive(pid) {
                        return true, nil
                }
                time.Sleep(50 * time.Millisecond)
        }
        return false, nil
}

// upAging is passed on to the server that up starts.
var upAging []string

func upCmd() *cobra.Command {
        var sb string
        var standby bool
        cmd := &cobra.Command{
                Use:   "up",
                Short: "Start the swarm server for this project in the background",
                Long: `Start the swarm server for this project in the background.

With --standby, also start a second server that waits and takes over if the first one
stops or dies. The leader is whoever holds the lock on .swarm, so the two never write at
once. Both must run on this machine.`,
                RunE: func(*cobra.Command, []string) error {
                        if standby {
                                pid, err := startStandby(sb)
                                if err != nil {
                                        return err
                                }
                                url, _ := serverURL()
                                fmt.Printf("%s\nstandby %d\n", url, pid)
                                return nil
                        }
                        url, err := startServer(sb)
                        if err != nil {
                                return err
                        }
                        fmt.Println(url)
                        return nil
                },
        }
        cmd.Flags().StringVar(&sb, "sandbox", "auto", "sandbox: auto, seatbelt, bwrap, docker or none")
        cmd.Flags().StringSliceVar(&upAging, "aging", nil, "raise priority after a wait, as wait=boost, such as 1h=5,4h=20")
        cmd.Flags().BoolVar(&standby, "standby", false, "also start a standby server that takes over if this one dies")
        return cmd
}

func downCmd() *cobra.Command {
        return &cobra.Command{
                Use:   "down",
                Short: "Stop the swarm server for this project",
                RunE: func(*cobra.Command, []string) error {
                        // The standby goes first, or it would take over from the leader being stopped.
                        if pid := pidFile(filepath.Join(dataDir, "standby.pid")); pid != 0 && processAlive(pid) {
                                if ok, err := stopPid(pid); err != nil {
                                        return err
                                } else if ok {
                                        fmt.Println("standby stopped")
                                }
                        }
                        url, ok := serverURL()
                        if !ok {
                                fmt.Println("no server is running")
                                return nil
                        }
                        b, err := os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(dataDir, "pid"))
                        if err != nil {
                                return err
                        }
                        pid, err := strconv.Atoi(strings.TrimSpace(string(b)))
                        if err != nil {
                                return fmt.Errorf("bad pid file: %w", err)
                        }
                        stopped, err := stopPid(pid)
                        if err != nil {
                                return err
                        }
                        if stopped {
                                fmt.Println("stopped")
                                return nil
                        }
                        if healthy(url) {
                                return errors.New("the server did not stop")
                        }
                        // A container with no init never reaps the process, so it looks alive forever.
                        fmt.Printf("stopped answering, but process %d has not exited\n", pid)
                        return nil
                },
        }
}

func selectHarnesses(arg string) ([]harness.Harness, error) {
        switch arg {
        case "", "installed", "detected":
                return harness.Detected(), nil
        case "all":
                return harness.All(), nil
        }
        var out []harness.Harness
        for _, id := range strings.Split(arg, ",") {
                h, ok := harness.Get(strings.TrimSpace(id))
                if !ok {
                        return nil, fmt.Errorf("unknown harness %q: see aiculator harness", id)
                }
                out = append(out, h)
        }
        return out, nil
}

// selfCommand prefers the bare name, so a committed config works on any machine.
func selfCommand() string {
        self, err := os.Executable()
        if err != nil {
                return "aiculator"
        }
        if found, err := exec.LookPath("aiculator"); err == nil {
                a, _ := filepath.EvalSymlinks(found)
                b, _ := filepath.EvalSymlinks(self)
                if a == b {
                        return "aiculator"
                }
        }
        return self
}

// setupPlan is what join and init have decided to do.
type setupPlan struct {
        harnesses          []harness.Harness
        skills, mcp, start bool
        tier               int
        planner            bool
        sandbox            string
        // global sets up the whole machine rather than this project.
        global bool
        // reuse leaves alone what a harness can already find, at either level.
        reuse bool
}

const swarmSkills = "swarm-*"

// bundledSwarmSkills lists the skills a project needs a harness to find.
var bundledSwarmSkills = []string{"swarm-join", "swarm-operate", "swarm-plan"}

// globalBackups is where config is copied before a user-level file is changed.
func globalBackups() string { return harness.ExpandHome("~/.aiculator/backups") }

// atUserLevel returns the harness with its MCP config pointed at the user-level file, or
// false if it has none.
func atUserLevel(h harness.Harness) (harness.Harness, bool) {
        if h.GlobalMCPFile == "" {
                return h, false
        }
        h.MCPFile = harness.ExpandHome(h.GlobalMCPFile)
        return h, true
}

// skillsFound reports whether a harness can already find all the swarm's skills, and where
// the nearest one is.
func skillsFound(h harness.Harness, root string) (string, bool) {
        level := ""
        for _, name := range bundledSwarmSkills {
                w := skillpack.Where(name, h, root)
                if w == "" {
                        return "", false
                }
                if level == "" || w == "project" {
                        level = w
                }
        }
        return level, true
}

// installSkills puts skills where the plan says, and returns how each harness finds them.
func installSkills(p setupPlan, root string) (map[string]string, error) {
        levels := map[string]string{}
        var need []harness.Harness
        for _, h := range p.harnesses {
                if p.global && !skillpack.HasGlobal(h) {
                        levels[h.ID] = "none"
                        continue
                }
                if p.reuse {
                        if level, ok := skillsFound(h, root); ok {
                                levels[h.ID] = level
                                continue
                        }
                }
                need = append(need, h)
                levels[h.ID] = "project"
                if p.global {
                        levels[h.ID] = "global"
                }
        }
        if len(need) == 0 {
                return levels, nil
        }
        acts, err := skillpack.Install(skillpack.Options{Root: root, Global: p.global, Patterns: []string{swarmSkills}, Harnesses: need})
        if err != nil {
                return nil, err
        }
        for _, a := range acts {
                if a.What == "conflict" || a.What == "invalid" {
                        fmt.Printf("warning: %s for %s: %s\n", a.Skill, a.Target, a.Detail)
                }
        }
        return levels, nil
}

// writeMCPFor adds a harness's MCP config, and says how it can reach the swarm.
func writeMCPFor(p setupPlan, h harness.Harness, root string, args []string) (string, error) {
        if h.MCP == harness.MCPNone {
                return "", nil
        }
        target, backups := h, filepath.Join(dataDir, "backups")
        if p.global {
                var ok bool
                if target, ok = atUserLevel(h); !ok {
                        return "no user-level MCP config, so use aiculator init --scoped in a project", nil
                }
                backups = globalBackups()
        } else if p.reuse {
                if user, ok := atUserLevel(h); ok && user.HasMCP(root) {
                        return "MCP is already set for every project, in " + h.GlobalMCPFile + ", at the tier chosen then", nil
                }
        }
        e := harness.Entry{Command: selfCommand(), Args: append(slices.Clone(args), "--harness", h.ID)}
        r, err := target.WriteMCP(root, e, backups)
        if err != nil {
                return "", err
        }
        if r.Path == "" {
                return "", nil
        }
        shown := h.MCPFile
        if p.global {
                shown = h.GlobalMCPFile
        }
        return "MCP in " + shown + " after a restart", nil
}

// runSetup does the writing for join and init. Each step can be run again safely.
func runSetup(p setupPlan) error {
        hs, tier := p.harnesses, p.tier
        if p.start {
                if _, err := startServer(p.sandbox); err != nil {
                        return err
                }
        }
        root := projectRoot()
        levels := map[string]string{}
        if p.skills {
                var err error
                if levels, err = installSkills(p, root); err != nil {
                        return err
                }
                if p.global {
                        fmt.Println("Skills are in ~/.agents/skills for every project. Edit them only there.")
                        fmt.Println()
                } else if slices.Contains(slices.Collect(maps.Values(levels)), "project") {
                        fmt.Printf("Skills are in %s. Edit them only there.\n\n", skillpack.CanonicalDir)
                } else {
                        fmt.Println("Skills were already installed for every project, so they were left as they are.")
                        fmt.Println()
                }
        }
        args := []string{"mcp", "--auto", "--tier", strconv.Itoa(tier)}
        if p.planner {
                args = append(args, "--planner")
        }
        for _, h := range hs {
                var parts []string
                switch {
                case !p.skills:
                case levels[h.ID] == "none":
                        parts = append(parts, "no user-level skills, so use aiculator init --scoped in a project")
                case p.global:
                        parts = append(parts, "skills for every project")
                default:
                        parts = append(parts, "shell (no restart needed)")
                }
                if p.mcp {
                        route, err := writeMCPFor(p, h, root, args)
                        if err != nil {
                                fmt.Printf("%-10s could not write its MCP config: %v\n", h.ID, err)
                                continue
                        }
                        if route != "" {
                                parts = append(parts, route)
                        }
                }
                if len(parts) == 0 {
                        parts = append(parts, "nothing installed")
                }
                fmt.Printf("%-10s %s\n", h.ID, strings.Join(parts, "; "))
                if h.Source != harness.SourceDocs {
                        fmt.Printf("%-10s paths come from a community table, not %s's docs; run aiculator skill --list to check\n", "", h.Name)
                }
                if h.Note != "" {
                        fmt.Printf("%-10s %s\n", "", h.Note)
                }
        }
        fmt.Println()
        switch {
        case p.global:
                fmt.Println("This machine is set up. In a project, start the swarm with: aiculator join")
        case p.skills:
                dir := skillpack.CanonicalDir
                if !slices.Contains(slices.Collect(maps.Values(levels)), "project") {
                        dir = "~/" + skillpack.CanonicalDir
                }
                fmt.Printf("In a NEW session, ask it to use the swarm-join skill (/swarm-join in Claude Code).\n")
                fmt.Printf("In a session ALREADY OPEN, paste this; it needs no restart:\n\n")
                fmt.Printf("  Read %s/swarm-join/SKILL.md and follow it. Join as tier %d.\n\n", dir, tier)
        case p.mcp:
                fmt.Println("Restart your harness, and ask it to use the swarm's wait_for_task tool.")
                fmt.Println()
        }
        if !p.global && !p.start {
                fmt.Println("The server is not running. Start it with: aiculator up")
        }
        if !p.skills && !p.mcp {
                fmt.Println("No harness was connected. To add that later, run aiculator init again.")
        }
        if selfCommand() != "aiculator" {
                fmt.Printf("Note: aiculator is not on PATH. The skills call it by name, so add %s to PATH.\n", filepath.Dir(selfCommand()))
        }
        if !p.global {
                fmt.Println("A joined session runs outside the sandbox, under its harness's own permissions.")
                fmt.Println("For sandboxed workers, use aiculator drive.")
        }
        return nil
}

It starts the server, and works on its own on a machine with nothing set up: it installs the
bundled skills into .agents/skills, links them to harnesses that need it, and registers the
