func skillCmd() *cobra.Command {
        var (
                install, uninstall             []string
                listFlag, lint, global, copyIt bool
                force, purge                   bool
                harnesses, newName, desc       string
                paths, sources                 []string
        )
        cmd := &cobra.Command{
                Use:   "skill [--install PATTERN...]",
                Short: "Manage skills in one place: .agents/skills",
                Long: `Skills live in .agents/skills. Installing puts them where each harness looks: harnesses
that scan .agents/skills need nothing, and the others get a link. Skills in .agent/skills
are picked up too. An edit in one place reaches every harness.

Patterns use * for anything, ? for one character and [abc] for a set. Quote any pattern
with a wildcard: an unquoted * alone also works, but zsh stops at an unmatched *-sth.`,
                Example: `  aiculator skill --install '*'                  all skills, to every installed harness
  aiculator skill --install 'swarm-*' 'lint-?'   by pattern
  aiculator skill --install '*-tool' --global    into ~/.agents/skills and home directories
  aiculator skill --install '*' --harness all    every supported harness, installed or not
  aiculator skill --install x --harness claude,pi
  aiculator skill --install x --path ./vendor/skills --harness none
  aiculator skill --install x --source ~/my-skills
  aiculator skill --list
  aiculator skill --lint
  aiculator skill --new my-skill --description "..."
  aiculator skill --uninstall 'swarm-*' --purge`,
                Args: cobra.ArbitraryArgs,
                RunE: func(c *cobra.Command, args []string) error {
                        root := projectRoot()
                        var hs []harness.Harness
                        if harnesses != "none" {
                                var err error
                                if hs, err = selectHarnesses(harnesses); err != nil {
                                        return err
                                }
                        }
                        o := skillpack.Options{Root: root, Global: global, Harnesses: hs, Paths: paths, Sources: sources, Copy: copyIt, Force: force, Purge: purge}
                        wd, _ := os.Getwd()
                        switch {
                        case c.Flags().Changed("install"):
                                // Words after --install are more patterns, including an expanded *.
                                o.Patterns = skillpack.NormalizeShellStar(append(install, args...), wd)
                                acts, err := skillpack.Install(o)
                                printActions(acts)
                                return err
                        case c.Flags().Changed("uninstall"):
                                o.Patterns = skillpack.NormalizeShellStar(append(uninstall, args...), wd)
                                acts, err := skillpack.Uninstall(o)
                                printActions(acts)
                                return err
                        case newName != "":
                                dir, err := skillpack.New(o, newName, desc)
                                if err != nil {
                                        return err
                                }
                                fmt.Printf("Created %s. Edit it, then run: aiculator skill --install %s\n", dir, newName)
                                return nil
                        case lint:
                                return lintAll(o)
                        case listFlag, len(args) == 0:
                                return listSkills(o)
                        }
                        return c.Help()
                },
        }
        f := cmd.Flags()
        f.StringSliceVar(&install, "install", nil, "install skills matching these patterns")
        f.StringSliceVar(&uninstall, "uninstall", nil, "remove skills matching these patterns from harnesses")
        f.BoolVar(&listFlag, "list", false, "list skills")
        f.BoolVar(&lint, "lint", false, "check skills against the Agent Skills spec")
        f.StringVar(&newName, "new", "", "create a skill with full metadata")
        f.StringVar(&desc, "description", "", "description for --new")
        f.StringVar(&harnesses, "harness", "installed", "installed, all, none, or comma-separated ids")
        f.StringSliceVar(&paths, "path", nil, "also install to this directory")
        f.StringSliceVar(&sources, "source", nil, "also read skills from this directory")
        f.BoolVar(&global, "global", false, "use ~/.agents/skills and home directories")
        f.BoolVar(&copyIt, "copy", false, "copy instead of linking, for tools that do not follow links")
        f.BoolVar(&force, "force", false, "refresh bundled skills and replace links; your own directories are never replaced")
        f.BoolVar(&purge, "purge", false, "with --uninstall, also delete from .agents/skills")
        return cmd
}

func printActions(acts []skillpack.Action) {
        w := tabwriter.NewWriter(os.Stdout, 0, 0, 2, ' ', 0)
        for _, a := range acts {
                fmt.Fprintf(w, "%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\n", a.Skill, a.What, a.Target, a.Detail)
        }
        _ = w.Flush()
}

func listSkills(o skillpack.Options) error {
        rows, err := skillpack.List(o)
        if err != nil {
                return err
        }
        w := tabwriter.NewWriter(os.Stdout, 0, 0, 2, ' ', 0)
        fmt.Fprintln(w, "SKILL\tVERSION\tKIND\tINSTALLED\tLINT\tHARNESSES\tSOURCE")
        for _, r := range rows {
                state := "-"
                if r.Installed {
                        state = "yes"
                }
                fmt.Fprintf(w, "%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\t%de %dw\t%s\t%s\n", r.Name, r.Version, r.Kind, state, r.Errors, r.Warnings, strings.Join(r.Harnesses, ","), r.Source)
        }
        return w.Flush()
}

func lintAll(o skillpack.Options) error {
        dir := filepath.Join(o.Root, skillpack.CanonicalDir)
        if o.Global {
                home, _ := os.UserHomeDir()
                dir = filepath.Join(home, skillpack.CanonicalDir)
        }
        entries, err := os.ReadDir(dir)
        if err != nil {
                return err
        }
        failed := false
        for _, e := range entries {
                p := filepath.Join(dir, e.Name())
                if _, err := os.Stat(filepath.Join(p, "SKILL.md")); err != nil {
                        continue
                }
                issues := skillpack.Lint(p)
                if len(issues) == 0 {
                        fmt.Printf("%s: ok\n", e.Name())
                }
                for _, i := range issues {
                        fmt.Printf("%s: %s: %s\n", e.Name(), i.Level, i.Msg)
                }
                failed = failed || skillpack.IssuesHaveErrors(issues)
        }
        if failed {
                return errors.New("some skills have errors")
        }
        return nil
}

func randomSuffix() string {
        var b [3]byte
        _, _ = rand.Read(b[:])
        return hex.EncodeToString(b[:])
}

// issueLocal mints a token with the local admin token. Reaching that file already
// means being this user, and the sandbox hides it from sandboxed agents.
func issueLocal(ctx context.Context, q api.TokenReq) (url, token string, err error) {
        c, err := adminClient()
        if err != nil {
                return "", "", fmt.Errorf("%w; start the server with: aiculator up", err)
        }
        var out map[string]string
        if err := c.Post(ctx, "/v1/tokens", q, &out); err != nil {
                return "", "", fmt.Errorf("no server answered at %s: %w; start it with: aiculator up", c.URL, err)
        }
        return c.URL, out["token"], nil
}

type bearer struct {
        token string
        next  http.RoundTripper
}

func (b bearer) RoundTrip(r *http.Request) (*http.Response, error) {
        r = r.Clone(r.Context())
        r.Header.Set("Authorization", "Bearer "+b.token)
        return b.next.RoundTrip(r)
}

// bridge forwards tool calls to the server, reconnecting if the server restarted.
type bridge struct {
        url, token string
        // issue gets a token when one is needed, for a bridge that finds its server by itself.
        issue   func(ctx context.Context) (url, token string, err error)
        mu      sync.Mutex
        session *mcp.ClientSession
}

func (b *bridge) connect(ctx context.Context) (*mcp.ClientSession, error) {
        b.mu.Lock()
        defer b.mu.Unlock()
        if b.session != nil {
                return b.session, nil
        }
        if b.issue != nil {
                // Looked up each time, so a server started after this session began is found, and
                // one that moved to a new port after a restart is found again.
                url, token, err := b.issue(ctx)
                if err != nil {
                        return nil, err
                }
                b.url, b.token = url, token
        }
        cl := mcp.NewClient(&mcp.Implementation{Name: "aiculator-bridge", Version: version}, nil)
        s, err := cl.Connect(ctx, &mcp.StreamableClientTransport{
                Endpoint:   b.url + "/mcp",
                HTTPClient: &http.Client{Transport: bearer{b.token, http.DefaultTransport}},
        }, nil)
        if err != nil {
                return nil, err
        }
        b.session = s
        return s, nil
}

// reset forgets the connection, so the next call finds the server again.
func (b *bridge) reset() {
        b.mu.Lock()
        defer b.mu.Unlock()
        if b.session != nil {
                _ = b.session.Close()
                b.session = nil
        }
}

func (b *bridge) drop(s *mcp.ClientSession) {
        b.mu.Lock()
        defer b.mu.Unlock()
        if b.session == s {
                b.session = nil
                _ = s.Close()
        }
}

func (b *bridge) call(ctx context.Context, p *mcp.CallToolParams) (*mcp.CallToolResult, error) {
        s, err := b.connect(ctx)
        if err != nil {
                return nil, err
        }
        r, err := s.CallTool(ctx, p)
        if err == nil || ctx.Err() != nil {
                return r, err
        }
        // The tool itself never ran or its reply was lost, and the lease model makes a
        // repeat safe: a lost grant simply expires. Reconnect once in case of a restart.
        b.drop(s)
        s, err = b.connect(ctx)
        if err != nil {
                return nil, fmt.Errorf("the swarm server is unreachable: %w", err)
        }
        return s.CallTool(ctx, p)
}

// mcpCmd bridges stdio to the server, for harnesses that launch MCP servers as
// subprocesses. --auto gets its own token locally, so harness config holds no secret.
// noSwarmHere is what a tool answers in a folder that has not joined a swarm. It says what
// to do, because the model reading it can pass that on.
const noSwarmHere = "This folder has no swarm server running. To start one, run: aiculator join. Then call this tool again; the session does not need a restart."

type realmUseInput struct {
        Name string `json:"name" jsonschema:"the realm to work in, as listed by realm_list"`
}

// serveAutoBridge offers the swarm's tools from any folder, and looks for a server only when
// one is called. So a config that applies to every project cannot show up as a broken MCP
// server in the ones that do not use the swarm. No server here is an answer, not a failure.
//
// A session stays in the realm of the folder it started in. With switching allowed it can
// also list the others and move between them, but never while it holds a task.
func serveAutoBridge(ctx context.Context, q api.TokenReq, harnessID string, switching bool) error {
        if q.Agent == "" {
                name := harnessID
                if name == "" {
                        name = "session"
                }
                q.Agent = name + "-" + randomSuffix()
        }
        tools, instructions, err := api.ToolDefinitions(ctx)
        if err != nil {
                return err
        }
        var from string
        if from, err = os.Getwd(); err != nil {
                return err
        }
        var heldMu sync.Mutex
        held := ""
        b := &bridge{}
        b.issue = func(ctx context.Context) (string, string, error) {
                if !dataDirFlagSet {
                        heldMu.Lock()
                        dataDir = findDataDirFrom(from)
                        heldMu.Unlock()
                }
                return issueLocal(ctx, q)
        }
        srv := mcp.NewServer(&mcp.Implementation{Name: "swarm", Version: version}, &mcp.ServerOptions{Instructions: instructions})
        for _, t := range tools {
                name := t.Name
                srv.AddTool(t, func(ctx context.Context, r *mcp.CallToolRequest) (*mcp.CallToolResult, error) {
                        res, err := b.call(ctx, &mcp.CallToolParams{Name: r.Params.Name, Arguments: r.Params.Arguments})
                        if err != nil && ctx.Err() == nil {
                                return &mcp.CallToolResult{IsError: true, Content: []mcp.Content{&mcp.TextContent{Text: noSwarmHere}}}, nil
                        }
                        if err == nil && switching {
                                heldMu.Lock()
                                held = trackHeld(held, name, res)
                                heldMu.Unlock()
                        }
                        return res, err
                })
        }
        if switching {
                mcp.AddTool(srv, &mcp.Tool{Name: "realm_list", Description: "List the projects on this machine that use the swarm, with which ones are running and which one this session is in."},
                        func(ctx context.Context, _ *mcp.CallToolRequest, _ struct{}) (*mcp.CallToolResult, any, error) {
                                all, err := realm.List()
                                if err != nil {
                                        return nil, nil, err
                                }
                                heldMu.Lock()
                                current := findDataDirFrom(from)
                                heldMu.Unlock()
                                views := make([]map[string]any, 0, len(all))
                                for _, r := range all {
                                        _, statErr := os.Stat(filepath.Join(r.DataDir, "addr"))
                                        views = append(views, map[string]any{"name": r.Name, "path": r.Path, "running": statErr == nil, "current": r.DataDir == current})
                                }
                                return nil, map[string]any{"realms": views}, nil
                        })
                mcp.AddTool(srv, &mcp.Tool{Name: "realm_use", Description: "Move this session to another project's swarm. Refused while you hold a task: finish or release it first, because a lease belongs to one realm."},
                        func(ctx context.Context, _ *mcp.CallToolRequest, in realmUseInput) (*mcp.CallToolResult, any, error) {
                                heldMu.Lock()
                                defer heldMu.Unlock()
                                if held != "" {
                                        return nil, nil, fmt.Errorf("you hold task %s here: submit, fail or release it before moving", held)
                                }
                                r, err := realm.Get(in.Name)
                                if err != nil {
                                        return nil, nil, err
                                }
                                from = r.Path
                                b.reset()
                                return nil, map[string]any{"realm": r.Name, "path": r.Path}, nil
                        })
        }
        defer b.reset()
        return srv.Run(ctx, &mcp.StdioTransport{})
}

// trackHeld works out which task this session holds after a tool call.
func trackHeld(held, tool string, r *mcp.CallToolResult) string {
        if r == nil || r.IsError {
                return held
        }
        switch tool {
        case "wait_for_task", "claim":
                b, err := json.Marshal(r.StructuredContent)
                if err != nil {
                        return held
                }
                var g struct {
                        Action string `json:"action"`
                        Task   struct {
                                ID string `json:"id"`
                        } `json:"task"`
                }
                if json.Unmarshal(b, &g) == nil && g.Action == "task" {
                        return g.Task.ID
                }
        case "submit", "fail", "release", "review_verdict":
                return ""
        }
        return held
}

func mcpCmd() *cobra.Command {
        var (
                url, harnessID, agent string
                auto, planner         bool
                realmSwitch           bool
                tier                  int
        )
        cmd := &cobra.Command{
                Use:   "mcp",
                Short: "Serve the swarm's MCP tools over stdio (--auto, or a token in SWARM_TOKEN)",
                RunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, _ []string) error {
                        ctx := cmd.Context()
                        if auto {
                                return serveAutoBridge(ctx, api.TokenReq{Agent: agent, Tier: tier, Planner: planner}, harnessID, realmSwitch)
                        }
                        token := os.Getenv("SWARM_TOKEN")
                        if token == "" {
                                return errors.New("SWARM_TOKEN is not set; or pass --auto")
                        }
                        b := &bridge{url: url, token: token}
                        session, err := b.connect(ctx)
                        if err != nil {
                                return err
                        }
                        defer func() { b.drop(session) }()
                        srv := mcp.NewServer(&mcp.Implementation{Name: "swarm", Version: version},
                                &mcp.ServerOptions{Instructions: session.InitializeResult().Instructions})
                        for t, err := range session.Tools(ctx, nil) {
                                if err != nil {
                                        return err
                                }
                                srv.AddTool(t, func(ctx context.Context, r *mcp.CallToolRequest) (*mcp.CallToolResult, error) {
                                        return b.call(ctx, &mcp.CallToolParams{Name: r.Params.Name, Arguments: r.Params.Arguments})
                                })
                        }
                        return srv.Run(ctx, &mcp.StdioTransport{})
                },
        }
        f := cmd.Flags()
        f.StringVar(&url, "url", "http://127.0.0.1:7777", "server URL; --auto finds it")
        f.BoolVar(&auto, "auto", false, "find the local server and get a token by itself")
        f.StringVar(&harnessID, "harness", "", "harness id, used in the agent's name")
        f.StringVar(&agent, "agent", "", "agent name; generated if empty")
        f.IntVar(&tier, "tier", 1, "tier, with --auto")
        f.BoolVar(&planner, "planner", false, "allow planning, with --auto")
        f.BoolVar(&realmSwitch, "realm-switch", false, "with --auto: let the session list other realms and move between them")
        cmd.AddCommand(mcpAddCmd(), mcpPrintCmd(), mcpRemoveCmd())
        return cmd
}

// workCmd is the shell route: every worker capability as a command, for harnesses with
// no MCP and for sessions that were open before MCP was configured.
func workCmd() *cobra.Command {
        cmd := &cobra.Command{
                Use:   "work",
                Short: "Work the queue from a shell: the route for any harness, no restart needed",
        }
        var harnessID string
        var tier int
        var plannerFlag bool
        var agentName string
        join := &cobra.Command{
                Use:   "join",
                Short: "Register this session as a worker and print its agent name",
                RunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, _ []string) error {
                        name := agentName
                        if name == "" {
                                prefix := harnessID
                                if prefix == "" {
                                        prefix = "session"
                                }
                                name = prefix + "-" + randomSuffix()
                        }
                        _, tok, err := issueLocal(cmd.Context(), api.TokenReq{Agent: name, Tier: tier, Planner: plannerFlag})
                        if err != nil {
                                return err
                        }
                        dir := filepath.Join(dataDir, "agents")
                        if err := os.MkdirAll(dir, 0o700); err != nil {
                                return err
                        }
                        if err := os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(dir, name+".token"), []byte(tok), 0o600); err != nil {
                                return err
                        }
                        fmt.Println(name)
                        return nil
                },
        }
        join.Flags().StringVar(&harnessID, "harness", "", "harness id, used in the agent's name")
        join.Flags().IntVar(&tier, "tier", 1, "tier: 1 standard, 2 advanced, 3 ultra")
        join.Flags().BoolVar(&plannerFlag, "planner", false, "also allow this session to plan")
        join.Flags().StringVar(&agentName, "agent", "", "agent name; generated if empty")

        var agent string
        agentClient := func() (*client.Client, error) {
                if agent == "" {
                        return nil, errors.New("--agent is required; aiculator work join prints your name")
                }
                // The name becomes a path, so it must not be able to leave the directory.
                if filepath.Base(agent) != agent || strings.HasPrefix(agent, ".") {
                        return nil, fmt.Errorf("invalid agent name %q", agent)
                }
                tok, err := os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(dataDir, "agents", agent+".token"))
                if err != nil {
                        return nil, fmt.Errorf("agent %s is not registered; run aiculator work join: %w", agent, err)
                }
                url, err := os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(dataDir, "addr"))
                if err != nil {
                        return nil, fmt.Errorf("no running server found: %w", err)
                }
                return client.New(strings.TrimSpace(string(url)), string(tok)), nil
        }

        var hold time.Duration
        wait := &cobra.Command{
                Use:   "wait",
                Short: "Get the next task, or be told to wait or exit",
                RunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, _ []string) error {
                        c, err := agentClient()
                        if err != nil {
                                return err
                        }
                        var g swarm.Grant
                        if err := c.Post(cmd.Context(), "/v1/agent/wait", api.WaitReq{HoldMs: hold.Milliseconds()}, &g); err != nil {
                                return err
                        }
                        return printJSON(g)
                },
        }
        wait.Flags().DurationVar(&hold, "hold", api.DefaultHold, "how long to hold if no work is available")

        var taskID string
        claim := &cobra.Command{
                Use:   "claim",
                Short: "Claim one specific ready task",
                RunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, _ []string) error {
                        c, err := agentClient()
                        if err != nil {
                                return err
                        }
                        var g swarm.Grant
                        if err := c.Post(cmd.Context(), "/v1/agent/claim", api.LeaseReq{TaskID: taskID}, &g); err != nil {
                                return err
                        }
                        return printJSON(g)
                },
        }
        claim.Flags().StringVar(&taskID, "task", "", "task id")

        var lease uint64
        var note string
        var cost, tokens int64
        var pass bool
        leased := func(use, short, path string) *cobra.Command {
                sub := &cobra.Command{
                        Use: use, Short: short,
                        RunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, _ []string) error {
                                c, err := agentClient()
                                if err != nil {
                                        return err
                                }
                                var t any
                                q := api.LeaseReq{TaskID: taskID, Lease: lease, Note: note, Cost: cost, Tokens: tokens, Pass: pass}
                                if err := c.Post(cmd.Context(), path, q, &t); err != nil {
                                        return err
                                }
                                return printJSON(t)
                        },
                }
                sub.Flags().StringVar(&taskID, "task", "", "task id")
                sub.Flags().Uint64Var(&lease, "lease", 0, "lease number from wait")
                sub.Flags().StringVar(&note, "note", "", "note saved for later attempts")
                sub.Flags().Int64Var(&cost, "cost", 0, "cost since your last report, in micro-dollars")
                sub.Flags().Int64Var(&tokens, "tokens", 0, "tokens used since your last report")
                return sub
        }
        verdict := leased("verdict", "Approve (--pass) or reject another agent's work", "/v1/agent/verdict")
        verdict.Flags().BoolVar(&pass, "pass", false, "approve; leave out to reject")

        situation := &cobra.Command{
                Use:   "situation",
                Short: "Show the swarm as this agent sees it",
                RunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, _ []string) error {
                        c, err := agentClient()
                        if err != nil {
                                return err
                        }
                        var s engine.Situation
                        if err := c.Get(cmd.Context(), "/v1/situation", &s); err != nil {
                                return err
                        }
                        return printJSON(s)
                },
        }
        cmd.PersistentFlags().StringVar(&agent, "agent", "", "agent name from aiculator work join")
        cmd.AddCommand(join, wait, claim,
                leased("heartbeat", "Extend your lease; this does not count as progress", "/v1/agent/heartbeat"),
                leased("progress", "Save your work; only real file changes count", "/v1/agent/progress"),
                leased("submit", "Submit finished work for verification", "/v1/agent/submit"),
                leased("fail", "Give up; saved work and note go to the next attempt", "/v1/agent/fail"),
                leased("release", "Hand back with no penalty, when the harness cannot do it", "/v1/agent/release"),
                verdict, situation)
        return cmd
}

package main

import (
        "context"
        "log/slog"
        "os"
        "path/filepath"
        "strconv"
        "strings"
        "time"
)

// standbyPoll is how often a standby tries the lock. Takeover costs at most this much on
// top of the store's own startup.
const standbyPoll = 200 * time.Millisecond

// lead makes this process the one writer for the data directory.
//
// The leader is whoever holds the lock on the data directory, not whoever answers health
// checks. The kernel drops the lock only when the process is gone, so a leader that is
// paused, swapped out or slow still holds it and no standby can start writing beside it.
// Electing on a missed health check would let a paused leader wake up next to a new one;
// spec/tla/Election.tla shows both versions, and the health one breaking.
//
// Without standby, a held lock is an error, as before. With it, the process waits until the
// lock comes free. A flock on a network filesystem is not reliable, so this covers servers
// on one machine sharing a local directory, not servers on several machines.
func lead(ctx context.Context, standby bool, log *slog.Logger) (unlock func(), term uint64, err error) {
        unlock, err = lockDataDir(dataDir)
        if err != nil && standby {
                pidPath := filepath.Join(dataDir, "standby.pid")
                _ = atomicWrite(pidPath, []byte(strconv.Itoa(os.Getpid())), 0o600)
                log.Info("standing by", "reason", err.Error())
                t := time.NewTicker(standbyPoll)
                for err != nil {
                        select {
                        case <-ctx.Done():
                                removeIfMine(pidPath)
                                return nil, 0, ctx.Err()
                        case <-t.C:
                        }
                        unlock, err = lockDataDir(dataDir)
                }
                t.Stop()
                removeIfMine(pidPath)
        }
        if err != nil {
                return nil, 0, err
        }
        // The term only moves while the lock is held, so two leaders never share one.
        term = readTerm() + 1
        if err := atomicWrite(filepath.Join(dataDir, "term"), []byte(strconv.FormatUint(term, 10)), 0o600); err != nil {
                unlock()
                return nil, 0, err
        }
        log.Info("became leader", "term", term, "standby", standby)
        return unlock, term, nil
}

func readTerm() uint64 {
        b, err := os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(dataDir, "term"))
        if err != nil {
                return 0
        }
        n, _ := strconv.ParseUint(strings.TrimSpace(string(b)), 10, 64)
        return n
}

// removeIfMine removes a pid file only if it names this process, so a standby leaving
// does not remove the file of the one that replaced it.
func removeIfMine(path string) {
        if pidFile(path) == os.Getpid() {
                _ = os.Remove(path)
        }
}

func pidFile(path string) int {
        b, err := os.ReadFile(path)
        if err != nil {
                return 0
        }
        n, _ := strconv.Atoi(strings.TrimSpace(string(b)))
        return n
}

// Command swarm runs the agent swarm: a single static binary with the embedded
// state store, the HTTP and MCP endpoints, the ACP driver and the CLI.
package main

import (
        "context"
        "encoding/json"
        "errors"
        "fmt"
        "net"
        "net/http"
        "os"
        "os/signal"
        "path/filepath"
        "strconv"
        "strings"
        "syscall"
        "time"

        "github.com/spf13/cobra"

        "github.com/Grano22/aiculator/internal/api"
        "github.com/Grano22/aiculator/internal/auth"
        "github.com/Grano22/aiculator/internal/client"
        "github.com/Grano22/aiculator/internal/core"
        "github.com/Grano22/aiculator/internal/engine"
        "github.com/Grano22/aiculator/internal/realm"
        "github.com/Grano22/aiculator/internal/sandbox"
        "github.com/Grano22/aiculator/internal/store"
        "github.com/Grano22/aiculator/internal/swarm"
        "github.com/Grano22/aiculator/internal/vlog"
        "github.com/Grano22/aiculator/internal/work"
)

var dataDir string

// dataDirFlagSet means --data was given, so nothing should search for the state directory.
var dataDirFlagSet bool

// realmFlag names the realm to act on, instead of the one this folder belongs to.
var realmFlag string

// version is set at build time with -ldflags "-X main.version=v1.2.3".
var version = "dev"

// findDataDir walks up from the working directory, so that commands work from a subdirectory
// and from inside a task's worktree, which lives under the data directory.
func findDataDir() string {
        dir, err := os.Getwd()
        if err != nil {
                return ".swarm"
        }
        return findDataDirFrom(dir)
}

// findDataDirFrom stops at the edge of the project. Without that, a repository nested inside
// another would silently use the outer one's server, and an agent would be given work from
// the wrong project. The home directory is an edge too, so that a stray ~/.swarm cannot
// claim every folder under it.
func findDataDirFrom(dir string) string {
        sep := string(filepath.Separator)
        // A task's worktree has its own .git, and it belongs to the data directory it is inside.
        if i := strings.LastIndex(dir+sep, sep+".swarm"+sep); i >= 0 {
                return dir[:i] + sep + ".swarm"
        }
        home, _ := os.UserHomeDir()
        if real, err := filepath.EvalSymlinks(home); err == nil {
                home = real
        }
        if real, err := filepath.EvalSymlinks(dir); err == nil {
                dir = real
        }
        start := dir
        for {
                if dir == home && start != home {
                        return ".swarm" // Working in the home directory itself is the one way to use it.
                }
                candidate := filepath.Join(dir, ".swarm")
                if fi, err := os.Stat(candidate); err == nil && fi.IsDir() {
                        return candidate
                }
                if _, err := os.Stat(filepath.Join(dir, ".git")); err == nil {
                        return ".swarm"
                }
                parent := filepath.Dir(dir)
                if parent == dir {
                        return ".swarm"
                }
                dir = parent
        }
}

func main() {
        root := rootCmd()
        if handled, code := runExternal(root, os.Args[1:]); handled {
                os.Exit(code)
        }
        if err := root.Execute(); err != nil {
                os.Exit(1)
        }
}

func rootCmd() *cobra.Command {
        root := &cobra.Command{
                Use: "aiculator", Short: "Run and control an agent swarm across coding harnesses",
                Version: version, SilenceUsage: true,
                PersistentPreRunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, _ []string) error {
                        dataDirFlagSet = cmd.Flags().Changed("data")
                        if realmFlag != "" {
                                if dataDirFlagSet {
                                        return errors.New("use --realm or --data, not both")
                                }
                                r, err := realm.Get(realmFlag)
                                if err != nil {
                                        return err
                                }
                                // Everything then acts as if it had been run in that project.
                                if err := os.Chdir(r.Path); err != nil {
                                        return fmt.Errorf("realm %s: %w", r.Name, err)
                                }
                        }
                        if !dataDirFlagSet {
                                dataDir = findDataDir()
                        }
                        return setupLogging(cmd)
                },
        }
        root.PersistentFlags().StringVar(&realmFlag, "realm", "", "act on this realm, from any folder; see aiculator realm ls")
        root.PersistentFlags().StringVar(&dataDir, "data", ".swarm", "state directory; found by searching upward when not set")
        addLoggingFlags(root)
        // Declared here so that cobra does not claim -v for it, since -v is the verbosity.
        root.Flags().Bool("version", false, "print the version")
        root.AddCommand(backupCmd(), doctorCmd(), exportCmd(), parallelCmd(), realmCmd(), initCmd(), importCmd(), sourceCmd(), syncCmd(), serveCmd(), upCmd(), downCmd(), taskCmd(), tokenCmd(), situationCmd(), planCmd(),
                mcpCmd(), driveCmd(), joinCmd(), unjoinCmd(), workCmd(), harnessCmd(), skillCmd(), templateCmd(), topCmd(), eventsCmd(), pluginCmd(), debugCmd(), logsCmd(), genDocsCmd())
        addPluginCommands(root)
        return root
}

func serveCmd() *cobra.Command {
        var (
                addr, repo, branch, sb string
                syncAlways             bool
                leaseTTL, progressTTL  time.Duration
                exitGrace              time.Duration
                restartGrace           time.Duration
                agingUnit              time.Duration
                agingArgs              []string
                standby                bool
        )
        cmd := &cobra.Command{
                Use:   "serve",
                Short: "Start the swarm server",
                RunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, _ []string) error {
                        ctx, stop := signal.NotifyContext(cmd.Context(), os.Interrupt, syscall.SIGTERM)
                        defer stop()
                        aging, err := core.ParseAging(agingArgs)
                        if err != nil {
                                return err
                        }
                        return serve(ctx, serveOpts{addr, repo, branch, sb, syncAlways, leaseTTL, progressTTL, exitGrace, restartGrace, agingUnit, aging, standby})
                },
        }
        f := cmd.Flags()
        f.StringVar(&addr, "addr", "127.0.0.1:7777", "listen address; port 0 picks a free one")
        f.StringVar(&repo, "repo", "", "git repository to work on; empty disables the work layer")
        f.StringVar(&branch, "branch", work.DefaultBranch, "branch that receives merged work")
        f.StringVar(&sb, "sandbox", "auto", "sandbox: auto, seatbelt, bwrap, docker or none")
        f.BoolVar(&syncAlways, "sync-always", false, "fsync every write; survives power loss but is slower")
        f.DurationVar(&leaseTTL, "lease-ttl", 2*time.Minute, "lease length")
        f.DurationVar(&progressTTL, "progress-ttl", 10*time.Minute, "time without file changes before an agent counts as a zombie")
        f.DurationVar(&exitGrace, "exit-grace", 30*time.Second, "quiet time before agents are told to exit")
        f.DurationVar(&restartGrace, "restart-grace", 15*time.Second, "no lease expires this soon after a restart")
        f.DurationVar(&agingUnit, "aging-unit", time.Minute, "waiting this long equals one priority point")
        f.StringSliceVar(&agingArgs, "aging", nil, "raise priority after a wait, as wait=boost, such as 1h=5,4h=20")
        f.BoolVar(&standby, "standby", false, "if another server holds this data directory, wait and take over when it stops")
        return cmd
}

type serveOpts struct {
        addr, repo, branch, sb string
        syncAlways             bool
        leaseTTL, progressTTL  time.Duration
        exitGrace              time.Duration
        restartGrace           time.Duration
        agingUnit              time.Duration
        aging                  []core.AgingStep
        standby                bool
}

func serve(ctx context.Context, o serveOpts) error {
        log := vlog.Slog("server")
        if err := os.MkdirAll(dataDir, 0o700); err != nil {
                return err
        }
        // The design relies on a single writer, so a second server must not start here, unless
        // it is a standby, which waits for the first to go.
        unlock, term, err := lead(ctx, o.standby, log)
        if err != nil {
                if o.standby && ctx.Err() != nil {
                        return nil
                }
                return err
        }
        defer unlock()
        authority, err := auth.LoadOrCreate(filepath.Join(dataDir, "signing.key"))
        if err != nil {
                return err
        }
        admin, err := authority.Issue(auth.Claims{Agent: "admin", Admin: true})
        if err != nil {
                return err
        }
        if err := atomicWrite(filepath.Join(dataDir, "admin.token"), []byte(admin), 0o600); err != nil {
                return err
        }
        st, err := store.Open(ctx, store.Options{Dir: filepath.Join(dataDir, "nats"), SyncAlways: o.syncAlways})
        if err != nil {
                return err
        }
        defer st.Close()
        if err := st.StartProjector(ctx); err != nil {
                return err
        }

        var wm *work.Manager
        if o.repo != "" {
                sb, err := sandbox.Open(o.sb)
                if err != nil {
                        return err
                }
                repo, err := filepath.Abs(o.repo)
                if err != nil {
                        return err
                }
                if wm, err = work.New(ctx, work.Options{Repo: repo, Root: filepath.Join(dataDir, "worktrees"), Branch: o.branch, Sandbox: sb, Hide: secretPaths()}); err != nil {
                        return err
                }
                log.Info("work layer ready", "repo", repo, "branch", wm.Branch(), "sandbox", sb.Name())
        }

        realmID := registerRealm(log)
        cfg := engine.Config{LeaseTTL: o.leaseTTL, ProgressTTL: o.progressTTL, ExitGrace: o.exitGrace, RestartGrace: o.restartGrace, AgingUnit: o.agingUnit, Aging: o.aging}
        svc, err := swarm.New(ctx, swarm.Options{Store: st, Work: wm, Engine: cfg, Log: log, Realm: realmID.name, RealmPath: realmID.path})
        if err != nil {
                return err
        }
        defer svc.Close()

        srv := &api.Server{S: svc, Auth: authority, Version: version, Instance: realmID.instance, Term: term}
        // Connectors are a side effect, so a bad sources file costs them, not the swarm.
        if y := startSync(ctx, svc, o.repo, log); y != nil {
                srv.Sync = y
                defer y.Close()
        }
        // Backups read the store, so they stop before it closes, which is deferred earlier.
        if b := startBackups(ctx, st, o.repo, log); b != nil {
                srv.Backup = b
                defer b.Close()
        }
        mux := srv.Routes()
        mux.Handle("/mcp", srv.MCPHandler())
        stopPlugins, err := startPlugins(ctx, srv, mux, log)
        if err != nil {
                return err
        }
        defer stopPlugins()
        ln, err := net.Listen("tcp", o.addr)
        if err != nil && o.standby {
                // The old leader's port may still be taken by something else after it died. Clients
                // read the address file, so a new port only costs open sessions a reconnect.
                log.Warn("leader address taken, picking another", "addr", o.addr, "err", err)
                ln, err = net.Listen("tcp", "127.0.0.1:0")
        }
        if err != nil {
                return err
        }
        hs := &http.Server{Handler: srv.Instrument(mux), ReadHeaderTimeout: 5 * time.Second}
        errc := make(chan error, 1)
        go func() { errc <- hs.Serve(ln) }()
        url := "http://" + ln.Addr().String()
        if err := atomicWrite(filepath.Join(dataDir, "addr"), []byte(url), 0o600); err != nil {
                return err
        }
        if err := atomicWrite(filepath.Join(dataDir, "pid"), []byte(strconv.Itoa(os.Getpid())), 0o600); err != nil {
                return err
        }
        defer os.Remove(filepath.Join(dataDir, "pid"))
        log.Info("swarm listening", "url", url)

        select {
        case <-ctx.Done():
        case err := <-errc:
                return err
        }
        shut, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 5*time.Second)
        defer cancel()
        _ = hs.Shutdown(shut)
        return nil
}

// secretPaths lists what sandboxed commands may not read. With the admin token or
// signing key, an agent could mint any identity and approve its own work.
func secretPaths() []string {
        abs, err := filepath.Abs(dataDir)
        if err != nil {
                abs = dataDir
        }
        paths := sandbox.SecretHome()
        for _, name := range []string{"admin.token", "signing.key", "agents", "nats"} {
                paths = append(paths, filepath.Join(abs, name))
        }
        return paths
}

func atomicWrite(path string, b []byte, mode os.FileMode) error {
        tmp := path + ".tmp"
        if err := os.WriteFile(tmp, b, mode); err != nil {
                return err
        }
        return os.Rename(tmp, path)
}

func adminClient() (*client.Client, error) {
        url, err := os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(dataDir, "addr"))
        if err != nil {
                return nil, fmt.Errorf("no running server found in %s: %w", dataDir, err)
        }
        tok, err := os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(dataDir, "admin.token"))
        if err != nil {
                return nil, err
        }
        return client.New(string(url), string(tok)), nil
}

func printJSON(v any) error {
        enc := json.NewEncoder(os.Stdout)
        enc.SetIndent("", "  ")
        return enc.Encode(v)
}

func taskCmd() *cobra.Command {
        cmd := &cobra.Command{Use: "task", Short: "Manage tasks"}
        var s engine.TaskSpec
        var labelArgs, agingArgs []string
        add := &cobra.Command{
                Use:   "add",
                Short: "Add a task",
                RunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, _ []string) error {
                        var err error
                        if s.Labels, err = parseLabels(labelArgs); err != nil {
                                return err
                        }
                        if s.Aging, err = core.ParseAging(agingArgs); err != nil {
                                return err
                        }
                        if !cmd.Flags().Changed("aging") {
                                s.Aging = nil // No flag means the server's steps apply, not "none".
                        }
                        c, err := adminClient()
                        if err != nil {
                                return err
                        }
                        var t core.Task
                        if err := c.Post(cmd.Context(), "/v1/tasks", s, &t); err != nil {
                                return err
                        }
                        fmt.Println(t.ID)
                        return nil
                },
        }
        f := add.Flags()
        f.StringVar(&s.ID, "id", "", "task id; generated if empty")
        f.StringVar(&s.Title, "title", "", "short title")
        f.StringVar(&s.Spec, "spec", "", "full instructions")
        f.IntVar(&s.Tier, "tier", 1, "tier: 1 standard, 2 advanced, 3 ultra")
        f.StringSliceVar(&s.Tags, "tag", nil, "required capability tag")
        f.IntVar(&s.Priority, "priority", 0, "higher runs sooner")
        f.StringArrayVar(&labelArgs, "label", nil, "label as name=value")
        f.StringSliceVar(&agingArgs, "aging", nil, "raise priority after a wait, as wait=boost, such as 1h=5,4h=20")
        f.StringSliceVar(&s.Deps, "dep", nil, "task id this depends on")
        f.StringSliceVar(&s.Touches, "touches", nil, "path this task will change")
        f.StringArrayVar(&s.Checks, "check", nil, "acceptance command")
        f.BoolVar(&s.RequireReview, "review", false, "also require an independent agent review")
        f.BoolVar(&s.AllowEmpty, "allow-empty", false, "allow a submission that changes no files")
        f.Int64Var(&s.Budget, "budget", 0, "budget in micro-dollars; 0 means no limit")

        ls := &cobra.Command{
                Use:   "ls",
                Short: "List tasks",
                RunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, _ []string) error {
                        c, err := adminClient()
                        if err != nil {
                                return err
                        }
                        var ts []core.Task
                        if err := c.Get(cmd.Context(), "/v1/tasks", &ts); err != nil {
                                return err
                        }
                        fmt.Printf("%-24s %-9s %-4s %-5s %-14s %s\n", "ID", "STATE", "TIER", "TRIES", "OWNER", "TITLE")
                        for _, t := range ts {
                                fmt.Printf("%-24s %-9s %-4d %-5d %-14s %s\n", t.ID, t.State, t.Tier, t.Attempt, t.Owner, t.Title)
                        }
                        return nil
                },
        }
        show := &cobra.Command{
                Use:   "show ID",
                Short: "Show one task",
                Args:  cobra.ExactArgs(1),
                RunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) error {
                        c, err := adminClient()
                        if err != nil {
                                return err
                        }
                        var t core.Task
                        if err := c.Get(cmd.Context(), "/v1/tasks/"+args[0], &t); err != nil {
                                return err
                        }
                        return printJSON(t)
                },
        }
        var note string
        var addBudget int64
        cancelCmd := &cobra.Command{
                Use:   "cancel ID",
                Short: "Cancel a task",
                Args:  cobra.ExactArgs(1),
                RunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) error {
                        c, err := adminClient()
                        if err != nil {
                                return err
                        }
                        return c.Post(cmd.Context(), "/v1/tasks/"+args[0]+"/cancel", map[string]string{"note": note}, nil)
                },
        }
        cancelCmd.Flags().StringVar(&note, "note", "", "reason")
        unpark := &cobra.Command{
                Use:   "unpark ID",
                Short: "Return a parked task to the queue",
                Args:  cobra.ExactArgs(1),
                RunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) error {
                        c, err := adminClient()
                        if err != nil {
                                return err
                        }
                        return c.Post(cmd.Context(), "/v1/tasks/"+args[0]+"/unpark", map[string]any{"note": note, "add_budget": addBudget}, nil)
                },
        }
        unpark.Flags().StringVar(&note, "note", "", "reason")
        unpark.Flags().Int64Var(&addBudget, "add-budget", 0, "budget to add, in micro-dollars")
        cmd.AddCommand(add, ls, show, cancelCmd, unpark, amendCmd(), priorityCmd())
        cmd.AddCommand(metaCmds()...)
        return cmd
}
