        if err != nil {
                return nil, err
        }
        var out []Version
        for _, r := range rules {
                if !r.IsDir() {
                        continue
                }
                jd := journalDir(dir, r.Name(), id)
                for _, n := range files(jd, ".json") {
                        e, err := ReadEntry(filepath.Join(jd, n))
                        if err != nil {
                                continue
                        }
                        out = append(out, Version{Rule: r.Name(), Kind: "journal", At: e.At, Seq: e.Seq, State: e.Task.State, Path: filepath.Join(jd, n)})
                }
                sd := snapshotDir(dir, r.Name())
                for _, n := range files(sd, ".json.gz") {
                        s, err := ReadSnapshot(filepath.Join(sd, n))
                        if err != nil {
                                continue
                        }
                        for _, e := range s.Tasks {
                                if e.Task.ID == id {
                                        out = append(out, Version{Rule: r.Name(), Kind: "snapshot", At: s.At, State: e.Task.State, Path: filepath.Join(sd, n)})
                                }
                        }
                }
        }
        slices.SortStableFunc(out, func(a, b Version) int { return a.At.Compare(b.At) })
        return out, nil
}

// Snapshots lists a rule's snapshots, oldest first.
func Snapshots(dir, rule string) []string {
        sd := snapshotDir(dir, rule)
        var out []string
        for _, n := range files(sd, ".json.gz") {
                out = append(out, filepath.Join(sd, n))
        }
        return out
}

// Pick chooses the copy to restore: the newest at or before a time, when one is given.
func Pick(vs []Version, before time.Time) (Version, bool) {
        for i := len(vs) - 1; i >= 0; i-- {
                if before.IsZero() || !vs[i].At.After(before) {
                        return vs[i], true
                }
        }
        return Version{}, false
}

// Find a task in the file a version points to.
func (v Version) Entry(id string) (Entry, error) {
        es, err := ReadAny(v.Path)
        if err != nil {
                return Entry{}, err
        }
        for _, e := range es {
                if e.Task.ID == id {
                        return e, nil
                }
        }
        return Entry{}, fmt.Errorf("%s holds no copy of %s", v.Path, id)
}

func seqOf(name string) uint64 {
        n, _ := strconv.ParseUint(strings.TrimSuffix(name, ".json"), 10, 64)
        return n
}

// Package client is a small typed HTTP client for the swarm API.
package client

import (
        "bytes"
        "context"
        "encoding/json"
        "fmt"
        "io"
        "net/http"
        "time"

        "github.com/Grano22/aiculator/internal/vlog"
)

var vl = vlog.For("client")

// Client talks to one server with one token.
type Client struct {
        URL   string
        Token string
        HTTP  *http.Client
}

// New returns a client with no overall timeout, because wait calls hold open.
func New(url, token string) *Client {
        return &Client{URL: url, Token: token, HTTP: &http.Client{}}
}

// StatusError is a non-2xx answer.
type StatusError struct {
        Code int
        Msg  string
}

func (e *StatusError) Error() string { return fmt.Sprintf("%d: %s", e.Code, e.Msg) }

// Do sends in as JSON, when it is not nil, and decodes the answer into out.
func (c *Client) Do(ctx context.Context, method, path string, in, out any) error {
        var body io.Reader
        if in != nil {
                b, err := json.Marshal(in)
                if err != nil {
                        return err
                }
                body = bytes.NewReader(b)
        }
        req, err := http.NewRequestWithContext(ctx, method, c.URL+path, body)
        if err != nil {
                return err
        }
        if c.Token != "" {
                req.Header.Set("Authorization", "Bearer "+c.Token)
        }
        if in != nil {
                req.Header.Set("Content-Type", "application/json")
        }
        if v := vl.V(vlog.LevelHeaders); v.Enabled() {
                v.Info("request headers", "method", method, "path", path, "headers", vlog.Headers(req.Header))
        }
        if limit := vlog.HTTPLimit("client"); limit > 0 && in != nil {
                if b, err := json.Marshal(in); err == nil {
                        vl.V(vlog.LevelBodies).Info("request body", "method", method, "path", path, "body", vlog.Body(b, limit))
                }
        }
        began := time.Now()
        resp, err := c.HTTP.Do(req)
        if err != nil {
                if v := vl.V(vlog.LevelRequests); v.Enabled() {
                        v.Info("request failed", "method", method, "url", c.URL+path, "took", time.Since(began), "err", err)
                }
                return err
        }
        defer resp.Body.Close()
        data, err := io.ReadAll(resp.Body)
        if err != nil {
                return err
        }
        if v := vl.V(vlog.LevelRequests); v.Enabled() {
                v.Info("request", "method", method, "url", c.URL+path, "status", resp.StatusCode, "took", time.Since(began), "bytes", len(data))
        }
        if v := vl.V(vlog.LevelHeaders); v.Enabled() {
                v.Info("response headers", "path", path, "headers", vlog.Headers(resp.Header))
        }
        if limit := vlog.HTTPLimit("client"); limit > 0 {
                vl.V(vlog.LevelBodies).Info("response body", "path", path, "status", resp.StatusCode, "body", vlog.Body(data, limit))
        }
        if resp.StatusCode/100 != 2 {
                var e struct {
                        Error string `json:"error"`
                }
                if json.Unmarshal(data, &e) != nil || e.Error == "" {
                        e.Error = string(data)
                }
                return &StatusError{resp.StatusCode, e.Error}
        }
        if out != nil {
                return json.Unmarshal(data, out)
        }
        return nil
}

// Post sends a POST.
func (c *Client) Post(ctx context.Context, path string, in, out any) error {
        return c.Do(ctx, http.MethodPost, path, in, out)
}

// Get sends a GET.
func (c *Client) Get(ctx context.Context, path string, out any) error {
        return c.Do(ctx, http.MethodGet, path, nil, out)
}

// Upload sends raw bytes and decodes the JSON answer.
func (c *Client) Upload(ctx context.Context, path, contentType string, body io.Reader, out any) error {
        req, err := http.NewRequestWithContext(ctx, http.MethodPost, c.URL+path, body)
        if err != nil {
                return err
        }
        if c.Token != "" {
                req.Header.Set("Authorization", "Bearer "+c.Token)
        }
        req.Header.Set("Content-Type", contentType)
        resp, err := c.HTTP.Do(req)
        if err != nil {
                return err
        }
        defer resp.Body.Close()
        data, err := io.ReadAll(resp.Body)
        if err != nil {
                return err
        }
        if resp.StatusCode/100 != 2 {
                return &StatusError{resp.StatusCode, string(data)}
        }
        return json.Unmarshal(data, out)
}

// Download streams a raw answer. The caller closes it.
func (c *Client) Download(ctx context.Context, path string) (io.ReadCloser, error) {
        req, err := http.NewRequestWithContext(ctx, http.MethodGet, c.URL+path, nil)
        if err != nil {
                return nil, err
        }
        if c.Token != "" {
                req.Header.Set("Authorization", "Bearer "+c.Token)
        }
        resp, err := c.HTTP.Do(req)
        if err != nil {
                return nil, err
        }
        if resp.StatusCode/100 != 2 {
                defer resp.Body.Close()
                data, _ := io.ReadAll(resp.Body)
                return nil, &StatusError{resp.StatusCode, string(data)}
        }
        return resp.Body, nil
}

// Package connect brings work in from other platforms and keeps it in step with them. It
// sits entirely beside the core: importing goes through the same API as any other client,
// and syncing reads the commit stream after the fact, so neither can slow a claim.
package connect

import (
        "bytes"
        "errors"
        "fmt"
        "os"
        "path/filepath"
        "regexp"
        "slices"
        "strings"
        "time"

        "go.yaml.in/yaml/v3"

        "github.com/Grano22/aiculator/internal/core"
)

// ConfigFiles are where the sources file is looked for, relative to the project root.
var ConfigFiles = []string{".agents/sources.yaml", ".agent/sources.yaml"}

// Config is the sources file.
type Config struct {
        Sources []*Source `yaml:"sources"`
        // Base is the directory that relative file paths start from.
        Base string `yaml:"-"`
}

// Source describes one external system and how its items become tasks. It has no field for
// a secret: credentials are named by environment variable, so this file can be committed.
type Source struct {
        Name string `yaml:"name"`
        Kind string `yaml:"kind"` // jira, notion, xlsx or csv.

        URL          string `yaml:"url,omitempty"`
        Auth         Auth   `yaml:"auth,omitempty"`
        AllowPrivate bool   `yaml:"allow_private,omitempty"` // For an on-premises service.

        Query      string `yaml:"query,omitempty"`       // JQL.
        DataSource string `yaml:"data_source,omitempty"` // Notion data source ID.
        Filter     any    `yaml:"filter,omitempty"`      // Notion filter object.
        APIVersion string `yaml:"api_version,omitempty"` // Notion-Version header.
        FetchBody  bool   `yaml:"fetch_body,omitempty"`  // Read each Notion page's text too.

        Path      string   `yaml:"path,omitempty"`       // xlsx or csv file.
        Sheet     string   `yaml:"sheet,omitempty"`      // xlsx sheet; the first if empty.
        HeaderRow int      `yaml:"header_row,omitempty"` // 1-based; 1 if empty.
        Regions   []Region `yaml:"regions,omitempty"`    // Treat cell ranges as lists.

        Fields   Fields      `yaml:"fields"`
        SkipWhen []When      `yaml:"skip_when,omitempty"`
        Defaults Defaults    `yaml:"defaults,omitempty"`
        Sync     *SyncConfig `yaml:"sync,omitempty"`
}

// Auth names the environment variables that hold credentials.
type Auth struct {
        EmailEnv string `yaml:"email_env,omitempty"` // With a token, means HTTP Basic, as Jira Cloud uses.
        TokenEnv string `yaml:"token_env,omitempty"`
}

// Region treats a range of cells as a list of items, for a sheet laid out as a grid, such
// as an Eisenhower matrix with one column per quadrant.
type Region struct {
        Name  string `yaml:"name"`
        Range string `yaml:"range"` // Such as A3:A40.
}

// When matches an item when every named field has the given value, ignoring case.
type When map[string]string

// Rule gives a value when its condition holds.
type Rule struct {
        When  When `yaml:"when"`
        Value any  `yaml:"value"`
}

// FieldSpec says where one attribute comes from: a field name, optionally translated by
// map, or a list of rules that can look at several fields at once.
type FieldSpec struct {
        From    string         `yaml:"from,omitempty"`
        Map     map[string]any `yaml:"map,omitempty"`
        Rules   []Rule         `yaml:"rules,omitempty"`
        Default any            `yaml:"default,omitempty"`
}

// UnmarshalYAML lets a plain string stand for just a field name.
func (f *FieldSpec) UnmarshalYAML(n *yaml.Node) error {
        if n.Kind == yaml.ScalarNode {
                return n.Decode(&f.From)
        }
        type plain FieldSpec
        dec := plain{}
        if err := n.Decode(&dec); err != nil {
                return err
        }
        *f = FieldSpec(dec)
        return nil
}

// Fields maps an item onto a task. There is deliberately no entry for checks, touches,
// budget or review: checks are commands the swarm runs, so whoever can edit a ticket must
// not be able to choose them. Those come only from Defaults, in this reviewed file.
type Fields struct {
        Key      *FieldSpec           `yaml:"key,omitempty"`
        Title    *FieldSpec           `yaml:"title,omitempty"`
        Spec     *FieldSpec           `yaml:"spec,omitempty"`
        Priority *FieldSpec           `yaml:"priority,omitempty"`
        Tier     *FieldSpec           `yaml:"tier,omitempty"`
        Tags     *FieldSpec           `yaml:"tags,omitempty"`
        Status   *FieldSpec           `yaml:"status,omitempty"`
        Labels   map[string]FieldSpec `yaml:"labels,omitempty"`
        Props    map[string]FieldSpec `yaml:"props,omitempty"`
}

// Defaults apply to every task from this source.
type Defaults struct {
        Spec          string            `yaml:"spec,omitempty"`
        Tier          int               `yaml:"tier,omitempty"`
        Priority      int               `yaml:"priority,omitempty"`
        Tags          []string          `yaml:"tags,omitempty"`
        Labels        map[string]string `yaml:"labels,omitempty"`
        Checks        []string          `yaml:"checks,omitempty"`
        Touches       []string          `yaml:"touches,omitempty"`
        RequireReview bool              `yaml:"require_review,omitempty"`
        AllowEmpty    bool              `yaml:"allow_empty,omitempty"`
        Budget        int64             `yaml:"budget,omitempty"`
        Aging         []string          `yaml:"aging,omitempty"` // Such as 1h=5.
}

// SyncConfig turns on keeping a source in step after the import. See sync.go.
type SyncConfig struct {
        Direction string     `yaml:"direction,omitempty"` // both, push or pull. both if empty.
        Create    bool       `yaml:"create,omitempty"`    // Pull in new items too.
        Push      PushConfig `yaml:"push,omitempty"`
        Pull      PullConfig `yaml:"pull,omitempty"`
        // Status says which remote status each task state becomes. A state left out is not sent.
        Status map[string]string `yaml:"status,omitempty"`
        // OnRemote says what a remote status does here. The only action is cancel.
        OnRemote map[string]string `yaml:"on_remote,omitempty"`
        // HookSecretEnv names the variable that holds the webhook signing secret.
        HookSecretEnv string `yaml:"hook_secret_env,omitempty"`
}

// PushConfig says how changes reach the other system.
type PushConfig struct {
        Mode    string        `yaml:"mode,omitempty"`    // realtime or interval. realtime if empty.
        Every   time.Duration `yaml:"every,omitempty"`   // For interval.
        Updates string        `yaml:"updates,omitempty"` // partial sends each change; last sends only the end.
}

// PullConfig says how changes come back.
type PullConfig struct {
        Mode  string        `yaml:"mode,omitempty"` // once, interval or webhook. interval if empty.
        Every time.Duration `yaml:"every,omitempty"`
}

var (
        sourceNameRE = regexp.MustCompile(`^[a-z0-9]+(-[a-z0-9]+)*$`)
        envNameRE    = regexp.MustCompile(`^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*$`)
)

// ErrNoConfig means no sources file exists.
var ErrNoConfig = errors.New("no sources file: create .agents/sources.yaml")

// Find loads the sources file under root. A missing file is ErrNoConfig.
func Find(root string) (*Config, error) {
        for _, name := range ConfigFiles {
                p := filepath.Join(root, name)
                if _, err := os.Stat(p); err == nil {
                        return Load(p, root)
                }
        }
        return nil, ErrNoConfig
}

// Load reads and checks one sources file. Unknown fields are errors, so a misspelling, or
// an attempt to map checks from outside, fails loudly rather than being ignored.
func Load(path, base string) (*Config, error) {
        b, err := os.ReadFile(path)
        if err != nil {
                return nil, err
        }
        dec := yaml.NewDecoder(bytes.NewReader(b))
        dec.KnownFields(true)
        var c Config
        if err := dec.Decode(&c); err != nil {
                return nil, fmt.Errorf("%s: %w", path, err)
        }
        c.Base = base
        seen := map[string]bool{}
        for _, s := range c.Sources {
                if err := s.check(); err != nil {
                        return nil, fmt.Errorf("%s: source %q: %w", path, s.Name, err)
                }
                if seen[s.Name] {
                        return nil, fmt.Errorf("%s: source %q is listed twice", path, s.Name)
                }
                seen[s.Name] = true
        }
        return &c, nil
}

// Get finds a source by name.
func (c *Config) Get(name string) (*Source, error) {
        for _, s := range c.Sources {
                if s.Name == name {
                        return s, nil
                }
        }
        names := make([]string, 0, len(c.Sources))
        for _, s := range c.Sources {
                names = append(names, s.Name)
        }
        return nil, fmt.Errorf("no source named %q; these exist: %s", name, strings.Join(names, ", "))
}

func (s *Source) check() error {
        if !sourceNameRE.MatchString(s.Name) {
                return errors.New("name: use lowercase letters, digits and hyphens")
        }
        switch s.Kind {
        case "jira":
                if s.URL == "" {
                        return errors.New("jira needs url")
                }
                if s.Query == "" {
                        return errors.New("jira needs query, in JQL; a search with no limit could import a whole site")
                }
        case "notion":
                if s.DataSource == "" {
                        return errors.New("notion needs data_source")
                }
        case "xlsx", "csv":
                if s.Path == "" {
                        return fmt.Errorf("%s needs path", s.Kind)
                }
        default:
                return fmt.Errorf("unknown kind %q: use jira, notion, xlsx or csv", s.Kind)
        }
        for _, e := range []string{s.Auth.EmailEnv, s.Auth.TokenEnv} {
                if e != "" && !envNameRE.MatchString(e) {
                        return fmt.Errorf("auth must name an environment variable, not hold a value: %q", redactEnv(e))
                }
        }
        if s.Fields.Title == nil && len(s.Regions) == 0 {
                return errors.New("fields.title is required")
        }
        if _, err := core.ParseAging(s.Defaults.Aging); err != nil {
                return fmt.Errorf("defaults.aging: %w", err)
        }
        if s.Sync != nil {
                return s.Sync.check(s.Kind)
        }
        return nil
}

func redactEnv(string) string { return "[hidden]" }

func (c *SyncConfig) check(kind string) error {
        if !slices.Contains([]string{"", "both", "push", "pull"}, c.Direction) {
                return fmt.Errorf("sync.direction %q", c.Direction)
        }
        if !slices.Contains([]string{"", "realtime", "interval"}, c.Push.Mode) {
                return fmt.Errorf("sync.push.mode %q", c.Push.Mode)
        }
        if c.Push.Mode == "interval" && c.Push.Every <= 0 {
                return errors.New("sync.push.every is required for interval")
        }
        if !slices.Contains([]string{"", "partial", "last"}, c.Push.Updates) {
                return fmt.Errorf("sync.push.updates %q: use partial or last", c.Push.Updates)
        }
        if !slices.Contains([]string{"", "once", "interval", "webhook"}, c.Pull.Mode) {
                return fmt.Errorf("sync.pull.mode %q", c.Pull.Mode)
        }
        if c.Pull.Mode == "webhook" && c.HookSecretEnv == "" {
                return errors.New("sync.hook_secret_env is required for webhook: an unsigned hook could cancel tasks")
        }
        if (kind == "xlsx" || kind == "csv") && c.Direction != "pull" {
                return fmt.Errorf("%s files can only be read: set sync.direction to pull", kind)
        }
        for state := range c.Status {
                if !slices.Contains(core.AllStates, core.State(state)) {
                        return fmt.Errorf("sync.status: unknown state %q", state)
                }
        }
        for remote, action := range c.OnRemote {
                if action != "cancel" {
                        return fmt.Errorf("sync.on_remote[%s]: the only action is cancel", remote)
                }
        }
        return nil
}

// AbsPath resolves a file source's path against the project root.
func (c *Config) AbsPath(s *Source) string {
        if filepath.IsAbs(s.Path) {
                return s.Path
        }
        return filepath.Join(c.Base, s.Path)
}

// SyncSummary says in a few words how a source is kept in step.
func (s *Source) SyncSummary() string {
        if s.Sync == nil {
                return "import only"
        }
        dir := s.Sync.Direction
        if dir == "" {
                dir = "both"
        }
        return dir
}

package connect

import (
        "bytes"
        "context"
        "crypto/hmac"
        "crypto/sha256"
        "encoding/hex"
        "encoding/json"
        "errors"
        "fmt"
        "io"
        "net/http"
        "net/url"
        "os"
        "strconv"
        "strings"
        "time"

        "github.com/Grano22/aiculator/internal/meta"
        "github.com/Grano22/aiculator/internal/vlog"
)

var log = vlog.For("connect")

// PullOptions narrows a pull.
type PullOptions struct {
        Query string    // Replaces the configured query, for this pull only.
        Since time.Time // Only items changed since then. Zero means everything.
}

// Connector reads items from another system. It is all an import needs.
type Connector interface {
        Pull(ctx context.Context, opts PullOptions, yield func(Item) error) error
}

// Getter reads one item. A webhook names what changed, and this fetches it once.
type Getter interface {
        Get(ctx context.Context, key string) (Item, error)
}

// Pusher writes a status back to the other system.
type Pusher interface {
        SetStatus(ctx context.Context, key, status string) error
}

// HookReader understands a system's webhooks.
type HookReader interface {
        // VerifyHook checks the signature, over the exact bytes received.
        VerifyHook(secret string, h http.Header, body []byte) error
        // HookKeys says which items a verified delivery is about.
        HookKeys(body []byte) ([]string, error)
}

// ErrPermanent marks a failure that trying again cannot fix, such as a status the other
// system's workflow does not allow right now.
var ErrPermanent = errors.New("permanent failure")

// Open returns the connector for a source.
func (c *Config) Open(s *Source) (Connector, error) {
        switch s.Kind {
        case "xlsx", "csv":
                return &fileSource{src: s, file: c.AbsPath(s)}, nil
        case "jira":
                return newJira(s)
        case "notion":
                return newNotion(s)
        }
        return nil, fmt.Errorf("unknown kind %q", s.Kind)
}

// webClient is the HTTP side of a remote connector. Credentials are read from the
// environment here, and go only to the configured host.
type webClient struct {
        base      string
        host      string
        source    string
        authorize func(*http.Request)
        client    *http.Client
        fetcher   *meta.Fetcher
}

func envValue(name, what string) (string, error) {
        if name == "" {
                return "", nil
        }
        v := os.Getenv(name)
        if v == "" {
                return "", fmt.Errorf("%s: environment variable %s is not set", what, name)
        }
        return v, nil
}

func newWebClient(s *Source, base string, authorize func(*http.Request)) (*webClient, error) {
        u, err := url.Parse(base)
        if err != nil || u.Host == "" {
                return nil, fmt.Errorf("bad url %q", base)
        }
        if u.Scheme != "https" && !s.AllowPrivate {
                return nil, fmt.Errorf("%s: credentials would be sent unencrypted: use https", base)
        }
        return &webClient{
                base: strings.TrimRight(base, "/"), host: u.Host, source: s.Name, authorize: authorize,
                client:  &http.Client{Timeout: time.Minute},
                fetcher: meta.NewFetcher(s.AllowPrivate),
        }, nil
}

const maxResponse = 64 << 20

// do sends one JSON request. It retries what the other side says is temporary and honours
// its Retry-After, because a sync that ignores a rate limit gets locked out.
func (w *webClient) do(ctx context.Context, method, path string, in, out any) error {
        var body []byte
        if in != nil {
                var err error
                if body, err = json.Marshal(in); err != nil {
                        return err
                }
        }
        delay := 500 * time.Millisecond
        var last error
        for attempt := range 6 {
                if attempt > 0 {
                        select {
                        case <-time.After(delay):
                        case <-ctx.Done():
                                return ctx.Err()
                        }
                        delay = min(delay*2, 30*time.Second)
                }
                req, err := http.NewRequestWithContext(ctx, method, w.base+path, bytes.NewReader(body))
                if err != nil {
                        return err
                }
                req.Header.Set("Accept", "application/json")
                if in != nil {
                        req.Header.Set("Content-Type", "application/json")
                }
                w.authorize(req)
                resp, err := w.client.Do(req)
                if err != nil {
                        last = err
                        continue
                }
                data, rerr := io.ReadAll(io.LimitReader(resp.Body, maxResponse))
                resp.Body.Close()
                if v := log.V(vlog.LevelRequests); v.Enabled() {
                        v.Info("connector request", "source", w.source, "method", method, "path", path, "status", resp.StatusCode)
                }
                switch {
                case resp.StatusCode == http.StatusTooManyRequests || resp.StatusCode >= 500:
                        last = fmt.Errorf("%s %s: status %d", method, path, resp.StatusCode)
                        if s, err := strconv.Atoi(resp.Header.Get("Retry-After")); err == nil && s > 0 {
                                delay = min(time.Duration(s)*time.Second, 2*time.Minute)
                        }
                        continue
                case resp.StatusCode/100 != 2:
                        return fmt.Errorf("%w: %s %s: status %d: %s", ErrPermanent, method, path, resp.StatusCode, snippet(data))
                }
                if rerr != nil {
                        last = rerr
                        continue
                }
                if out != nil && len(data) > 0 {
                        if err := json.Unmarshal(data, out); err != nil {
                                return fmt.Errorf("%s %s: %w", method, path, err)
                        }
                }
                return nil
        }
        return last
}

// snippet keeps an error useful without pulling a whole response into the log.
func snippet(b []byte) string {
        if len(b) > 300 {
                b = b[:300]
        }
        return string(bytes.ToValidUTF8(b, []byte("?")))
}

// Download implements meta.Downloader. The token goes only to the configured host, so a
// link edited to point elsewhere gets nothing. Go also drops it on a redirect to another
// domain, which is what a Jira attachment does on its way to its file store.
func (w *webClient) Download(ctx context.Context, r meta.Resource) (io.ReadCloser, string, error) {
        u, err := url.Parse(r.URL)
        if err != nil || u.Host != w.host {
                // Unauthenticated, through the guarded fetcher.
                return w.fetcher.Download(ctx, r)
        }
        req, err := http.NewRequestWithContext(ctx, http.MethodGet, r.URL, nil)
        if err != nil {
                return nil, "", err
        }
        w.authorize(req)
        client := &http.Client{Timeout: 10 * time.Minute}
        resp, err := client.Do(req)
        if err != nil {
                return nil, "", err
        }
        if resp.StatusCode/100 != 2 {
                resp.Body.Close()
                return nil, "", fmt.Errorf("downloading %s: status %d", r.Name, resp.StatusCode)
        }
        return resp.Body, resp.Header.Get("Content-Type"), nil
}

// verifySHA256 checks a signature of the form sha256=HEX, in constant time.
func verifySHA256(secret, header string, body []byte) error {
        sig, ok := strings.CutPrefix(header, "sha256=")
        if !ok {
                return errors.New("missing or unsupported signature")
        }
        got, err := hex.DecodeString(sig)
        if err != nil {
                return errors.New("malformed signature")
        }
        mac := hmac.New(sha256.New, []byte(secret))
        mac.Write(body)
        if !hmac.Equal(got, mac.Sum(nil)) {
                return errors.New("wrong signature")
        }
        return nil
}

package connect

import (
        "archive/zip"
        "context"
        "crypto/sha256"
        "encoding/csv"
        "encoding/hex"
        "encoding/xml"
        "errors"
        "fmt"
        "io"
        "os"
        "path"
        "regexp"
        "strconv"
        "strings"
        "time"
)

// Limits for reading spreadsheets. A file is a few kilobytes of zip that can claim to hold
// gigabytes, so every part is read through a limit.
const (
        maxSheetFile = 64 << 20
        maxSheetPart = 256 << 20
        maxRows      = 1 << 20
)

// sheet is a grid of text, addressed from zero.
type sheet [][]string

func (s sheet) cell(row, col int) string {
        if row < len(s) && col < len(s[row]) {
                return strings.TrimSpace(s[row][col])
        }
        return ""
}

// readXLSX reads one sheet using only the standard library, so that a format this simple
// adds no dependency and nothing to the binary's size. It reads values, not formulas:
// a file saved by Excel stores each formula's last result, and that is what comes back.
func readXLSX(file, sheetName string) (sheet, error) {
        if fi, err := os.Stat(file); err != nil {
                return nil, err
        } else if fi.Size() > maxSheetFile {
                return nil, fmt.Errorf("%s is larger than %d bytes", file, maxSheetFile)
        }
        z, err := zip.OpenReader(file)
        if err != nil {
                return nil, fmt.Errorf("%s: not an .xlsx file: %w", file, err)
        }
        defer z.Close()
        parts := make(map[string]*zip.File, len(z.File))
        for _, f := range z.File {
                parts[f.Name] = f
        }
        target, err := sheetPath(parts, sheetName)
        if err != nil {
                return nil, fmt.Errorf("%s: %w", file, err)
        }
        shared, err := sharedStrings(parts)
        if err != nil {
                return nil, fmt.Errorf("%s: %w", file, err)
        }
        dates, err := dateStyles(parts)
        if err != nil {
                return nil, fmt.Errorf("%s: %w", file, err)
        }
        f := parts[target]
        if f == nil {
                return nil, fmt.Errorf("%s: missing %s", file, target)
        }
        return parseSheet(f, shared, dates)
}

func openPart(f *zip.File) (io.ReadCloser, *xml.Decoder, error) {
        rc, err := f.Open()
        if err != nil {
                return nil, nil, err
        }
        return rc, xml.NewDecoder(io.LimitReader(rc, maxSheetPart)), nil
}

func decodePart(f *zip.File, v any) error {
        rc, dec, err := openPart(f)
        if err != nil {
                return err
        }
        defer rc.Close()
        return dec.Decode(v)
}

func sheetPath(parts map[string]*zip.File, want string) (string, error) {
        wb := parts["xl/workbook.xml"]
        rels := parts["xl/_rels/workbook.xml.rels"]
        if wb == nil || rels == nil {
                return "", errors.New("not an .xlsx workbook")
        }
        var book struct {
                Sheets []struct {
                        Name string `xml:"name,attr"`
                        RID  string `xml:"http://schemas.openxmlformats.org/officeDocument/2006/relationships id,attr"`
                } `xml:"sheets>sheet"`
        }
        if err := decodePart(wb, &book); err != nil {
                return "", err
        }
        var rel struct {
                Items []struct {
                        ID     string `xml:"Id,attr"`
                        Target string `xml:"Target,attr"`
                } `xml:"Relationship"`
        }
        if err := decodePart(rels, &rel); err != nil {
                return "", err
        }
        if len(book.Sheets) == 0 {
                return "", errors.New("the workbook has no sheets")
        }
        var names []string
        for _, sh := range book.Sheets {
                names = append(names, sh.Name)
                if want != "" && !strings.EqualFold(sh.Name, want) {
                        continue
                }
                for _, r := range rel.Items {
                        if r.ID == sh.RID {
                                if strings.HasPrefix(r.Target, "/") {
                                        return strings.TrimPrefix(r.Target, "/"), nil
                                }
                                return path.Join("xl", r.Target), nil
                        }
                }
        }
        return "", fmt.Errorf("no sheet named %q; these exist: %s", want, strings.Join(names, ", "))
}

// richText is a run of text, possibly split into styled pieces. Phonetic hints are left out.
type richText struct {
        T string `xml:"t"`
        R []struct {
                T string `xml:"t"`
        } `xml:"r"`
}

func (t richText) text() string {
        if len(t.R) == 0 {
                return t.T
        }
        var b strings.Builder
        for _, r := range t.R {
                b.WriteString(r.T)
        }
        return b.String()
}

func sharedStrings(parts map[string]*zip.File) ([]string, error) {
        f := parts["xl/sharedStrings.xml"]
        if f == nil {
                return nil, nil // A sheet of only numbers or inline text has none.
        }
        rc, dec, err := openPart(f)
        if err != nil {
                return nil, err
        }
        defer rc.Close()
        var out []string
        for {
                tok, err := dec.Token()
                if errors.Is(err, io.EOF) {
                        return out, nil
                }
                if err != nil {
                        return nil, err
                }
                if se, ok := tok.(xml.StartElement); ok && se.Name.Local == "si" {
                        var t richText
                        if err := dec.DecodeElement(&t, &se); err != nil {
                                return nil, err
                        }
                        out = append(out, t.text())
                }
        }
}

var dateFormat = regexp.MustCompile(`(?i)[ymdh]`)

// dateStyles finds which cell styles show a date. A date is stored as a plain number, and
// only its style says otherwise.
func dateStyles(parts map[string]*zip.File) (map[int]bool, error) {
        f := parts["xl/styles.xml"]
        if f == nil {
                return nil, nil
        }
        var st struct {
                NumFmts []struct {
                        ID   int    `xml:"numFmtId,attr"`
                        Code string `xml:"formatCode,attr"`
                } `xml:"numFmts>numFmt"`
                Xfs []struct {
                        NumFmt int `xml:"numFmtId,attr"`
                } `xml:"cellXfs>xf"`
        }
        if err := decodePart(f, &st); err != nil {
                return nil, err
        }
        custom := map[int]bool{}
        for _, n := range st.NumFmts {
                clean := regexp.MustCompile(`"[^"]*"|\[[^\]]*\]|\\.`).ReplaceAllString(n.Code, "")
                custom[n.ID] = dateFormat.MatchString(clean)
        }
        out := map[int]bool{}
        for i, x := range st.Xfs {
                if (x.NumFmt >= 14 && x.NumFmt <= 22) || (x.NumFmt >= 45 && x.NumFmt <= 47) || custom[x.NumFmt] {
                        out[i] = true
                }
        }
        return out, nil
}

// serialDate converts Excel's day count. Its epoch is 1899-12-30, which absorbs the 1900
// leap year bug for every date after February of that year.
func serialDate(v string) (string, bool) {
        f, err := strconv.ParseFloat(v, 64)
        if err != nil || f < 1 || f > 2958465 {
                return "", false
        }
        days := int(f)
        t := time.Date(1899, 12, 30, 0, 0, 0, 0, time.UTC).AddDate(0, 0, days)
        frac := f - float64(days)
        if frac < 1e-9 {
                return t.Format("2006-01-02"), true
        }
        return t.Add(time.Duration(frac * float64(24*time.Hour)).Round(time.Second)).Format("2006-01-02 15:04:05"), true
}

// parseRef reads a reference such as BC12 into zero-based column and row.
func parseRef(ref string) (col, row int, ok bool) {
        i := 0
        for i < len(ref) && ref[i] >= 'A' && ref[i] <= 'Z' {
                col = col*26 + int(ref[i]-'A') + 1
                i++
        }
        if i == 0 || i == len(ref) || col > 1<<14 {
                return 0, 0, false
        }
        n, err := strconv.Atoi(ref[i:])
        if err != nil || n < 1 || n > maxRows {
                return 0, 0, false
        }
        return col - 1, n - 1, true
}

func parseSheet(f *zip.File, shared []string, dates map[int]bool) (sheet, error) {
        rc, dec, err := openPart(f)
        if err != nil {
                return nil, err
        }
        defer rc.Close()
        var grid sheet
        nextRow := 0
        for {
                tok, err := dec.Token()
                if errors.Is(err, io.EOF) {
                        return grid, nil
                }
                if err != nil {
                        return nil, err
                }
                se, ok := tok.(xml.StartElement)
                if !ok || se.Name.Local != "c" {
                        continue
                }
                var c struct {
                        Ref   string   `xml:"r,attr"`
                        Type  string   `xml:"t,attr"`
                        Style int      `xml:"s,attr"`
                        V     string   `xml:"v"`
                        Is    richText `xml:"is"`
                }
                if err := dec.DecodeElement(&c, &se); err != nil {
                        return nil, err
                }
                col, row, ok := parseRef(c.Ref)
                if !ok {
                        col, row = 0, nextRow
                }
                nextRow = row
                var text string
                switch c.Type {
                case "s":
                        if i, err := strconv.Atoi(c.V); err == nil && i >= 0 && i < len(shared) {
                                text = shared[i]
                        }
                case "inlineStr":
                        text = c.Is.text()
                case "b":
                        text = strconv.FormatBool(c.V == "1")
                case "e":
                        continue // An error value such as #REF! is not data.
                case "str":
                        text = c.V
                default:
                        text = c.V
                        if dates[c.Style] {
                                if d, ok := serialDate(c.V); ok {
                                        text = d
                                }
                        }
                }
                for len(grid) <= row {
                        grid = append(grid, nil)
                }
                for len(grid[row]) <= col {
                        grid[row] = append(grid[row], "")
                }
                grid[row][col] = text
        }
}

func readCSV(file string) (sheet, error) {
        if fi, err := os.Stat(file); err != nil {
                return nil, err
        } else if fi.Size() > maxSheetFile {
                return nil, fmt.Errorf("%s is larger than %d bytes", file, maxSheetFile)
        }
        f, err := os.Open(file)
        if err != nil {
                return nil, err
        }
        defer f.Close()
        r := csv.NewReader(f)
        r.FieldsPerRecord = -1
        r.LazyQuotes = true
        rows, err := r.ReadAll()
        if err != nil {
                return nil, fmt.Errorf("%s: %w", file, err)
        }
        if len(rows) > 0 && len(rows[0]) > 0 {
                rows[0][0] = strings.TrimPrefix(rows[0][0], "\xef\xbb\xbf") // Excel writes a byte order mark.
        }
        return sheet(rows), nil
}

// fileSource reads a spreadsheet, either as a table with a header row or as regions.
type fileSource struct {
        src  *Source
        file string
}

func hashText(parts ...string) string {
        h := sha256.New()
        for _, p := range parts {
                _, _ = io.WriteString(h, p)
                _, _ = h.Write([]byte{0})
        }
        return hex.EncodeToString(h.Sum(nil))[:16]
}

// Pull implements Connector.
func (f *fileSource) Pull(ctx context.Context, opts PullOptions, yield func(Item) error) error {
        var (
                grid sheet
                err  error
        )
        if f.src.Kind == "xlsx" {
                grid, err = readXLSX(f.file, f.src.Sheet)
        } else {
                grid, err = readCSV(f.file)
        }
        if err != nil {
                return err
        }
        if len(f.src.Regions) > 0 {
                return f.pullRegions(ctx, grid, yield)
        }
        return f.pullTable(ctx, grid, yield)
}

func (f *fileSource) pullTable(ctx context.Context, grid sheet, yield func(Item) error) error {
        header := max(f.src.HeaderRow, 1) - 1
        if header >= len(grid) {
                return fmt.Errorf("%s: no row %d to use as the header", f.file, header+1)
        }
        names := make([]string, len(grid[header]))
        for i := range names {
                names[i] = grid.cell(header, i)
        }
        for row := header + 1; row < len(grid); row++ {
                if err := ctx.Err(); err != nil {
                        return err
                }
                fields := make(map[string]any, len(names))
                var all []string
                for col, name := range names {
                        v := grid.cell(row, col)
                        all = append(all, v)
                        if name != "" && v != "" {
                                fields[name] = v
                        }
                }
                if len(fields) == 0 {
                        continue // Blank rows are common at the end of a sheet.
                }
                it := Item{Fields: fields, Version: hashText(all...)}
                it.Key = resolveText(f.src.Fields.Key, it)
                if it.Key == "" {
                        // With no key column the title identifies a row, so that adding rows above it,
                        // or sorting the sheet, cannot turn it into a different task.
                        it.Key = hashText(resolveText(f.src.Fields.Title, it))
                }
                if err := yield(it); err != nil {
                        return err
                }
        }
        return nil
}

func (f *fileSource) pullRegions(ctx context.Context, grid sheet, yield func(Item) error) error {
        for _, r := range f.src.Regions {
                left, right, ok := strings.Cut(r.Range, ":")
                if !ok {
                        right = left
                }
                c1, r1, ok1 := parseRef(left)
                c2, r2, ok2 := parseRef(right)
                if !ok1 || !ok2 || c2 < c1 || r2 < r1 {
                        return fmt.Errorf("region %s: bad range %q", r.Name, r.Range)
                }
                for row := r1; row <= min(r2, len(grid)-1); row++ {
                        if err := ctx.Err(); err != nil {
                                return err
                        }
                        for col := c1; col <= c2; col++ {
                                v := grid.cell(row, col)
                                if v == "" {
                                        continue
                                }
                                it := Item{
                                        Key: hashText(v), Version: hashText(v, r.Name),
                                        Fields: map[string]any{"value": v, "region": r.Name},
                                }
                                if err := yield(it); err != nil {
                                        return err
                                }
                        }
                }
        }
        return nil
}

package connect

import (
        "context"
        "errors"
        "fmt"
)

// ImportOptions shapes one import.
type ImportOptions struct {
        Query string
        Limit int
}

// Report says what an import did, or would do.
type Report struct {
        Mapped  []Mapped `json:"-"`
        Read    int      `json:"read"`
        Skipped int      `json:"skipped"`
        Failed  []string `json:"failed,omitempty"`
        Cyclic  []string `json:"cyclic,omitempty"`
}

var errLimit = errors.New("limit reached")

// Read pulls and maps once, without touching the swarm. An item that cannot be mapped is
// reported rather than stopping the rest: one bad row should not lose a thousand good ones.
// A failure to reach the system still stops it, since then the list would be incomplete.
func Read(ctx context.Context, c Connector, s *Source, o ImportOptions) (Report, error) {
        var r Report
        var items []Mapped
        err := c.Pull(ctx, PullOptions{Query: o.Query}, func(it Item) error {
                r.Read++
                if s.Skip(it) {
                        r.Skipped++
                        return nil
                }
                m, err := s.Map(it)
                if err != nil {
                        r.Failed = append(r.Failed, err.Error())
                        return nil
                }
                items = append(items, m)
                if o.Limit > 0 && len(items) >= o.Limit {
                        return errLimit
                }
                return nil
        })
        if err != nil && !errors.Is(err, errLimit) {
                return r, fmt.Errorf("reading %s: %w", s.Name, err)
        }
        // Two rows with one key would race for one task, so the later one is refused.
        seen := make(map[string]bool, len(items))
        unique := items[:0]
        for _, m := range items {
                if seen[m.Spec.ID] {
                        r.Failed = append(r.Failed, fmt.Sprintf("%s: the key %q appears twice", s.Name, m.Link.Key))
                        continue
                }
                seen[m.Spec.ID] = true
                unique = append(unique, m)
        }
        r.Mapped, r.Cyclic = Order(unique)
        return r, nil
}

package connect

import (
        "context"
        "encoding/json"
        "fmt"
        "maps"
        "net/http"
        "net/url"
        "regexp"
        "slices"
        "strings"
        "time"

        "github.com/Grano22/aiculator/internal/meta"
)

// jira reads and updates Jira Cloud through its REST API v3.
type jira struct {
        *webClient
        src    *Source
        fields []string
}

func newJira(s *Source) (*jira, error) {
        token, err := envValue(s.Auth.TokenEnv, s.Name)
        if err != nil {
                return nil, err
        }
        email, err := envValue(s.Auth.EmailEnv, s.Name)
        if err != nil {
                return nil, err
        }
        w, err := newWebClient(s, s.URL, func(r *http.Request) {
                switch {
                case email != "" && token != "":
                        r.SetBasicAuth(email, token)
                case token != "":
                        r.Header.Set("Authorization", "Bearer "+token)
                }
        })
        if err != nil {
                return nil, err
        }
        return &jira{webClient: w, src: s, fields: jiraFields(s)}, nil
}

// jiraFields asks only for what the mapping uses, which makes a large search far cheaper.
func jiraFields(s *Source) []string {
        set := map[string]bool{"summary": true, "status": true, "updated": true, "attachment": true, "issuelinks": true}
        addSpec := func(f FieldSpec) {
                if f.From != "" {
                        set[strings.SplitN(f.From, ".", 2)[0]] = true
                }
                for _, r := range f.Rules {
                        for k := range r.When {
                                set[strings.SplitN(k, ".", 2)[0]] = true
                        }
                }
        }
        for _, f := range []*FieldSpec{s.Fields.Title, s.Fields.Spec, s.Fields.Priority, s.Fields.Tier, s.Fields.Tags, s.Fields.Status} {
                if f != nil {
                        addSpec(*f)
                }
        }
        for _, f := range s.Fields.Labels {
                addSpec(f)
        }
        for _, f := range s.Fields.Props {
                addSpec(f)
        }
        for _, w := range s.SkipWhen {
                for k := range w {
                        set[strings.SplitN(k, ".", 2)[0]] = true
                }
        }
        delete(set, "key") // The key is not a field; it comes with every issue.
        return slices.Sorted(maps.Keys(set))
}

type jiraIssue struct {
        Key    string         `json:"key"`
        Fields map[string]any `json:"fields"`
}

var orderBy = regexp.MustCompile(`(?i)\s+order\s+by\s+`)

// withSince narrows a query to recent changes. The JQL may end in ORDER BY, which must stay
// outside the parentheses. JQL dates have minute precision and use the account's time zone,
// so this reads a day further back than needed and lets the version check drop repeats.
func withSince(jql string, since time.Time) string {
        if since.IsZero() {
                return jql
        }
        clause := fmt.Sprintf(`updated >= "%s"`, since.UTC().Add(-24*time.Hour).Format("2006-01-02 15:04"))
        if loc := orderBy.FindStringIndex(jql); loc != nil {
                return "(" + jql[:loc[0]] + ") AND " + clause + jql[loc[0]:]
        }
        return "(" + jql + ") AND " + clause
}

// Pull implements Connector, using the enhanced search and its opaque page tokens.
func (j *jira) Pull(ctx context.Context, opts PullOptions, yield func(Item) error) error {
        jql := j.src.Query
        if opts.Query != "" {
                jql = opts.Query
        }
        jql = withSince(jql, opts.Since)
        next := ""
        for {
                body := map[string]any{"jql": jql, "maxResults": 100, "fields": j.fields}
                if next != "" {
                        body["nextPageToken"] = next
                }
                var page struct {
                        Issues        []jiraIssue `json:"issues"`
                        NextPageToken string      `json:"nextPageToken"`
                }
                if err := j.do(ctx, http.MethodPost, "/rest/api/3/search/jql", body, &page); err != nil {
                        return err
                }
                for _, issue := range page.Issues {
                        if err := yield(j.toItem(issue)); err != nil {
                                return err
                        }
                }
                if page.NextPageToken == "" {
                        return nil
                }
                next = page.NextPageToken
        }
}

// Get implements Getter.
func (j *jira) Get(ctx context.Context, key string) (Item, error) {
        var issue jiraIssue
        q := url.Values{"fields": {strings.Join(j.fields, ",")}}
        if err := j.do(ctx, http.MethodGet, "/rest/api/3/issue/"+url.PathEscape(key)+"?"+q.Encode(), nil, &issue); err != nil {
                return Item{}, err
        }
        return j.toItem(issue), nil
}

func (j *jira) toItem(issue jiraIssue) Item {
        f := issue.Fields
        if f == nil {
                f = map[string]any{}
        }
        fields := make(map[string]any, len(f)+1)
        for k, v := range f {
                fields[k] = plainField(v)
        }
        fields["key"] = issue.Key
        it := Item{
                Key: issue.Key, Fields: fields, URL: j.base + "/browse/" + issue.Key,
                Version: Text(f["updated"]), Status: nested(f["status"], "name"),
        }
        if atts, ok := f["attachment"].([]any); ok {
                for _, a := range atts {
                        m, ok := a.(map[string]any)
                        if !ok {
                                continue
                        }
                        size, _ := m["size"].(float64)
                        name := Text(m["filename"])
                        it.Attachments = append(it.Attachments, Attachment{Name: name, Resource: meta.Resource{
                                Kind: "jira.attachment", URL: Text(m["content"]), Name: name,
                                MediaType: Text(m["mimeType"]), Size: int64(size), Connection: j.src.Name,
                        }})
                }
        }
        // A link of type Blocks with an inward issue means that issue blocks this one.
        if links, ok := f["issuelinks"].([]any); ok {
                for _, l := range links {
                        m, ok := l.(map[string]any)
                        if !ok || nested(m["type"], "name") != "Blocks" {
                                continue
                        }
                        if key := nested(m["inwardIssue"], "key"); key != "" {
                                it.BlockedBy = append(it.BlockedBy, key)
                        }
                }
        }
        return it
}

func nested(v any, key string) string {
        if m, ok := v.(map[string]any); ok {
                return Text(m[key])
        }
        return ""
}

// plainField turns rich text into plain text. API v3 sends descriptions in the Atlassian
// Document Format, and everything else stays as it came.
func plainField(v any) any {
        if m, ok := v.(map[string]any); ok && m["type"] == "doc" {
                var b strings.Builder
                adfText(m, &b)
                return strings.TrimSpace(b.String())
        }
        return v
}

func adfText(node map[string]any, b *strings.Builder) {
        if t, ok := node["text"].(string); ok {
                b.WriteString(t)
        }
        if node["type"] == "hardBreak" {
                b.WriteByte('\n')
        }
        if kids, ok := node["content"].([]any); ok {
                for _, k := range kids {
                        if m, ok := k.(map[string]any); ok {
                                adfText(m, b)
                        }
                }
        }
        switch node["type"] {
        case "paragraph", "heading", "listItem", "codeBlock", "blockquote":
                b.WriteByte('\n')
        }
}

// SetStatus implements Pusher. Jira has no "set status": it moves an issue through a
// workflow, so this finds the transition that leads to the wanted status.
func (j *jira) SetStatus(ctx context.Context, key, status string) error {
        var out struct {
                Transitions []struct {
                        ID string `json:"id"`
                        To struct {
                                Name string `json:"name"`
                        } `json:"to"`
                } `json:"transitions"`
        }
        path := "/rest/api/3/issue/" + url.PathEscape(key) + "/transitions"
        if err := j.do(ctx, http.MethodGet, path, nil, &out); err != nil {
                return err
        }
        var names []string
        for _, t := range out.Transitions {
                names = append(names, t.To.Name)
                if strings.EqualFold(t.To.Name, status) {
                        return j.do(ctx, http.MethodPost, path, map[string]any{"transition": map[string]string{"id": t.ID}}, nil)
                }
        }
        return fmt.Errorf("%w: %s cannot move to %q from where it is; it can move to: %s", ErrPermanent, key, status, strings.Join(names, ", "))
}

// VerifyHook implements HookReader.
func (j *jira) VerifyHook(secret string, h http.Header, body []byte) error {
        return verifySHA256(secret, h.Get("X-Hub-Signature"), body)
}

// HookKeys implements HookReader.
func (j *jira) HookKeys(body []byte) ([]string, error) {
        var ev struct {
                Issue struct {
                        Key string `json:"key"`
                } `json:"issue"`
        }
        if err := json.Unmarshal(body, &ev); err != nil {
                return nil, err
        }
        if ev.Issue.Key == "" {
                return nil, nil
        }
        return []string{ev.Issue.Key}, nil
}

package connect

import (
        "crypto/sha256"
        "encoding/hex"
        "encoding/json"
        "fmt"
        "maps"
        "regexp"
        "slices"
        "strconv"
        "strings"

        "github.com/Grano22/aiculator/internal/core"
        "github.com/Grano22/aiculator/internal/engine"
        "github.com/Grano22/aiculator/internal/meta"
        "github.com/Grano22/aiculator/internal/store"
)

// Labels every imported task carries. The syncer finds its tasks by them, and an agent
// is told that a task with a source holds text from outside.
const (
        LabelSource   = "source"
        LabelExternal = "external"
)

// Attachment is a file on an item, by reference.
type Attachment struct {
        Name     string
        Resource meta.Resource
}

// Item is one thing from another system, before any mapping.
type Item struct {
        Key         string
        Version     string // Changes when the item changes.
        URL         string
        Status      string
        Fields      map[string]any
        Attachments []Attachment
        BlockedBy   []string // Keys of the items this one depends on.
}

// lookup finds a field by exact name, then ignoring case, then as a dotted path.
func (it Item) lookup(path string) (any, bool) {
        if v, ok := it.Fields[path]; ok {
                return v, v != nil
        }
        for k, v := range it.Fields {
                if strings.EqualFold(k, path) {
                        return v, v != nil
                }
        }
        var cur any = map[string]any(it.Fields)
        for _, part := range strings.Split(path, ".") {
                m, ok := cur.(map[string]any)
                if !ok {
                        return nil, false
                }
                if cur, ok = m[part]; !ok {
                        return nil, false
                }
        }
        return cur, cur != nil
}

// Text renders any field value as text.
func Text(v any) string {
        switch x := v.(type) {
        case nil:
                return ""
        case string:
                return x
        case []string:
                return strings.Join(x, ", ")
        case bool:
                return strconv.FormatBool(x)
        case float64:
                return strconv.FormatFloat(x, 'f', -1, 64)
        case []any:
                parts := make([]string, 0, len(x))
                for _, e := range x {
                        parts = append(parts, Text(e))
                }
                return strings.Join(parts, ", ")
        case map[string]any:
                for _, k := range []string{"name", "value", "displayName", "key"} {
                        if s, ok := x[k]; ok {
                                return Text(s)
                        }
                }
                b, _ := json.Marshal(x)
                return string(b)
        }
        return fmt.Sprint(v)
}

func (w When) matches(it Item) bool {
        for field, want := range w {
                v, _ := it.lookup(field)
                if !strings.EqualFold(strings.TrimSpace(Text(v)), strings.TrimSpace(want)) {
                        return false
                }
        }
        return true
}

// resolve works out one attribute. Rules are tried in order, then the named field through
// its map, then the default.
func (f FieldSpec) resolve(it Item) (any, bool) {
        for _, r := range f.Rules {
                if r.When.matches(it) {
                        return r.Value, true
                }
        }
        if f.From != "" {
                if v, ok := it.lookup(f.From); ok {
                        if f.Map == nil {
                                return v, true
                        }
                        text := Text(v)
                        for k, out := range f.Map {
                                if strings.EqualFold(k, text) {
                                        return out, true
                                }
                        }
                }
        }
        return f.Default, f.Default != nil
}

func resolveText(f *FieldSpec, it Item) string {
        if f == nil {
                return ""
        }
        v, _ := f.resolve(it)
        return strings.TrimSpace(Text(v))
}

func resolveInt(f *FieldSpec, it Item) (int, bool, error) {
        if f == nil {
                return 0, false, nil
        }
        v, ok := f.resolve(it)
        if !ok {
                return 0, false, nil
        }
        if n, isInt := v.(int); isInt {
                return n, true, nil
        }
        s := strings.TrimSpace(Text(v))
        if s == "" {
                return 0, false, nil
        }
        n, err := strconv.ParseFloat(s, 64)
        if err != nil {
                return 0, false, fmt.Errorf("%q is not a number", s)
        }
        return int(n), true, nil
}

func resolveList(f *FieldSpec, it Item) []string {
        if f == nil {
                return nil
        }
        v, ok := f.resolve(it)
        if !ok {
                return nil
        }
        var out []string
        switch x := v.(type) {
        case []string:
                out = x
        case []any:
                for _, e := range x {
                        out = append(out, Text(e))
                }
        default:
                for _, p := range strings.Split(Text(v), ",") {
                        if p = strings.TrimSpace(p); p != "" {
                                out = append(out, p)
                        }
                }
        }
        return out
}

var unsafeID = regexp.MustCompile(`[^A-Za-z0-9_-]+`)

// TaskID derives a stable ID from a source and a key, so importing twice finds the same
// task. Keys that do not survive cleaning get a short hash, so two can never collide.
func TaskID(source, key string) string {
        clean := strings.Trim(unsafeID.ReplaceAllString(key, "-"), "-")
        if clean == key && len(source)+1+len(clean) <= 128 {
                return source + "-" + clean
        }
        h := sha256.Sum256([]byte(key))
        suffix := hex.EncodeToString(h[:6])
        if room := 128 - len(source) - len(suffix) - 2; len(clean) > room {
                clean = clean[:room]
        }
        if clean == "" {
                return source + "-" + suffix
        }
        return source + "-" + clean + "-" + suffix
}

// Mapped is an item turned into what the swarm stores.
type Mapped struct {
        Spec  engine.TaskSpec       `json:"spec"`
        Props map[string]*meta.Prop `json:"props,omitempty"`
        Link  store.Link            `json:"link"`
}

// Skip reports whether the source's skip rules leave this item out.
func (s *Source) Skip(it Item) bool {
        return slices.ContainsFunc(s.SkipWhen, func(w When) bool { return w.matches(it) })
}

// Map turns an item into a task. Everything an outside system controls goes through here,
// and none of it can reach checks, touches, budget or review.
func (s *Source) Map(it Item) (Mapped, error) {
        title := resolveText(s.Fields.Title, it)
        if title == "" {
                return Mapped{}, fmt.Errorf("%s: no title", it.Key)
        }
        if len(title) > 512 {
                title = title[:512]
        }
        d := s.Defaults
        spec := engine.TaskSpec{
                ID: TaskID(s.Name, it.Key), Title: title, Spec: d.Spec, Tier: d.Tier, Priority: d.Priority,
                Tags: slices.Clone(d.Tags), Checks: slices.Clone(d.Checks), Touches: slices.Clone(d.Touches),
                RequireReview: d.RequireReview, AllowEmpty: d.AllowEmpty, Budget: d.Budget,
                Labels: maps.Clone(d.Labels),
        }
        if text := resolveText(s.Fields.Spec, it); text != "" {
                spec.Spec = text
        }
        var err error
        if n, ok, e := resolveInt(s.Fields.Priority, it); e != nil {
                return Mapped{}, fmt.Errorf("%s: priority: %w", it.Key, e)
        } else if ok {
                spec.Priority = n
        }
        if n, ok, e := resolveInt(s.Fields.Tier, it); e != nil {
                return Mapped{}, fmt.Errorf("%s: tier: %w", it.Key, e)
        } else if ok {
                spec.Tier = n
        }
        if tags := resolveList(s.Fields.Tags, it); tags != nil {
                spec.Tags = append(spec.Tags, tags...)
        }
        if spec.Aging, err = core.ParseAging(d.Aging); err != nil {
                return Mapped{}, err
        }
        if len(d.Aging) == 0 {
                spec.Aging = nil // No steps here means the server's steps apply.
        }
        if spec.Labels == nil {
                spec.Labels = map[string]string{}
        }
        for name, f := range s.Fields.Labels {
                if v, ok := f.resolve(it); ok {
                        if text := strings.TrimSpace(Text(v)); text != "" {
                                if len(text) > core.MaxLabelValue {
                                        text = text[:core.MaxLabelValue]
                                }
                                spec.Labels[name] = text
                        }
                }
        }
        // These two come last, so a mapping cannot point a task at another source's item.
        spec.Labels[LabelSource] = s.Name
        spec.Labels[LabelExternal] = trimLabel(it.Key)

        for _, dep := range it.BlockedBy {
                spec.Deps = append(spec.Deps, TaskID(s.Name, dep))
        }
        props := map[string]*meta.Prop{}
        for name, f := range s.Fields.Props {
                if v, ok := f.resolve(it); ok {
                        props[name] = &meta.Prop{Value: v}
                }
        }
        if it.URL != "" {
                props["external_url"] = &meta.Prop{Value: it.URL}
        }
        for _, a := range it.Attachments {
                r := a.Resource
                props[attachmentProp(a.Name)] = &meta.Prop{Resource: &r}
        }
        status := it.Status
        if s.Fields.Status != nil {
                status = resolveText(s.Fields.Status, it)
        }
        return Mapped{
                Spec: spec, Props: props,
                Link: store.Link{Source: s.Name, Key: it.Key, TaskID: spec.ID, URL: it.URL, Version: it.Version, RemoteStatus: status},
        }, nil
}

func trimLabel(s string) string {
        if len(s) > core.MaxLabelValue {
                return s[:core.MaxLabelValue]
        }
        return s
}

var unsafeProp = regexp.MustCompile(`[^A-Za-z0-9._/-]+`)

func attachmentProp(name string) string {
        p := "attachment/" + strings.Trim(unsafeProp.ReplaceAllString(name, "-"), "-./")
        if len(p) > 128 {
                p = p[:128]
        }
        return p
}

// Order puts tasks after what they depend on, and reports what cannot be imported: items in
// a dependency cycle, and items depending on them. A dependency on something outside this
// import stays for the server to judge, since it may already have that task.
func Order(items []Mapped) (ordered []Mapped, cyclic []string) {
        byID := make(map[string]int, len(items))
        for i, m := range items {
                byID[m.Spec.ID] = i
        }
        const (
                unseen = iota
                visiting
                finished
                broken
        )
        mark := make([]int, len(items))
        var visit func(i int) bool
        visit = func(i int) bool {
                switch mark[i] {
                case visiting, broken:
                        return false
                case finished:
                        return true
                }
                mark[i] = visiting
                for _, d := range items[i].Spec.Deps {
                        if j, ok := byID[d]; ok && !visit(j) {
                                mark[i] = broken
                                cyclic = append(cyclic, items[i].Spec.ID)
                                return false
                        }
                }
                mark[i] = finished
                ordered = append(ordered, items[i])
                return true
        }
        for i := range items {
                visit(i)
        }
        slices.Sort(cyclic)
        return ordered, slices.Compact(cyclic)
}

package connect

import (
        "context"
        "encoding/json"
        "errors"
        "fmt"
        "net/http"
        "net/url"
        "strings"
        "time"

        "github.com/Grano22/aiculator/internal/meta"
)

const defaultNotionVersion = "2026-03-11"

// notion reads and updates pages of a Notion data source.
type notion struct {
        *webClient
        src *Source
}

func newNotion(s *Source) (*notion, error) {
        token, err := envValue(s.Auth.TokenEnv, s.Name)
        if err != nil {
                return nil, err
        }
        version := s.APIVersion
        if version == "" {
                version = defaultNotionVersion
        }
        base := s.URL
        if base == "" {
                base = "https://api.notion.com"
        }
        w, err := newWebClient(s, base, func(r *http.Request) {
                r.Header.Set("Notion-Version", version)
                if token != "" {
                        r.Header.Set("Authorization", "Bearer "+token)
                }
        })
        if err != nil {
                return nil, err
        }
        return &notion{webClient: w, src: s}, nil
}

type notionPage struct {
        ID             string         `json:"id"`
        URL            string         `json:"url"`
        LastEditedTime string         `json:"last_edited_time"`
        InTrash        bool           `json:"in_trash"`
        Properties     map[string]any `json:"properties"`
}

// Pull implements Connector.
func (n *notion) Pull(ctx context.Context, opts PullOptions, yield func(Item) error) error {
        var filter any = n.src.Filter
        if opts.Query != "" {
                var parsed any
                if err := json.Unmarshal([]byte(opts.Query), &parsed); err != nil {
                        return fmt.Errorf("a Notion query is a JSON filter: %w", err)
                }
                filter = parsed
        }
        if !opts.Since.IsZero() {
                recent := map[string]any{"timestamp": "last_edited_time", "last_edited_time": map[string]any{
                        "on_or_after": opts.Since.UTC().Add(-time.Minute).Format(time.RFC3339),
                }}
                if filter == nil {
                        filter = recent
                } else {
                        filter = map[string]any{"and": []any{filter, recent}}
                }
        }
        cursor := ""
        for {
                body := map[string]any{"page_size": 100}
                if filter != nil {
                        body["filter"] = filter
                }
                if cursor != "" {
                        body["start_cursor"] = cursor
                }
                var page struct {
                        Results    []notionPage `json:"results"`
                        HasMore    bool         `json:"has_more"`
                        NextCursor *string      `json:"next_cursor"`
                }
                path := "/v1/data_sources/" + url.PathEscape(n.src.DataSource) + "/query"
                if err := n.do(ctx, http.MethodPost, path, body, &page); err != nil {
                        return err
                }
                for _, p := range page.Results {
                        it, err := n.toItem(ctx, p)
                        if err != nil {
                                return err
                        }
                        if err := yield(it); err != nil {
                                return err
                        }
                }
                if !page.HasMore || page.NextCursor == nil || *page.NextCursor == "" {
                        return nil
                }
                cursor = *page.NextCursor
        }
}

// Get implements Getter.
func (n *notion) Get(ctx context.Context, key string) (Item, error) {
        var p notionPage
        if err := n.do(ctx, http.MethodGet, "/v1/pages/"+url.PathEscape(key), nil, &p); err != nil {
                return Item{}, err
        }
        return n.toItem(ctx, p)
}

func (n *notion) toItem(ctx context.Context, p notionPage) (Item, error) {
        fields := make(map[string]any, len(p.Properties)+2)
        it := Item{Key: p.ID, Version: p.LastEditedTime, URL: p.URL, Fields: fields}
        for name, raw := range p.Properties {
                m, ok := raw.(map[string]any)
                if !ok {
                        continue
                }
                kind, _ := m["type"].(string)
                v := notionValue(kind, m[kind])
                if kind == "files" {
                        it.Attachments = append(it.Attachments, n.notionFiles(m[kind])...)
                }
                fields[name] = v
                if kind == "status" {
                        it.Status = Text(v)
                }
        }
        fields["id"], fields["url"] = p.ID, p.URL
        if p.InTrash {
                it.Status = "in_trash"
        }
        if n.src.FetchBody {
                body, err := n.pageText(ctx, p.ID)
                if err != nil {
                        return Item{}, err
                }
                fields["body"] = body
        }
        return it, nil
}

// notionValue reduces a property to plain data, whatever its type.
func notionValue(kind string, v any) any {
        switch kind {
        case "title", "rich_text":
                list, _ := v.([]any)
                var b strings.Builder
                for _, e := range list {
                        if m, ok := e.(map[string]any); ok {
                                b.WriteString(Text(m["plain_text"]))
                        }
                }
                return b.String()
        case "select", "status":
                return nested(v, "name")
        case "multi_select", "people":
                list, _ := v.([]any)
                out := make([]string, 0, len(list))
                for _, e := range list {
                        out = append(out, nested(e, "name"))
                }
                return out
        case "date":
                return nested(v, "start")
        case "relation":
                list, _ := v.([]any)
                out := make([]string, 0, len(list))
                for _, e := range list {
                        out = append(out, nested(e, "id"))
                }
                return out
        case "formula", "rollup":
                if m, ok := v.(map[string]any); ok {
                        inner, _ := m["type"].(string)
                        return notionValue(inner, m[inner])
                }
        case "files":
                return nil // These become attachments instead.
        }
        return v
}

func (n *notion) notionFiles(v any) []Attachment {
        list, _ := v.([]any)
        var out []Attachment
        for _, e := range list {
                m, ok := e.(map[string]any)
                if !ok {
                        continue
                }
                kind, _ := m["type"].(string)
                link := nested(m[kind], "url")
                if link == "" {
                        continue
                }
                name := Text(m["name"])
                // A file Notion hosts has a link that expires after about an hour, and needs no
                // token, so it goes through the guarded fetcher like any other public URL.
                out = append(out, Attachment{Name: name, Resource: meta.Resource{Kind: "notion.file", URL: link, Name: name}})
        }
        return out
}

const maxBodyPages = 20

// pageText reads a page's text blocks. It costs a request per page, so it is opt-in.
func (n *notion) pageText(ctx context.Context, id string) (string, error) {
        var b strings.Builder
        cursor := ""
        for range maxBodyPages {
                q := url.Values{"page_size": {"100"}}
                if cursor != "" {
                        q.Set("start_cursor", cursor)
                }
                var page struct {
                        Results    []map[string]any `json:"results"`
                        HasMore    bool             `json:"has_more"`
                        NextCursor *string          `json:"next_cursor"`
                }
                if err := n.do(ctx, http.MethodGet, "/v1/blocks/"+url.PathEscape(id)+"/children?"+q.Encode(), nil, &page); err != nil {
                        return "", err
                }
                for _, block := range page.Results {
                        kind, _ := block["type"].(string)
                        inner, _ := block[kind].(map[string]any)
                        if inner == nil {
                                continue
                        }
                        if text := Text(notionValue("rich_text", inner["rich_text"])); text != "" {
                                b.WriteString(text)
                                b.WriteByte('\n')
                        }
                }
                if !page.HasMore || page.NextCursor == nil {
                        break
                }
                cursor = *page.NextCursor
        }
        return strings.TrimSpace(b.String()), nil
}

// SetStatus implements Pusher. The property is named by the mapping's status field, and
// must be of Notion's status type.
func (n *notion) SetStatus(ctx context.Context, key, status string) error {
        prop := "Status"
        if f := n.src.Fields.Status; f != nil && f.From != "" {
                prop = f.From
        }
        body := map[string]any{"properties": map[string]any{prop: map[string]any{"status": map[string]string{"name": status}}}}
        return n.do(ctx, http.MethodPatch, "/v1/pages/"+url.PathEscape(key), body, nil)
}

// VerifyHook implements HookReader.
func (n *notion) VerifyHook(secret string, h http.Header, body []byte) error {
        return verifySHA256(secret, h.Get("X-Notion-Signature"), body)
}

// HookKeys implements HookReader. Notion's events name a page and carry no content.
func (n *notion) HookKeys(body []byte) ([]string, error) {
        var ev struct {
                Type   string `json:"type"`
                Entity struct {
                        ID   string `json:"id"`
                        Type string `json:"type"`
                } `json:"entity"`
        }
        if err := json.Unmarshal(body, &ev); err != nil {
                return nil, err
        }
        if ev.Entity.ID == "" {
                return nil, errors.New("event names no entity")
        }
        if ev.Entity.Type != "page" {
                return nil, nil
        }
        return []string{ev.Entity.ID}, nil
}

package connect
