        }
        return nil
}

func contains(list []string, s string) bool {
        for _, x := range list {
                if x == s {
                        return true
                }
        }
        return false
}

// allowed applies the permission policy. Writes are also checked against the
// worktree here, in addition to the sandbox, so that the refusal is visible to
// the agent instead of arriving as a mysterious failure.
func (h *handler) allowed(tc acp.ToolCallUpdate) bool {
        kind := "other"
        if tc.Kind != nil {
                kind = string(*tc.Kind)
        }
        if contains(h.m.DeniedTools, kind) {
                return false
        }
        switch kind {
        case "read", "search", "think", "fetch", "execute":
                return true
        case "edit", "delete", "move":
                for _, l := range tc.Locations {
                        if _, err := h.confine(l.Path); err != nil {
                                return false
                        }
                }
                return true
        }
        return contains(h.m.AllowedTools, kind)
}

// RequestPermission implements acp.Client.
func (h *handler) RequestPermission(_ context.Context, p acp.RequestPermissionRequest) (acp.RequestPermissionResponse, error) {
        ok := h.allowed(p.ToolCall)
        want := []acp.PermissionOptionKind{acp.PermissionOptionKindRejectOnce, acp.PermissionOptionKindRejectAlways}
        if ok {
                want = []acp.PermissionOptionKind{acp.PermissionOptionKindAllowOnce, acp.PermissionOptionKindAllowAlways}
        }
        if v := vl.V(vlog.LevelChanges); v.Enabled() {
                kind := "other"
                if p.ToolCall.Kind != nil {
                        kind = string(*p.ToolCall.Kind)
                }
                v.Info("permission decision", "allowed", ok, "tool", p.ToolCall.ToolCallId, "kind", kind)
        }
        for _, k := range want {
                for _, o := range p.Options {
                        if o.Kind == k {
                                return acp.RequestPermissionResponse{Outcome: acp.RequestPermissionOutcome{
                                        Selected: &acp.RequestPermissionOutcomeSelected{OptionId: o.OptionId},
                                }}, nil
                        }
                }
        }
        // No matching option was offered, so refuse rather than guess.
        return acp.RequestPermissionResponse{Outcome: acp.RequestPermissionOutcome{Cancelled: &acp.RequestPermissionOutcomeCancelled{}}}, nil
}

// confine resolves a path and refuses anything outside the worktree, including
// through symlinks.
func (h *handler) confine(p string) (string, error) {
        if !filepath.IsAbs(p) {
                p = filepath.Join(h.root, p)
        }
        p = filepath.Clean(p)
        // Resolve the deepest part that exists, since the file itself may be new.
        dir, rest := p, ""
        for {
                r, err := filepath.EvalSymlinks(dir)
                if err == nil {
                        p = filepath.Join(r, rest)
                        break
                }
                if !errors.Is(err, os.ErrNotExist) {
                        return "", err
                }
                parent := filepath.Dir(dir)
                if parent == dir {
                        return "", fmt.Errorf("cannot resolve %s", p)
                }
                rest = filepath.Join(filepath.Base(dir), rest)
                dir = parent
        }
        if p != h.root && !strings.HasPrefix(p, h.root+string(filepath.Separator)) {
                return "", fmt.Errorf("path %s is outside the worktree", p)
        }
        return p, nil
}

// ReadTextFile implements acp.Client.
func (h *handler) ReadTextFile(_ context.Context, r acp.ReadTextFileRequest) (acp.ReadTextFileResponse, error) {
        p, err := h.confine(r.Path)
        if err != nil {
                return acp.ReadTextFileResponse{}, err
        }
        b, err := os.ReadFile(p)
        if err != nil {
                return acp.ReadTextFileResponse{}, err
        }
        s := string(b)
        if r.Line != nil || r.Limit != nil {
                lines := strings.Split(s, "\n")
                start := 0
                if r.Line != nil && *r.Line > 1 {
                        start = min(*r.Line-1, len(lines))
                }
                end := len(lines)
                if r.Limit != nil {
                        end = min(start+*r.Limit, len(lines))
                }
                s = strings.Join(lines[start:end], "\n")
        }
        return acp.ReadTextFileResponse{Content: s}, nil
}

// WriteTextFile implements acp.Client.
func (h *handler) WriteTextFile(_ context.Context, r acp.WriteTextFileRequest) (acp.WriteTextFileResponse, error) {
        p, err := h.confine(r.Path)
        if err != nil {
                return acp.WriteTextFileResponse{}, err
        }
        if err := os.MkdirAll(filepath.Dir(p), 0o755); err != nil {
                return acp.WriteTextFileResponse{}, err
        }
        return acp.WriteTextFileResponse{}, os.WriteFile(p, []byte(r.Content), 0o644)
}

var errNoTerminal = errors.New("terminal is not offered; run commands with your own tools")

// CreateTerminal implements acp.Client. The driver does not advertise terminals.
func (h *handler) CreateTerminal(context.Context, acp.CreateTerminalRequest) (acp.CreateTerminalResponse, error) {
        return acp.CreateTerminalResponse{}, errNoTerminal
}

// KillTerminal implements acp.Client.
func (h *handler) KillTerminal(context.Context, acp.KillTerminalRequest) (acp.KillTerminalResponse, error) {
        return acp.KillTerminalResponse{}, errNoTerminal
}

// TerminalOutput implements acp.Client.
func (h *handler) TerminalOutput(context.Context, acp.TerminalOutputRequest) (acp.TerminalOutputResponse, error) {
        return acp.TerminalOutputResponse{}, errNoTerminal
}

// ReleaseTerminal implements acp.Client.
func (h *handler) ReleaseTerminal(context.Context, acp.ReleaseTerminalRequest) (acp.ReleaseTerminalResponse, error) {
        return acp.ReleaseTerminalResponse{}, errNoTerminal
}

// WaitForTerminalExit implements acp.Client.
func (h *handler) WaitForTerminalExit(context.Context, acp.WaitForTerminalExitRequest) (acp.WaitForTerminalExitResponse, error) {
        return acp.WaitForTerminalExitResponse{}, errNoTerminal
}

var _ acp.Client = (*handler)(nil)

//go:build !windows

package driver

import (
        "os/exec"
        "syscall"
        "time"
)

// killGroup runs the harness in its own process group, so that stopping it also
// stops whatever it started.
func killGroup(cmd *exec.Cmd) {
        cmd.SysProcAttr = &syscall.SysProcAttr{Setpgid: true}
        cmd.Cancel = func() error { return syscall.Kill(-cmd.Process.Pid, syscall.SIGKILL) }
        cmd.WaitDelay = 3 * time.Second
}

func killTree(cmd *exec.Cmd) {
        if cmd.Process != nil {
                _ = syscall.Kill(-cmd.Process.Pid, syscall.SIGKILL)
        }
}

package engine

import (
        "container/heap"
        "context"
        "errors"
        "fmt"
        "slices"
        "strings"
        "time"

        "github.com/Grano22/aiculator/internal/core"
        "github.com/Grano22/aiculator/internal/store"
        "github.com/Grano22/aiculator/internal/vlog"
)

// readyItem is one entry in a tier's ready heap. key is priority·agingUnit minus
// the time the task became ready. Comparing it gives the same order as comparing
// priority+waited/agingUnit at any moment, so priority aging needs no re-sorting.
type readyItem struct {
        id  string
        key int64
        seq uint64
}

type readyHeap []readyItem

func (h readyHeap) Len() int { return len(h) }
func (h readyHeap) Less(i, j int) bool {
        if h[i].key != h[j].key {
                return h[i].key > h[j].key
        }
        return h[i].seq < h[j].seq
}
func (h readyHeap) Swap(i, j int) { h[i], h[j] = h[j], h[i] }
func (h *readyHeap) Push(x any)   { *h = append(*h, x.(readyItem)) }
func (h *readyHeap) Pop() any {
        old := *h
        n := len(old) - 1
        it := old[n]
        *h = old[:n]
        return it
}
func (h *readyHeap) pushItem(it readyItem) { heap.Push(h, it) }

// boostItem says when a ready task next reaches an aging step. seq ties it to one heap
// entry: a task that was claimed or moved since then no longer matches, and is skipped.
type boostItem struct {
        at  time.Time
        id  string
        seq uint64
}

type boostHeap []boostItem

func (h boostHeap) Len() int           { return len(h) }
func (h boostHeap) Less(i, j int) bool { return h[i].at.Before(h[j].at) }
func (h boostHeap) Swap(i, j int)      { h[i], h[j] = h[j], h[i] }
func (h *boostHeap) Push(x any)        { *h = append(*h, x.(boostItem)) }
func (h *boostHeap) Pop() any {
        old := *h
        n := len(old) - 1
        it := old[n]
        old[n] = boostItem{}
        *h = old[:n]
        return it
}

// Wait answers an agent's wait_for_task call with one of three actions.
const (
        ActionTask = "task"
        ActionWait = "wait"
        ActionExit = "exit"
)

// Reasons an agent is told to wait or exit.
const (
        ReasonPlanning    = "planning"
        ReasonPlannerLost = "planner_lost"
        ReasonDeps        = "deps"
        ReasonTierBusy    = "tier_busy"
        ReasonIdle        = "idle"
        ReasonPlanDone    = "no_work_left"
        ReasonNoneExpect  = "no_work_expected"
)

// PlanningView is what waiting agents see of the planner.
type PlanningView struct {
        Epoch         uint64      `json:"epoch"`
        Active        bool        `json:"active"`
        Phase         string      `json:"phase,omitempty"`
        ExpectedTasks map[int]int `json:"expected_tasks,omitempty"`
        ETAMs         int64       `json:"eta_ms,omitempty"`
        AgeMs         int64       `json:"age_ms"`
        Stale         bool        `json:"stale"`
}

// WaitResponse is the result of Wait.
type WaitResponse struct {
        Action     string        `json:"action"`
        Job        string        `json:"job,omitempty"` // "work" or "review".
        Task       *core.Task    `json:"task,omitempty"`
        Lease      uint64        `json:"lease,omitempty"`
        LeaseTTLMs int64         `json:"lease_ttl_ms,omitempty"`
        Reason     string        `json:"reason,omitempty"`
        Planning   *PlanningView `json:"planning,omitempty"`
}

type waiter struct {
        agent    Agent
        since    time.Time
        ch       chan WaitResponse
        deadline time.Time
}

func (e *Engine) reply(w *waiter, r WaitResponse) {
        if v := log.V(vlog.LevelDebug); v.Enabled() {
                v.Info("wait answered", "agent", w.agent.ID, "tier", w.agent.Tier, "action", r.Action, "reason", r.Reason)
        }
        w.ch <- r // Buffered with capacity 1, and each waiter is replied to once.
        e.waiters[w.agent.Tier] = slices.DeleteFunc(e.waiters[w.agent.Tier], func(x *waiter) bool { return x == w })
}

// Wait returns a leased task, or holds for up to hold, then says wait or exit.
// A task it returns is already claimed, so there is no second round trip and
// nothing for agents to race on. hold 0 is a non-blocking try.
func (e *Engine) Wait(ctx context.Context, a Agent, hold time.Duration) (WaitResponse, error) {
        if a.ID == "" || core.IsSystem(a.ID) || a.Tier < 1 {
                return WaitResponse{}, fmt.Errorf("%w: agent %q tier %d", ErrInvalid, a.ID, a.Tier)
        }
        e.touch(a)
        hold = min(hold, e.cfg.MaxHold)
        type out struct {
                resp WaitResponse
                w    *waiter
        }
        o, err := do(ctx, e, func() (out, error) {
                since := e.markSeen(a.ID)
                if r, ok := e.tryMatch(a); ok {
                        delete(e.seen, a.ID)
                        return out{resp: r}, nil
                }
                if hold <= 0 {
                        r := e.idleResponse(a.Tier, since)
                        if v := log.V(vlog.LevelDebug); v.Enabled() {
                                v.Info("wait answered", "agent", a.ID, "tier", a.Tier, "action", r.Action, "reason", r.Reason)
                        }
                        return out{resp: r}, nil
                }
                // An exit answer is immediate; there is nothing to hold the agent for.
                if r := e.idleResponse(a.Tier, since); r.Action == ActionExit {
                        return out{resp: r}, nil
                }
                w := &waiter{agent: a, since: since, ch: make(chan WaitResponse, 1), deadline: e.now().Add(hold)}
                e.waiters[a.Tier] = append(e.waiters[a.Tier], w)
                return out{w: w}, nil
        })
        if err != nil {
                return WaitResponse{}, err
        }
        if o.w == nil {
                return o.resp, nil
        }
        select {
        case r, ok := <-o.w.ch:
                if !ok {
                        return WaitResponse{}, ErrStopped
                }
                return r, nil
        case <-ctx.Done():
                e.abandon(o.w)
                return WaitResponse{}, ctx.Err()
        case <-e.dead:
                return WaitResponse{}, ErrStopped
        }
}

// markSeen returns when the agent's current stretch of waiting began. A gap of
// two holds means it went away, so its next call starts a new stretch.
func (e *Engine) markSeen(id string) time.Time {
        now := e.now()
        s, ok := e.seen[id]
        if !ok || now.Sub(s.last) > 2*e.cfg.MaxHold {
                s.first = now
        }
        s.last = now
        e.seen[id] = s
        return s.first
}

// abandon removes a waiter whose caller disconnected. If a grant raced with the
// disconnect, the lease goes straight back instead of waiting out its timeout.
func (e *Engine) abandon(w *waiter) {
        ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 5*time.Second)
        defer cancel()
        _, _ = do(ctx, e, func() (struct{}, error) {
                e.waiters[w.agent.Tier] = slices.DeleteFunc(e.waiters[w.agent.Tier], func(x *waiter) bool { return x == w })
                select {
                case r := <-w.ch:
                        if r.Task != nil {
                                _, _ = e.commit(r.Task.ID, core.Cmd{Kind: core.CmdExpire, Actor: "system:lease", Note: "caller_disconnected"})
                        }
                default:
                }
                return struct{}{}, nil
        })
}

// Claim takes one specific ready task, for agents that preview before committing.
func (e *Engine) Claim(ctx context.Context, a Agent, id string) (WaitResponse, error) {
        if a.ID == "" || core.IsSystem(a.ID) || a.Tier < 1 {
                return WaitResponse{}, fmt.Errorf("%w: agent %q tier %d", ErrInvalid, a.ID, a.Tier)
        }
        e.touch(a)
        return do(ctx, e, func() (WaitResponse, error) {
                ent := e.tasks[id]
                if ent == nil {
                        return WaitResponse{}, fmt.Errorf("%w: %s", ErrNotFound, id)
                }
                if ent.task.State != core.Ready || !e.eligible(a, ent.task) {
                        return WaitResponse{}, fmt.Errorf("%w: %s is %s", ErrNoMatch, id, ent.task.State)
                }
                return e.grant(a, id, "work")
        })
}

func (e *Engine) grant(a Agent, id, job string) (WaitResponse, error) {
        t, err := e.commit(id, core.Cmd{
                Kind: core.CmdGrant, Actor: a.ID, AgentTier: a.Tier,
                LeaseTTL: e.cfg.LeaseTTL, ProgressTTL: e.cfg.ProgressTTL,
        })
        if err != nil {
                return WaitResponse{}, err
        }
        e.grants.Add(1)
        if v := log.V(vlog.LevelChanges); v.Enabled() {
                v.Info("grant", "task", id, "job", job, "agent", a.ID, "agent_tier", a.Tier, "task_tier", t.Tier, "lease", t.LeaseEpoch)
        }
        c := t.Clone()
        return WaitResponse{
                Action: ActionTask, Job: job, Task: &c, Lease: t.LeaseEpoch,
                LeaseTTLMs: e.cfg.LeaseTTL.Milliseconds(),
        }, nil
}

// eligible applies the filters: tier (with steal rules), tags and file conflicts.
func (e *Engine) eligible(a Agent, t core.Task) bool {
        if a.Tier < t.Tier {
                return false
        }
        if a.Tier > t.Tier && !e.stealAllowed(a.Tier, t) {
                return false
        }
        for _, tag := range t.Tags {
                if !slices.Contains(a.Tags, tag) {
                        return false
                }
        }
        return !e.touchConflict(t)
}

func (e *Engine) stealAllowed(agentTier int, t core.Task) bool {
        for _, r := range e.cfg.Steal {
                if r.AgentTier == agentTier && r.TaskTier == t.Tier {
                        return e.now().Sub(t.ReadyAt) >= r.After
                }
        }
        return false
}

func (e *Engine) touchConflict(t core.Task) bool {
        for id, paths := range e.active {
                if id == t.ID {
                        continue
                }
                for _, a := range t.Touches {
                        for _, b := range paths {
                                if pathsOverlap(a, b) {
                                        return true
                                }
                        }
                }
        }
        return false
}

// pathsOverlap reports whether one path equals or contains the other, so "src"
// conflicts with "src/a.go" but "src2" does not.
func pathsOverlap(a, b string) bool {
        a, b = strings.TrimSuffix(a, "/"), strings.TrimSuffix(b, "/")
        return a == b || strings.HasPrefix(a, b+"/") || strings.HasPrefix(b, a+"/")
}

// tryMatch finds work for an agent: review jobs first, then its own tier, then
// lower tiers it may steal from. It is the only place new leases are created.
func (e *Engine) tryMatch(a Agent) (WaitResponse, bool) {
        // The tick also does this, but a claim must not see an order up to a tick out of date. It
        // costs one look at the top of a heap when nothing is due.
        e.applyBoosts()
        if r, ok := e.matchReview(a); ok {
                return r, true
        }
        for tier := a.Tier; tier >= 1; tier-- {
                if r, ok := e.matchTier(a, tier); ok {
                        return r, true
                }
        }
        return WaitResponse{}, false
}

func (e *Engine) matchReview(a Agent) (WaitResponse, bool) {
        for i := 0; i < len(e.reviews); {
                id := e.reviews[i]
                ent := e.tasks[id]
                if ent == nil || !needsReviewer(ent.task) {
                        e.reviews = slices.Delete(e.reviews, i, i+1)
                        continue
                }
                t := ent.task
                if a.ID == t.Submitter || a.Tier < t.Tier {
                        i++
                        continue
                }
                if r, err := e.grant(a, id, "review"); err == nil {
                        e.reviews = slices.Delete(e.reviews, i, i+1)
                        return r, true
                }
                i++
        }
        return WaitResponse{}, false
}

func (e *Engine) matchTier(a Agent, tier int) (WaitResponse, bool) {
        h := e.ready[tier]
        if h == nil || h.Len() == 0 {
                return WaitResponse{}, false
        }
        var rejected []readyItem
        defer func() {
                for _, it := range rejected {
                        heap.Push(h, it)
                }
        }()
        for h.Len() > 0 {
                it := heap.Pop(h).(readyItem)
                ent := e.tasks[it.id]
                // A task's older heap entries are skipped: only its latest seq counts.
                if ent == nil || ent.task.State != core.Ready || ent.readySeq != it.seq {
                        continue
                }
                if ent.task.Tier != tier {
                        continue
                }
                if !e.eligible(a, ent.task) {
                        if v := log.V(vlog.LevelTrace); v.Enabled() {
                                v.Info("not eligible", "task", it.id, "agent", a.ID, "agent_tier", a.Tier, "task_tier", ent.task.Tier, "needs_tags", ent.task.Tags, "file_conflict", e.touchConflict(ent.task))
                        }
                        rejected = append(rejected, it)
                        continue
                }
                r, err := e.grant(a, it.id, "work")
                if err != nil {
                        if !errors.Is(err, store.ErrConflict) {
                                rejected = append(rejected, it)
                        }
                        continue
                }
                return r, true
        }
        return WaitResponse{}, false
}

// matchWaiters assigns available work, lowest tier first so that a task reaches
// an agent of its own tier before a higher tier can take it.
func (e *Engine) matchWaiters() {
        tiers := make([]int, 0, len(e.waiters))
        for t := range e.waiters {
                tiers = append(tiers, t)
        }
        slices.Sort(tiers)
        for _, tier := range tiers {
                for _, w := range slices.Clone(e.waiters[tier]) {
                        r, ok := e.tryMatch(w.agent)
                        if !ok {
                                continue
                        }
                        delete(e.seen, w.agent.ID)
                        e.reply(w, r)
                }
        }
}

// settleWaiters updates quiet timers, releases holds that ran out, and sends
// exit as soon as an agent's answer becomes exit.
func (e *Engine) settleWaiters() {
        now := e.now()
        e.updateQuiet(now)
        for _, ws := range e.waiters {
                for _, w := range slices.Clone(ws) {
                        r := e.idleResponse(w.agent.Tier, w.since)
                        if r.Action == ActionExit || !now.Before(w.deadline) {
                                e.reply(w, r)
                        }
                }
        }
}

// reach counts live tasks that could reach an agent of this tier, directly or by
// failing and escalating. Tasks above the tier can never come down to it.
func (e *Engine) reach(tier int) int {
        n := 0
        for t, states := range e.counts {
                if t > tier {
                        continue
                }
                for s, c := range states {
                        if s.Live() {
                                n += c
                        }
                }
        }
        return n
}

func (e *Engine) updateQuiet(now time.Time) {
        for tier := 1; tier <= e.cfg.Policy.MaxTier; tier++ {
                if e.planning.Active || e.reach(tier) > 0 {
                        delete(e.quietSince, tier)
                } else if _, ok := e.quietSince[tier]; !ok {
                        e.quietSince[tier] = now
                }
        }
}

func (e *Engine) planningView() *PlanningView {
        p := e.planning
        if p.Epoch == 0 {
                return nil
        }
        age := e.now().Sub(p.UpdatedAt)
        return &PlanningView{
                Epoch: p.Epoch, Active: p.Active, Phase: p.Phase, ExpectedTasks: p.Expected, ETAMs: p.ETAMs,
                AgeMs: age.Milliseconds(), Stale: p.Active && age > e.cfg.StaleAfter,
        }
}

// idleResponse decides wait or exit for an agent with nothing assigned. Exit is
// only ever sent when nothing alive could still produce work for this tier.
func (e *Engine) idleResponse(tier int, agentSince time.Time) WaitResponse {
        now := e.now()
        view := e.planningView()
        wait := func(reason string) WaitResponse {
                return WaitResponse{Action: ActionWait, Reason: reason, Planning: view}
        }
        if e.planning.Active {
                if e.planning.Expected != nil && e.reach(tier) == 0 {
                        if expectedUpTo(e.planning.Expected, tier) == 0 {
                                return WaitResponse{Action: ActionExit, Reason: ReasonNoneExpect, Planning: view}
                        }
                }
                return wait(ReasonPlanning)
        }
        if !e.planning.LostAt.IsZero() && now.Sub(e.planning.LostAt) < e.cfg.PlanLostGrace {
                return wait(ReasonPlannerLost)
        }
        if e.reach(tier) > 0 {
                if e.onlyBlockedDrafts(tier) {
                        return wait(ReasonDeps)
                }
                return wait(ReasonTierBusy)
        }
        since, ok := e.quietSince[tier]
        if !ok {
                since = now
        }
        if agentSince.After(since) {
                since = agentSince
        }
        if now.Sub(since) >= e.cfg.ExitGrace {
                return WaitResponse{Action: ActionExit, Reason: ReasonPlanDone, Planning: view}
        }
        return wait(ReasonIdle)
}

func (e *Engine) onlyBlockedDrafts(tier int) bool {
        drafts := 0
        for t, states := range e.counts {
                if t <= tier {
                        drafts += states[core.Draft]
                }
        }
        return drafts > 0 && drafts == e.reach(tier)
}

// PlanBegin takes the planner lease BEFORE the planner reads its input, so no
// agent can be told to exit just before a plan lands.
func (e *Engine) PlanBegin(ctx context.Context, planner string, ttl time.Duration) (uint64, error) {
        return do(ctx, e, func() (uint64, error) {
                if e.planning.Active && e.now().Before(e.planning.Deadline) {
                        return 0, fmt.Errorf("%w: %s", ErrPlanBusy, e.planning.Planner)
                }
                e.reconcile() // Clears orphan drafts before the committed epoch can advance past them.
                for _, ent := range e.tasks {
                        if ent.task.State == core.Draft && ent.task.PlanEpoch > e.planning.Committed {
                                return 0, fmt.Errorf("%w: orphan drafts still present", ErrInvalid)
                        }
                }
                p := e.planning
                now := e.now()
                p.Epoch++
                p.Active, p.Planner, p.Phase, p.Expected, p.ETAMs = true, planner, "starting", nil, 0
                p.Deadline, p.UpdatedAt, p.LostAt = now.Add(ttl), now, time.Time{}
                if err := e.savePlanning(p); err != nil {
                        return 0, err
                }
                if v := log.V(vlog.LevelSteady); v.Enabled() {
                        v.Info("plan begun", "planner", planner, "epoch", p.Epoch, "ttl", ttl)
                }
                return p.Epoch, nil
        })
}

// PlanUpdate renews the lease and publishes hints to waiting agents.
func (e *Engine) PlanUpdate(ctx context.Context, planner string, epoch uint64, ttl time.Duration, phase string, expected map[int]int, etaMs int64) error {
        _, err := do(ctx, e, func() (struct{}, error) {
                if err := e.planFence(planner, epoch); err != nil {
                        return struct{}{}, err
                }
                p := e.planning
                now := e.now()
                if expected == nil {
                        expected = p.Expected // A phase-only update keeps the earlier promise.
                }
                // A hint is a promise: agents may already have left because of it. Found by
                // the Planner.tla model, whose NoExitBeforeWork fails without this rule.
                if p.Expected != nil {
                        for tier := 1; tier <= e.cfg.Policy.MaxTier; tier++ {
                                if expectedUpTo(p.Expected, tier) == 0 && expectedUpTo(expected, tier) > 0 {
                                        return struct{}{}, fmt.Errorf("%w: hints already promised no work up to tier %d", ErrInvalid, tier)
                                }
                        }
                }
                p.Phase, p.Expected, p.ETAMs, p.Deadline, p.UpdatedAt = phase, expected, etaMs, now.Add(ttl), now
                if v := log.V(vlog.LevelChanges); v.Enabled() {
                        v.Info("plan updated", "planner", planner, "epoch", epoch, "phase", phase, "expected", expected)
                }
                return struct{}{}, e.savePlanning(p)
        })
        return err
}

// PlanAdd creates a draft task inside the plan. It stays invisible to agents
// until PlanCommit.
func (e *Engine) PlanAdd(ctx context.Context, planner string, epoch uint64, s TaskSpec) (core.Task, error) {
        return do(ctx, e, func() (core.Task, error) {
                if err := e.planFence(planner, epoch); err != nil {
                        return core.Task{}, err
                }
                t, err := e.buildTask(s, epoch)
                if err != nil {
                        return t, err
                }
                if e.planning.Expected != nil && expectedUpTo(e.planning.Expected, t.Tier) == 0 {
                        return t, fmt.Errorf("%w: hints promised no work up to tier %d", ErrInvalid, t.Tier)
                }
                return e.create(t)
        })
}

// expectedUpTo counts hinted tasks that could reach an agent of this tier.
func expectedUpTo(expected map[int]int, tier int) int {
        n := 0
        for t, c := range expected {
                if t <= tier {
                        n += c
                }
        }
        return n
}

// PlanCommit makes the whole plan visible with a single write to the planning
// key. Tasks of this epoch become publishable at that moment, not one by one.
func (e *Engine) PlanCommit(ctx context.Context, planner string, epoch uint64) error {
        _, err := do(ctx, e, func() (struct{}, error) {
                if err := e.planFence(planner, epoch); err != nil {
                        return struct{}{}, err
                }
                if err := e.checkPlanGraph(epoch); err != nil {
                        return struct{}{}, err
                }
                p := e.planning
                p.Committed, p.Active, p.Planner, p.Phase, p.Expected, p.ETAMs = epoch, false, "", "", nil, 0
                p.UpdatedAt = e.now()
                if err := e.savePlanning(p); err != nil {
                        return struct{}{}, err
                }
                if v := log.V(vlog.LevelSteady); v.Enabled() {
                        v.Info("plan committed", "planner", planner, "epoch", epoch)
                }
                e.dirty = true
                return struct{}{}, nil
        })
        return err
}

func (e *Engine) planFence(planner string, epoch uint64) error {
        if !e.planning.Active || e.planning.Epoch != epoch || e.planning.Planner != planner {
                return fmt.Errorf("%w: epoch %d is not active for %s", ErrPlanLost, epoch, planner)
        }
        return nil
}

// checkPlanGraph rejects missing dependencies and cycles, which would otherwise
// leave tasks waiting forever.
func (e *Engine) checkPlanGraph(epoch uint64) error {
        const (
                unseen = iota
                visiting
                finished
        )
        mark := map[string]int{}
        var visit func(id string) error
        visit = func(id string) error {
                switch mark[id] {
                case visiting:
                        return fmt.Errorf("%w: dependency cycle through %s", ErrInvalid, id)
                case finished:
                        return nil
                }
                ent := e.tasks[id]
                if ent == nil {
                        return fmt.Errorf("%w: unknown dependency %s", ErrInvalid, id)
                }
                mark[id] = visiting
                for _, d := range ent.task.Deps {
                        if err := visit(d); err != nil {
                                return err
                        }
                }
                mark[id] = finished
                return nil
        }
        for id, ent := range e.tasks {
                if ent.task.PlanEpoch == epoch {
                        if err := visit(id); err != nil {
                                return err
                        }
                }
        }
        return nil
}

func (e *Engine) savePlanning(p store.Planning) error {
        rev, err := e.st.PutPlanning(p, e.planRev)
        if err != nil {
                if errors.Is(err, store.ErrConflict) {
                        if cur, curRev, gerr := e.st.GetPlanning(); gerr == nil {
                                e.planning, e.planRev = cur, curRev
                        }
                }
                return err
        }
        e.planning, e.planRev = p, rev
        e.dirty = true
        return nil
}

// Situation is a snapshot of the swarm. Every value carries its age, so a reader
// can tell fresh data from old.
type Situation struct {
        Agent        string                 `json:"agent,omitempty"`
        Counts       map[int]map[string]int `json:"counts"`
        Planning     *PlanningView          `json:"planning,omitempty"`
        Advice       string                 `json:"advice"`
        WaitingAgent map[int]int            `json:"waiting_agents"`
        OldestReady  int64                  `json:"oldest_ready_age_ms"`
        Grants       uint64                 `json:"grants"`
        AgeMs        int64                  `json:"age_ms"`
        Stale        bool                   `json:"stale"`
}

// Situation returns the snapshot for an agent of the given tier.
func (e *Engine) Situation(ctx context.Context, a Agent) (Situation, error) {
        return do(ctx, e, func() (Situation, error) {
                s := Situation{
                        Agent: a.ID, Counts: map[int]map[string]int{}, WaitingAgent: map[int]int{},
                        Planning: e.planningView(), Grants: e.grants.Load(),
                }
                for tier, states := range e.counts {
                        m := map[string]int{}
                        for st, n := range states {
                                if n > 0 {
                                        m[string(st)] = n
                                }
                        }
                        s.Counts[tier] = m
                }
                for tier, ws := range e.waiters {
                        s.WaitingAgent[tier] = len(ws)
                }
                now := e.now()
                for _, ent := range e.tasks {
                        if ent.task.State == core.Ready {
                                s.OldestReady = max(s.OldestReady, now.Sub(ent.task.ReadyAt).Milliseconds())
                        }
                }
                tier := a.Tier
                if tier == 0 {
                        tier = e.cfg.Policy.MaxTier
                }
                r := e.idleResponse(tier, time.Time{})
                s.Advice = r.Action
                if r.Reason != "" {
                        s.Advice += ": " + r.Reason
                }
                return s, nil
        })
}

// Package engine is the single writer. One goroutine owns all task state, checks
// each command with core.Apply, commits it with a compare-and-swap, and only then
// wakes whoever is waiting. Tasks are assigned here rather than pulled from a
// queue, so the dispatcher can choose by tier, tags and file conflicts.
package engine

import (
        "container/heap"
        "context"
        "crypto/rand"
        "encoding/hex"
        "encoding/json"
        "errors"
        "fmt"
        "regexp"
        "slices"
        "strings"
        "sync/atomic"
        "time"

        "github.com/Grano22/aiculator/internal/core"
        "github.com/Grano22/aiculator/internal/store"
        "github.com/Grano22/aiculator/internal/vlog"
        "github.com/Grano22/aiculator/pkg/observe"
)

var log = vlog.For("engine")

// Clock is swappable so that lease tests do not need to sleep.
type Clock interface{ Now() time.Time }

type realClock struct{}

func (realClock) Now() time.Time { return time.Now() }

// Agent is an authenticated agent identity.
type Agent struct {
        ID   string   `json:"id"`
        Tier int      `json:"tier"`
        Tags []string `json:"tags,omitempty"`
}

// StealRule lets idle agents of a higher tier take a lower tier's tasks once
// those have waited for After. Pairs with no rule never steal.
type StealRule struct {
        AgentTier, TaskTier int
        After               time.Duration
}

// Hooks hand tasks to the work layer. They must return quickly and be safe to
// call more than once, because recovery calls them again after a restart.
type Hooks struct {
        OnChecks  func(core.Task) // A review task needs machine checks.
        OnMerging func(core.Task) // A verified task needs merging.
}

// Config tunes the engine. Zero values take the defaults from DefaultConfig.
type Config struct {
        Policy        core.Policy
        Clock         Clock
        LeaseTTL      time.Duration
        ProgressTTL   time.Duration
        MaxHold       time.Duration // Longest wait_for_task hold.
        ExitGrace     time.Duration // Quiet time before an agent is told to exit.
        PlanLostGrace time.Duration // How long waiters see planner_lost.
        RestartGrace  time.Duration // No lease expires this soon after a restart.
        // DurableHeartbeats writes every heartbeat to the store, instead of only those that
        // change something or that a crash could otherwise cut short.
        DurableHeartbeats bool
        StaleAfter        time.Duration // Age at which a read value is flagged stale.
        Tick              time.Duration
        AgingUnit         time.Duration    // Waiting this long equals one priority point.
        Aging             []core.AgingStep // Extra boosts after a wait. A task's own steps replace these.
        Steal             []StealRule
        PresenceTTL       time.Duration
        Hooks             Hooks
}

// DefaultConfig holds production defaults.
func DefaultConfig() Config {
        return Config{
                Policy:        core.DefaultPolicy(),
                Clock:         realClock{},
                LeaseTTL:      2 * time.Minute,
                ProgressTTL:   10 * time.Minute,
                MaxHold:       40 * time.Second,
                ExitGrace:     30 * time.Second,
                PlanLostGrace: 30 * time.Second,
                RestartGrace:  15 * time.Second,
                StaleAfter:    30 * time.Second,
                Tick:          25 * time.Millisecond,
                AgingUnit:     time.Minute,
                Steal: []StealRule{
                        {AgentTier: 2, TaskTier: 1, After: 2 * time.Minute},
                        {AgentTier: 3, TaskTier: 2, After: 5 * time.Minute},
                },
                PresenceTTL: 30 * time.Second,
        }
}

// Errors returned by the engine, on top of those from core.
var (
        ErrNotFound = errors.New("task not found")
        ErrExists   = errors.New("task already exists")
        ErrInvalid  = errors.New("invalid request")
        ErrPlanBusy = errors.New("another planner holds the lease")
        ErrPlanLost = errors.New("planning lease lost")
        ErrStopped  = errors.New("engine stopped")
        ErrNoMatch  = errors.New("task is not available to this agent")
)

type entry struct {
        task     core.Task
        rev      uint64
        readySeq uint64
        // durableLease is the lease deadline as last written to the store. Heartbeats can run
        // ahead of it in memory; see commit.
        durableLease time.Time
}

type op struct {
        fn   func()
        done chan struct{}
}

// Engine is the single writer. All fields below ops are owned by run.
type Engine struct {
        cfg   Config
        st    *store.Store
        ops   chan op
        stop  chan struct{}
        dead  chan struct{}
        start time.Time

        presence chan Agent
        obs      *observe.Collector
        grants   atomic.Uint64

        tasks      map[string]*entry
        ready      map[int]*readyHeap
        boosts     boostHeap
        seq        uint64
        reviews    []string
        drafts     map[string]bool
        failed     map[string]bool
        leased     map[string]bool
        merging    map[string]bool
        active     map[string][]string // Task ID → touched paths, while being worked on.
        counts     map[int]map[core.State]int
        waiters    map[int][]*waiter
        dirty      bool
        planning   store.Planning
        planRev    uint64
        quietSince map[int]time.Time
        seen       map[string]seenAgent
        repairs    []Repair
}

// Repair records one record that had to be fixed at startup.
type Repair struct {
        TaskID string    `json:"task_id"`
        Did    []string  `json:"did"`
        At     time.Time `json:"at"`
}

// seenAgent tracks when an agent started its current stretch of waiting, so that
// one arriving at a long-idle swarm still gets the full grace before an exit.
type seenAgent struct {
        first, last time.Time
}

// New starts the engine: it loads all tasks, rebuilds the indexes, and resumes
// any work that a crash interrupted.
func New(ctx context.Context, st *store.Store, cfg Config) (*Engine, error) {
        d := DefaultConfig()
        if cfg.Policy.MaxTier == 0 {
                cfg.Policy = d.Policy
        }
        if cfg.Clock == nil {
                cfg.Clock = d.Clock
        }
        setDur := func(p *time.Duration, v time.Duration) {
                if *p == 0 {
                        *p = v
                }
        }
        setDur(&cfg.LeaseTTL, d.LeaseTTL)
        setDur(&cfg.ProgressTTL, d.ProgressTTL)
        setDur(&cfg.MaxHold, d.MaxHold)
        setDur(&cfg.ExitGrace, d.ExitGrace)
        setDur(&cfg.PlanLostGrace, d.PlanLostGrace)
        setDur(&cfg.RestartGrace, d.RestartGrace)
        setDur(&cfg.StaleAfter, d.StaleAfter)
        setDur(&cfg.Tick, d.Tick)
        setDur(&cfg.AgingUnit, d.AgingUnit)
        setDur(&cfg.PresenceTTL, d.PresenceTTL)
        if cfg.Steal == nil {
                cfg.Steal = d.Steal
        }

        e := &Engine{
                cfg: cfg, st: st,
                ops:        make(chan op, 1024),
                stop:       make(chan struct{}),
                dead:       make(chan struct{}),
                start:      cfg.Clock.Now(),
                presence:   make(chan Agent, 256),
                obs:        observe.New(time.Now()),
                tasks:      map[string]*entry{},
                ready:      map[int]*readyHeap{},
                drafts:     map[string]bool{},
                failed:     map[string]bool{},
                leased:     map[string]bool{},
                merging:    map[string]bool{},
                active:     map[string][]string{},
                counts:     map[int]map[core.State]int{},
                waiters:    map[int][]*waiter{},
                quietSince: map[int]time.Time{},
                seen:       map[string]seenAgent{},
        }
        stored, unreadable, err := st.LoadTasks(ctx)
        if err != nil {
                return nil, fmt.Errorf("load tasks: %w", err)
        }
        stored = append(stored, e.recoverUnreadable(unreadable)...)
        for _, s := range stored {
                s = e.repairOnLoad(s)
                e.index(core.Task{}, s.Task, s.Rev)
                // Hooks are not fired from index during load; resume them here.
                e.resume(s.Task)
        }
        if e.planning, e.planRev, err = st.GetPlanning(); err != nil {
                return nil, fmt.Errorf("load planning: %w", err)
        }
        e.dirty = true
        log.V(vlog.LevelDefault).Info("engine started", "tasks", len(stored), "planning_epoch", e.planning.Epoch)
        go e.run()
        go e.presenceLoop()
        return e, nil
}

// repairOnLoad fixes a record that breaks the invariants, keeping the original in quarantine.
// Without this, one bad record would make every agent's work stall or go wrong in a way that
// is hard to trace back.
func (e *Engine) repairOnLoad(s store.Stored) store.Stored {
        if core.Validate(s.Task) == nil && core.ValidateAttrs(s.Task) == nil {
                return s
        }
        fixed, did := core.Repair(s.Task, e.now())
        raw, _ := json.Marshal(s.Task)
        if err := e.st.Quarantine(s.Task.ID, s.Rev, raw, strings.Join(did, "; ")); err != nil {
                log.Error("could not keep the original of a damaged task; leaving it as it is", "task", s.Task.ID, "err", err)
                return s
        }
        rev, err := e.st.RawPut(fixed, s.Rev)
        if err != nil {
                log.Error("could not repair a damaged task", "task", s.Task.ID, "err", err)
                return s
        }
        log.V(vlog.LevelDefault).Warn("repaired a damaged task", "task", s.Task.ID, "did", did)
        e.repairs = append(e.repairs, Repair{TaskID: s.Task.ID, Did: did, At: e.now()})
        return store.Stored{Task: fixed, Rev: rev}
}

// recoverUnreadable keeps each record that cannot be decoded, and puts a parked stand-in in
// its place, so the swarm starts and a person can see what happened.
func (e *Engine) recoverUnreadable(bad []store.Unreadable) []store.Stored {
        var out []store.Stored
        for _, b := range bad {
                why := "unreadable record: " + b.Err.Error()
                if err := e.st.Quarantine(b.ID, b.Rev, b.Raw, why); err != nil {
                        log.Error("could not keep an unreadable task; it is left out until restart", "task", b.ID, "err", err)
                        continue
                }
                now := e.now()
                t := core.Task{ID: b.ID, Title: "Unreadable record, kept in quarantine", Tier: 1, State: core.Parked,
                        Reason: "unreadable_record", CreatedAt: now, UpdatedAt: now}
                rev, err := e.st.RawPut(t, b.Rev)
                if err != nil {
                        log.Error("could not replace an unreadable task", "task", b.ID, "err", err)
                        continue
                }
                log.Error("a task could not be read; the original is kept, and the task is parked", "task", b.ID, "err", b.Err)
                e.repairs = append(e.repairs, Repair{TaskID: b.ID, Did: []string{why, "parked, with the original in quarantine"}, At: now})
                out = append(out, store.Stored{Task: t, Rev: rev})
        }
        return out
}

// Repairs lists what was fixed when the engine started.
func (e *Engine) Repairs(ctx context.Context) ([]Repair, error) {
        return do(ctx, e, func() ([]Repair, error) { return slices.Clone(e.repairs), nil })
}

func (e *Engine) resume(t core.Task) {
        switch {
        case t.State == core.Review && len(t.Checks) > 0 && !t.ChecksRun && e.cfg.Hooks.OnChecks != nil:
                e.cfg.Hooks.OnChecks(t)
        case t.State == core.Merging && e.cfg.Hooks.OnMerging != nil:
                e.cfg.Hooks.OnMerging(t)
        }
}

// Close stops the writer goroutine and waits for it.
func (e *Engine) Close() {
        select {
        case <-e.stop:
        default:
                close(e.stop)
        }
        <-e.dead
}

func (e *Engine) run() {
        defer close(e.dead)
        tick := time.NewTicker(e.cfg.Tick)
        defer tick.Stop()
        e.pump(true)
        for {
                select {
                case o := <-e.ops:
                        o.fn()
                        e.pump(false)
                        close(o.done)
                case <-tick.C:
                        e.pump(true)
                case <-e.stop:
                        for _, ws := range e.waiters {
                                for _, w := range ws {
                                        close(w.ch)
                                }
                        }
                        return
                }
        }
}

// do runs fn on the writer goroutine and waits for it.
func do[T any](ctx context.Context, e *Engine, fn func() (T, error)) (T, error) {
        var (
                res T
                err error
        )
        o := op{fn: func() { res, err = fn() }, done: make(chan struct{})}
        select {
        case e.ops <- o:
        case <-e.stop:
                return res, ErrStopped
        case <-ctx.Done():
                return res, ctx.Err()
        }
        select {
        case <-o.done:
                return res, err
        case <-e.dead:
                return res, ErrStopped
        }
}

func (e *Engine) now() time.Time { return e.cfg.Clock.Now() }

// index moves a task between the in-memory indexes. Everything it maintains can
// be rebuilt from KV, which is how recovery works.
func (e *Engine) index(old, t core.Task, rev uint64) {
        ent := e.tasks[t.ID]
        if ent == nil {
                ent = &entry{}
                e.tasks[t.ID] = ent
        }
        if old.ID != "" && e.counts[old.Tier] != nil {
                e.counts[old.Tier][old.State]--
        }
        if rev != ent.rev {
                ent.durableLease = t.LeaseDeadline
        }
        ent.task, ent.rev = t, rev
        if e.counts[t.Tier] == nil {
                e.counts[t.Tier] = map[core.State]int{}
        }
        e.counts[t.Tier][t.State]++

        setIf := func(m map[string]bool, on bool) {
                if on {
                        m[t.ID] = true
                } else {
                        delete(m, t.ID)
                }
        }
        setIf(e.drafts, t.State == core.Draft)
        setIf(e.failed, t.State == core.Failed)
        setIf(e.merging, t.State == core.Merging)
        setIf(e.leased, t.Owner != "")

        // A new priority needs a new heap position too. The old entry is skipped later.
        if t.State == core.Ready && (old.State != core.Ready || old.ID == "" ||
                old.Priority != t.Priority || !slices.Equal(old.Aging, t.Aging)) {
                e.enqueue(ent)
        }
        if t.State == core.Review && needsReviewer(t) && !slices.Contains(e.reviews, t.ID) {
                e.reviews = append(e.reviews, t.ID)
        }
        switch t.State {
        case core.Claimed, core.Running, core.Review, core.Merging:
                if len(t.Touches) > 0 {
                        e.active[t.ID] = t.Touches
                }
        default:
                delete(e.active, t.ID)
        }
        // Only a change that could make work available is worth waking waiters for. A heartbeat
        // is by far the most common command, and is not one of those.
        if old.ID == "" || old.State != t.State || old.Owner != t.Owner || old.Tier != t.Tier || old.Priority != t.Priority {
                e.dirty = true
        }
}

// agingOf returns the steps that apply to a task.
func (e *Engine) agingOf(t core.Task) []core.AgingStep {
        if t.Aging != nil {
                return t.Aging
        }
        return e.cfg.Aging
}

// enqueue gives a ready task its place in the heap, and schedules its next boost. Every
// value comes from the task and the clock, so restarting rebuilds exactly the same queue.
func (e *Engine) enqueue(ent *entry) {
        t := ent.task
        boost, next := core.AgingBoost(e.agingOf(t), e.now().Sub(t.ReadyAt))
        e.seq++
        ent.readySeq = e.seq
        e.heap(t.Tier).pushItem(readyItem{
                id:  t.ID,
                key: int64(t.Priority+boost)*int64(e.cfg.AgingUnit) - t.ReadyAt.UnixNano(),
                seq: e.seq,
        })
        if next > 0 {
                heap.Push(&e.boosts, boostItem{at: e.now().Add(next), id: t.ID, seq: e.seq})
        }
}

// applyBoosts moves tasks that have just reached an aging step. The cost is per boost,
// and nothing is re-sorted, so a claim stays as fast with aging on as with it off.
func (e *Engine) applyBoosts() {
        now := e.now()
        for len(e.boosts) > 0 && !e.boosts[0].at.After(now) {
                it := heap.Pop(&e.boosts).(boostItem)
                ent := e.tasks[it.id]
                if ent == nil || ent.task.State != core.Ready || ent.readySeq != it.seq {
                        continue // It was claimed or moved since, so this boost no longer applies.
                }
                e.enqueue(ent)
                if v := log.V(vlog.LevelChanges); v.Enabled() {
                        v.Info("priority raised by waiting", "task", it.id, "waited", now.Sub(ent.task.ReadyAt))
                }
                e.dirty = true
        }
}

// PriorityInfo says how a task's place in the queue is worked out right now.
type PriorityInfo struct {
        Base      int   `json:"base"`
        Boost     int   `json:"boost"`
        Effective int   `json:"effective"`
        WaitedMs  int64 `json:"waited_ms"`
        NextInMs  int64 `json:"next_in_ms,omitempty"`
        // AgingPoints is the steady rise on top, one point per aging unit.
        AgingPoints int `json:"aging_points"`
}

// Priority explains a task's current priority.
func (e *Engine) Priority(ctx context.Context, id string) (PriorityInfo, error) {
        return do(ctx, e, func() (PriorityInfo, error) {
                ent := e.tasks[id]
                if ent == nil {
                        return PriorityInfo{}, fmt.Errorf("%w: %s", ErrNotFound, id)
                }
                t := ent.task
                p := PriorityInfo{Base: t.Priority, Effective: t.Priority}
                if t.State != core.Ready {
                        return p, nil
                }
                waited := e.now().Sub(t.ReadyAt)
                boost, next := core.AgingBoost(e.agingOf(t), waited)
                p.Boost, p.Effective = boost, t.Priority+boost
                p.WaitedMs, p.NextInMs = waited.Milliseconds(), next.Milliseconds()
                p.AgingPoints = int(waited / e.cfg.AgingUnit)
                return p, nil
        })
}

func needsReviewer(t core.Task) bool {
        if t.State != core.Review || t.Owner != "" {
                return false
        }
        if len(t.Checks) == 0 {
                return true
        }
        return t.RequireReview && t.ChecksRun && t.ChecksPassed
}

func (e *Engine) heap(tier int) *readyHeap {
        h := e.ready[tier]
        if h == nil {
                h = &readyHeap{}
                e.ready[tier] = h
        }
        return h
}

// commit is the only path to a state change: legality check, compare-and-swap,
// then memory. If the swap loses, memory is reloaded and the command is rejected.
func (e *Engine) commit(id string, c core.Cmd) (core.Task, error) {
        ent := e.tasks[id]
        if ent == nil {
                return core.Task{}, fmt.Errorf("%w: %s", ErrNotFound, id)
        }
        n, err := core.Apply(ent.task, c, e.now(), e.cfg.Policy)
        if err != nil {
                if v := log.V(vlog.LevelChanges); v.Enabled() {
                        v.Info("command rejected", "task", id, "kind", c.Kind, "actor", c.Actor, "state", ent.task.State, "err", err)
                }
                return ent.task, err
        }
        if e.heartbeatInMemory(ent, n, c) {
                old := ent.task
                e.index(old, n, ent.rev)
                e.obs.Count(observe.SeriesCoalesced, time.Now(), 1)
                return n, nil
        }
        began := time.Now()
        rev, err := e.st.UpdateTask(n, ent.rev)
        if err != nil {
                if errors.Is(err, store.ErrConflict) {
                        log.V(vlog.LevelDefault).Warn("stale revision: another writer changed this task", "task", id, "rev", ent.rev)
                        e.reload(id)
                } else {
                        log.Error("commit failed", "task", id, "kind", c.Kind, "err", err)
                }
                return ent.task, err
        }
        took := time.Since(began)
        e.obs.Observe(observe.LatencyCommit, took)
        if v := log.V(vlog.LevelChanges); v.Enabled() {
                v.Info("commit", "task", id, "kind", c.Kind, "actor", c.Actor, "took", took)
        }
        if v := log.V(vlog.LevelTrace); v.Enabled() {
                v.Info("compare-and-swap", "task", id, "from_rev", ent.rev, "to_rev", rev, "lease", n.LeaseEpoch)
        }
        old := ent.task
        e.index(old, n, rev)
        e.record(old, n, c)
        e.fireHooks(old, n)
        return n, nil
}

// heartbeatInMemory decides whether a heartbeat can skip the store. Heartbeats are by far
// the most common command, and most only push a deadline forward. Each one written is a
// disk write and a revision that every follower reads.
//
// It is safe to keep one in memory when the stored deadline is still more than half a
// lease away. Fencing depends on the lease number, which a heartbeat never changes, so a
// stale stored deadline cannot let a second agent in while the first still holds the task.
// After a crash or a takeover, the stored deadline is at least half a lease from when the
// last heartbeat was written, and no lease expires within RestartGrace of a start anyway,
// which leaves the agent time to send the next one. A heartbeat that changes anything else,
// such as the first one moving Claimed to Running, is always written.
func (e *Engine) heartbeatInMemory(ent *entry, n core.Task, c core.Cmd) bool {
        if c.Kind != core.CmdHeartbeat || n.State != ent.task.State || c.LeaseTTL <= 0 || e.cfg.DurableHeartbeats {
                return false
        }
        return ent.durableLease.Sub(e.now()) > c.LeaseTTL/2
}

// record feeds the dashboards. Rates use real time. Task ages use the engine's clock,
// which is what their timestamps came from.
func (e *Engine) record(old, n core.Task, c core.Cmd) {
        wall := time.Now()
        e.obs.Count(observe.SeriesCommits, wall, 1)
        if !core.IsSystem(c.Actor) && c.Actor != "" && (c.Cost > 0 || c.Tokens > 0) {
                e.obs.Usage(c.Actor, max(c.Tokens, 0), max(c.Cost, 0))
        }
        if old.State == n.State {
                return
        }
        e.obs.Transition(string(old.State), string(n.State))
        if v := log.V(vlog.LevelSteady); v.Enabled() {
                v.Info("task transition", "task", n.ID, "from", old.State, "to", n.State, "tier", n.Tier, "attempt", n.Attempt, "actor", c.Actor, "reason", n.Reason)
        }
        now := e.now()
        switch n.State {
        case core.Claimed:
                e.obs.Count(observe.SeriesGrants, wall, 1)
                e.obs.Observe(observe.LatencyQueue, now.Sub(old.ReadyAt))
        case core.Done:
                e.obs.Count(observe.SeriesDone, wall, 1)
                e.obs.Observe(observe.LatencyCycle, now.Sub(n.CreatedAt))
                if n.Submitter != "" {
                        e.obs.Outcome(n.Submitter, true)
                }
        case core.Failed:
                e.obs.Count(observe.SeriesFailed, wall, 1)
                who := old.Owner
                if who == "" {
                        who = n.Submitter
                }
                if who != "" {
                        e.obs.Outcome(who, false)
                }
                if n.Reason == "no_progress" {
                        e.obs.Count(observe.SeriesZombies, wall, 1)
                }
        }
}

// Collector exposes the metrics, so the API can add its own request timings.
func (e *Engine) Collector() *observe.Collector { return e.obs }

func (e *Engine) reload(id string) {
        t, rev, err := e.st.GetTask(id)
        if err == nil {
                e.index(e.tasks[id].task, t, rev)
        }
}

func (e *Engine) fireHooks(old, n core.Task) {
        if n.State == core.Review && old.State != core.Review && len(n.Checks) > 0 && e.cfg.Hooks.OnChecks != nil {
                e.cfg.Hooks.OnChecks(n)
        }
        if n.State == core.Merging && old.State != core.Merging && e.cfg.Hooks.OnMerging != nil {
                e.cfg.Hooks.OnMerging(n)
        }
}

// pump runs after every command and on every tick, until nothing is left to do.
func (e *Engine) pump(tick bool) {
        if tick {
                e.sweep()
                e.dirty = true
        }
        changed := e.dirty
        for range 64 { // Bounded, so a bug cannot hang the writer.
                if !e.dirty {
                        break
                }
                e.dirty = false
                e.reconcile()
                e.matchWaiters()
        }
        if changed {
                e.settleWaiters()
        }
}

// sweep enforces deadlines. It runs on the writer's clock, so tests can drive it.
func (e *Engine) sweep() {
        e.applyBoosts()
        now := e.now()
        if e.planning.Active && now.After(e.planning.Deadline) {
                log.V(vlog.LevelDefault).Warn("planner lease expired", "planner", e.planning.Planner, "epoch", e.planning.Epoch)
                p := e.planning
                p.Active, p.Planner, p.Phase, p.Expected, p.ETAMs = false, "", "", nil, 0
                p.Epoch++ // A planner returning from the dead now holds an old epoch.
                p.LostAt, p.UpdatedAt = now, now
                e.savePlanning(p)
        }
        if now.Sub(e.start) < e.cfg.RestartGrace {
                // Agents could not reach us while we were down, so give them time to
                // come back before their leases count against them.
                return
        }
        for id := range e.leased {
                t := e.tasks[id].task
                switch {
                case now.After(t.LeaseDeadline):
                        _, _ = e.commit(id, core.Cmd{Kind: core.CmdExpire, Actor: "system:lease", Note: "lease_expired"})
                case t.State == core.Running && !t.ProgressDeadline.IsZero() && now.After(t.ProgressDeadline):
                        // Heartbeats are alive but nothing has changed: a zombie.
                        _, _ = e.commit(id, core.Cmd{Kind: core.CmdExpire, Actor: "system:lease", Note: "no_progress"})
                }
        }
}

// reconcile drives every automatic transition. Each is computed from durable
// state, so a crash between two steps is simply finished on restart.
func (e *Engine) reconcile() {
        for id := range e.failed {
                _, _ = e.commit(id, core.Cmd{Kind: core.CmdRecover, Actor: "system:recover"})
        }
        for id := range e.drafts {
                t := e.tasks[id].task
                switch e.draftFate(t) {
                case fatePublish:
                        _, _ = e.commit(id, core.Cmd{Kind: core.CmdPublish, Actor: "system:plan"})
                case fateOrphan:
                        _, _ = e.commit(id, core.Cmd{Kind: core.CmdCancel, Actor: "system:plan", Note: "plan_abandoned"})
                case fateDepCanceled:
                        _, _ = e.commit(id, core.Cmd{Kind: core.CmdCancel, Actor: "system:plan", Note: "dependency_canceled"})
                }
        }
        if e.cfg.Hooks.OnMerging == nil {
                for id := range e.merging {
                        _, _ = e.commit(id, core.Cmd{Kind: core.CmdMerged, Actor: "system:merge"})
                }
        }
}

type draftFate int

const (
        fateWait draftFate = iota
        fatePublish
        fateOrphan
        fateDepCanceled
)

func (e *Engine) draftFate(t core.Task) draftFate {
        if t.PlanEpoch != 0 && t.PlanEpoch > e.planning.Committed {
                if !e.planning.Active || t.PlanEpoch != e.planning.Epoch {
                        return fateOrphan
                }
                return fateWait
        }
        for _, d := range t.Deps {
                dep := e.tasks[d]
                if dep == nil {
                        return fateWait
                }
                switch dep.task.State {
                case core.Done:
                case core.Canceled:
                        return fateDepCanceled
                default:
                        return fateWait
                }
        }
        return fatePublish
}

// TaskSpec is the input for creating a task.
type TaskSpec struct {
        ID            string            `json:"id,omitempty"`
        Title         string            `json:"title"`
        Spec          string            `json:"spec,omitempty"`
        Tier          int               `json:"tier,omitempty"`
        Tags          []string          `json:"tags,omitempty"`
        Priority      int               `json:"priority,omitempty"`
        Labels        map[string]string `json:"labels,omitempty"`
        Aging         []core.AgingStep  `json:"aging,omitempty"`
        Deps          []string          `json:"deps,omitempty"`
        Touches       []string          `json:"touches,omitempty"`
        Checks        []string          `json:"checks,omitempty"`
        RequireReview bool              `json:"require_review,omitempty"`
        AllowEmpty    bool              `json:"allow_empty,omitempty"`
        Budget        int64             `json:"budget,omitempty"`
}

var idRE = regexp.MustCompile(`^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,128}$`)

func newID() string {
        var b [6]byte
        _, _ = rand.Read(b[:])
        return "t-" + hex.EncodeToString(b[:])
}

func (e *Engine) buildTask(s TaskSpec, epoch uint64) (core.Task, error) {
        if s.ID == "" {
                s.ID = newID()
        }
        if !idRE.MatchString(s.ID) {
                return core.Task{}, fmt.Errorf("%w: task id %q", ErrInvalid, s.ID)
        }
        if strings.TrimSpace(s.Title) == "" {
                return core.Task{}, fmt.Errorf("%w: task needs a title", ErrInvalid)
        }
        if s.Tier == 0 {
                s.Tier = 1
        }
        if s.Tier < 1 || s.Tier > e.cfg.Policy.MaxTier {
                return core.Task{}, fmt.Errorf("%w: tier %d", ErrInvalid, s.Tier)
        }
        now := e.now()
        t := core.Task{
                ID: s.ID, Title: s.Title, Spec: s.Spec, Tier: s.Tier, Tags: s.Tags, Priority: s.Priority,
                Labels: s.Labels, Aging: s.Aging,
                Deps: s.Deps, Touches: s.Touches, Checks: s.Checks, RequireReview: s.RequireReview,
                AllowEmpty: s.AllowEmpty, Budget: s.Budget, PlanEpoch: epoch, State: core.Draft,
                CreatedAt: now, UpdatedAt: now,
        }
        if err := core.ValidateAttrs(t); err != nil {
                return core.Task{}, fmt.Errorf("%w: %v", ErrInvalid, err)
        }
        return t, nil
}

func (e *Engine) create(t core.Task) (core.Task, error) {
        if e.tasks[t.ID] != nil {
                return core.Task{}, fmt.Errorf("%w: %s", ErrExists, t.ID)
        }
        rev, err := e.st.CreateTask(t)
        if errors.Is(err, store.ErrConflict) {
                return core.Task{}, fmt.Errorf("%w: %s", ErrExists, t.ID)
        }
        if err != nil {
                return core.Task{}, err
        }
        e.index(core.Task{}, t, rev)
        e.obs.Count(observe.SeriesCommits, time.Now(), 1)
        e.obs.Transition("new", string(t.State))
        if v := log.V(vlog.LevelSteady); v.Enabled() {
                v.Info("task created", "task", t.ID, "title", t.Title, "tier", t.Tier, "plan_epoch", t.PlanEpoch)
        }
        return t, nil
}

// AddTask creates a task outside any plan. Its dependencies must already exist,
// which also makes cycles impossible on this path.
func (e *Engine) AddTask(ctx context.Context, s TaskSpec) (core.Task, error) {
        return do(ctx, e, func() (core.Task, error) {
                t, err := e.buildTask(s, 0)
                if err != nil {
                        return t, err
                }
                for _, d := range t.Deps {
                        if e.tasks[d] == nil {
                                return t, fmt.Errorf("%w: unknown dependency %s", ErrInvalid, d)
                        }
                }
                return e.create(t)
        })
}

// AddResult is the outcome for one task of a batch.
type AddResult struct {
        Task core.Task
        Err  error
}

// AddMany creates a batch in one writer turn, so that it costs one wake-up for waiting
// agents and not one each. Keep batches small enough not to hold up claims.
func (e *Engine) AddMany(ctx context.Context, specs []TaskSpec) ([]AddResult, error) {
        return do(ctx, e, func() ([]AddResult, error) {
                out := make([]AddResult, len(specs))
                for i, s := range specs {
                        t, err := e.buildTask(s, 0)
                        if err == nil {
                                for _, d := range t.Deps {
                                        if e.tasks[d] == nil {
                                                err = fmt.Errorf("%w: unknown dependency %s", ErrInvalid, d)
                                                break
                                        }
                                }
                        }
                        if err == nil {
                                t, err = e.create(t)
                        }
                        out[i] = AddResult{t, err}
                }
                return out, nil
        })
}

// Existing returns which of these tasks exist, in one writer turn.
func (e *Engine) Existing(ctx context.Context, ids []string) (map[string]core.Task, error) {
        return do(ctx, e, func() (map[string]core.Task, error) {
                out := make(map[string]core.Task, len(ids))
                for _, id := range ids {
                        if ent := e.tasks[id]; ent != nil {
                                out[id] = ent.task.Clone()
                        }
                }
                return out, nil
        })
}

// Get returns one task.
func (e *Engine) Get(ctx context.Context, id string) (core.Task, error) {
        return do(ctx, e, func() (core.Task, error) {
                if ent := e.tasks[id]; ent != nil {
                        return ent.task.Clone(), nil
                }
                return core.Task{}, fmt.Errorf("%w: %s", ErrNotFound, id)
        })
}

// List returns every task, sorted by ID.
func (e *Engine) List(ctx context.Context) ([]core.Task, error) {
        return do(ctx, e, func() ([]core.Task, error) {
                out := make([]core.Task, 0, len(e.tasks))
                for _, ent := range e.tasks {
                        out = append(out, ent.task.Clone())
                }
                slices.SortFunc(out, func(a, b core.Task) int { return strings.Compare(a.ID, b.ID) })
                return out, nil
        })
}

// Heartbeat extends a lease. It proves the agent is alive, not that it is working.
func (e *Engine) Heartbeat(ctx context.Context, a Agent, id string, lease uint64) (core.Task, error) {
        e.touch(a)
        return do(ctx, e, func() (core.Task, error) {
                return e.commit(id, core.Cmd{Kind: core.CmdHeartbeat, Actor: a.ID, Lease: lease, LeaseTTL: e.cfg.LeaseTTL})
        })
}

// Progress records evidence of work. Only changed evidence resets the zombie timer.
func (e *Engine) Progress(ctx context.Context, a Agent, id string, lease uint64, evidence, ref, note string, u core.Usage) (core.Task, error) {
        e.touch(a)
        return do(ctx, e, func() (core.Task, error) {
                return e.commit(id, core.Cmd{
                        Kind: core.CmdProgress, Actor: a.ID, Lease: lease, LeaseTTL: e.cfg.LeaseTTL,
                        ProgressTTL: e.cfg.ProgressTTL, Evidence: evidence, Ref: ref, Note: note, Cost: u.Cost, Tokens: u.Tokens,
                })
        })
}

// Submit moves the task to review. It is a claim of completion, nothing more.
func (e *Engine) Submit(ctx context.Context, a Agent, id string, lease uint64, evidence, ref, note string, u core.Usage) (core.Task, error) {
        e.touch(a)
        return do(ctx, e, func() (core.Task, error) {
                return e.commit(id, core.Cmd{Kind: core.CmdSubmit, Actor: a.ID, Lease: lease, Evidence: evidence, Ref: ref, Note: note, Cost: u.Cost, Tokens: u.Tokens})
        })
}

// Fail reports that the agent gave up on the task.
func (e *Engine) Fail(ctx context.Context, a Agent, id string, lease uint64, note string, u core.Usage) (core.Task, error) {
        e.touch(a)
        return do(ctx, e, func() (core.Task, error) {
                return e.commit(id, core.Cmd{Kind: core.CmdFail, Actor: a.ID, Lease: lease, Note: note, Cost: u.Cost, Tokens: u.Tokens})
        })
}

// Release hands a task back with no penalty, because the harness was at fault.
func (e *Engine) Release(ctx context.Context, a Agent, id string, lease uint64, note string) (core.Task, error) {
        return do(ctx, e, func() (core.Task, error) {
                return e.commit(id, core.Cmd{Kind: core.CmdRelease, Actor: a.ID, Lease: lease, Note: note})
        })
}

// Verdict records an independent review.
func (e *Engine) Verdict(ctx context.Context, a Agent, id string, lease uint64, pass bool, note string) (core.Task, error) {
        e.touch(a)
        return do(ctx, e, func() (core.Task, error) {
                return e.commit(id, core.Cmd{Kind: core.CmdVerdict, Actor: a.ID, Lease: lease, Pass: pass, Note: note})
        })
}

// ReportChecks records a machine check result. Only the work layer calls it.
func (e *Engine) ReportChecks(ctx context.Context, id string, pass bool, note string) (core.Task, error) {
        return do(ctx, e, func() (core.Task, error) {
                return e.commit(id, core.Cmd{Kind: core.CmdChecks, Actor: "system:checks", Pass: pass, Note: note})
        })
}

// ReportMerged marks a task done. Only the merge queue calls it.
func (e *Engine) ReportMerged(ctx context.Context, id, ref string) (core.Task, error) {
        return do(ctx, e, func() (core.Task, error) {
                return e.commit(id, core.Cmd{Kind: core.CmdMerged, Actor: "system:merge", Ref: ref})
        })
}

// SystemFail fails a task on the swarm's own authority, for example on a merge conflict.
func (e *Engine) SystemFail(ctx context.Context, id, note string) (core.Task, error) {
        return do(ctx, e, func() (core.Task, error) {
                return e.commit(id, core.Cmd{Kind: core.CmdFail, Actor: "system:work", Note: note})
        })
}

// Unpark returns a parked task to the queue, optionally raising its budget.
func (e *Engine) Unpark(ctx context.Context, id string, addBudget int64, note string) (core.Task, error) {
        return do(ctx, e, func() (core.Task, error) {
                return e.commit(id, core.Cmd{Kind: core.CmdUnpark, Actor: "system:operator", AddBudget: addBudget, Note: note})
        })
}

// Amend changes what a task says, without touching its progress. An operator or a
// connector calls it, never an agent. A task that is being worked on keeps its lease.
func (e *Engine) Amend(ctx context.Context, id, actor string, a core.Amendment) (core.Task, error) {
        if !core.IsSystem(actor) {
                return core.Task{}, fmt.Errorf("%w: actor %q", core.ErrForbidden, actor)
        }
        return do(ctx, e, func() (core.Task, error) {
                return e.commit(id, core.Cmd{Kind: core.CmdAmend, Actor: actor, Amend: &a})
        })
}

// Cancel stops a task.
func (e *Engine) Cancel(ctx context.Context, id, note string) (core.Task, error) {
        return do(ctx, e, func() (core.Task, error) {
                return e.commit(id, core.Cmd{Kind: core.CmdCancel, Actor: "system:operator", Note: note})
        })
}

func (e *Engine) touch(a Agent) {
        e.obs.Seen(a.ID, a.Tier, time.Now())
        select {
        case e.presence <- a:
        default: // Presence is informational; never block work on it.
        }
}

func (e *Engine) presenceLoop() {
        last := map[string]time.Time{}
        for {
                select {
                case <-e.stop:
                        return
                case a := <-e.presence:
                        now := time.Now()
                        if now.Sub(last[a.ID]) < e.cfg.PresenceTTL/2 {
                                continue
                        }
                        last[a.ID] = now
                        if err := e.st.TouchPresence(a.ID, []byte(fmt.Sprintf("tier=%d", a.Tier)), e.cfg.PresenceTTL); err != nil {
                                log.V(vlog.LevelDebug).Warn("presence update failed", "agent", a.ID, "err", err)
                        }
                }
        }
}

// GrantCount returns how many grants have been committed since start.
func (e *Engine) GrantCount() uint64 { return e.grants.Load() }

// Sync waits until the writer has processed everything queued before the call.
func (e *Engine) Sync(ctx context.Context) error {
        _, err := do(ctx, e, func() (struct{}, error) { return struct{}{}, nil })
        return err
}

package engine

import (
        "cmp"
        "context"
        "slices"
        "strings"
        "time"

        "github.com/Grano22/aiculator/internal/core"
        "github.com/Grano22/aiculator/pkg/observe"
)

// maxLiveTasks caps the task list, so a huge queue cannot make every dashboard refresh
// heavy. Tasks with problems sort first, so they are what stays in view.
const maxLiveTasks = 200

// atRiskFraction marks a lease as at risk when less than this share of it is left.
const atRiskFraction = 4

func remaining(deadline, now time.Time) *int64 {
        if deadline.IsZero() {
                return nil
        }
        ms := deadline.Sub(now).Milliseconds()
        return &ms
}

func (e *Engine) liveTask(t core.Task, now time.Time) observe.TaskLive {
        l := observe.TaskLive{
                ID: t.ID, Title: t.Title, State: string(t.State), Tier: t.Tier, Owner: t.Owner, Attempt: t.Attempt,
                Failures: t.Failures, AgeMs: now.Sub(t.UpdatedAt).Milliseconds(), Reason: t.Reason,
                Tokens: t.Tokens, Spent: t.Spent, Budget: t.Budget, Health: observe.HealthQueued,
        }
        if t.Owner == "" {
                return l
        }
        l.LeaseRemainingMs = remaining(t.LeaseDeadline, now)
        if t.State == core.Running || t.State == core.Claimed {
                l.ProgressRemaining = remaining(t.ProgressDeadline, now)
        }
        l.Health = observe.HealthOK
        check := func(left *int64, ttl time.Duration) {
                switch {
                case left == nil:
                case *left <= 0:
                        l.Health = observe.HealthExpired
                case *left < ttl.Milliseconds()/atRiskFraction && l.Health == observe.HealthOK:
                        l.Health = observe.HealthAtRisk
                }
        }
        check(l.LeaseRemainingMs, e.cfg.LeaseTTL)
        check(l.ProgressRemaining, e.cfg.ProgressTTL)
        return l
}

func healthRank(h, state string) int {
        switch {
        case h == observe.HealthExpired:
                return 0
        case h == observe.HealthAtRisk:
                return 1
        case state == string(core.Parked):
                return 2
        case state == string(core.Failed):
                return 3
        case h == observe.HealthOK:
                return 4
        }
        return 5
}

// Observe builds the snapshot on the writer goroutine, which makes it consistent. It
// reads every task, so TestPerfObserve holds it to a budget.
func (e *Engine) Observe(ctx context.Context) (observe.Snapshot, error) {
        return do(ctx, e, func() (observe.Snapshot, error) {
                now := e.now()
                wall := time.Now()
                m := e.obs.Read(wall)
                s := observe.Snapshot{
                        Time: wall, UptimeMs: m.Uptime.Milliseconds(), States: map[string]int{},
                        Throughput: m.Throughput, Latency: m.Latency, Flow: m.Flow,
                        Planning: observe.Planning{Epoch: e.planning.Epoch, Active: e.planning.Active, Phase: e.planning.Phase,
                                Lost: !e.planning.LostAt.IsZero() && now.Sub(e.planning.LostAt) < e.cfg.PlanLostGrace},
