                }
                tiers := map[int]*observe.TierUsage{}
                var live []observe.TaskLive
                var tight []observe.BudgetLine
                working := map[string]string{}
                for _, ent := range e.tasks {
                        t := ent.task
                        s.States[string(t.State)]++
                        tu := tiers[t.Tier]
                        if tu == nil {
                                tu = &observe.TierUsage{Tier: t.Tier}
                                tiers[t.Tier] = tu
                        }
                        tu.Tasks++
                        tu.Tokens += t.Tokens
                        tu.Spent += t.Spent
                        tu.Budget += t.Budget
                        s.Usage.Tokens += t.Tokens
                        s.Usage.Spent += t.Spent
                        s.Usage.Budgeted += t.Budget
                        if t.Budget > 0 && !t.State.Terminal() {
                                if t.Spent > 0 { // A budget nothing has touched is not worth a row.
                                        tight = append(tight, observe.BudgetLine{ID: t.ID, Title: t.Title, Spent: t.Spent, Budget: t.Budget, State: string(t.State)})
                                }
                                if t.Spent >= t.Budget {
                                        s.Usage.OverBudget++
                                }
                        }
                        switch t.State {
                        case core.Ready:
                                s.OldestMs = max(s.OldestMs, now.Sub(t.ReadyAt).Milliseconds())
                        case core.Claimed, core.Running, core.Review, core.Merging, core.Failed, core.Parked:
                                live = append(live, e.liveTask(t, now))
                                if t.Owner != "" {
                                        working[t.Owner] = t.ID
                                }
                        }
                }
                slices.SortFunc(live, func(a, b observe.TaskLive) int {
                        return cmp.Or(cmp.Compare(healthRank(a.Health, a.State), healthRank(b.Health, b.State)), strings.Compare(a.ID, b.ID))
                })
                if len(live) > maxLiveTasks {
                        s.Truncated = len(live) - maxLiveTasks
                        live = live[:maxLiveTasks]
                }
                s.Tasks = live
                for _, tu := range tiers {
                        s.Usage.ByTier = append(s.Usage.ByTier, *tu)
                }
                slices.SortFunc(s.Usage.ByTier, func(a, b observe.TierUsage) int { return cmp.Compare(a.Tier, b.Tier) })
                slices.SortFunc(tight, func(a, b observe.BudgetLine) int {
                        // Compare spent/budget without division, so the order is exact.
                        return cmp.Or(cmp.Compare(b.Spent*a.Budget, a.Spent*b.Budget), strings.Compare(a.ID, b.ID))
                })
                s.Usage.Tightest = tight[:min(len(tight), 10)]

                waiting := map[string]bool{}
                for _, ws := range e.waiters {
                        for _, w := range ws {
                                waiting[w.agent.ID] = true
                                s.Waiting++
                        }
                }
                for id, a := range m.Agents {
                        seen := m.LastSeen[id]
                        if seen.IsZero() {
                                continue // Only usage so far, from before it was last seen.
                        }
                        ago := wall.Sub(seen)
                        state := "idle"
                        switch {
                        case working[id] != "":
                                state = "working"
                        case waiting[id]:
                                state = "waiting"
                        case ago > e.cfg.PresenceTTL:
                                state = "gone"
                        }
                        s.Agents = append(s.Agents, observe.AgentLive{
                                ID: id, Tier: a.Tier, State: state, Task: working[id], SeenAgoMs: ago.Milliseconds(),
                                Tokens: a.Tokens, Cost: a.Cost, Done: a.Done, Failed: a.Failed,
                        })
                }
                slices.SortFunc(s.Agents, func(a, b observe.AgentLive) int { return strings.Compare(a.ID, b.ID) })
                return s, nil
        })
}

package engine

import (
        "context"
        "encoding/json"
        "errors"
        "fmt"
        "time"

        "github.com/Grano22/aiculator/internal/core"
        "github.com/Grano22/aiculator/internal/store"
        "github.com/Grano22/aiculator/internal/vlog"
)

// Restored says what a restore did to one task.
type Restored struct {
        Task core.Task `json:"task"`
        // Did lists what had to change for the copy to be safe to put back.
        Did []string `json:"did,omitempty"`
        // Replaced is true when a task with that ID existed. Its record is then in quarantine.
        Replaced bool `json:"replaced"`
}

// Restore puts an earlier copy of a task back, from a backup.
//
// A copy is history, not a command, so it cannot be put back exactly as it was:
//   - Work that was in flight in the copy is not in flight now. A claimed, running, review or
//     merging copy goes back to Ready, keeping what it was, and its owner is cleared.
//   - The lease number moves past both the copy's and the current record's, so an agent
//     still holding a lease on the current record can write nothing more to it.
//   - Anything else that breaks the rules is fixed by the same repair as at startup. A Done
//     copy without an independent check is parked, never put back as Done.
//
// The record being replaced goes to quarantine first, so a restore can itself be undone.
func (e *Engine) Restore(ctx context.Context, t core.Task) (Restored, error) {
        if !idRE.MatchString(t.ID) {
                return Restored{}, fmt.Errorf("%w: task id %q", ErrInvalid, t.ID)
        }
        return do(ctx, e, func() (Restored, error) {
                now := e.now()
                n := t.Clone()
                var did []string
                switch n.State {
                case core.Claimed, core.Running, core.Review, core.Merging:
                        did = append(did, fmt.Sprintf("was %s in the copy; back to ready", n.State))
                        n.State, n.Owner, n.Submitter, n.Ref, n.Verifier = core.Ready, "", "", "", ""
                        n.ChecksRun, n.ChecksPassed = false, false
                        n.LeaseDeadline, n.ProgressDeadline = time.Time{}, time.Time{}
                        n.ReadyAt = now
                }
                ent := e.tasks[n.ID]
                var old core.Task
                var rev uint64
                if ent != nil {
                        old, rev = ent.task, ent.rev
                }
                n.LeaseEpoch = max(n.LeaseEpoch, old.LeaseEpoch) + 1
                fixed, more := core.Repair(n, now)
                did = append(did, more...)
                if err := core.Validate(fixed); err != nil {
                        return Restored{}, fmt.Errorf("%w: the copy cannot be made valid: %v", ErrInvalid, err)
                }
                var err error
                if ent != nil {
                        raw, _ := json.Marshal(old)
                        if err := e.st.Quarantine(old.ID, rev, raw, "replaced by a restore"); err != nil {
                                return Restored{}, fmt.Errorf("keep the record being replaced: %w", err)
                        }
                        rev, err = e.st.UpdateTask(fixed, rev)
                } else {
                        rev, err = e.st.CreateTask(fixed)
                }
                if err != nil {
                        if errors.Is(err, store.ErrConflict) && ent != nil {
                                e.reload(n.ID)
                        }
                        return Restored{}, err
                }
                e.index(old, fixed, rev)
                if ent != nil && old.State != fixed.State {
                        e.obs.Transition(string(old.State), string(fixed.State))
                }
                log.V(vlog.LevelDefault).Warn("restored a task from a backup", "task", fixed.ID, "state", fixed.State, "lease", fixed.LeaseEpoch, "did", did)
                return Restored{Task: fixed, Did: did, Replaced: ent != nil}, nil
        })
}

// Package export writes records as JSON, YAML, CSV, TSV, Excel, HTML or Markdown.
//
// Task titles and specs can come from agents or from outside systems, and an export is
// often opened somewhere that acts on what it reads. So every format here treats a value as
// text: HTML is escaped, Excel cells are stored as strings, and in CSV a value that a
// spreadsheet would run as a formula is neutralized.
package export

import (
        "encoding/csv"
        "encoding/json"
        "errors"
        "fmt"
        "html/template"
        "io"
        "maps"
        "path/filepath"
        "slices"
        "strconv"
        "strings"
        "unicode"

        "go.yaml.in/yaml/v3"
)

// Formats lists what Write accepts.
var Formats = []string{"json", "yaml", "csv", "tsv", "xlsx", "html", "md"}

// Record is one row, in the shape of its JSON form.
type Record = map[string]any

// FormatFor infers a format from a file name, or returns "" if the name does not say.
func FormatFor(path string) string {
        switch strings.ToLower(filepath.Ext(path)) {
        case ".json":
                return "json"
        case ".yaml", ".yml":
                return "yaml"
        case ".csv":
                return "csv"
        case ".tsv":
                return "tsv"
        case ".xlsx":
                return "xlsx"
        case ".html", ".htm":
                return "html"
        case ".md", ".markdown":
                return "md"
        }
        return ""
}

// Lookup finds a value by a dotted path, such as labels.team. A key that itself holds the
// dots wins, so an exact name is never shadowed.
func Lookup(r Record, path string) (any, bool) {
        if v, ok := r[path]; ok {
                return v, true
        }
        var cur any = r
        for _, part := range strings.Split(path, ".") {
                m, ok := cur.(map[string]any)
                if !ok {
                        return nil, false
                }
                if cur, ok = m[part]; !ok {
                        return nil, false
                }
        }
        return cur, true
}

// FieldNames lists every path that appears in these records, including labels.x and meta.x.
func FieldNames(records []Record) []string {
        seen := map[string]bool{}
        var walk func(prefix string, m map[string]any)
        walk = func(prefix string, m map[string]any) {
                for k, v := range m {
                        name := prefix + k
                        seen[name] = true
                        if inner, ok := v.(map[string]any); ok {
                                walk(name+".", inner)
                        }
                }
        }
        for _, r := range records {
                walk("", r)
        }
        return slices.Sorted(maps.Keys(seen))
}

// Select keeps these fields, flat, under their dotted names.
func Select(records []Record, fields []string) []Record {
        out := make([]Record, len(records))
        for i, r := range records {
                row := make(Record, len(fields))
                for _, f := range fields {
                        if v, ok := Lookup(r, f); ok {
                                row[f] = v
                        } else {
                                row[f] = nil
                        }
                }
                out[i] = row
        }
        return out
}

// Text renders a value for a cell.
func Text(v any) string {
        switch x := v.(type) {
        case nil:
                return ""
        case string:
                return x
        case bool:
                return strconv.FormatBool(x)
        case float64:
                return strconv.FormatFloat(x, 'f', -1, 64)
        case int:
                return strconv.Itoa(x)
        case int64:
                return strconv.FormatInt(x, 10)
        }
        b, err := json.Marshal(v)
        if err != nil {
                return fmt.Sprint(v)
        }
        return string(b)
}

// Options shapes the output.
type Options struct {
        Format  string
        Columns []string // Column order for the table formats. Empty means every field, sorted.
        Title   string   // Shown by HTML, and names the Excel sheet.
}

// Write writes the records in the chosen format.
func Write(w io.Writer, records []Record, o Options) error {
        cols := o.Columns
        if len(cols) == 0 {
                seen := map[string]bool{}
                for _, r := range records {
                        for k := range r {
                                seen[k] = true
                        }
                }
                cols = slices.Sorted(maps.Keys(seen))
        }
        switch o.Format {
        case "json":
                enc := json.NewEncoder(w)
                enc.SetIndent("", "  ")
                enc.SetEscapeHTML(false)
                if records == nil {
                        records = []Record{}
                }
                return enc.Encode(records)
        case "yaml":
                enc := yaml.NewEncoder(w)
                enc.SetIndent(2)
                defer enc.Close()
                if records == nil {
                        records = []Record{}
                }
                return enc.Encode(records)
        case "csv":
                return writeDelimited(w, ',', records, cols)
        case "tsv":
                return writeDelimited(w, '\t', records, cols)
        case "xlsx":
                return writeXLSX(w, records, cols, o.Title)
        case "html":
                return writeHTML(w, records, cols, o.Title)
        case "md":
                return writeMarkdown(w, records, cols)
        }
        return fmt.Errorf("unknown format %q: use %s", o.Format, strings.Join(Formats, ", "))
}

// GuardFormula stops a spreadsheet from running text as a formula. Excel and others treat a
// cell starting with these as one when they open a CSV, and a ticket title could be
// =HYPERLINK(...) or worse. A leading quote is the usual way to say "this is text".
func GuardFormula(s string) string {
        if s == "" {
                return s
        }
        switch s[0] {
        case '=', '+', '-', '@', '\t', '\r':
                return "'" + s
        }
        return s
}

func writeDelimited(w io.Writer, comma rune, records []Record, cols []string) error {
        cw := csv.NewWriter(w)
        cw.Comma = comma
        if err := cw.Write(cols); err != nil {
                return err
        }
        row := make([]string, len(cols))
        for _, r := range records {
                for i, c := range cols {
                        v := r[c]
                        text := Text(v)
                        if _, isString := v.(string); isString || v == nil {
                                text = GuardFormula(text)
                        } else if _, isNumber := v.(float64); !isNumber {
                                if _, isBool := v.(bool); !isBool {
                                        text = GuardFormula(text) // A list or object rendered as text.
                                }
                        }
                        row[i] = text
                }
                if err := cw.Write(row); err != nil {
                        return err
                }
        }
        cw.Flush()
        return cw.Error()
}

// mdCell keeps a value on one line, and keeps it from ending the cell or forming markup.
func mdCell(s string) string {
        s = strings.Map(func(r rune) rune {
                if unicode.IsControl(r) {
                        return ' '
                }
                return r
        }, s)
        return strings.NewReplacer(`\`, `\\`, `|`, `\|`, `<`, `&lt;`, `>`, `&gt;`, "`", "\\`", "[", `\[`, "]", `\]`).Replace(s)
}

func writeMarkdown(w io.Writer, records []Record, cols []string) error {
        if len(cols) == 0 {
                _, err := io.WriteString(w, "No records.\n")
                return err
        }
        var b strings.Builder
        head := make([]string, len(cols))
        for i, c := range cols {
                head[i] = mdCell(c)
        }
        b.WriteString("| " + strings.Join(head, " | ") + " |\n|" + strings.Repeat(" --- |", len(cols)) + "\n")
        for _, r := range records {
                cells := make([]string, len(cols))
                for i, c := range cols {
                        cells[i] = mdCell(Text(r[c]))
                }
                b.WriteString("| " + strings.Join(cells, " | ") + " |\n")
        }
        _, err := io.WriteString(w, b.String())
        return err
}

// html/template escapes every value, so a title cannot become markup. The page loads nothing
// from elsewhere, and its policy stops anything inside it from running.
var htmlPage = template.Must(template.New("export").Parse(`<!doctype html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
<meta charset="utf-8">
<meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">
<meta http-equiv="Content-Security-Policy" content="default-src 'none'; style-src 'unsafe-inline'">
<title>{{.Title}}</title>
<style>
:root { color-scheme: light dark; --line: #d0d7de; --head: #f6f8fa; }
@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark) { :root { --line: #30363d; --head: #161b22; } }
body { font: 14px/1.5 system-ui, sans-serif; margin: 24px; }
h1 { font-size: 18px; margin: 0 0 4px; }
p { margin: 0 0 16px; opacity: .7; }
.wrap { overflow-x: auto; }
table { border-collapse: collapse; }
th, td { border: 1px solid var(--line); padding: 6px 10px; text-align: left; vertical-align: top; }
th { background: var(--head); position: sticky; top: 0; white-space: nowrap; }
</style>
</head>
<body>
<h1>{{.Title}}</h1>
<p>{{len .Rows}} rows</p>
<div class="wrap"><table>
<thead><tr>{{range .Cols}}<th scope="col">{{.}}</th>{{end}}</tr></thead>
<tbody>{{range .Rows}}
<tr>{{range .}}<td>{{.}}</td>{{end}}</tr>{{end}}
</tbody>
</table></div>
</body>
</html>
`))

func writeHTML(w io.Writer, records []Record, cols []string, title string) error {
        rows := make([][]string, len(records))
        for i, r := range records {
                rows[i] = make([]string, len(cols))
                for j, c := range cols {
                        rows[i][j] = Text(r[c])
                }
        }
        if title == "" {
                title = "Export"
        }
        return htmlPage.Execute(w, struct {
                Title string
                Cols  []string
                Rows  [][]string
        }{title, cols, rows})
}

// ErrNeedsFile means a binary format was asked for on a terminal.
var ErrNeedsFile = errors.New("xlsx is a binary format: choose a file with -o")

package export

import (
        "archive/zip"
        "encoding/xml"
        "fmt"
        "io"
        "regexp"
        "strconv"
        "strings"
        "time"
        "unicode/utf8"
)

// The format allows 32,767 characters in a cell, and refuses the whole file if one has more.
const maxCell = 32767

var sheetUnsafe = regexp.MustCompile(`[\[\]:*?/\\']`)

func sheetName(title string) string {
        s := strings.TrimSpace(sheetUnsafe.ReplaceAllString(title, " "))
        if s == "" {
                return "Export"
        }
        if r := []rune(s); len(r) > 31 {
                s = string(r[:31])
        }
        return s
}

// colName turns 0 into A and 26 into AA.
func colName(i int) string {
        s := ""
        for i++; i > 0; i = (i - 1) / 26 {
                s = string(rune('A'+(i-1)%26)) + s
        }
        return s
}

// validXML drops what XML cannot hold at all, which would make the file refuse to open.
func validXML(s string) string {
        return strings.Map(func(r rune) rune {
                switch {
                case r == '\t', r == '\n', r == '\r':
                        return r
                case r < 0x20, r == 0xFFFE, r == 0xFFFF, r == utf8.RuneError:
                        return -1
                }
                return r
        }, s)
}

func escapeXML(s string) string {
        var b strings.Builder
        _ = xml.EscapeText(&b, []byte(validXML(s)))
        return b.String()
}

func textCell(b *strings.Builder, ref, text string, style int) {
        if r := []rune(text); len(r) > maxCell {
                text = string(r[:maxCell])
        }
        // An inline string is always text. Excel does not run it as a formula, whatever it says.
        fmt.Fprintf(b, `<c r="%s" s="%d" t="inlineStr"><is><t xml:space="preserve">%s</t></is></c>`, ref, style, escapeXML(text))
}

func writeXLSX(w io.Writer, records []Record, cols []string, title string) error {
        z := zip.NewWriter(w)
        part := func(name, body string) error {
                // A fixed time means the same data gives the same file.
                f, err := z.CreateHeader(&zip.FileHeader{Name: name, Method: zip.Deflate, Modified: time.Date(2020, 1, 1, 0, 0, 0, 0, time.UTC)})
                if err != nil {
                        return err
                }
                _, err = io.WriteString(f, body)
                return err
        }
        const head = `<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8" standalone="yes"?>` + "\n"
        files := []struct{ name, body string }{
                {"[Content_Types].xml", head + `<Types xmlns="http://schemas.openxmlformats.org/package/2006/content-types"><Default Extension="rels" ContentType="application/vnd.openxmlformats-package.relationships+xml"/><Default Extension="xml" ContentType="application/xml"/><Override PartName="/xl/workbook.xml" ContentType="application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet.main+xml"/><Override PartName="/xl/worksheets/sheet1.xml" ContentType="application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.worksheet+xml"/><Override PartName="/xl/styles.xml" ContentType="application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.styles+xml"/></Types>`},
                {"_rels/.rels", head + `<Relationships xmlns="http://schemas.openxmlformats.org/package/2006/relationships"><Relationship Id="rId1" Type="http://schemas.openxmlformats.org/officeDocument/2006/relationships/officeDocument" Target="xl/workbook.xml"/></Relationships>`},
                {"xl/workbook.xml", head + `<workbook xmlns="http://schemas.openxmlformats.org/spreadsheetml/2006/main" xmlns:r="http://schemas.openxmlformats.org/officeDocument/2006/relationships"><sheets><sheet name="` + escapeXML(sheetName(title)) + `" sheetId="1" r:id="rId1"/></sheets></workbook>`},
                {"xl/_rels/workbook.xml.rels", head + `<Relationships xmlns="http://schemas.openxmlformats.org/package/2006/relationships"><Relationship Id="rId1" Type="http://schemas.openxmlformats.org/officeDocument/2006/relationships/worksheet" Target="worksheets/sheet1.xml"/><Relationship Id="rId2" Type="http://schemas.openxmlformats.org/officeDocument/2006/relationships/styles" Target="styles.xml"/></Relationships>`},
                {"xl/styles.xml", head + `<styleSheet xmlns="http://schemas.openxmlformats.org/spreadsheetml/2006/main"><fonts count="2"><font><sz val="11"/><name val="Calibri"/></font><font><b/><sz val="11"/><name val="Calibri"/></font></fonts><fills count="2"><fill><patternFill patternType="none"/></fill><fill><patternFill patternType="gray125"/></fill></fills><borders count="1"><border><left/><right/><top/><bottom/><diagonal/></border></borders><cellStyleXfs count="1"><xf numFmtId="0" fontId="0" fillId="0" borderId="0"/></cellStyleXfs><cellXfs count="2"><xf numFmtId="0" fontId="0" fillId="0" borderId="0" xfId="0"/><xf numFmtId="0" fontId="1" fillId="0" borderId="0" xfId="0" applyFont="1"/></cellXfs><cellStyles count="1"><cellStyle name="Normal" xfId="0" builtinId="0"/></cellStyles></styleSheet>`},
        }
        for _, f := range files {
                if err := part(f.name, f.body); err != nil {
                        return err
                }
        }
        var b strings.Builder
        b.WriteString(head + `<worksheet xmlns="http://schemas.openxmlformats.org/spreadsheetml/2006/main">`)
        if len(cols) > 0 {
                // Keep the header in view, and make it filterable.
                b.WriteString(`<sheetViews><sheetView workbookViewId="0"><pane ySplit="1" topLeftCell="A2" activePane="bottomLeft" state="frozen"/></sheetView></sheetViews>`)
        }
        b.WriteString(`<sheetData>`)
        if len(cols) > 0 {
                b.WriteString(`<row r="1">`)
                for i, c := range cols {
                        textCell(&b, colName(i)+"1", c, 1)
                }
                b.WriteString(`</row>`)
        }
        for ri, r := range records {
                row := ri + 2
                fmt.Fprintf(&b, `<row r="%d">`, row)
                for i, c := range cols {
                        ref := colName(i) + strconv.Itoa(row)
                        switch v := r[c].(type) {
                        case nil:
                        case float64:
                                fmt.Fprintf(&b, `<c r="%s"><v>%s</v></c>`, ref, strconv.FormatFloat(v, 'f', -1, 64))
                        case bool:
                                n := 0
                                if v {
                                        n = 1
                                }
                                fmt.Fprintf(&b, `<c r="%s" t="b"><v>%d</v></c>`, ref, n)
                        default:
                                textCell(&b, ref, Text(v), 0)
                        }
                }
                b.WriteString(`</row>`)
        }
        b.WriteString(`</sheetData>`)
        if len(cols) > 0 {
                fmt.Fprintf(&b, `<autoFilter ref="A1:%s%d"/>`, colName(len(cols)-1), len(records)+1)
        }
        b.WriteString(`</worksheet>`)
        if err := part("xl/worksheets/sheet1.xml", b.String()); err != nil {
                return err
        }
        return z.Close()
}

// Package harness is the registry of supported coding agents: how to launch each
// one over ACP, where it looks for skills, and how to give it the swarm's MCP tools.
//
// Confidence is recorded per entry, because these paths change often and a wrong
// one fails silently. Update Source when you re-verify an entry.
package harness

import (
        "cmp"
        "os"
        "os/exec"
        "path/filepath"
        "slices"
        "strings"
)

// Source says how an entry's facts were established.
type Source string

const (
        // SourceDocs means the skill and MCP facts come from the harness's own docs.
        SourceDocs Source = "docs"
        // SourceTable means the skill path comes from the vercel-labs/skills agent
        // table and the ACP command from the ACP registry, not from the harness's docs.
        SourceTable Source = "table"
)

// MCPFormat is how a harness stores MCP servers.
type MCPFormat string

const (
        // MCPNone means there is no project config to write; use the shell route.
        MCPNone MCPFormat = ""
        // MCPServersJSON is a JSON file with an "mcpServers" object.
        MCPServersJSON MCPFormat = "mcpServers-json"
        // MCPOpenCode is opencode.json with an "mcp" object.
        MCPOpenCode MCPFormat = "opencode-json"
        // MCPCodexTOML is a TOML file with [mcp_servers.NAME] tables.
        MCPCodexTOML MCPFormat = "codex-toml"
)

// Harness describes one coding agent.
type Harness struct {
        ID   string
        Name string
        // Bins are executables that show the harness is installed.
        Bins []string
        // ACP launches the harness as an ACP agent. Empty means it has no ACP mode.
        // npx commands are pinned to the version in the ACP registry on purpose, so a
        // new upstream release cannot change what runs without review.
        ACP []string
        // PassEnv names API key variables the driver forwards. Nothing else is inherited.
        PassEnv []string
        // Env sets extra variables for the driver; {private} is the session's temp directory.
        Env []string
        // StateDirs are writable from the sandbox, for the harness's login and state.
        StateDirs []string
        // SkillsDir is the project skill directory, relative to the project root.
        SkillsDir string
        // GlobalSkillsDir is the user skill directory, starting with ~/.
        GlobalSkillsDir string
        // ReadsAgents means it scans <project>/.agents/skills, so it needs no link.
        ReadsAgents bool
        // ReadsGlobalAgents means it scans ~/.agents/skills.
        ReadsGlobalAgents bool
        MCP               MCPFormat
        MCPFile           string
        // GlobalMCPFile is the user-level config, starting with ~/.
        GlobalMCPFile string
        // QuestionTool is the built-in tool for asking the user, from the harness's docs.
        QuestionTool string
        // TodoTool, PlanEnter and PlanExit come from the harness's docs too.
        TodoTool, PlanEnter, PlanExit string
        // CLIAdd is the harness's own command for adding a server, when confirmed.
        CLIAdd []string
        Source Source
        // Note is shown to the user when joining.
        Note string
}

// All returns the registry, sorted by ID.
func All() []Harness {
        out := slices.Clone(registry)
        slices.SortFunc(out, func(a, b Harness) int { return cmp.Compare(a.ID, b.ID) })
        return out
}

// Get finds a harness by ID.
func Get(id string) (Harness, bool) {
        for _, h := range registry {
                if h.ID == id {
                        return h, true
                }
        }
        return Harness{}, false
}

// Installed reports whether one of the harness's executables is on PATH.
func (h Harness) Installed() bool {
        for _, b := range h.Bins {
                if _, err := exec.LookPath(b); err == nil {
                        return true
                }
        }
        return false
}

// Detected returns the harnesses installed on this machine.
func Detected() []Harness {
        var out []Harness
        for _, h := range All() {
                if h.Installed() {
                        out = append(out, h)
                }
        }
        return out
}

// ExpandHome turns a leading ~/ into the user's home directory.
func ExpandHome(p string) string {
        if rest, ok := strings.CutPrefix(p, "~/"); ok {
                if home, err := os.UserHomeDir(); err == nil {
                        return filepath.Join(home, rest)
                }
        }
        return p
}

func table(id, name string, bins, acp []string, skills, global string, readsAgents bool) Harness {
        state := []string{"~/." + id}
        if len(acp) > 0 && acp[0] == "npx" {
                state = append(state, npm)
        }
        return Harness{
                ID: id, Name: name, Bins: bins, ACP: acp, StateDirs: state,
                SkillsDir: skills, GlobalSkillsDir: global, ReadsAgents: readsAgents,
                ReadsGlobalAgents: global == "~/.agents/skills", Source: SourceTable,
        }
}

package harness

import (
        "bytes"
        "encoding/json"
        "errors"
        "fmt"
        "os"
        "path/filepath"
        "regexp"
        "slices"
        "strings"
        "time"
)

// ServerName is the name the swarm's MCP server is registered under.
const ServerName = "swarm"

// Entry is the command that starts the MCP bridge. It holds no secrets: the bridge
// gets its token locally when it starts, so these files are safe to commit.
type Entry struct {
        Name    string // Server name; empty means the swarm's own.
        Command string
        Args    []string
        Env     map[string]string
}

func (e Entry) name() string {
        if e.Name == "" {
                return ServerName
        }
        return e.Name
}

// toolTimeoutMs leaves room above the longest wait_for_task hold.
const toolTimeoutMs = 60000

// Result reports what a config change did.
type Result struct {
        Path    string
        Changed bool
}

func (h Harness) mcpPath(root string) string {
        if filepath.IsAbs(h.MCPFile) {
                return h.MCPFile
        }
        return filepath.Join(root, h.MCPFile)
}

// At returns the same format pointed at a specific config file.
func At(format MCPFormat, path string) Harness {
        return Harness{ID: "custom", MCP: format, MCPFile: path}
}

// FormatForPath infers a config format from a file name.
func FormatForPath(path string) MCPFormat {
        base := strings.ToLower(filepath.Base(path))
        switch {
        case strings.HasSuffix(base, ".toml"):
                return MCPCodexTOML
        case strings.HasPrefix(base, "opencode"):
                return MCPOpenCode
        }
        return MCPServersJSON
}

func jsonEntry(e Entry) map[string]any {
        m := map[string]any{
                "type": "stdio", "command": e.Command, "args": e.Args,
                "timeout": toolTimeoutMs, "tools": []string{"*"},
        }
        if len(e.Env) > 0 {
                m["env"] = e.Env
        }
        return m
}

// Snippet returns the config piece to paste by hand, in this harness's format.
func (h Harness) Snippet(e Entry) string {
        name := e.name()
        switch h.MCP {
        case MCPOpenCode:
                b, _ := encodeJSON(map[string]any{"mcp": map[string]any{"servers": map[string]any{name: openCodeEntry(e)}}})
                return string(b)
        case MCPCodexTOML:
                return tomlBlockFor(e)
        }
        b, _ := encodeJSON(map[string]any{"mcpServers": map[string]any{name: jsonEntry(e)}})
        return string(b)
}

// WriteMCP registers the swarm's server in the harness's project config. Other
// settings are preserved, and the previous file is copied to backupDir first.
func (h Harness) WriteMCP(root string, e Entry, backupDir string) (Result, error) {
        switch h.MCP {
        case MCPServersJSON:
                return h.writeJSON(root, "mcpServers", e.name(), jsonEntry(e), backupDir)
        case MCPOpenCode:
                if _, err := os.Stat(filepath.Join(filepath.Dir(h.mcpPath(root)), "opencode.jsonc")); err == nil {
                        return Result{}, fmt.Errorf("opencode.jsonc may hold comments that rewriting would lose; add this by hand:\n%s", h.Snippet(e))
                }
                return h.writeOpenCode(root, e, backupDir)
        case MCPCodexTOML:
                return h.writeTOML(root, e, backupDir)
        }
        return Result{}, nil
}

// openCodeEntry uses the v2 shape, the one opencode mcp add writes in 2.0.32. Its docs
// page still shows the deprecated v1 shape, with "enabled" and a numeric timeout.
func openCodeEntry(e Entry) map[string]any {
        m := map[string]any{
                "type": "local", "command": append([]string{e.Command}, e.Args...),
                "timeout": map[string]any{"execution": toolTimeoutMs},
        }
        if len(e.Env) > 0 {
                m["environment"] = e.Env
        }
        return m
}

func (h Harness) writeOpenCode(root string, e Entry, backupDir string) (Result, error) {
        path := h.mcpPath(root)
        doc, old, err := readJSON(path)
        if err != nil {
                return Result{}, err
        }
        mcp, ok := doc["mcp"].(map[string]any)
        if !ok {
                if doc["mcp"] != nil {
                        return Result{}, fmt.Errorf("%s: \"mcp\" is not an object, so the file was left alone", path)
                }
                mcp = map[string]any{}
        }
        servers, ok := mcp["servers"].(map[string]any)
        if !ok {
                if mcp["servers"] != nil {
                        return Result{}, fmt.Errorf("%s: \"mcp.servers\" is not an object, so the file was left alone", path)
                }
                servers = map[string]any{}
        }
        delete(mcp, e.name()) // An entry in the old shape must not linger beside the new one.
        servers[e.name()] = openCodeEntry(e)
        mcp["servers"] = servers
        doc["mcp"] = mcp
        data, err := encodeJSON(doc)
        if err != nil {
                return Result{}, err
        }
        return commit(path, old, data, backupDir)
}

func (h Harness) removeOpenCode(root, name, backupDir string) (Result, error) {
        path := h.mcpPath(root)
        doc, old, err := readJSON(path)
        if err != nil || old == nil {
                return Result{Path: path}, err
        }
        mcp, _ := doc["mcp"].(map[string]any)
        servers, _ := mcp["servers"].(map[string]any)
        _, inServers := servers[name]
        _, inOld := mcp[name]
        if !inServers && !inOld {
                return Result{Path: path}, nil
        }
        delete(servers, name)
        delete(mcp, name)
        if len(servers) == 0 {
                delete(mcp, "servers")
        }
        if len(mcp) == 0 {
                delete(doc, "mcp")
        }
        if len(doc) == 0 {
                if err := backup(path, old, backupDir); err != nil {
                        return Result{}, err
                }
                return Result{Path: path, Changed: true}, os.Remove(path)
        }
        data, err := encodeJSON(doc)
        if err != nil {
                return Result{}, err
        }
        return commit(path, old, data, backupDir)
}

// RemoveMCP removes the swarm's server and nothing else.
func (h Harness) RemoveMCP(root, backupDir string) (Result, error) {
        return h.RemoveNamed(root, ServerName, backupDir)
}

// RemoveNamed removes one named server and nothing else.
func (h Harness) RemoveNamed(root, name, backupDir string) (Result, error) {
        switch h.MCP {
        case MCPServersJSON:
                return h.removeJSON(root, "mcpServers", name, backupDir)
        case MCPOpenCode:
                return h.removeOpenCode(root, name, backupDir)
        case MCPCodexTOML:
                return h.removeTOML(root, name, backupDir)
        }
        return Result{}, nil
}

// HasMCP reports whether the swarm's server is registered.
func (h Harness) HasMCP(root string) bool { return h.HasNamed(root, ServerName) }

// HasNamed reports whether a named server is registered.
func (h Harness) HasNamed(root, name string) bool {
        b, err := os.ReadFile(h.mcpPath(root))
        if err != nil {
                return false
        }
        switch h.MCP {
        case MCPServersJSON, MCPOpenCode:
                var doc map[string]any
                if json.Unmarshal(b, &doc) != nil {
                        return false
                }
                servers, _ := doc["mcpServers"].(map[string]any)
                if h.MCP == MCPOpenCode {
                        mcp, _ := doc["mcp"].(map[string]any)
                        servers, _ = mcp["servers"].(map[string]any)
                }
                _, ok := servers[name]
                return ok
        case MCPCodexTOML:
                return tomlTable(name).Match(b)
        }
        return false
}

func readJSON(path string) (map[string]any, []byte, error) {
        b, err := os.ReadFile(path)
        if errors.Is(err, os.ErrNotExist) {
                return map[string]any{}, nil, nil
        }
        if err != nil {
                return nil, nil, err
        }
        doc := map[string]any{}
        if len(bytes.TrimSpace(b)) == 0 {
                return doc, b, nil
        }
        // Never rewrite a file that cannot be understood: that would destroy it.
        if err := json.Unmarshal(b, &doc); err != nil {
                return nil, nil, fmt.Errorf("%s is not valid JSON, so it was left alone: %w", path, err)
        }
        return doc, b, nil
}

func encodeJSON(doc map[string]any) ([]byte, error) {
        var buf bytes.Buffer
        enc := json.NewEncoder(&buf)
        enc.SetEscapeHTML(false)
        enc.SetIndent("", "  ")
        if err := enc.Encode(doc); err != nil {
                return nil, err
        }
        return buf.Bytes(), nil
}

func (h Harness) writeJSON(root, key, name string, entry map[string]any, backupDir string) (Result, error) {
        path := h.mcpPath(root)
        doc, old, err := readJSON(path)
        if err != nil {
                return Result{}, err
        }
        var servers map[string]any
        switch v := doc[key].(type) {
        case nil:
                servers = map[string]any{}
        case map[string]any:
                servers = v
        default:
                return Result{}, fmt.Errorf("%s: %q is not an object, so the file was left alone", path, key)
        }
        servers[name] = entry
        doc[key] = servers
        data, err := encodeJSON(doc)
        if err != nil {
                return Result{}, err
        }
        return commit(path, old, data, backupDir)
}

func (h Harness) removeJSON(root, key, name, backupDir string) (Result, error) {
        path := h.mcpPath(root)
        doc, old, err := readJSON(path)
        if err != nil || old == nil {
                return Result{Path: path}, err
        }
        servers, _ := doc[key].(map[string]any)
        if _, ok := servers[name]; !ok {
                return Result{Path: path}, nil
        }
        delete(servers, name)
        if len(servers) == 0 {
                delete(doc, key)
        }
        if len(doc) == 0 { // Nothing else was in it, so the swarm made this file.
                if err := backup(path, old, backupDir); err != nil {
                        return Result{}, err
                }
                return Result{Path: path, Changed: true}, os.Remove(path)
        }
        data, err := encodeJSON(doc)
        if err != nil {
                return Result{}, err
        }
        return commit(path, old, data, backupDir)
}

func tomlBegin(name string) string { return "# BEGIN " + name + " (managed by aiculator; do not edit)" }
func tomlEnd(name string) string   { return "# END " + name }

func tomlTable(name string) *regexp.Regexp {
        return regexp.MustCompile(`(?m)^\[mcp_servers\.` + regexp.QuoteMeta(name) + `\]`)
}

func tomlBlockRE(name string) *regexp.Regexp {
        return regexp.MustCompile(`(?s)\n?` + regexp.QuoteMeta(tomlBegin(name)) + `.*?` + regexp.QuoteMeta(tomlEnd(name)) + `\n?`)
}

// tomlString writes a TOML basic string, whose escapes differ from Go's for
// control characters.
func tomlString(s string) string {
        r := strings.NewReplacer(`\`, `\\`, `"`, `\"`, "\n", `\n`, "\r", `\r`, "\t", `\t`)
        return `"` + r.Replace(s) + `"`
}

func tomlBlockFor(e Entry) string {
        name := e.name()
        args := make([]string, len(e.Args))
        for i, a := range e.Args {
                args[i] = tomlString(a)
        }
        var b strings.Builder
        fmt.Fprintf(&b, "%s\n[mcp_servers.%s]\ncommand = %s\nargs = [%s]\ntool_timeout_sec = %d\n",
                tomlBegin(name), name, tomlString(e.Command), strings.Join(args, ", "), toolTimeoutMs/1000)
        if len(e.Env) > 0 {
                fmt.Fprintf(&b, "\n[mcp_servers.%s.env]\n", name)
                keys := make([]string, 0, len(e.Env))
                for k := range e.Env {
                        keys = append(keys, k)
                }
                slices.Sort(keys)
                for _, k := range keys {
                        fmt.Fprintf(&b, "%s = %s\n", k, tomlString(e.Env[k]))
                }
        }
        b.WriteString(tomlEnd(name) + "\n")
        return b.String()
}

// writeTOML works on text inside clearly marked lines, so the rest of the file
// keeps its exact comments and formatting without needing a TOML library.
func (h Harness) writeTOML(root string, e Entry, backupDir string) (Result, error) {
        path := h.mcpPath(root)
        name := e.name()
        old, err := os.ReadFile(path)
        if err != nil && !errors.Is(err, os.ErrNotExist) {
                return Result{}, err
        }
        rest := old
        if re := tomlBlockRE(name); re.Match(old) {
                rest = re.ReplaceAll(old, []byte("\n"))
        }
        if tomlTable(name).Match(rest) {
                return Result{}, fmt.Errorf("%s already defines [mcp_servers.%s] by hand, so it was left alone", path, name)
        }
        block := tomlBlockFor(e)
        body := bytes.TrimRight(rest, "\n")
        var data []byte
        if len(body) > 0 {
                data = append(append(slices.Clone(body), "\n\n"...), block...)
        } else {
                data = []byte(block)
        }
        return commit(path, old, data, backupDir)
}

func (h Harness) removeTOML(root, name, backupDir string) (Result, error) {
        path := h.mcpPath(root)
        old, err := os.ReadFile(path)
        if errors.Is(err, os.ErrNotExist) {
                return Result{Path: path}, nil
        }
        if err != nil {
                return Result{}, err
        }
        re := tomlBlockRE(name)
        if !re.Match(old) {
                return Result{Path: path}, nil
        }
        body := bytes.TrimRight(re.ReplaceAll(old, []byte("\n")), "\n")
        if len(bytes.TrimSpace(body)) == 0 {
                if err := backup(path, old, backupDir); err != nil {
                        return Result{}, err
                }
                return Result{Path: path, Changed: true}, os.Remove(path)
        }
        return commit(path, old, append(slices.Clone(body), '\n'), backupDir)
}

func commit(path string, old, data []byte, backupDir string) (Result, error) {
        if bytes.Equal(old, data) {
                return Result{Path: path}, nil
        }
        if err := backup(path, old, backupDir); err != nil {
                return Result{}, err
        }
        if err := os.MkdirAll(filepath.Dir(path), 0o755); err != nil {
                return Result{}, err
        }
        mode := os.FileMode(0o644)
        if fi, err := os.Stat(path); err == nil {
                mode = fi.Mode().Perm()
        }
        tmp := path + ".swarm-tmp"
        if err := os.WriteFile(tmp, data, mode); err != nil {
                return Result{}, err
        }
        if err := os.Rename(tmp, path); err != nil {
                _ = os.Remove(tmp)
                return Result{}, err
        }
        return Result{Path: path, Changed: true}, nil
}

func backup(path string, old []byte, dir string) error {
        if old == nil || dir == "" {
                return nil
        }
        if err := os.MkdirAll(dir, 0o700); err != nil {
                return err
        }
        name := strings.ReplaceAll(strings.TrimLeft(path, "/"), "/", "_")
        stamp := time.Now().Format("20060102-150405.000000000")
        return os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(dir, name+"."+stamp), old, 0o600)
}

package meta

import (
        "context"
        "errors"
        "fmt"
        "io"
        "net"
        "net/http"
        "net/netip"
        "syscall"
        "time"
)

// Downloader reads a foreign object's bytes.
type Downloader interface {
        Download(ctx context.Context, r Resource) (body io.ReadCloser, mediaType string, err error)
}

// Fetcher reads plain URLs. A URL can come from outside, such as a Jira attachment or a
// Notion page, so the server must not be talked into reaching its own network: it refuses
// private addresses at connect time, after DNS, which also defeats DNS rebinding.
type Fetcher struct{ client *http.Client }

// ErrBlockedAddress means a URL resolved to an address the server will not contact.
var ErrBlockedAddress = errors.New("address is not reachable from the swarm")

// NewFetcher returns a fetcher. allowPrivate turns the address check off, for an
// on-premises service that a person has deliberately configured.
func NewFetcher(allowPrivate bool) *Fetcher {
        d := &net.Dialer{Timeout: 15 * time.Second}
        if !allowPrivate {
                d.Control = func(_, address string, _ syscall.RawConn) error {
                        ap, err := netip.ParseAddrPort(address)
                        if err != nil {
                                return fmt.Errorf("%w: %s", ErrBlockedAddress, address)
                        }
                        if !publicAddr(ap.Addr()) {
                                return fmt.Errorf("%w: %s", ErrBlockedAddress, ap.Addr())
                        }
                        return nil
                }
        }
        return &Fetcher{client: &http.Client{
                Transport: &http.Transport{
                        // No proxy: a proxy would make the connection for us, past the check above.
                        DialContext:           d.DialContext,
                        TLSHandshakeTimeout:   15 * time.Second,
                        ResponseHeaderTimeout: 30 * time.Second,
                },
                CheckRedirect: func(_ *http.Request, via []*http.Request) error {
                        if len(via) >= 5 {
                                return errors.New("too many redirects")
                        }
                        return nil
                },
        }}
}

func publicAddr(a netip.Addr) bool {
        a = a.Unmap()
        if !a.IsGlobalUnicast() || a.IsPrivate() || a.IsLoopback() || a.IsLinkLocalUnicast() {
                return false
        }
        // Carrier-grade NAT, which IsPrivate leaves out, and the cloud metadata range.
        for _, p := range []string{"100.64.0.0/10", "169.254.0.0/16", "fc00::/7"} {
                if netip.MustParsePrefix(p).Contains(a) {
                        return false
                }
        }
        return true
}

// Download implements Downloader.
func (f *Fetcher) Download(ctx context.Context, r Resource) (io.ReadCloser, string, error) {
        req, err := http.NewRequestWithContext(ctx, http.MethodGet, r.URL, nil)
        if err != nil {
                return nil, "", err
        }
        resp, err := f.client.Do(req)
        if err != nil {
                return nil, "", err
        }
        if resp.StatusCode/100 != 2 {
                resp.Body.Close()
                return nil, "", fmt.Errorf("fetching %s: status %d", r.Name, resp.StatusCode)
        }
        return resp.Body, resp.Header.Get("Content-Type"), nil
}

// Package meta holds what a task carries besides its working state: properties, blobs and
// references to things that live elsewhere, such as a Jira attachment.
//
// It is stored apart from the task record on purpose. That record is rewritten on every
// heartbeat, so anything large there would slow every commit. Nothing on the claim path
// reads this package.
package meta

import (
        "encoding/json"
        "errors"
        "fmt"
        "net/url"
        "regexp"
        "time"
)

// Limits. A property too large for these belongs in a blob.
const (
        MaxBytes = 256 << 10
        MaxProps = 512
)

// ErrInvalid marks a rejected change.
var ErrInvalid = errors.New("invalid metadata")

// BlobRef points at bytes held by the swarm. The hash is the identity, so storing the same
// file twice costs nothing, and what is read back can be checked.
type BlobRef struct {
        SHA256    string `json:"sha256"`
        Size      int64  `json:"size"`
        Name      string `json:"name,omitempty"`
        MediaType string `json:"media_type,omitempty"`
}

// Resource is a foreign object: something that lives elsewhere, and is only referred to.
// Its bytes are fetched on request, once, and kept as a blob.
type Resource struct {
        // Kind says what this is, such as http, jira.attachment or notion.file.
        Kind      string `json:"kind"`
        URL       string `json:"url"`
        Name      string `json:"name,omitempty"`
        MediaType string `json:"media_type,omitempty"`
        Size      int64  `json:"size,omitempty"`
        // Connection names the configured source whose credentials can read this.
        Connection string `json:"connection,omitempty"`
        // Blob is set once the bytes have been fetched.
        Blob      *BlobRef  `json:"blob,omitempty"`
        FetchedAt time.Time `json:"fetched_at,omitzero"`
}

// Prop is one property: exactly one of a value, a blob or a foreign resource.
type Prop struct {
        Value    any       `json:"value,omitempty"`
        Blob     *BlobRef  `json:"blob,omitempty"`
        Resource *Resource `json:"resource,omitempty"`
}

// Meta is everything extra about one task.
type Meta struct {
        Props     map[string]Prop `json:"props,omitempty"`
        UpdatedAt time.Time       `json:"updated_at,omitzero"`
}

// Patch changes some properties. A null removes one, so that two writers changing
// different properties cannot undo each other.
type Patch struct {
        Props map[string]*Prop `json:"props"`
}

var (
        nameRE = regexp.MustCompile(`^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._/-]{0,127}$`)
        shaRE  = regexp.MustCompile(`^[0-9a-f]{64}$`)
)

// ValidSHA reports whether s is a lowercase SHA-256 in hex.
func ValidSHA(s string) bool { return shaRE.MatchString(s) }

func (p Prop) validate() error {
        n := 0
        if p.Value != nil {
                n++
        }
        if p.Blob != nil {
                n++
                if !ValidSHA(p.Blob.SHA256) {
                        return fmt.Errorf("blob hash %q", p.Blob.SHA256)
                }
        }
        if r := p.Resource; r != nil {
                n++
                if r.Kind == "" {
                        return errors.New("a resource needs a kind")
                }
                u, err := url.Parse(r.URL)
                if err != nil || u.Host == "" || (u.Scheme != "https" && u.Scheme != "http") {
                        return fmt.Errorf("resource URL %q: only http and https are allowed", r.URL)
                }
        }
        if n != 1 {
                return errors.New("a property must hold exactly one of value, blob or resource")
        }
        return nil
}

// Apply returns m with the patch applied, or an error that leaves m as it was.
func (m Meta) Apply(p Patch, now time.Time) (Meta, error) {
        out := Meta{Props: make(map[string]Prop, len(m.Props)+len(p.Props)), UpdatedAt: now}
        for k, v := range m.Props {
                out.Props[k] = v
        }
        for k, v := range p.Props {
                if !nameRE.MatchString(k) {
                        return m, fmt.Errorf("%w: property name %q", ErrInvalid, k)
                }
                if v == nil {
                        delete(out.Props, k)
                        continue
                }
                if err := v.validate(); err != nil {
                        return m, fmt.Errorf("%w: property %s: %v", ErrInvalid, k, err)
                }
                out.Props[k] = *v
        }
        if len(out.Props) > MaxProps {
                return m, fmt.Errorf("%w: %d properties, over the limit of %d", ErrInvalid, len(out.Props), MaxProps)
        }
        b, err := json.Marshal(out)
        if err != nil {
                return m, fmt.Errorf("%w: %v", ErrInvalid, err)
        }
        if len(b) > MaxBytes {
                return m, fmt.Errorf("%w: %d bytes of properties, over the limit of %d: use a blob", ErrInvalid, len(b), MaxBytes)
        }
        return out, nil
}

// Package parallel decides what can safely run at the same time in one working tree.
//
// Worktrees keep tasks apart, each in its own checkout. This is the level below: one task
// split among subagents in one checkout, with no merge afterwards to catch a collision. So it
// is deliberately conservative. Jobs share a wave only if what they claim cannot overlap, a
// job that claims nothing runs alone, and Verify checks with git what each wave really did.
//
// It holds no state, and neither reads nor changes the swarm's own.
package parallel

import (
        "bytes"
        "cmp"
        "errors"
        "fmt"
        "os"
        "path"
        "path/filepath"
        "regexp"
        "slices"
        "strconv"
        "strings"
)

// Granularity is how finely claims are compared. Coarser is safer, and finer runs more at once.
// Symbol lets two jobs share a file, so it relies on them keeping to their parts.
type Granularity string

// The levels, coarsest first. Auto picks between Dir and File, and Symbol is only by request.
const (
        Repo   Granularity = "repo"
        Dir    Granularity = "dir"
        File   Granularity = "file"
        Symbol Granularity = "symbol"
        Auto   Granularity = "auto"
)

// ExactLimit is how many jobs are solved exactly. It takes moments at this size, and the work
// grows too fast to go much higher. Beyond it, a greedy schedule is used.
const ExactLimit = 14

// Job is one piece of work to give a subagent.
type Job struct {
        ID string `json:"id" yaml:"id"`
        // Touches are what it writes: a file, a directory ending in /, file#symbol or file:10-40.
        Touches []string `json:"touches,omitempty" yaml:"touches,omitempty"`
        // Reads are what it depends on staying the same while it works.
        Reads []string `json:"reads,omitempty" yaml:"reads,omitempty"`
        // Deps must finish, in an earlier wave, before this starts.
        Deps []string `json:"deps,omitempty" yaml:"deps,omitempty"`
        // Exclusive runs it alone, as for a formatter or a dependency install.
        Exclusive bool `json:"exclusive,omitempty" yaml:"exclusive,omitempty"`
        // Weight is its rough size, used to run long chains first. 1 if empty.
        Weight int `json:"weight,omitempty" yaml:"weight,omitempty"`
}

// Input is a set of jobs and how to plan them.
type Input struct {
        Jobs        []Job       `json:"jobs" yaml:"jobs"`
        Granularity Granularity `json:"granularity,omitempty" yaml:"granularity,omitempty"`
        Max         int         `json:"max,omitempty" yaml:"max,omitempty"` // Most at once.
}

// Conflict says why two jobs cannot share a wave.
type Conflict struct {
        A   string `json:"a"`
        B   string `json:"b"`
        Why string `json:"why"`
}

// Wave is a set of jobs to run at the same time.
type Wave struct {
        N    int      `json:"n"`
        Jobs []string `json:"jobs"`
}

// Plan is the schedule.
type Plan struct {
        // Verdict is parallel if anything runs at once, and sequential if nothing can.
        Verdict     string      `json:"verdict"`
        Granularity Granularity `json:"granularity"`
        Waves       []Wave      `json:"waves"`
        Conflicts   []Conflict  `json:"conflicts,omitempty"`
        // Alone lists jobs that claim nothing, or asked to be exclusive.
        Alone  []string `json:"alone,omitempty"`
        Method string   `json:"method"` // exact or greedy.
        // Optimal is true if no schedule could use fewer waves.
        Optimal bool `json:"optimal"`
        // Tried says how many waves each level took, when the level was chosen automatically.
        Tried map[Granularity]int `json:"tried,omitempty"`
        // Writes is what each job may change, which Verify checks against.
        Writes map[string][]string `json:"writes"`
        Max    int                 `json:"max"`
}

// claim is one parsed path, with an optional part of a file.
type claim struct {
        raw      string
        path     string
        isDir    bool
        symbol   string
        from, to int
}

var linesRE = regexp.MustCompile(`^(.+):(\d+)-(\d+)$`)

func parseClaim(s string) (claim, error) {
        c := claim{raw: s}
        p := strings.TrimSpace(strings.ReplaceAll(s, `\`, "/"))
        if p == "" {
                return c, errors.New("an empty path")
        }
        if m := linesRE.FindStringSubmatch(p); m != nil {
                from, err1 := strconv.Atoi(m[2])
                to, err2 := strconv.Atoi(m[3])
                if err1 != nil || err2 != nil || from < 1 || to < from {
                        return c, fmt.Errorf("%q: bad line range", s)
                }
                p, c.from, c.to = m[1], from, to
        } else if before, sym, ok := strings.Cut(p, "#"); ok {
                if sym == "" {
                        return c, fmt.Errorf("%q: no symbol after #", s)
                }
                p, c.symbol = before, sym
        }
        // A wildcard could match anything below it, so it claims that whole directory.
        if i := strings.IndexAny(p, "*?["); i >= 0 {
                p = p[:strings.LastIndex(p[:i], "/")+1]
                if p == "" {
                        p = "./"
                }
                c.symbol, c.from, c.to = "", 0, 0
        }
        c.isDir = strings.HasSuffix(p, "/")
        if strings.HasPrefix(p, "/") {
                return c, fmt.Errorf("%q: use a path relative to the project", s)
        }
        p = path.Clean(p)
        if p == ".." || strings.HasPrefix(p, "../") {
                return c, fmt.Errorf("%q: outside the project", s)
        }
        if p == "." {
                c.isDir = true
        }
        // Compared without case, since on macOS and Windows these can be one file.
        c.path = strings.ToLower(p)
        return c, nil
}

// at reduces a claim to a granularity.
func (c claim) at(g Granularity) claim {
        out := claim{raw: c.raw, path: c.path, isDir: c.isDir}
        switch g {
        case Repo:
                out.path, out.isDir = ".", true
        case Dir:
                if !c.isDir {
                        out.path, out.isDir = path.Dir(c.path), true
                }
        case File:
        default:
                out.symbol, out.from, out.to = c.symbol, c.from, c.to
        }
        return out
}

func pathsOverlap(a, b string) bool {
        if a == "." || b == "." || a == b {
                return true
        }
        return strings.HasPrefix(a, b+"/") || strings.HasPrefix(b, a+"/")
}

func overlap(a, b claim) bool {
        if !pathsOverlap(a.path, b.path) {
                return false
        }
        if a.path != b.path {
                return true
        }
        switch {
        case a.symbol != "" && b.symbol != "":
                return a.symbol == b.symbol
        case a.from != 0 && b.from != 0:
                return a.from <= b.to && b.from <= a.to
        }
        // A whole file against a part, or a symbol against lines, which could be the same place.
        return true
}

type parsed struct {
        job           Job
        writes, reads []claim
        alone         bool
}

func parse(jobs []Job) ([]parsed, error) {
        if len(jobs) == 0 {
                return nil, errors.New("no jobs")
        }
        seen := make(map[string]bool, len(jobs))
        out := make([]parsed, len(jobs))
        for i, j := range jobs {
                if j.ID == "" {
                        return nil, fmt.Errorf("job %d has no id", i+1)
                }
                if seen[j.ID] {
                        return nil, fmt.Errorf("job %s is listed twice", j.ID)
                }
                seen[j.ID] = true
                p := parsed{job: j, alone: j.Exclusive || len(j.Touches) == 0}
                for _, s := range j.Touches {
                        c, err := parseClaim(s)
                        if err != nil {
                                return nil, fmt.Errorf("job %s: %w", j.ID, err)
                        }
                        p.writes = append(p.writes, c)
                }
                for _, s := range j.Reads {
                        c, err := parseClaim(s)
                        if err != nil {
                                return nil, fmt.Errorf("job %s: %w", j.ID, err)
                        }
                        p.reads = append(p.reads, c)
                }
                out[i] = p
        }
        for _, p := range out {
                for _, d := range p.job.Deps {
                        if !seen[d] {
                                return nil, fmt.Errorf("job %s depends on %s, which is not listed", p.job.ID, d)
                        }
                }
        }
        return out, nil
}

// conflictBetween says why two jobs cannot run together, or "" if they can.
func conflictBetween(a, b parsed, g Granularity) string {
        if a.alone {
                return a.job.ID + " must run alone"
        }
        if b.alone {
                return b.job.ID + " must run alone"
        }
        for _, x := range a.writes {
                for _, y := range b.writes {
                        if overlap(x.at(g), y.at(g)) {
                                return fmt.Sprintf("both write: %s and %s", x.raw, y.raw)
                        }
                }
                for _, y := range b.reads {
                        if overlap(x.at(g), y.at(g)) {
                                return fmt.Sprintf("%s writes %s, which %s reads as %s", a.job.ID, x.raw, b.job.ID, y.raw)
                        }
                }
        }
        for _, x := range b.writes {
                for _, y := range a.reads {
                        if overlap(x.at(g), y.at(g)) {
                                return fmt.Sprintf("%s writes %s, which %s reads as %s", b.job.ID, x.raw, a.job.ID, y.raw)
                        }
                }
        }
        return ""
}

// graph is the problem in the form the schedulers use.
type graph struct {
        n         int
        conflict  [][]bool
        depMask   []uint64
        deps      [][]int
        dependent [][]int
        weight    []int
        priority  []int
        ids       []string
}

func build(ps []parsed, g Granularity) (*graph, []Conflict, error) {
        n := len(ps)
        gr := &graph{n: n, conflict: make([][]bool, n), depMask: make([]uint64, n), deps: make([][]int, n), dependent: make([][]int, n), weight: make([]int, n), priority: make([]int, n), ids: make([]string, n)}
        index := make(map[string]int, n)
        for i, p := range ps {
                index[p.job.ID] = i
                gr.ids[i] = p.job.ID
                gr.conflict[i] = make([]bool, n)
                gr.weight[i] = max(p.job.Weight, 1)
        }
        for i, p := range ps {
                for _, d := range p.job.Deps {
                        j := index[d]
                        if j == i {
                                return nil, nil, fmt.Errorf("job %s depends on itself", p.job.ID)
                        }
                        gr.deps[i] = append(gr.deps[i], j)
                        gr.dependent[j] = append(gr.dependent[j], i)
                        if n <= 64 {
                                gr.depMask[i] |= 1 << j
                        }
                }
        }
        if err := gr.computePriority(); err != nil {
                return nil, nil, err
        }
        var conflicts []Conflict
        for i := range n {
                for j := i + 1; j < n; j++ {
                        if why := conflictBetween(ps[i], ps[j], g); why != "" {
                                gr.conflict[i][j], gr.conflict[j][i] = true, true
                                conflicts = append(conflicts, Conflict{ps[i].job.ID, ps[j].job.ID, why})
                        }
                }
        }
        return gr, conflicts, nil
}

// computePriority works out how much must still follow each job, and refuses a cycle.
func (g *graph) computePriority() error {
        const (
                unseen = iota
                visiting
                finished
        )
        mark := make([]int, g.n)
        var visit func(i int) error
        visit = func(i int) error {
                switch mark[i] {
                case visiting:
                        return fmt.Errorf("a dependency cycle goes through %s", g.ids[i])
                case finished:
                        return nil
                }
                mark[i] = visiting
                tail := 0
                for _, d := range g.dependent[i] {
                        if err := visit(d); err != nil {
                                return err
                        }
                        tail = max(tail, g.priority[d])
                }
                g.priority[i] = g.weight[i] + tail
                mark[i] = finished
                return nil
        }
        for i := range g.n {
                if err := visit(i); err != nil {
                        return err
                }
        }
        return nil
}

// order ranks jobs: the longest chain first, then the most contested, then by name, so that
// the same input always gives the same plan.
func (g *graph) order() []int {
        degree := make([]int, g.n)
        for i := range g.n {
                for j := range g.n {
                        if g.conflict[i][j] {
                                degree[i]++
                        }
                }
        }
        idx := make([]int, g.n)
        for i := range idx {
                idx[i] = i
        }
        slices.SortFunc(idx, func(a, b int) int {
                return cmp.Or(cmp.Compare(g.priority[b], g.priority[a]), cmp.Compare(degree[b], degree[a]), cmp.Compare(g.ids[a], g.ids[b]))
        })
        return idx
}

func (g *graph) greedy(limit int) [][]int {
        order := g.order()
        done := make([]bool, g.n)
        var waves [][]int
        for left := g.n; left > 0; {
                var wave []int
                for _, i := range order {
                        if done[i] || len(wave) == limit {
                                continue
                        }
                        ready := !slices.ContainsFunc(g.deps[i], func(d int) bool { return !done[d] })
                        clash := slices.ContainsFunc(wave, func(w int) bool { return g.conflict[i][w] })
                        if ready && !clash {
                                wave = append(wave, i)
                        }
                }
                for _, i := range wave {
                        done[i] = true
                }
                left -= len(wave)
                waves = append(waves, wave)
        }
        return waves
}

// exact finds a schedule with the fewest waves, by search over which jobs are finished. Only
// sets that cannot take another job need trying, because running a job sooner never hurts:
// it can always be taken back out of a later wave without breaking anything.
func (g *graph) exact(limit int) [][]int {
        order := g.order()
        all := uint64(1)<<g.n - 1
        type answer struct {
                waves int
                next  uint64
        }
        memo := map[uint64]answer{all: {0, 0}}
        var solve func(done uint64) int
        solve = func(done uint64) int {
                if a, ok := memo[done]; ok {
                        return a.waves
                }
                var ready []int
                for _, i := range order {
                        if done&(1<<i) == 0 && g.depMask[i]&^done == 0 {
                                ready = append(ready, i)
                        }
                }
                best := answer{waves: g.n + 1}
                var pick func(k int, chosen uint64, count int)
                pick = func(k int, chosen uint64, count int) {
                        if count == limit || k == len(ready) {
                                if chosen == 0 {
                                        return
                                }
                                if count < limit && !g.maximal(ready, chosen) {
                                        return
                                }
                                if w := 1 + solve(done|chosen); w < best.waves {
                                        best = answer{w, chosen}
                                }
                                return
                        }
                        i := ready[k]
                        fits := true
                        for j := range g.n {
                                if chosen&(1<<j) != 0 && g.conflict[i][j] {
                                        fits = false
                                        break
                                }
                        }
                        if fits {
                                pick(k+1, chosen|1<<i, count+1)
                        }
                        pick(k+1, chosen, count)
                }
                pick(0, 0, 0)
                memo[done] = best
                return best.waves
        }
        solve(0)
        var waves [][]int
        for done := uint64(0); done != all; {
                next := memo[done].next
                var wave []int
                for _, i := range order {
                        if next&(1<<i) != 0 {
                                wave = append(wave, i)
                        }
                }
                waves = append(waves, wave)
                done |= next
        }
        return waves
}

// maximal reports whether no ready job could be added to this set.
func (g *graph) maximal(ready []int, chosen uint64) bool {
        for _, i := range ready {
                if chosen&(1<<i) != 0 {
                        continue
                }
                fits := true
                for j := range g.n {
                        if chosen&(1<<j) != 0 && g.conflict[i][j] {
                                fits = false
                                break
                        }
                }
                if fits {
                        return false
                }
        }
        return true
}

// lowerBound is a number of waves no schedule can beat, which can prove a greedy one optimal.
func (g *graph) lowerBound(limit int) int {
        chain := make([]int, g.n)
        var depth func(i int) int
        depth = func(i int) int {
                if chain[i] != 0 {
                        return chain[i]
                }
                d := 1
                for _, x := range g.dependent[i] {
                        d = max(d, 1+depth(x))
                }
                chain[i] = d
                return d
        }
        best := (g.n + limit - 1) / limit
        for i := range g.n {
                best = max(best, depth(i))
        }
        // Jobs that all conflict with one another need a wave each.
        var clique []int
        for _, i := range g.order() {
                if !slices.ContainsFunc(clique, func(c int) bool { return !g.conflict[i][c] }) {
                        clique = append(clique, i)
                }
        }
        return max(best, len(clique))
}

func makePlan(ps []parsed, level Granularity, limit int) (*Plan, error) {
        g, conflicts, err := build(ps, level)
        if err != nil {
                return nil, err
        }
        p := &Plan{Granularity: level, Conflicts: conflicts, Max: limit, Writes: map[string][]string{}}
        var waves [][]int
        if g.n <= ExactLimit {
                waves, p.Method, p.Optimal = g.exact(limit), "exact", true
        } else {
                waves, p.Method = g.greedy(limit), "greedy"
                p.Optimal = len(waves) == g.lowerBound(limit)
        }
        for n, w := range waves {
                ids := make([]string, len(w))
                for i, j := range w {
                        ids[i] = g.ids[j]
                }
                slices.Sort(ids)
                p.Waves = append(p.Waves, Wave{N: n + 1, Jobs: ids})
        }
        p.Verdict = "sequential"
        if len(p.Waves) < g.n {
                p.Verdict = "parallel"
        }
        for _, x := range ps {
                p.Writes[x.job.ID] = x.job.Touches
                if x.alone {
                        p.Alone = append(p.Alone, x.job.ID)
                }
        }
        return p, nil
}

// Schedule plans the jobs. Auto uses the coarser of directory and file level that loses no
// parallelism, and never goes below whole files. Two subagents in one file can overwrite each
// other, and a symbol is only a name someone wrote down: a real model, told to split one file,
// made up symbols to fit. So working inside one file has to be asked for by name.
func Schedule(in Input) (*Plan, error) {
        ps, err := parse(in.Jobs)
        if err != nil {
                return nil, err
        }
        limit := in.Max
        if limit <= 0 {
                limit = 4
        }
        level := in.Granularity
        switch level {
        case "":
                level = Auto
        case Auto, Repo, Dir, File, Symbol:
        default:
                return nil, fmt.Errorf("granularity %q: use repo, dir, file, symbol or auto", level)
        }
        if level != Auto {
                return makePlan(ps, level, limit)
        }
        finest, err := makePlan(ps, File, limit)
        if err != nil {
                return nil, err
        }
        coarse, err := makePlan(ps, Dir, limit)
        if err != nil {
                return nil, err
        }
        tried := map[Granularity]int{File: len(finest.Waves), Dir: len(coarse.Waves)}
        best := finest
        if len(coarse.Waves) <= len(finest.Waves) {
                best = coarse
        }
        best.Tried = tried
        return best, nil
}

// CheckClaims confirms that the parts of files a plan relies on exist. It catches a claim made
// up to fit, such as a symbol that appears nowhere in the file. A file that does not exist yet
// passes, since a job may be creating it. It says nothing about whether a job stays inside.
func CheckClaims(dir string, jobs []Job) error {
        for _, j := range jobs {
                for _, s := range append(slices.Clone(j.Touches), j.Reads...) {
                        c, err := parseClaim(s)
                        if err != nil {
                                return err
                        }
                        if c.symbol == "" && c.from == 0 {
                                continue
                        }
                        raw, _, _ := strings.Cut(strings.ReplaceAll(s, `\`, "/"), "#")
                        if m := linesRE.FindStringSubmatch(raw); m != nil {
                                raw = m[1]
                        }
                        b, err := os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(dir, filepath.FromSlash(raw)))
                        if errors.Is(err, os.ErrNotExist) {
                                continue
                        }
                        if err != nil {
                                return fmt.Errorf("job %s: %w", j.ID, err)
                        }
                        if c.symbol != "" && !bytes.Contains(b, []byte(c.symbol)) {
                                return fmt.Errorf("job %s claims %s, but %q appears nowhere in that file", j.ID, s, c.symbol)
                        }
                        if lines := bytes.Count(b, []byte("\n")) + 1; c.to > lines {
                                return fmt.Errorf("job %s claims %s, but that file has %d lines", j.ID, s, lines)
                        }
                }
        }
        return nil
}

package parallel

import (
        "bytes"
        "errors"
        "fmt"
        "os"
        "os/exec"
        "path/filepath"
        "slices"
        "strings"
)

func git(dir string, env []string, args ...string) (string, error) {
        c := exec.Command("git", args...)
        c.Dir = dir
        c.Env = append(os.Environ(), env...)
        var out, errb bytes.Buffer
        c.Stdout, c.Stderr = &out, &errb
        if err := c.Run(); err != nil {
                return "", fmt.Errorf("git %s: %w: %s", args[0], err, strings.TrimSpace(errb.String()))
        }
        return strings.TrimSpace(out.String()), nil
}

// Snapshot records the state of the working tree, including uncommitted and new files, and
