// returns a name for it. It uses a private index, so the real staging area is left untouched,
// and it makes no commit and moves no branch.
func Snapshot(dir string) (string, error) {
        idx, err := git(dir, nil, "rev-parse", "--path-format=absolute", "--git-path", "index")
        if err != nil {
                return "", err
        }
        tmp, err := os.CreateTemp("", "aiculator-index-*")
        if err != nil {
                return "", err
        }
        name := tmp.Name()
        tmp.Close()
        defer os.Remove(name)
        defer os.Remove(name + ".lock")
        // Starting from the real index means only changed files have to be read again.
        if b, err := os.ReadFile(idx); err == nil {
                if err := os.WriteFile(name, b, 0o600); err != nil {
                        return "", err
                }
        } else if errors.Is(err, os.ErrNotExist) {
                os.Remove(name)
        } else {
                return "", err
        }
        env := []string{"GIT_INDEX_FILE=" + name}
        if _, err := git(dir, env, "add", "-A"); err != nil {
                return "", err
        }
        return git(dir, env, "write-tree")
}

// Report says what a wave really did.
type Report struct {
        OK bool `json:"ok"`
        // Changed lists every file that differs since the snapshot.
        Changed []string `json:"changed"`
        // Unclaimed lists files no job in this wave was allowed to change.
        Unclaimed []string `json:"unclaimed,omitempty"`
        // Idle lists jobs that changed nothing, which may mean a subagent did not do its work.
        Idle []string `json:"idle,omitempty"`
        // Note says what this check cannot see.
        Note string `json:"note"`
}

const verifyNote = "Checked per file, so it cannot tell which job in a wave changed a file, or whether a job stayed inside a symbol or line range. Files ignored by git are not seen."

// Verify compares the working tree with a snapshot taken before a wave began, and reports any
// change that the wave's jobs did not claim.
func Verify(dir string, plan *Plan, wave int, since string) (*Report, error) {
        if wave < 1 || wave > len(plan.Waves) {
                return nil, fmt.Errorf("the plan has waves 1 to %d, not %d", len(plan.Waves), wave)
        }
        now, err := Snapshot(dir)
        if err != nil {
                return nil, err
        }
        out, err := git(dir, nil, "diff-tree", "-r", "--name-only", "--no-renames", since, now)
        if err != nil {
                return nil, fmt.Errorf("comparing with snapshot %s: %w", since, err)
        }
        r := &Report{OK: true, Note: verifyNote, Changed: []string{}}
        if out != "" {
                r.Changed = strings.Split(out, "\n")
        }
        type claimOf struct {
                job string
                c   claim
        }
        var claims []claimOf
        jobs := plan.Waves[wave-1].Jobs
        for _, id := range jobs {
                for _, s := range plan.Writes[id] {
                        c, err := parseClaim(s)
                        if err != nil {
                                return nil, err
                        }
                        claims = append(claims, claimOf{id, c})
                }
        }
        busy := map[string]bool{}
        for _, f := range r.Changed {
                lower := strings.ToLower(filepath.ToSlash(f))
                claimed := false
                for _, c := range claims {
                        if pathsOverlap(c.c.path, lower) && (c.c.path == lower || c.c.isDir || c.c.path == ".") {
                                claimed = true
                                busy[c.job] = true
                        }
                }
                if !claimed {
                        r.Unclaimed = append(r.Unclaimed, f)
                }
        }
        for _, id := range jobs {
                if !busy[id] {
                        r.Idle = append(r.Idle, id)
                }
        }
        slices.Sort(r.Idle)
        r.OK = len(r.Unclaimed) == 0
        return r, nil
}

// Package prompt asks questions in a terminal: yes or no, one choice, or several. In a real
// terminal it uses arrow keys and checkboxes. When input is piped it reads plain lines, so
// scripts and tests get the same questions.
package prompt

import (
        "bufio"
        "errors"
        "fmt"
        "io"
        "os"
        "strconv"
        "strings"

        "golang.org/x/term"
)

// ErrCanceled means the person backed out, with Ctrl-C, Esc or q.
var ErrCanceled = errors.New("canceled")

// ErrNoInput means input ended before an answer came, as in a script with nothing piped in.
var ErrNoInput = errors.New("no answer: input ended")

// Option is one choice.
type Option struct {
        Label    string
        Detail   string // Shown dimmed, after the label.
        Selected bool   // Checked at the start, in a multi-select.
}

// Prompter asks questions on one input and output.
type Prompter struct {
        in  io.Reader
        out io.Writer
        // keys means read single keys. Otherwise it reads whole lines.
        keys  bool
        color bool
        lines *bufio.Reader
        raw   func() (restore func(), err error)
        // pending holds keys read after the last question ended. Fast typing or a paste delivers
        // several at once, and those are the answers to the questions that come next.
        pending []key
}

// New returns a prompter, using keys only when both ends are a real terminal.
func New(in, out *os.File) *Prompter {
        p := &Prompter{in: in, out: out, lines: bufio.NewReader(in)}
        if term.IsTerminal(int(in.Fd())) && term.IsTerminal(int(out.Fd())) {
                p.keys = true
                p.color = os.Getenv("NO_COLOR") == "" && os.Getenv("TERM") != "dumb"
                p.raw = func() (func(), error) {
                        st, err := term.MakeRaw(int(in.Fd()))
                        if err != nil {
                                return nil, err
                        }
                        return func() { _ = term.Restore(int(in.Fd()), st) }, nil
                }
        }
        return p
}

// Lines returns a prompter that reads plain lines.
func Lines(in io.Reader, out io.Writer) *Prompter {
        return &Prompter{in: in, out: out, lines: bufio.NewReader(in)}
}

func (p *Prompter) style(code, s string) string {
        if !p.color {
                return s
        }
        return "\x1b[" + code + "m" + s + "\x1b[0m"
}

// Say prints a line of explanation.
func (p *Prompter) Say(format string, args ...any) {
        fmt.Fprintf(p.out, format+"\n", args...)
}

func (p *Prompter) readLine() (string, error) {
        s, err := p.lines.ReadString('\n')
        if err != nil && s == "" {
                if errors.Is(err, io.EOF) {
                        return "", ErrNoInput
                }
                return "", err
        }
        return strings.TrimSpace(s), nil
}

// Confirm asks a yes or no question. Enter takes the default.
func (p *Prompter) Confirm(question string, def bool) (bool, error) {
        hint := "y/N"
        if def {
                hint = "Y/n"
        }
        if p.keys {
                return p.confirmKeys(question, hint, def)
        }
        for {
                fmt.Fprintf(p.out, "? %s (%s) ", question, hint)
                s, err := p.readLine()
                if err != nil {
                        return false, err
                }
                fmt.Fprintln(p.out)
                switch strings.ToLower(s) {
                case "":
                        return def, nil
                case "y", "yes":
                        return true, nil
                case "n", "no":
                        return false, nil
                }
                p.Say("  Please answer y or n.")
        }
}

func (p *Prompter) word(b bool) string {
        if b {
                return "yes"
        }
        return "no"
}

func (p *Prompter) confirmKeys(question, hint string, def bool) (bool, error) {
        fmt.Fprintf(p.out, "%s %s %s ", p.style("36", "?"), p.style("1", question), p.style("2", "("+hint+")"))
        var answer bool
        err := p.withKeys(func(k key) (bool, error) {
                switch k {
                case keyEnter:
                        answer = def
                case keyYes:
                        answer = true
                case keyNo:
                        answer = false
                case keyCancel:
                        return true, ErrCanceled
                default:
                        return false, nil
                }
                return true, nil
        })
        if err != nil {
                fmt.Fprint(p.out, "\r\n")
                return false, err
        }
        fmt.Fprintf(p.out, "%s\n", p.style("36", p.word(answer)))
        return answer, nil
}

// Select asks for exactly one choice.
func (p *Prompter) Select(question string, options []Option, def int) (int, error) {
        if !p.keys {
                return p.selectLines(question, options, def)
        }
        cursor := def
        drawn := 0
        draw := func() {
                p.clear(drawn)
                drawn = p.drawList(question, p.style("2", "(arrows, Enter)"), options, cursor, nil)
        }
        draw()
        err := p.withKeys(func(k key) (bool, error) {
                switch k {
                case keyUp:
                        cursor = (cursor - 1 + len(options)) % len(options)
                case keyDown:
                        cursor = (cursor + 1) % len(options)
                case keyEnter:
                        return true, nil
                case keyCancel:
                        return true, ErrCanceled
                default:
                        return false, nil
                }
                draw()
                return false, nil
        })
        p.clear(drawn)
        if err != nil {
                return 0, err
        }
        fmt.Fprintf(p.out, "%s %s %s\n", p.style("36", "?"), p.style("1", question), p.style("36", options[cursor].Label))
        return cursor, nil
}

// MultiSelect asks for any number of choices, and returns their positions in order.
func (p *Prompter) MultiSelect(question string, options []Option) ([]int, error) {
        if !p.keys {
                return p.multiLines(question, options)
        }
        checked := make([]bool, len(options))
        for i, o := range options {
                checked[i] = o.Selected
        }
        cursor, drawn := 0, 0
        draw := func() {
                p.clear(drawn)
                drawn = p.drawList(question, p.style("2", "(arrows, Space to toggle, a for all, Enter)"), options, cursor, checked)
        }
        draw()
        err := p.withKeys(func(k key) (bool, error) {
                switch k {
                case keyUp:
                        cursor = (cursor - 1 + len(options)) % len(options)
                case keyDown:
                        cursor = (cursor + 1) % len(options)
                case keySpace:
                        checked[cursor] = !checked[cursor]
                case keyAll:
                        all := true
                        for _, c := range checked {
                                all = all && c
                        }
                        for i := range checked {
                                checked[i] = !all
                        }
                case keyEnter:
                        return true, nil
                case keyCancel:
                        return true, ErrCanceled
                default:
                        return false, nil
                }
                draw()
                return false, nil
        })
        p.clear(drawn)
        if err != nil {
                return nil, err
        }
        var out []int
        var names []string
        for i, c := range checked {
                if c {
                        out = append(out, i)
                        names = append(names, options[i].Label)
                }
        }
        summary := strings.Join(names, ", ")
        if summary == "" {
                summary = "none"
        }
        fmt.Fprintf(p.out, "%s %s %s\n", p.style("36", "?"), p.style("1", question), p.style("36", summary))
        return out, nil
}

// clear removes what was drawn, which is n lines above the cursor.
func (p *Prompter) clear(n int) {
        if n > 0 {
                fmt.Fprintf(p.out, "\x1b[%dA\r\x1b[J", n)
        }
}

// drawList writes the question and options, and returns how many lines that took. It uses
// \r\n because the terminal is in raw mode, and cuts lines to fit, because a wrapped line
// would throw off the count that the next redraw depends on.
func (p *Prompter) drawList(question, hint string, options []Option, cursor int, checked []bool) int {
        width := 100
        if f, ok := p.out.(*os.File); ok {
                if w, _, err := term.GetSize(int(f.Fd())); err == nil && w > 10 {
                        width = w
                }
        }
        fmt.Fprintf(p.out, "%s %s %s\r\n", p.style("36", "?"), p.style("1", question), hint)
        for i, o := range options {
                mark := " "
                if i == cursor {
                        mark = p.style("36", ">")
                }
                box := ""
                if checked != nil {
                        box = "[ ] "
                        if checked[i] {
                                box = p.style("32", "[x]") + " "
                        }
                }
                text := o.Label
                room := width - 8 - len(o.Label)
                detail := o.Detail
                if len(detail) > room {
                        detail = detail[:max(room, 0)]
                }
                if detail != "" {
                        text += "  " + p.style("2", detail)
                }
                fmt.Fprintf(p.out, "%s %s%s\r\n", mark, box, text)
        }
        return len(options) + 1
}

type key int

const (
        keyNone key = iota
        keyUp
        keyDown
        keySpace
        keyEnter
        keyAll
        keyYes
        keyNo
        keyCancel
)

// parseKeys splits one read into keys. Fast typing or a paste can deliver several at once. An
// arrow's bytes arrive together, which is what tells it apart from a lone Esc.
func parseKeys(b []byte) []key {
        var out []key
        for len(b) > 0 {
                if b[0] == 0x1b && len(b) >= 3 && (b[1] == '[' || b[1] == 'O') {
                        switch b[2] {
                        case 'A':
                                out = append(out, keyUp)
                        case 'B':
                                out = append(out, keyDown)
                        default:
                                out = append(out, keyNone)
                        }
                        b = b[3:]
                        continue
                }
                switch b[0] {
                case 'k':
                        out = append(out, keyUp)
                case 'j':
                        out = append(out, keyDown)
                case ' ':
                        out = append(out, keySpace)
                case '\r', '\n':
                        out = append(out, keyEnter)
                case 'a', 'A':
                        out = append(out, keyAll)
                case 'y', 'Y':
                        out = append(out, keyYes)
                case 'n', 'N':
                        out = append(out, keyNo)
                case 0x03, 0x1b, 'q', 'Q':
                        out = append(out, keyCancel)
                default:
                        out = append(out, keyNone)
                }
                b = b[1:]
        }
        return out
}

// withKeys hands each key to fn until it says it has finished, with the terminal in raw
// mode and the cursor hidden. The terminal is put back however this ends.
func (p *Prompter) withKeys(fn func(key) (bool, error)) error {
        if p.raw != nil {
                restore, err := p.raw()
                if err != nil {
                        return err
                }
                defer restore()
        }
        fmt.Fprint(p.out, "\x1b[?25l")
        defer fmt.Fprint(p.out, "\x1b[?25h")
        buf := make([]byte, 64)
        for {
                for len(p.pending) > 0 {
                        k := p.pending[0]
                        p.pending = p.pending[1:]
                        done, ferr := fn(k)
                        if done || ferr != nil {
                                return ferr
                        }
                }
                n, err := p.in.Read(buf)
                p.pending = append(p.pending, parseKeys(buf[:n])...)
                if err != nil && len(p.pending) == 0 {
                        if errors.Is(err, io.EOF) {
                                return ErrNoInput
                        }
                        return err
                }
        }
}

func (p *Prompter) printNumbered(options []Option, checked []bool) {
        for i, o := range options {
                box := ""
                if checked != nil {
                        box = "[ ] "
                        if checked[i] {
                                box = "[x] "
                        }
                }
                line := fmt.Sprintf("  %d. %s%s", i+1, box, o.Label)
                if o.Detail != "" {
                        line += "  " + o.Detail
                }
                p.Say("%s", line)
        }
}

func (p *Prompter) selectLines(question string, options []Option, def int) (int, error) {
        p.Say("? %s", question)
        p.printNumbered(options, nil)
        for {
                fmt.Fprintf(p.out, "Number (%d): ", def+1)
                s, err := p.readLine()
                if err != nil {
                        return 0, err
                }
                fmt.Fprintln(p.out)
                if s == "" {
                        return def, nil
                }
                if n, err := strconv.Atoi(s); err == nil && n >= 1 && n <= len(options) {
                        return n - 1, nil
                }
                p.Say("  Please give a number from 1 to %d.", len(options))
        }
}

func (p *Prompter) multiLines(question string, options []Option) ([]int, error) {
        checked := make([]bool, len(options))
        for i, o := range options {
                checked[i] = o.Selected
        }
        p.Say("? %s", question)
        p.printNumbered(options, checked)
        for {
                fmt.Fprint(p.out, "Numbers such as 1,3, or all or none (Enter keeps the marked ones): ")
                s, err := p.readLine()
                if err != nil {
                        return nil, err
                }
                fmt.Fprintln(p.out)
                out, ok := parseChoices(s, len(options), checked)
                if ok {
                        return out, nil
                }
                p.Say("  Please give numbers from 1 to %d.", len(options))
        }
}

func parseChoices(s string, n int, checked []bool) ([]int, bool) {
        out := []int{}
        switch strings.ToLower(s) {
        case "":
                for i, c := range checked {
                        if c {
                                out = append(out, i)
                        }
                }
                return out, true
        case "none":
                return out, true
        case "all":
                for i := range n {
                        out = append(out, i)
                }
                return out, true
        }
        seen := make([]bool, n)
        for _, part := range strings.FieldsFunc(s, func(r rune) bool { return r == ',' || r == ' ' }) {
                v, err := strconv.Atoi(part)
                if err != nil || v < 1 || v > n {
                        return nil, false
                }
                seen[v-1] = true
        }
        for i, on := range seen {
                if on {
                        out = append(out, i)
                }
        }
        return out, true
}

// Package realm gives each project on a machine a name, and a way to see them all together.
//
// A realm is one project with its own server and its own store. They are deliberately not
// merged into one server: one crash or one damaged store stays in one project, and a token
// from one project is refused by every other, since each signs with its own key. This
// package is only a directory of them, plus a read-only view across them.
package realm

import (
        "context"
        "crypto/sha256"
        "encoding/hex"
        "encoding/json"
        "errors"
        "fmt"
        "os"
        "path/filepath"
        "regexp"
        "slices"
        "strings"
        "sync"
        "time"

        "github.com/Grano22/aiculator/internal/client"
        "github.com/Grano22/aiculator/pkg/observe"
)

// Realm is one project in the directory. It holds no secrets: a realm's tokens stay in its
// own data directory.
type Realm struct {
        Name    string    `json:"name"`
        Path    string    `json:"path"`
        DataDir string    `json:"data_dir"`
        Created time.Time `json:"created"`
}

// ErrNotFound means no realm has that name.
var ErrNotFound = errors.New("no such realm")

// Dir is where the directory lives. Each realm is one file, written atomically, so that
// servers starting at the same moment cannot damage each other's entries.
func Dir() string {
        if d := os.Getenv("AICULATOR_REALMS"); d != "" {
                return d
        }
        home, err := os.UserHomeDir()
        if err != nil {
                return ""
        }
        return filepath.Join(home, ".aiculator", "realms")
}

// Instance identifies a server by its data directory, so that a client can tell its own
// server from another project's that took over the same port after a crash.
func Instance(dataDir string) string {
        h := sha256.Sum256([]byte(dataDir))
        return hex.EncodeToString(h[:8])
}

func fileFor(dataDir string) string { return filepath.Join(Dir(), Instance(dataDir)+".json") }

var (
        nameRE   = regexp.MustCompile(`^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9._-]{0,63}$`)
        unsafeRE = regexp.MustCompile(`[^a-z0-9._-]+`)
)

func slug(path string) string {
        s := strings.Trim(unsafeRE.ReplaceAllString(strings.ToLower(filepath.Base(path)), "-"), "-._")
        if s == "" {
                s = "project"
        }
        if len(s) > 48 {
                s = s[:48]
        }
        return s
}

// List returns every realm, sorted by name. A damaged entry is skipped, not fatal.
func List() ([]Realm, error) {
        dir := Dir()
        if dir == "" {
                return nil, nil
        }
        entries, err := os.ReadDir(dir)
        if errors.Is(err, os.ErrNotExist) {
                return nil, nil
        }
        if err != nil {
                return nil, err
        }
        out := make([]Realm, 0, len(entries))
        for _, e := range entries {
                if !strings.HasSuffix(e.Name(), ".json") {
                        continue
                }
                b, err := os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(dir, e.Name()))
                if err != nil {
                        continue
                }
                var r Realm
                if json.Unmarshal(b, &r) == nil && r.Name != "" && r.DataDir != "" {
                        out = append(out, r)
                }
        }
        slices.SortFunc(out, func(a, b Realm) int { return strings.Compare(a.Name, b.Name) })
        return out, nil
}

func write(r Realm) error {
        if err := os.MkdirAll(Dir(), 0o700); err != nil {
                return err
        }
        b, err := json.MarshalIndent(r, "", "  ")
        if err != nil {
                return err
        }
        tmp, err := os.CreateTemp(Dir(), ".realm-*")
        if err != nil {
                return err
        }
        defer os.Remove(tmp.Name())
        if _, err := tmp.Write(b); err != nil {
                tmp.Close()
                return err
        }
        if err := tmp.Close(); err != nil {
                return err
        }
        return os.Rename(tmp.Name(), fileFor(r.DataDir))
}

// Register records a project, and returns its realm. A project keeps the name it has. A new
// one is named after its folder, with a short suffix if another project has that name.
func Register(path, dataDir string) (Realm, error) {
        all, err := List()
        if err != nil {
                return Realm{}, err
        }
        if i := slices.IndexFunc(all, func(r Realm) bool { return r.DataDir == dataDir }); i >= 0 {
                return all[i], nil
        }
        name := slug(path)
        if slices.ContainsFunc(all, func(r Realm) bool { return r.Name == name }) {
                name += "-" + Instance(dataDir)[:4]
        }
        r := Realm{Name: name, Path: path, DataDir: dataDir, Created: time.Now().UTC()}
        return r, write(r)
}

// Get finds a realm by name.
func Get(name string) (Realm, error) {
        all, err := List()
        if err != nil {
                return Realm{}, err
        }
        names := make([]string, 0, len(all))
        for _, r := range all {
                if r.Name == name {
                        return r, nil
                }
                names = append(names, r.Name)
        }
        if len(names) == 0 {
                return Realm{}, fmt.Errorf("%w: %q, and none exist yet; a project becomes one when its server starts", ErrNotFound, name)
        }
        return Realm{}, fmt.Errorf("%w: %q; these exist: %s", ErrNotFound, name, strings.Join(names, ", "))
}

// Rename gives a realm a new name.
func Rename(from, to string) error {
        if !nameRE.MatchString(to) {
                return fmt.Errorf("realm name %q: use lowercase letters, digits, dots, dashes and underscores", to)
        }
        r, err := Get(from)
        if err != nil {
                return err
        }
        if _, err := Get(to); err == nil {
                return fmt.Errorf("a realm named %s already exists", to)
        }
        r.Name = to
        return write(r)
}

// Forget removes a realm from the directory. The project and its data stay, and it comes
// back the next time its server starts.
func Forget(name string) error {
        r, err := Get(name)
        if err != nil {
                return err
        }
        return os.Remove(fileFor(r.DataDir))
}

// View is what one realm looks like right now.
type View struct {
        Realm    Realm             `json:"realm"`
        Live     bool              `json:"live"`
        Missing  bool              `json:"missing,omitempty"` // Its folder is gone.
        Error    string            `json:"error,omitempty"`
        Snapshot *observe.Snapshot `json:"snapshot,omitempty"`
        // Link opens this realm's own dashboard, when asked for.
        Link string `json:"link,omitempty"`
}

// Local connects to a realm's server as its owner, using the files in its data directory.
func Local(r Realm) (*client.Client, error) {
        addr, err := os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(r.DataDir, "addr"))
        if err != nil {
                return nil, errors.New("not running")
        }
        tok, err := os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(r.DataDir, "admin.token"))
        if err != nil {
                return nil, errors.New("not running")
        }
        return client.New(strings.TrimSpace(string(addr)), strings.TrimSpace(string(tok))), nil
}

// perRealm bounds how long one stuck server can hold up the view of all the others.
const perRealm = 2 * time.Second

// Gather reads every realm at once. A realm that is down shows as down, and never delays or
// fails the rest. Each server checks the token itself, so a stale address that now reaches
// another project's server gets a refusal, and the realm shows as not running.
func Gather(ctx context.Context, each func(context.Context, Realm, *View)) ([]View, error) {
        all, err := List()
        if err != nil {
                return nil, err
        }
        out := make([]View, len(all))
        var wg sync.WaitGroup
        for i, r := range all {
                out[i].Realm = r
                if _, err := os.Stat(r.Path); err != nil {
                        out[i].Missing = true
                        continue
                }
                wg.Go(func() {
                        c, cancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, perRealm)
                        defer cancel()
                        cl, err := Local(r)
                        if err != nil {
                                out[i].Error = err.Error()
                                return
                        }
                        var s observe.Snapshot
                        if err := cl.Get(c, "/v1/observe", &s); err != nil {
                                out[i].Error = "not running"
                                return
                        }
                        out[i].Live, out[i].Snapshot = true, &s
                        if each != nil {
                                each(c, r, &out[i])
                        }
                })
        }
        wg.Wait()
        return out, nil
}

// Package sandbox runs commands with restricted file and network access. Running
// unsandboxed must be asked for by name; there is no silent fallback to it.
package sandbox

import (
        "context"
        "errors"
        "fmt"
        "os"
        "os/exec"
        "path/filepath"
        "runtime"
        "strings"

        "github.com/Grano22/aiculator/internal/vlog"
)

// Spec describes one sandboxed command.
type Spec struct {
        Dir        string   // Working directory; always writable.
        Argv       []string // Command and arguments.
        WritePaths []string // Extra writable paths.
        Network    bool     // Whether network access is allowed.
        Hide       []string // Paths the command may not read at all, such as secrets.
        Env        []string // Complete environment. The parent's is never inherited.
}

// Sandbox builds a command that runs under some isolation.
type Sandbox interface {
        Name() string
        Command(ctx context.Context, s Spec) (*exec.Cmd, error)
}

// Open returns the named sandbox. "auto" picks the native one for this platform
// and fails if there is none, rather than running without isolation.
func Open(name string) (Sandbox, error) {
        switch name {
        case "auto":
                switch runtime.GOOS {
                case "linux":
                        if _, err := exec.LookPath("bwrap"); err == nil {
                                return Bubblewrap{}, nil
                        }
                case "darwin":
                        if _, err := exec.LookPath("sandbox-exec"); err == nil {
                                return Seatbelt{}, nil
                        }
                }
                if _, err := exec.LookPath("docker"); err == nil {
                        return Docker{Image: DefaultDockerImage}, nil
                }
                return nil, errors.New("no sandbox available: install bubblewrap or Docker, or pass --sandbox none to accept the risk")
        case "seatbelt":
                return Seatbelt{}, nil
        case "bwrap":
                return Bubblewrap{}, nil
        case "docker":
                return Docker{Image: DefaultDockerImage}, nil
        case "none":
                return None{}, nil
        }
        return nil, fmt.Errorf("unknown sandbox %q", name)
}

// BaseEnv is a minimal environment holding no credentials from the parent.
func BaseEnv(home string) []string {
        return []string{
                "PATH=" + os.Getenv("PATH"),
                "HOME=" + home,
                "TMPDIR=" + filepath.Join(home, ".tmp"),
                "LANG=C.UTF-8",
        }
}

// SecretHome lists credential stores in the home directory. Harnesses that use the
// real home for their own login still have no reason to read these.
func SecretHome() []string {
        home, err := os.UserHomeDir()
        if err != nil {
                return nil
        }
        var out []string
        for _, d := range []string{".aiculator", ".ssh", ".aws", ".gnupg", ".kube", ".docker/config.json", ".netrc", ".config/gh", ".config/gcloud"} {
                out = append(out, filepath.Join(home, d))
        }
        return out
}

func finish(ctx context.Context, s Spec, argv []string) *exec.Cmd {
        if v := vlog.For("sandbox").V(vlog.LevelTrace); v.Enabled() {
                v.Info("sandbox command", "argv", argv, "dir", s.Dir)
        } else if v := vlog.For("sandbox").V(vlog.LevelDebug); v.Enabled() {
                v.Info("sandbox command", "program", s.Argv, "dir", s.Dir, "network", s.Network)
        }
        c := exec.CommandContext(ctx, argv[0], argv[1:]...)
        c.Dir = s.Dir
        c.Env = s.Env
        if c.Env == nil {
                c.Env = []string{} // A nil Env would inherit the parent's, secrets included.
        }
        return c
}

func validate(s Spec) (string, error) {
        if len(s.Argv) == 0 {
                return "", errors.New("sandbox: empty command")
        }
        if s.Dir == "" {
                return "", errors.New("sandbox: empty directory")
        }
        return realPath(s.Dir), nil
}

// realPath resolves symlinks, because Seatbelt matches resolved paths: on macOS
// /tmp and /var are symlinks into /private.
func realPath(p string) string {
        abs, err := filepath.Abs(p)
        if err != nil {
                return p
        }
        if r, err := filepath.EvalSymlinks(abs); err == nil {
                return r
        }
        return abs
}

// None provides no isolation. It exists for trusted setups and is never chosen
// automatically.
type None struct{}

// Name implements Sandbox.
func (None) Name() string { return "none" }

// Command implements Sandbox.
func (None) Command(ctx context.Context, s Spec) (*exec.Cmd, error) {
        if _, err := validate(s); err != nil {
                return nil, err
        }
        return finish(ctx, s, s.Argv), nil
}

// Seatbelt uses macOS sandbox-exec. Apple marks it deprecated, though it still
// works; Docker is the alternative on macOS.
type Seatbelt struct{}

// Name implements Sandbox.
func (Seatbelt) Name() string { return "seatbelt" }

func seatbeltQuote(p string) string {
        return `"` + strings.NewReplacer(`\`, `\\`, `"`, `\"`).Replace(p) + `"`
}

// Profile returns the policy: reads allowed, writes only in the listed paths,
// and no network unless asked for.
func (Seatbelt) Profile(dir string, writes, hide []string, network bool) string {
        var b strings.Builder
        b.WriteString("(version 1)\n(allow default)\n(deny file-write*)\n")
        b.WriteString(`(allow file-write* (literal "/dev/null") (literal "/dev/zero") (literal "/dev/dtracehelper") (regex #"^/dev/tty") (regex #"^/dev/fd/"))` + "\n")
        for _, p := range append([]string{dir}, writes...) {
                b.WriteString("(allow file-write* (subpath " + seatbeltQuote(realPath(p)) + "))\n")
        }
        if !network {
                b.WriteString("(deny network*)\n")
        }
        // Last match wins in a profile, so these beat every allow above.
        for _, p := range hide {
                q := seatbeltQuote(realPath(p))
                b.WriteString("(deny file-read* file-write* (subpath " + q + "))\n")
        }
        return b.String()
}

// Command implements Sandbox.
func (x Seatbelt) Command(ctx context.Context, s Spec) (*exec.Cmd, error) {
        dir, err := validate(s)
        if err != nil {
                return nil, err
        }
        argv := append([]string{"sandbox-exec", "-p", x.Profile(dir, s.WritePaths, s.Hide, s.Network)}, s.Argv...)
        return finish(ctx, s, argv), nil
}

// Bubblewrap uses Linux namespaces, with a read-only root and new PID space.
type Bubblewrap struct{}

// Name implements Sandbox.
func (Bubblewrap) Name() string { return "bwrap" }

// Args returns the bwrap arguments, separated out so they can be tested anywhere.
func (Bubblewrap) Args(dir string, writes, hide []string, network bool, argv []string) []string {
        out := []string{"--ro-bind", "/", "/", "--dev", "/dev", "--proc", "/proc", "--tmpfs", "/tmp",
                "--unshare-pid", "--unshare-ipc", "--unshare-uts", "--die-with-parent", "--new-session"}
        if !network {
                out = append(out, "--unshare-net")
        }
        for _, p := range append([]string{dir}, writes...) {
                out = append(out, "--bind", p, p)
        }
        // /tmp is replaced by an empty one above, so a program installed under it would
        // vanish. Bind just that program back, read-only.
        if len(argv) > 0 && filepath.IsAbs(argv[0]) && strings.HasPrefix(filepath.Clean(argv[0]), "/tmp/") {
                out = append(out, "--ro-bind", argv[0], argv[0])
        }
        for _, p := range hide {
                fi, err := os.Stat(p)
                switch {
                case err != nil:
                        // Nothing there to hide.
                case fi.IsDir():
                        out = append(out, "--tmpfs", p)
                default:
                        out = append(out, "--ro-bind", "/dev/null", p)
                }
        }
        out = append(out, "--chdir", dir, "--")
        return append(out, argv...)
}

// Command implements Sandbox.
func (x Bubblewrap) Command(ctx context.Context, s Spec) (*exec.Cmd, error) {
        dir, err := validate(s)
        if err != nil {
                return nil, err
        }
        return finish(ctx, s, append([]string{"bwrap"}, x.Args(dir, s.WritePaths, s.Hide, s.Network, s.Argv)...)), nil
}

// DefaultDockerImage has a shell and git; projects will usually set their own.
const DefaultDockerImage = "alpine/git:latest"

// Docker runs the command in a throwaway container. Spec.Hide needs no handling:
// a container sees only what is mounted, and nothing else is.
type Docker struct{ Image string }

// Name implements Sandbox.
func (Docker) Name() string { return "docker" }

// Args returns the docker arguments, separated out so they can be tested anywhere.
func (d Docker) Args(dir string, writes []string, network bool, env, argv []string) []string {
        out := []string{"run", "--rm", "-i", "--cap-drop=ALL", "--security-opt=no-new-privileges", "--workdir", dir}
        if !network {
                out = append(out, "--network=none")
        }
        for _, p := range append([]string{dir}, writes...) {
                out = append(out, "-v", p+":"+p)
        }
        for _, e := range env {
                if !strings.HasPrefix(e, "PATH=") { // PATH belongs to the image.
                        out = append(out, "-e", e)
                }
        }
        // Some utility images (including alpine/git) define a non-shell
        // entrypoint. Clear it so argv is always the command requested by the
        // caller rather than arguments to the image's default executable.
        out = append(out, "--entrypoint", "", d.Image)
        return append(out, argv...)
}

// Command implements Sandbox.
func (d Docker) Command(ctx context.Context, s Spec) (*exec.Cmd, error) {
        dir, err := validate(s)
        if err != nil {
                return nil, err
        }
        argv := append([]string{"docker"}, d.Args(dir, s.WritePaths, s.Network, s.Env, s.Argv)...)
        c := finish(ctx, Spec{Dir: dir, Env: []string{"PATH=" + os.Getenv("PATH"), "HOME=" + os.Getenv("HOME")}}, argv)
        return c, nil
}

package skillpack

import (
        "bytes"
        "errors"
        "fmt"
        "os"
        "path"
        "path/filepath"
        "regexp"
        "strings"
        "unicode/utf8"

        "go.yaml.in/yaml/v3"
)

// Issue levels. Errors break the Agent Skills spec and block installation. Warnings
// are portability risks. Info explains what a harness-specific field does.
const (
        LevelError = "error"
        LevelWarn  = "warn"
        LevelInfo  = "info"
)

// Issue is one finding.
type Issue struct {
        Level, Msg string
}

// IssuesHaveErrors reports whether any issue is an error.
func IssuesHaveErrors(list []Issue) bool {
        for _, i := range list {
                if i.Level == LevelError {
                        return true
                }
        }
        return false
}

var nameRE = regexp.MustCompile(`^[a-z0-9]+(-[a-z0-9]+)*$`)

// extras are fields outside the spec, with who honors them. They are fine in project
// skills, since other clients ignore unknown fields, but they are rejected by claude.ai
// uploads and the Skills API.
var extras = map[string]string{
        "disable-model-invocation": "Claude Code, Cursor and Pi; others may invoke the skill on their own, so also say when to use it in description",
        "when_to_use":              "Claude Code",
        "argument-hint":            "Claude Code",
        "arguments":                "Claude Code",
        "user-invocable":           "Claude Code",
        "disallowed-tools":         "Claude Code",
        "model":                    "Claude Code",
        "effort":                   "Claude Code",
        "context":                  "Claude Code",
        "agent":                    "Claude Code",
        "background":               "Claude Code",
        "hooks":                    "Claude Code",
        "shell":                    "Claude Code",
        "paths":                    "Claude Code and Cursor",
        "icon":                     "Cursor",
        "color":                    "Cursor",
}

var specFields = map[string]bool{
        "name": true, "description": true, "license": true,
        "compatibility": true, "metadata": true, "allowed-tools": true,
}

type frontmatter struct {
        raw  map[string]any
        meta map[string]any
        body string
}

func parseText(b []byte) (frontmatter, error) {
        s := string(bytes.TrimPrefix(b, []byte("\xef\xbb\xbf")))
        if !strings.HasPrefix(s, "---") {
                return frontmatter{}, errors.New("SKILL.md must start with --- frontmatter")
        }
        rest := s[3:]
        end := strings.Index(rest, "\n---")
        if end < 0 {
                return frontmatter{}, errors.New("frontmatter has no closing ---")
        }
        fm := frontmatter{raw: map[string]any{}}
        if err := yaml.Unmarshal([]byte(rest[:end]), &fm.raw); err != nil {
                return fm, fmt.Errorf("frontmatter is not valid YAML (a colon in an unquoted value is the usual cause): %w", err)
        }
        fm.meta, _ = fm.raw["metadata"].(map[string]any)
        fm.body = strings.TrimLeft(rest[end+4:], "\r\n")
        return fm, nil
}

func parseSkill(file string) (frontmatter, error) {
        b, err := os.ReadFile(file)
        if err != nil {
                return frontmatter{}, err
        }
        return parseText(b)
}

func parseBundled(name string) (frontmatter, error) {
        b, err := bundled.ReadFile(path.Join("skills", name, "SKILL.md"))
        if err != nil {
                return frontmatter{}, err
        }
        return parseText(b)
}

// Lint checks a skill directory against the Agent Skills specification.
func Lint(dir string) []Issue {
        var out []Issue
        add := func(level, format string, args ...any) {
                out = append(out, Issue{level, fmt.Sprintf(format, args...)})
        }
        fm, err := parseSkill(filepath.Join(dir, "SKILL.md"))
        if err != nil {
                add(LevelError, "%v", err)
                return out
        }

        name, _ := fm.raw["name"].(string)
        base := filepath.Base(dir)
        switch {
        case name == "":
                add(LevelError, "name is required")
        case len(name) > 64:
                add(LevelError, "name is over 64 characters")
        case !nameRE.MatchString(name):
                add(LevelError, "name %q may use only lowercase letters, numbers and single hyphens", name)
        case name != base:
                add(LevelError, "name %q must match its directory %q", name, base)
        }

        desc, _ := fm.raw["description"].(string)
        switch {
        case strings.TrimSpace(desc) == "":
                add(LevelError, "description is required")
        case utf8.RuneCountInString(desc) > 1024:
                add(LevelError, "description is over 1024 characters")
        case utf8.RuneCountInString(desc) < 40:
                add(LevelWarn, "description is very short; say what the skill does and when to use it")
        }
        if strings.Contains(desc, "TODO") {
                add(LevelWarn, "description still has a TODO")
        }
        when, _ := fm.raw["when_to_use"].(string)
        if utf8.RuneCountInString(desc)+utf8.RuneCountInString(when) > 1536 {
                add(LevelWarn, "Claude Code truncates description plus when_to_use past 1536 characters")
        }

        if v, ok := fm.raw["compatibility"]; ok {
                s, isStr := v.(string)
                if !isStr || s == "" || utf8.RuneCountInString(s) > 500 {
                        add(LevelError, "compatibility must be 1 to 500 characters")
                }
        }
        if v, ok := fm.raw["allowed-tools"]; ok {
                if _, isStr := v.(string); !isStr {
                        add(LevelError, "allowed-tools must be a space-separated string, not a list")
                }
        }
        if v, ok := fm.raw["metadata"]; ok {
                m, isMap := v.(map[string]any)
                if !isMap {
                        add(LevelError, "metadata must be a map")
                }
                for k, val := range m {
                        if _, isStr := val.(string); !isStr {
                                add(LevelError, "metadata.%s must be a string; quote it, as in version: \"1.0\"", k)
                        }
                }
                if _, ok := m["version"]; !ok {
                        add(LevelInfo, "metadata.version is not set")
                }
        } else {
                add(LevelInfo, "no metadata; a version helps track updates")
        }
        for k := range fm.raw {
                if specFields[k] {
                        continue
                }
                if who, known := extras[k]; known {
                        add(LevelInfo, "%s is honored by %s, ignored by other harnesses, and rejected by claude.ai uploads", k, who)
                } else {
                        add(LevelWarn, "unknown field %s; put your own data under metadata", k)
                }
        }
        if lines := strings.Count(fm.body, "\n") + 1; lines > 500 {
                add(LevelWarn, "body is %d lines; the spec recommends under 500, with details in references/", lines)
        }
        if strings.TrimSpace(fm.body) == "" {
                add(LevelWarn, "body is empty")
        }
        return out
}

// Package skillpack manages skills in one place. Skills live in .agents/skills, the
// cross-client convention from agentskills.io. Harnesses that scan it need nothing;
// the rest get a symlink, so there is never a second copy to keep in sync.
package skillpack

import (
        "embed"
        "errors"
        "fmt"
        "io/fs"
        "os"
        "path"
        "path/filepath"
        "runtime"
        "slices"
        "sort"
        "strings"

        "github.com/Grano22/aiculator/internal/harness"
)

//go:embed all:skills
var bundled embed.FS

// CanonicalDir is where skills live, relative to the project or home directory.
const CanonicalDir = ".agents/skills"

// aliasDir is also read as a source, for projects that use the singular name. Skills
// found there still reach .agents/skills, because that is the path harnesses scan.
const aliasDir = ".agent/skills"

// managedMarker identifies a copy this tool made, and so may replace or delete.
const managedMarker = ".aiculator-managed"

// Options configures an operation.
type Options struct {
        Root      string // Project directory.
        Home      string // Home directory; empty means the real one.
        Global    bool   // Use the home directory instead of the project.
        Patterns  []string
        Harnesses []harness.Harness
        Paths     []string // Extra target directories.
        Sources   []string // Extra source directories.
        Copy      bool     // Copy rather than link.
        Force     bool     // Replace links and managed copies, and refresh bundled skills.
        Purge     bool     // Uninstall also deletes the skill from .agents/skills.
}

func (o Options) base() string {
        if !o.Global {
                return o.Root
        }
        if o.Home != "" {
                return o.Home
        }
        home, err := os.UserHomeDir()
        if err != nil {
                return o.Root
        }
        return home
}

// Base is the directory the scope points at: the project, or home when global.
func (o Options) Base() string { return o.base() }

// Expand resolves a user-supplied path within the scope's project and home.
func (o Options) Expand(p string) string { return o.expand(p) }

func (o Options) canonical() string { return filepath.Join(o.base(), filepath.FromSlash(CanonicalDir)) }

func (o Options) expand(p string) string {
        if rest, ok := strings.CutPrefix(p, "~/"); ok {
                home := o.Home
                if home == "" {
                        home, _ = os.UserHomeDir()
                }
                return filepath.Join(home, rest)
        }
        if !filepath.IsAbs(p) {
                return filepath.Join(o.Root, p)
        }
        return p
}

// target is where a harness wants skills. Empty means it reads .agents/skills itself.
func (o Options) target(h harness.Harness) string {
        if o.Global {
                if h.ReadsGlobalAgents {
                        return ""
                }
                return o.expand(h.GlobalSkillsDir)
        }
        if h.ReadsAgents {
                return ""
        }
        return filepath.Join(o.Root, filepath.FromSlash(h.SkillsDir))
}

// HasGlobal reports whether a harness has a user-level place for skills at all.
func HasGlobal(h harness.Harness) bool { return h.ReadsGlobalAgents || h.GlobalSkillsDir != "" }

// Where says where a harness would find a skill, nearest first: "project", "global", or ""
// if it would not find it. It looks where that harness reads, not just that a copy exists.
func Where(name string, h harness.Harness, root string) string {
        found := func(o Options) bool {
                dir := o.target(h)
                if dir == "" {
                        dir = o.canonical()
                }
                _, err := os.Stat(filepath.Join(dir, name, "SKILL.md"))
                return err == nil
        }
        if found(Options{Root: root}) {
                return "project"
        }
        if HasGlobal(h) && found(Options{Root: root, Global: true}) {
                return "global"
        }
        return ""
}

// Action reports one thing an operation did.
type Action struct {
        Skill  string
        Target string
        What   string // created, kept, refreshed, linked, copied, ok, native, conflict, invalid, removed.
        Detail string
}

// available maps every known skill to its source directory; "" means bundled.
func (o Options) available() (map[string]string, error) {
        out := map[string]string{}
        entries, err := fs.ReadDir(bundled, "skills")
        if err != nil {
                return nil, err
        }
        for _, e := range entries {
                out[e.Name()] = ""
        }
        sources := []string{filepath.Join(o.base(), filepath.FromSlash(aliasDir)), o.canonical()}
        for _, s := range o.Sources {
                sources = append(sources, o.expand(s))
        }
        // Later sources win: a custom source beats .agents/skills, which beats .agent/skills.
        for _, dir := range sources {
                list, err := os.ReadDir(dir)
                if errors.Is(err, os.ErrNotExist) {
                        continue
                }
                if err != nil {
                        return nil, err
                }
                for _, e := range list {
                        p := filepath.Join(dir, e.Name())
                        if _, err := os.Stat(filepath.Join(p, "SKILL.md")); err == nil {
                                out[e.Name()] = p
                        }
                }
        }
        return out, nil
}

// Match returns the skills a pattern set selects. Patterns use shell wildcards:
// * for any run of characters, ? for one character, and [abc] for a set.
func Match(patterns, names []string) ([]string, error) {
        seen := map[string]bool{}
        for _, p := range patterns {
                matched := false
                for _, n := range names {
                        ok, err := path.Match(p, n)
                        if err != nil {
                                return nil, fmt.Errorf("bad pattern %q: %w", p, err)
                        }
                        if ok {
                                seen[n] = true
                                matched = true
                        }
                }
                if !matched {
                        return nil, fmt.Errorf("no skill matches %q; available: %s", p, strings.Join(names, ", "))
                }
        }
        out := make([]string, 0, len(seen))
        for n := range seen {
                out = append(out, n)
        }
        sort.Strings(out)
        return out, nil
}

// NormalizeShellStar undoes shell expansion. An unquoted * reaches the program as the
// list of files in the working directory, so when the arguments are exactly that
// list, the user meant "all". Anything else is left as written.
func NormalizeShellStar(args []string, dir string) []string {
        if len(args) < 2 {
                return args
        }
        entries, err := os.ReadDir(dir)
        if err != nil {
                return args
        }
        var visible []string
        for _, e := range entries {
                if !strings.HasPrefix(e.Name(), ".") {
                        visible = append(visible, e.Name())
                }
        }
        got := slices.Clone(args)
        sort.Strings(got)
        sort.Strings(visible)
        if slices.Equal(got, visible) {
                return []string{"*"}
        }
        return args
}

// Install brings the selected skills into .agents/skills and links them to each harness.
func Install(o Options) ([]Action, error) {
        if runtime.GOOS == "windows" {
                o.Copy = true // Creating symlinks needs special rights on Windows.
        }
        avail, err := o.available()
        if err != nil {
                return nil, err
        }
        names := make([]string, 0, len(avail))
        for n := range avail {
                names = append(names, n)
        }
        sort.Strings(names)
        selected, err := Match(o.Patterns, names)
        if err != nil {
                return nil, err
        }
        if err := os.MkdirAll(o.canonical(), 0o755); err != nil {
                return nil, err
        }
        var acts []Action
        for _, name := range selected {
                a, err := o.ensureCanonical(name, avail[name])
                if err != nil {
                        return acts, err
                }
                acts = append(acts, a)
                dir := filepath.Join(o.canonical(), name)
                // A broken skill must not spread to every harness.
                if IssuesHaveErrors(Lint(dir)) {
                        acts = append(acts, Action{name, dir, "invalid", "fix it, then run aiculator skill --lint"})
                        continue
                }
                done := map[string]bool{}
                for _, h := range o.Harnesses {
                        tdir := o.target(h)
                        if tdir == "" {
                                acts = append(acts, Action{name, h.ID, "native", "reads " + CanonicalDir})
                                continue
                        }
                        if done[tdir] {
                                continue
                        }
                        done[tdir] = true
                        acts = append(acts, o.place(name, dir, tdir, h.ID))
                }
                for _, p := range o.Paths {
                        tdir := o.expand(p)
                        if !done[tdir] {
                                done[tdir] = true
                                acts = append(acts, o.place(name, dir, tdir, tdir))
                        }
                }
        }
        return acts, nil
}

func (o Options) ensureCanonical(name, src string) (Action, error) {
        dir := filepath.Join(o.canonical(), name)
        if src == dir {
                // It exists already. Only an explicit --force replaces a bundled skill, since
                // the user may have edited it; a skill of their own is never touched.
                if _, err := bundled.ReadFile(path.Join("skills", name, "SKILL.md")); err != nil || !o.Force {
                        return Action{name, dir, "kept", ""}, nil
                }
                if err := writeBundled(name, dir); err != nil {
                        return Action{}, err
                }
                return Action{name, dir, "refreshed", ""}, nil
        }
        if src != "" { // It lives elsewhere, such as .agent/skills or a custom source.
                if _, err := os.Lstat(dir); err == nil {
                        if o.isLinkTo(dir, src) {
                                return Action{name, dir, "kept", ""}, nil
                        }
                        return Action{name, dir, "conflict", "already exists and is not a link to " + src}, nil
                }
                return Action{name, dir, "linked", "from " + src}, link(src, dir)
        }
        _, statErr := os.Lstat(dir)
        exists := statErr == nil
        if exists && !o.Force {
                return Action{name, dir, "kept", ""}, nil
        }
        if err := writeBundled(name, dir); err != nil {
                return Action{}, err
        }
        if exists {
                return Action{name, dir, "refreshed", ""}, nil
        }
        return Action{name, dir, "created", ""}, nil
}

func writeBundled(name, dir string) error {
        root := path.Join("skills", name)
        return fs.WalkDir(bundled, root, func(p string, d fs.DirEntry, err error) error {
                if err != nil {
                        return err
                }
                rel, err := filepath.Rel(filepath.FromSlash(root), filepath.FromSlash(p))
                if err != nil {
                        return err
                }
                out := filepath.Join(dir, rel)
                if d.IsDir() {
                        return os.MkdirAll(out, 0o755)
                }
                b, err := bundled.ReadFile(p)
                if err != nil {
                        return err
                }
                return os.WriteFile(out, b, 0o644)
        })
}

func (o Options) isLinkTo(linkPath, dest string) bool {
        got, err := filepath.EvalSymlinks(linkPath)
        if err != nil {
                return false
        }
        want, err := filepath.EvalSymlinks(dest)
        return err == nil && got == want
}

func link(dest, at string) error {
        if err := os.MkdirAll(filepath.Dir(at), 0o755); err != nil {
                return err
        }
        // A relative link keeps working when the repository is moved or cloned.
        realDir, err := filepath.EvalSymlinks(filepath.Dir(at))
        if err != nil {
                return err
        }
        realDest, err := filepath.EvalSymlinks(dest)
        if err != nil {
                return err
        }
        rel, err := filepath.Rel(realDir, realDest)
        if err != nil {
                rel = realDest
        }
        return os.Symlink(rel, at)
}

// place puts one skill into one target directory. It never removes anything it
// did not make.
func (o Options) place(name, src, tdir, label string) Action {
        at := filepath.Join(tdir, name)
        fi, err := os.Lstat(at)
        switch {
        case err == nil && fi.Mode()&os.ModeSymlink != 0:
                if !o.Copy && o.isLinkTo(at, src) {
                        return Action{name, label, "ok", at}
                }
                if !o.Force {
                        return Action{name, label, "conflict", at + " links elsewhere; use --force to replace it"}
                }
                if err := os.Remove(at); err != nil {
                        return Action{name, label, "conflict", err.Error()}
                }
        case err == nil:
                if _, merr := os.Stat(filepath.Join(at, managedMarker)); merr != nil {
                        return Action{name, label, "conflict", at + " is your own directory and was left alone"}
                }
                if err := os.RemoveAll(at); err != nil {
                        return Action{name, label, "conflict", err.Error()}
                }
        }
        if o.Copy {
                if err := copyTree(src, at); err != nil {
                        return Action{name, label, "conflict", err.Error()}
                }
                return Action{name, label, "copied", at}
        }
        if err := link(src, at); err != nil {
                return Action{name, label, "conflict", err.Error()}
        }
        return Action{name, label, "linked", at}
}

func copyTree(src, dst string) error {
        realSrc, err := filepath.EvalSymlinks(src)
        if err != nil {
                return err
        }
        err = filepath.WalkDir(realSrc, func(p string, d fs.DirEntry, err error) error {
                if err != nil {
                        return err
                }
                rel, err := filepath.Rel(realSrc, p)
                if err != nil {
                        return err
                }
                out := filepath.Join(dst, rel)
                if d.IsDir() {
                        return os.MkdirAll(out, 0o755)
                }
                if !d.Type().IsRegular() {
                        return nil // A symlink in a skill could point anywhere, so it is not copied.
                }
                b, err := os.ReadFile(p)
                if err != nil {
                        return err
                }
                info, err := d.Info()
                if err != nil {
                        return err
                }
                return os.WriteFile(out, b, info.Mode().Perm())
        })
        if err != nil {
                return err
        }
        return os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(dst, managedMarker), []byte("Copied by aiculator from "+realSrc+"\n"), 0o644)
}

// Uninstall removes the selected skills from harnesses and extra paths, touching only
// links and managed copies. With Purge it also deletes them from .agents/skills.
func Uninstall(o Options) ([]Action, error) {
        avail, err := o.available()
        if err != nil {
                return nil, err
        }
        names := make([]string, 0, len(avail))
        for n := range avail {
                names = append(names, n)
        }
        sort.Strings(names)
        selected, err := Match(o.Patterns, names)
        if err != nil {
                return nil, err
        }
        var acts []Action
        for _, name := range selected {
                dirs := map[string]string{}
                for _, h := range o.Harnesses {
                        if t := o.target(h); t != "" {
                                dirs[t] = h.ID
                        }
                }
                for _, p := range o.Paths {
                        dirs[o.expand(p)] = p
                }
                for dir, label := range dirs {
                        at := filepath.Join(dir, name)
                        fi, err := os.Lstat(at)
                        if err != nil {
                                continue
                        }
                        _, merr := os.Stat(filepath.Join(at, managedMarker))
                        isLink := fi.Mode()&os.ModeSymlink != 0
                        if !isLink && merr != nil {
                                acts = append(acts, Action{name, label, "conflict", at + " is your own directory and was left alone"})
                                continue
                        }
                        if err := os.RemoveAll(at); err != nil {
                                return acts, err
                        }
                        acts = append(acts, Action{name, label, "removed", at})
                }
                if o.Purge {
                        at := filepath.Join(o.canonical(), name)
                        if _, err := os.Lstat(at); err == nil {
                                if err := os.RemoveAll(at); err != nil {
                                        return acts, err
                                }
                                acts = append(acts, Action{name, at, "removed", "deleted from " + CanonicalDir})
                        }
                }
        }
        return acts, nil
}

// Row is one skill in a listing.
type Row struct {
        Name, Source, Version, Kind string
        Installed                   bool
        Errors, Warnings            int
        Harnesses                   []string // Harnesses that can see it.
}

// List describes every known skill.
func List(o Options) ([]Row, error) {
        avail, err := o.available()
        if err != nil {
                return nil, err
        }
        names := make([]string, 0, len(avail))
        for n := range avail {
                names = append(names, n)
        }
        sort.Strings(names)
        var rows []Row
        for _, n := range names {
                dir := filepath.Join(o.canonical(), n)
                _, statErr := os.Stat(filepath.Join(dir, "SKILL.md"))
                row := Row{Name: n, Source: "bundled", Installed: statErr == nil}
                check := dir
                switch {
                case avail[n] != "":
                        row.Source = avail[n]
                        check = avail[n]
                case statErr != nil:
                        check = ""
                }
                if check != "" {
                        for _, is := range Lint(check) {
                                switch is.Level {
                                case LevelError:
                                        row.Errors++
                                case LevelWarn:
                                        row.Warnings++
                                }
                        }
                        if fm, err := parseSkill(filepath.Join(check, "SKILL.md")); err == nil {
                                row.Version, _ = fm.meta["version"].(string)
                                row.Kind, _ = fm.meta["aiculator.kind"].(string)
                        }
                } else if fm, err := parseBundled(n); err == nil {
                        row.Version, _ = fm.meta["version"].(string)
                        row.Kind, _ = fm.meta["aiculator.kind"].(string)
                }
                if row.Installed {
                        for _, h := range o.Harnesses {
                                t := o.target(h)
                                if t == "" || o.isLinkTo(filepath.Join(t, n), dir) || hasManaged(filepath.Join(t, n)) {
                                        row.Harnesses = append(row.Harnesses, h.ID)
                                }
                        }
                }
                rows = append(rows, row)
        }
        return rows, nil
}

func hasManaged(dir string) bool {
        _, err := os.Stat(filepath.Join(dir, managedMarker))
        return err == nil
}

// New creates a skill in .agents/skills with full metadata.
func New(o Options, name, description string) (string, error) {
        if !nameRE.MatchString(name) || strings.Contains(name, "--") || len(name) > 64 {
                return "", fmt.Errorf("invalid skill name %q: use lowercase letters, numbers and single hyphens", name)
        }
        dir := filepath.Join(o.canonical(), name)
        if _, err := os.Lstat(dir); err == nil {
                return "", fmt.Errorf("%s already exists", dir)
        }
        if description == "" {
                description = "TODO: say what this skill does and when to use it, with keywords that match how people ask."
        }
        body := fmt.Sprintf(`---
name: %s
description: %q
# license: MIT
# compatibility: Requires git and internet access.
# allowed-tools: Read Bash(git:*)
# disable-model-invocation: true
# argument-hint: "[argument]"
metadata:
  version: "0.1.0"
---

# %s

Step-by-step instructions go here. Keep this file under 500 lines and move long
reference material into references/.
`, name, description, name)
        if err := os.MkdirAll(dir, 0o755); err != nil {
                return "", err
        }
        return dir, os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(dir, "SKILL.md"), []byte(body), 0o644)
}

package store

import (
        "bytes"
        "context"
        "encoding/json"
        "errors"
        "fmt"
        "strings"
        "sync"
        "time"

        "github.com/nats-io/nats.go/jetstream"

        "github.com/Grano22/aiculator/internal/core"
)

// Event is one committed task revision.
type Event struct {
        Rev  uint64    `json:"rev"`
        Task core.Task `json:"task"`
}

// StartProjector follows the bucket's stream with a durable consumer and copies
// each committed revision into the event log. It runs at-least-once; the message
// ID is the revision, so a replay after a crash cannot create a duplicate.
func (s *Store) StartProjector(ctx context.Context) error {
        cons, err := s.js.CreateOrUpdateConsumer(ctx, "KV_"+bucket, jetstream.ConsumerConfig{
                Durable:       "projector",
                AckPolicy:     jetstream.AckExplicitPolicy,
                FilterSubject: "$KV." + bucket + "." + taskPrefix + ">",
                AckWait:       5 * time.Second,
        })
        if err != nil {
                return fmt.Errorf("projector consumer: %w", err)
        }
        done := make(chan struct{})
        cc, err := cons.Consume(func(m jetstream.Msg) {
                meta, err := m.Metadata()
                if err != nil {
                        _ = m.Nak()
                        return
                }
                id := strings.TrimPrefix(m.Subject(), "$KV."+bucket+"."+taskPrefix)
                rev := meta.Sequence.Stream
                pubCtx, cancel := opCtx()
                defer cancel()
                _, err = s.js.Publish(pubCtx, eventSubject+"."+id, m.Data(),
                        jetstream.WithMsgID(fmt.Sprintf("%s:%d", id, rev)))
                if err != nil {
                        _ = m.NakWithDelay(100 * time.Millisecond)
                        return
                }
                _ = m.Ack()
        })
        if err != nil {
                return fmt.Errorf("projector consume: %w", err)
        }
        s.mu.Lock()
        s.projectStop = func() { cc.Stop(); close(done) }
        s.projectDone = done
        s.mu.Unlock()
        return nil
}

// TailEvents calls fn for each event at or after seq, then keeps following until
// ctx ends. The dashboard's live feed uses it.
func (s *Store) TailEvents(ctx context.Context, fn func(core.Task)) error {
        cons, err := s.stream.OrderedConsumer(ctx, jetstream.OrderedConsumerConfig{
                DeliverPolicy: jetstream.DeliverNewPolicy,
        })
        if err != nil {
                return err
        }
        cc, err := cons.Consume(func(m jetstream.Msg) {
                var t core.Task
                if json.Unmarshal(m.Data(), &t) == nil {
                        fn(t)
                }
        })
        if err != nil {
                return err
        }
        <-ctx.Done()
        cc.Stop()
        return nil
}

// ReplayEvents returns the whole event log in commit order. Replaying it must
// produce the same final task states as the bucket, and a test asserts that.
func (s *Store) ReplayEvents(ctx context.Context) ([]core.Task, error) {
        info, err := s.stream.Info(ctx)
        if err != nil {
                return nil, err
        }
        total := info.State.Msgs
        if total == 0 {
                return nil, nil
        }
        cons, err := s.stream.OrderedConsumer(ctx, jetstream.OrderedConsumerConfig{})
        if err != nil {
                return nil, err
        }
        out := make([]core.Task, 0, total)
        for uint64(len(out)) < total {
                m, err := cons.Next(jetstream.FetchContext(ctx))
                if err != nil {
                        if errors.Is(err, context.DeadlineExceeded) || errors.Is(err, context.Canceled) {
                                return nil, fmt.Errorf("replay read %d of %d events: %w", len(out), total, err)
                        }
                        return nil, err
                }
                var t core.Task
                if err := json.Unmarshal(m.Data(), &t); err != nil {
                        return nil, fmt.Errorf("decode event: %w", err)
                }
                out = append(out, t)
        }
        return out, nil
}

// ProjectorLag says how many committed revisions the event log has not recorded yet.
func (s *Store) ProjectorLag(ctx context.Context) (uint64, error) {
        c, err := s.js.Consumer(ctx, "KV_"+bucket, "projector")
        if err != nil {
                return 0, err
        }
        info, err := c.Info(ctx)
        if err != nil {
                return 0, err
        }
        return info.NumPending + uint64(info.NumAckPending), nil
}

// WaitProjected blocks until the projector has recorded every task revision committed before
// this call, or ctx ends. It is used by replay and by tests.
//
// It waits for the newest revision by its sequence number. Asking the consumer whether it has
// anything pending is not enough: a revision just written can take a moment to count as
// pending, so a busy machine could report "caught up" with the last events still missing.
func (s *Store) WaitProjected(ctx context.Context) error {
        src, err := s.js.Stream(ctx, "KV_"+bucket)
        if err != nil {
                return err
        }
        last, err := src.GetLastMsgForSubject(ctx, "$KV."+bucket+"."+taskPrefix+">")
        if errors.Is(err, jetstream.ErrMsgNotFound) {
                return nil // No task has ever been written.
        }
        if err != nil {
                return err
        }
        c, err := s.js.Consumer(ctx, "KV_"+bucket, "projector")
        if err != nil {
                return err
        }
        for {
                info, err := c.Info(ctx)
                if err != nil {
                        return err
                }
                if info.AckFloor.Stream >= last.Sequence {
                        return nil
                }
                select {
                case <-ctx.Done():
                        return ctx.Err()
                case <-time.After(5 * time.Millisecond):
                }
        }
}

// followAckWait is how long after a crash a change that was mid-flight is delivered again.
// A follower still working on one sees it come back, which must do no harm.
const followAckWait = 15 * time.Second

// Delivery settles one revision. Ack means it is finished with. Nak hands it back.
type Delivery struct {
        Ack, Nak func()
}

// FollowTasks delivers every committed task revision to a durable consumer, starting from
// now on the first use, and from where it stopped after that. It reads the bucket's stream
// directly, so a follower sees a commit as soon as it lands and adds nothing to the commit.
//
// Revisions that do not contain filter are acknowledged without being decoded, which is
// what keeps a follower cheap when most tasks are not its own. A revision that is not
// acknowledged is delivered again, soon after a crash and at once after Nak.
func (s *Store) FollowTasks(ctx context.Context, durable string, filter []byte, fn func(t core.Task, seq uint64, d Delivery)) (stop func(), err error) {
        cons, err := s.js.CreateOrUpdateConsumer(ctx, "KV_"+bucket, jetstream.ConsumerConfig{
                Durable:       durable,
                AckPolicy:     jetstream.AckExplicitPolicy,
                DeliverPolicy: jetstream.DeliverNewPolicy,
                FilterSubject: "$KV." + bucket + "." + taskPrefix + ">",
                AckWait:       followAckWait,
                MaxAckPending: 8192,
        })
        if err != nil {
                return nil, fmt.Errorf("consumer %s: %w", durable, err)
        }
        cc, err := cons.Consume(func(m jetstream.Msg) {
                if len(filter) > 0 && !bytes.Contains(m.Data(), filter) {
                        _ = m.Ack()
                        return
                }
                var t core.Task
                meta, err := m.Metadata()
                if err != nil || json.Unmarshal(m.Data(), &t) != nil {
                        _ = m.Ack() // Not a task record; holding it would stop nothing but this consumer.
                        return
                }
                fn(t, meta.Sequence.Stream, Delivery{Ack: func() { _ = m.Ack() }, Nak: func() { _ = m.Nak() }})
        }, jetstream.PullMaxMessages(512))
        if err != nil {
                return nil, fmt.Errorf("consume %s: %w", durable, err)
        }
        // Stop returns once no more can arrive, so that handing work back after it cannot deliver
        // that work to the follower that is going away.
        return func() {
                cc.Stop()
                select {
                case <-cc.Closed():
                case <-time.After(5 * time.Second):
                }
        }, nil
}

// ReadEvents calls fn for every event in the log, oldest first, with the time it was
// recorded. It calls caughtUp once it has delivered everything that was there when it
// started, then keeps delivering new events until ctx ends. Events are decoded one at a
// time, so reading a long log does not hold it all in memory.
func (s *Store) ReadEvents(ctx context.Context, fn func(t core.Task, at time.Time), caughtUp func()) error {
        info, err := s.stream.Info(ctx)
        if err != nil {
                return err
        }
        last := info.State.LastSeq
        cons, err := s.stream.OrderedConsumer(ctx, jetstream.OrderedConsumerConfig{})
        if err != nil {
                return err
        }
        var once sync.Once
        if info.State.Msgs == 0 {
                once.Do(caughtUp)
        }
        cc, err := cons.Consume(func(m jetstream.Msg) {
                meta, err := m.Metadata()
                if err != nil {
                        return
                }
                var t core.Task
                if json.Unmarshal(m.Data(), &t) == nil {
                        fn(t, meta.Timestamp)
                }
                if meta.Sequence.Stream >= last {
                        once.Do(caughtUp)
                }
        })
        if err != nil {
                return err
        }
        <-ctx.Done()
        cc.Stop()
        return nil
}

package store

import (
        "encoding/json"
        "errors"
        "fmt"
        "time"

        "github.com/nats-io/nats.go/jetstream"
)

// Link ties a task to the item it came from, with what each side last said. Keeping this
