        if !strings.HasPrefix(s, "---") {
                return "", s
        }
        end := strings.Index(s[3:], "\n---")
        if end < 0 {
                return "", s
        }
        cut := 3 + end + 4
        return s[:cut], s[cut:]
}

// stampMetadata records where the skill came from, on the spec's metadata map.
func stampMetadata(fm, name string, h *harness.Harness) (string, error) {
        inner := strings.TrimSuffix(strings.TrimPrefix(fm, "---"), "---")
        var doc yaml.Node
        if err := yaml.Unmarshal([]byte(inner), &doc); err != nil {
                return "", fmt.Errorf("rendered frontmatter is not valid YAML: %w", err)
        }
        if len(doc.Content) == 0 || doc.Content[0].Kind != yaml.MappingNode {
                return "", errors.New("rendered frontmatter is not a mapping")
        }
        top := doc.Content[0]
        var meta *yaml.Node
        for i := 0; i+1 < len(top.Content); i += 2 {
                if top.Content[i].Value == "metadata" {
                        meta = top.Content[i+1]
                }
        }
        if meta == nil {
                meta = &yaml.Node{Kind: yaml.MappingNode}
                top.Content = append(top.Content, &yaml.Node{Kind: yaml.ScalarNode, Value: "metadata"}, meta)
        }
        add := func(k, v string) {
                meta.Content = append(meta.Content, &yaml.Node{Kind: yaml.ScalarNode, Value: k},
                        &yaml.Node{Kind: yaml.ScalarNode, Tag: "!!str", Value: v, Style: yaml.DoubleQuotedStyle})
        }
        add("aiculator.generated-from", name)
        if h != nil {
                add("aiculator.harness", h.ID)
        }
        var b bytes.Buffer
        enc := yaml.NewEncoder(&b)
        enc.SetIndent(2)
        if err := enc.Encode(&doc); err != nil {
                return "", err
        }
        _ = enc.Close()
        return "---\n" + b.String() + "---", nil
}

const maxComponentDepth = 16

var (
        componentTag = regexp.MustCompile(`<(/?)([A-Z][A-Za-z0-9]*)((?:\s+[a-zA-Z_][\w-]*(?:=(?:"[^"]*"|'[^']*'|\{[^}]*\}))?)*)\s*(/?)>`)
        propRE       = regexp.MustCompile(`([a-zA-Z_][\w-]*)(?:=(?:"([^"]*)"|'([^']*)'|\{([^}]*)\}))?`)
        fenceRE      = regexp.MustCompile("(?m)^ {0,3}(```|~~~).*$")
        inlineCode   = regexp.MustCompile("`[^`\n]+`")
        fenceBlocks  = regexp.MustCompile("(?s)(?m)^ {0,3}(```|~~~).*?^ {0,3}(```|~~~)")
)

// protectedRanges finds code, where a <Tag> is an example and not a component.
func protectedRanges(s string) [][2]int {
        var out [][2]int
        fences := fenceRE.FindAllStringIndex(s, -1)
        for i := 0; i+1 < len(fences); i += 2 {
                out = append(out, [2]int{fences[i][0], fences[i+1][1]})
        }
        if len(fences)%2 == 1 { // An unclosed fence runs to the end, as Markdown treats it.
                out = append(out, [2]int{fences[len(fences)-1][0], len(s)})
        }
        for _, m := range inlineCode.FindAllStringIndex(s, -1) {
                out = append(out, [2]int{m[0], m[1]})
        }
        return out
}

func inRanges(pos int, ranges [][2]int) bool {
        for _, r := range ranges {
                if pos >= r[0] && pos < r[1] {
                        return true
                }
        }
        return false
}

func parseProps(s string) map[string]any {
        props := map[string]any{}
        for _, m := range propRE.FindAllStringSubmatch(s, -1) {
                switch {
                case strings.Contains(m[0], "={"):
                        props[m[1]] = strings.TrimSpace(m[4])
                case strings.Contains(m[0], "="):
                        props[m[1]] = m[2] + m[3]
                default:
                        props[m[1]] = "true"
                }
        }
        return props
}

// expandComponents replaces component tags, innermost first, until none remain.
func (s *Set) expandComponents(owner, body string, vars map[string]any, depth int) (string, error) {
        if depth > maxComponentDepth {
                return "", fmt.Errorf("%s: components are nested too deeply, or include each other", owner)
        }
        for {
                protected := protectedRanges(body)
                var tags [][]int
                for _, m := range componentTag.FindAllStringSubmatchIndex(body, -1) {
                        if !inRanges(m[0], protected) {
                                tags = append(tags, m)
                        }
                }
                // The first closing tag closes the nearest opening tag before it, and a
                // self-closing tag met first is complete already. Either way, what gets
                // expanded has no tags inside it.
                target := -1
                for i, m := range tags {
                        closing := m[2] != m[3]
                        selfClosing := m[8] != m[9]
                        if body[m[4]:m[5]] == "Toc" && !closing {
                                continue // The table of contents is filled in last.
                        }
                        if selfClosing || closing {
                                target = i
                                break
                        }
                }
                if target < 0 {
                        for _, m := range tags {
                                if name := body[m[4]:m[5]]; name != "Toc" {
                                        return "", fmt.Errorf("%s: <%s> is never closed", owner, name)
                                }
                        }
                        return body, nil
                }
                m := tags[target]
                name := body[m[4]:m[5]]
                start, end := m[0], m[1]
                props := parseProps(body[m[6]:m[7]])
                if m[2] != m[3] { // A closing tag: its opener is the previous open tag.
                        open := -1
                        for i := target - 1; i >= 0; i-- {
                                if body[tags[i][4]:tags[i][5]] != "Toc" {
                                        open = i
                                        break
                                }
                        }
                        if open < 0 {
                                return "", fmt.Errorf("%s: </%s> has no opening tag", owner, name)
                        }
                        o := tags[open]
                        if openName := body[o[4]:o[5]]; openName != name {
                                return "", fmt.Errorf("%s: </%s> closes <%s>", owner, name, openName)
                        }
                        props = parseProps(body[o[6]:o[7]])
                        props["children"] = strings.Trim(body[o[1]:m[0]], "\n")
                        start = o[0]
                }
                rendered, err := s.component(owner, name, props, vars, depth)
                if err != nil {
                        return "", err
                }
                body = body[:start] + rendered + body[end:]
        }
}

func (s *Set) component(owner, name string, props, vars map[string]any, depth int) (string, error) {
        src, err := s.read("components/" + name + ".md")
        if err != nil {
                return "", fmt.Errorf("%s: unknown component <%s>: add components/%s.md", owner, name, name)
        }
        ctx := maps.Clone(vars)
        maps.Copy(ctx, props)
        out, err := s.jinja("components/"+name+".md", string(src), ctx)
        if err != nil {
                return "", err
        }
        out, err = s.expandComponents(owner, out, ctx, depth+1)
        if err != nil {
                return "", err
        }
        return strings.TrimRight(out, "\n"), nil
}

var (
        tocTag     = regexp.MustCompile(`<Toc(?:\s+depth="([0-9]+)")?\s*/>`)
        headingRE  = regexp.MustCompile(`^(#{2,3})\s+(.+?)\s*$`)
        anchorLine = regexp.MustCompile(`^<!-- anchor: ([^ ]+) -->$`)
        blankRuns  = regexp.MustCompile(`\n{3,}`)
)

type tocEntry struct {
        level        int
        title, label string
        line         int
}

func scanHeadings(text string) []tocEntry {
        var out []tocEntry
        lines := strings.Split(text, "\n")
        fenced := false
        for i, l := range lines {
                if fenceRE.MatchString(l) {
                        fenced = !fenced
                        continue
                }
                if fenced {
                        continue
                }
                m := headingRE.FindStringSubmatch(l)
                if m == nil || m[2] == "Contents" {
                        continue
                }
                e := tocEntry{level: len(m[1]), title: m[2], line: i + 1}
                for j := i + 1; j < len(lines) && j <= i+2; j++ {
                        if a := anchorLine.FindStringSubmatch(lines[j]); a != nil {
                                e.label = a[1]
                        }
                }
                out = append(out, e)
        }
        return out
}

func renderToc(entries []tocEntry, depth int) string {
        var b strings.Builder
        b.WriteString("## Contents\n\n")
        for _, e := range entries {
                if e.level > depth {
                        continue
                }
                b.WriteString(strings.Repeat("  ", e.level-2))
                fmt.Fprintf(&b, "- %s: line %d", e.title, e.line)
                if e.label != "" {
                        fmt.Fprintf(&b, ", anchor `%s`", e.label)
                }
                b.WriteString("\n")
        }
        return strings.TrimRight(b.String(), "\n")
}

// finish tidies the body and fills in the table of contents. It lists real line
// numbers, which lets a model read just the part it needs.
func finish(fm, body string) string {
        body = blankRuns.ReplaceAllString(strings.TrimLeft(body, "\n"), "\n\n")
        head := ""
        if fm != "" {
                head = fm + "\n\n"
        }
        loc := tocTag.FindStringSubmatchIndex(body)
        if loc == nil {
                return head + strings.TrimRight(body, "\n") + "\n"
        }
        assemble := func(toc string) string {
                return head + strings.TrimRight(body[:loc[0]]+toc+body[loc[1]:], "\n") + "\n"
        }
        // depth="2" lists only the top sections, which keeps a long skill's list short.
        depth := 3
        if loc[2] >= 0 && body[loc[2]:loc[3]] == "2" {
                depth = 2
        }
        // The table's own length shifts the lines after it, so measure, then fill in.
        sized := renderToc(scanHeadings(assemble(renderToc(nil, depth))), depth)
        return assemble(renderToc(scanHeadings(assemble(sized)), depth))
}

// BundledComponents lists the components that ship in the binary.
func BundledComponents() []string {
        entries, err := fs.ReadDir(library, "library/components")
        if err != nil {
                return nil
        }
        out := make([]string, 0, len(entries)+1)
        for _, e := range entries {
                out = append(out, strings.TrimSuffix(e.Name(), ".md"))
        }
        return append(out, "Toc") // Toc is built in, and has no file.
}

package tui

import (
        "context"
        "fmt"
        "strings"

        "github.com/Grano22/aiculator/pkg/observe"
)

// FleetRow is one realm in the view across projects.
type FleetRow struct {
        Name, Path string
        Live       bool
        Missing    bool
        Snapshot   observe.Snapshot
}

// FleetFetch reads every realm.
type FleetFetch func(ctx context.Context) ([]FleetRow, error)

var fleetViews = []string{"1 realms", "2 tasks", "3 agents"}

// RenderFleet draws one frame across all realms. It only reads, and every value shown
// comes from that realm's own server.
func RenderFleet(rows []FleetRow, o Options) string {
        if o.Width <= 0 {
                o.Width = 100
        }
        if o.Height <= 0 {
                o.Height = 40
        }
        f := &frame{o: o}
        live := 0
        for _, r := range rows {
                if r.Live {
                        live++
                }
        }
        parts := []string{f.paint(bold, "aiculator"), fmt.Sprintf("%d realms, %d running", len(rows), live)}
        if o.Paused {
                parts = append(parts, f.paint(yellow, "PAUSED"))
        }
        if o.Stale != "" {
                parts = append(parts, f.paint(red, "STALE: "+cut(Clean(o.Stale), 40)))
        }
        f.add(strings.Join(parts, "  "))
        view := int(o.View) % len(fleetViews)
        var tabs []string
        for i, n := range fleetViews {
                if i == view {
                        tabs = append(tabs, f.paint(bold, "["+n+"]"))
                } else {
                        tabs = append(tabs, f.paint(dim, " "+n+" "))
                }
        }
        f.add(strings.Join(tabs, " "))
        f.add("")
        switch view {
        case 1:
                f.fleetTasks(rows, o.Height-len(f.lines)-1, o.Scroll)
        case 2:
                f.fleetAgents(rows, o.Height-len(f.lines)-1, o.Scroll)
        default:
                f.fleetRealms(rows)
        }
        if o.Plain {
                return strings.TrimRight(strings.Join(f.lines, "\n"), "\n")
        }
        body := f.lines
        if len(body) > o.Height-1 {
                body = body[:o.Height-1]
        }
        for len(body) < o.Height-1 {
                body = append(body, "")
        }
        return strings.Join(append(body, f.paint(dim, cut("q quit  tab next  p pause  ↑↓ scroll", o.Width))), "\n")
}

func (f *frame) fleetRealms(rows []FleetRow) {
        if len(rows) == 0 {
                f.add(f.paint(dim, "No realms yet. A project becomes one when its server starts: aiculator join"))
                return
        }
        f.add(f.paint(dim, col("REALM", 22)+col("STATE", 10)+right("READY", 6)+right("WORK", 6)+right("REVIEW", 7)+right("DONE", 6)+right("PARKED", 7)+right("AGENTS", 7)+right("WAIT", 7)+"  PATH"))
        for _, r := range rows {
                state := f.paint(dim, col("stopped", 10))
                if r.Missing {
                        state = f.paint(yellow, col("missing", 10))
                }
                if !r.Live {
                        f.add(col(r.Name, 22) + state + f.paint(dim, right("-", 6)+right("-", 6)+right("-", 7)+right("-", 6)+right("-", 7)+right("-", 7)+right("-", 7)+"  "+Clean(r.Path)))
                        continue
                }
                s := r.Snapshot
                state = f.paint(green, col("running", 10))
                if !s.Ready {
                        state = f.paint(red, col("unwell", 10))
                }
                working := 0
                for _, a := range s.Agents {
                        if a.State == "working" {
                                working++
                        }
                }
                active := s.States["claimed"] + s.States["running"]
                parked := fmt.Sprint(s.States["parked"])
                if s.States["parked"] > 0 {
                        parked = f.paint(yellow, right(parked, 7))
                } else {
                        parked = right(parked, 7)
                }
                f.add(col(r.Name, 22) + state + right(fmt.Sprint(s.States["ready"]), 6) + right(fmt.Sprint(active), 6) +
                        right(fmt.Sprint(s.States["review"]+s.States["merging"]), 7) + right(fmt.Sprint(s.States["done"]), 6) + parked +
                        right(fmt.Sprintf("%d/%d", working, len(s.Agents)), 7) + right(Millis(s.OldestMs), 7) + "  " + f.paint(dim, Clean(r.Path)))
        }
}

func (f *frame) fleetTasks(rows []FleetRow, room, scroll int) {
        type line struct {
                realm string
                t     observe.TaskLive
        }
        var all []line
        hidden := 0
        for _, r := range rows {
                hidden += r.Snapshot.Truncated
                for _, t := range r.Snapshot.Tasks {
                        all = append(all, line{r.Name, t})
                }
        }
        // Each server lists what is in progress or needs attention. The first view counts the rest.
        title := fmt.Sprintf("Tasks in progress or needing attention: %d", len(all))
        if hidden > 0 {
                title += fmt.Sprintf(" (%d more not listed)", hidden)
        }
        f.section(title)
        f.add(f.paint(dim, col("REALM", 18)+col("TASK", 22)+col("STATE", 9)+col("T", 2)+col("OWNER", 18)+"TITLE"))
        if len(all) == 0 {
                f.add(f.paint(dim, "none"))
                return
        }
        shown := all[min(max(scroll, 0), len(all)-1):]
        room -= 2
        for i, l := range shown {
                if i >= room-1 && len(shown) > room {
                        f.add(f.paint(dim, fmt.Sprintf("… %d more", len(shown)-i)))
                        return
                }
                f.add(f.paint(cyan, col(l.realm, 18)) + col(l.t.ID, 22) + col(l.t.State, 9) + col(fmt.Sprint(l.t.Tier), 2) + col(l.t.Owner, 18) + Clean(l.t.Title))
        }
}

func (f *frame) fleetAgents(rows []FleetRow, room, scroll int) {
        type line struct {
                realm string
                a     observe.AgentLive
        }
        var all []line
        for _, r := range rows {
                for _, a := range r.Snapshot.Agents {
                        all = append(all, line{r.Name, a})
                }
        }
        f.section(fmt.Sprintf("Agents: %d", len(all)))
        f.add(f.paint(dim, col("REALM", 18)+col("AGENT", 22)+col("T", 2)+col("STATE", 9)+col("TASK", 22)+right("SEEN", 8)))
        if len(all) == 0 {
                f.add(f.paint(dim, "none yet"))
                return
        }
        shown := all[min(max(scroll, 0), len(all)-1):]
        room -= 2
        for i, l := range shown {
                if i >= room-1 && len(shown) > room {
                        f.add(f.paint(dim, fmt.Sprintf("… %d more", len(shown)-i)))
                        return
                }
                f.add(f.paint(cyan, col(l.realm, 18)) + col(l.a.ID, 22) + col(fmt.Sprint(l.a.Tier), 2) + col(l.a.State, 9) + col(l.a.Task, 22) + right(Millis(l.a.SeenAgoMs), 8))
        }
}

// Package tui draws the live terminal dashboard. Render is a pure function from a
// snapshot to text, so what it draws can be tested exactly, with no terminal involved.
package tui

import (
        "fmt"
        "slices"
        "strings"
        "unicode"

        "github.com/Grano22/aiculator/pkg/observe"
)

// View selects a screen.
type View int

// The screens.
const (
        Overview View = iota
        Tasks
        Agents
        Flow
        Usage
)

var viewNames = []string{"1 overview", "2 tasks", "3 agents", "4 flow", "5 usage"}

// Options controls one frame.
type Options struct {
        View          View
        Width, Height int
        Scroll        int
        Color         bool
        Paused        bool
        Stale         string // Set when the server stopped answering.
        Plain         bool   // A one-off print: no padding to the screen, no key help.
}

const (
        red    = "31"
        green  = "32"
        yellow = "33"
        cyan   = "36"
        dim    = "2"
        bold   = "1"
)

type frame struct {
        o     Options
        lines []string
}

func (f *frame) paint(code, s string) string {
        if !f.o.Color || s == "" {
                return s
        }
        return "\x1b[" + code + "m" + s + "\x1b[0m"
}

func (f *frame) add(s string) { f.lines = append(f.lines, s) }

// Clean removes everything that could control the terminal. Task titles and agent names
// come from agents, so an escape sequence in one must not reach the screen as anything
// but harmless text.
func Clean(s string) string {
        return strings.Map(func(r rune) rune {
                if unicode.IsControl(r) || unicode.Is(unicode.Cf, r) {
                        return ' '
                }
                return r
        }, s)
}

// cut fits text to a width in runes, marking anything it removes.
func cut(s string, w int) string {
        r := []rune(s)
        if w <= 0 {
                return ""
        }
        if len(r) <= w {
                return s
        }
        if w == 1 {
                return "…"
        }
        return string(r[:w-1]) + "…"
}

// col pads or cuts to an exact width.
func col(s string, w int) string {
        s = cut(Clean(s), w)
        if n := w - len([]rune(s)); n > 0 {
                s += strings.Repeat(" ", n)
        }
        return s
}

func right(s string, w int) string {
        s = cut(s, w)
        if n := w - len([]rune(s)); n > 0 {
                s = strings.Repeat(" ", n) + s
        }
        return s
}

// Micros formats a duration in microseconds.
func Micros(us int64) string {
        switch {
        case us < 1000:
                return fmt.Sprintf("%dµs", us)
        case us < 1_000_000:
                return fmt.Sprintf("%.1fms", float64(us)/1000)
        case us < 60_000_000:
                return fmt.Sprintf("%.1fs", float64(us)/1e6)
        }
        return Millis(us / 1000)
}

// Millis formats a longer time, down to whole seconds.
func Millis(ms int64) string {
        neg := ""
        if ms < 0 {
                neg, ms = "-", -ms
        }
        sec := ms / 1000
        if neg != "" {
                sec = max(sec, 1) // Never show a past deadline as "-0s".
        }
        switch {
        case sec < 60:
                return fmt.Sprintf("%s%ds", neg, sec)
        case sec < 3600:
                return fmt.Sprintf("%s%dm%02ds", neg, sec/60, sec%60)
        case sec < 86400:
                return fmt.Sprintf("%s%dh%02dm", neg, sec/3600, sec/60%60)
        }
        return fmt.Sprintf("%s%dd%02dh", neg, sec/86400, sec/3600%24)
}

// Count shortens a large number.
func Count(n int64) string {
        switch {
        case n < 10_000:
                return fmt.Sprint(n)
        case n < 1_000_000:
                return fmt.Sprintf("%.1fk", float64(n)/1e3)
        case n < 1_000_000_000:
                return fmt.Sprintf("%.1fM", float64(n)/1e6)
        }
        return fmt.Sprintf("%.1fG", float64(n)/1e9)
}

// Money formats micro-dollars.
func Money(micro int64) string { return fmt.Sprintf("$%.2f", float64(micro)/1e6) }

const sparks = "▁▂▃▄▅▆▇█"

// Spark draws a history as one line, scaled to its own peak.
func Spark(values []int64, width int) string {
        if width <= 0 {
                return ""
        }
        if len(values) > width {
                values = values[len(values)-width:]
        }
        var peak int64
        for _, v := range values {
                peak = max(peak, v)
        }
        blocks := []rune(sparks)
        var b strings.Builder
        for _, v := range values {
                if v <= 0 || peak == 0 {
                        b.WriteRune(' ')
                        continue
                }
                b.WriteRune(blocks[min(int(v*int64(len(blocks))/(peak+1)), len(blocks)-1)])
        }
        return b.String()
}

// Render draws one frame, at most Height lines of at most Width columns.
func Render(s observe.Snapshot, o Options) string {
        if o.Width <= 0 {
                o.Width = 100
        }
        if o.Height <= 0 {
                o.Height = 40
        }
        f := &frame{o: o}
        f.header(s)
        switch o.View {
        case Tasks:
                f.tasks(s, o.Height-len(f.lines)-1, o.Scroll)
        case Agents:
                f.agents(s, o.Height-len(f.lines)-1, o.Scroll)
        case Flow:
                f.flow(s)
        case Usage:
                f.usage(s)
        default:
                f.overview(s)
        }
        if o.Plain {
                return strings.TrimRight(strings.Join(f.lines, "\n"), "\n")
        }
        body := f.lines
        if len(body) > o.Height-1 {
                body = body[:o.Height-1]
        }
        for len(body) < o.Height-1 {
                body = append(body, "")
        }
        help := "q quit  tab next  p pause  ↑↓ scroll"
        return strings.Join(append(body, f.paint(dim, cut(help, o.Width))), "\n")
}

func (f *frame) header(s observe.Snapshot) {
        state := f.paint(green, "READY")
        if !s.Ready {
                state = f.paint(red, "NOT READY")
        }
        parts := []string{f.paint(bold, "aiculator"), Clean(s.Version), "up " + Millis(s.UptimeMs), state}
        if s.Realm != "" {
                parts = append(parts, f.paint(cyan, "realm: "+Clean(s.Realm)))
        }
        switch {
        case s.Planning.Active:
                parts = append(parts, f.paint(cyan, "planning: "+Clean(s.Planning.Phase)))
        case s.Planning.Lost:
                parts = append(parts, f.paint(red, "planner lost"))
        }
        if f.o.Paused {
                parts = append(parts, f.paint(yellow, "PAUSED"))
        }
        if f.o.Stale != "" {
                parts = append(parts, f.paint(red, "STALE: "+cut(Clean(f.o.Stale), 40)))
        }
        f.add(strings.Join(parts, "  "))
        var tabs []string
        for i, n := range viewNames {
                if View(i) == f.o.View {
                        tabs = append(tabs, f.paint(bold, "["+n+"]"))
                } else {
                        tabs = append(tabs, f.paint(dim, " "+n+" "))
                }
        }
        f.add(strings.Join(tabs, " "))
        f.add("")
}

func (f *frame) section(title string) { f.add(f.paint(bold, title)) }

var pipeline = []string{"draft", "ready", "claimed", "running", "review", "merging", "done"}

func (f *frame) stateLine(s observe.Snapshot) {
        parts := make([]string, 0, len(pipeline))
        for _, st := range pipeline {
                parts = append(parts, fmt.Sprintf("%s %d", st, s.States[st]))
        }
        f.add(strings.Join(parts, " → "))
        line := fmt.Sprintf("failed %d  parked %d  canceled %d  agents waiting %d", s.States["failed"], s.States["parked"], s.States["canceled"], s.Waiting)
        if s.OldestMs > 0 {
                line += "  oldest ready " + Millis(s.OldestMs)
        }
        if s.States["parked"] > 0 || s.States["failed"] > 0 {
                f.add(f.paint(yellow, line))
        } else {
                f.add(line)
        }
}

func (f *frame) overview(s observe.Snapshot) {
        f.section("Flow")
        f.stateLine(s)
        f.add("")
        f.throughput(s)
        f.add("")
        f.latency(s)
        f.add("")
        f.probes(s)
        f.add("")
        f.usageLine(s)
        f.add("")
        left := f.o.Height - len(f.lines) - 2
        if left > 2 {
                f.tasks(s, left, 0)
        }
}

func (f *frame) throughput(s observe.Snapshot) {
        t := s.Throughput
        f.section("Throughput")
        f.add(fmt.Sprintf("done %.1f/min   grants %.1f/min   failed %.1f/min   commits %.1f/s   api %.1f/s", t.DonePerMin, t.GrantsPerMin, t.FailedPerMin, t.CommitsPerSec, t.APIPerSec))
        f.add(fmt.Sprintf("since start: %s done, %s grants, %s failures, %s zombies caught", Count(t.TotalDone), Count(t.TotalGrants), Count(t.TotalFailed), Count(t.TotalZombies)))
        w := max(f.o.Width-10, 10)
        f.add("commits " + f.paint(cyan, Spark(t.Commits, w)))
        f.add("done    " + f.paint(green, Spark(t.Done, w)))
}

var latencyRows = []struct{ key, label string }{
        {observe.LatencyQueue, "queue wait"},
        {observe.LatencyCommit, "commit"},
        {observe.LatencyAPI, "api call"},
        {observe.LatencyCycle, "task cycle"},
}

func (f *frame) latency(s observe.Snapshot) {
        f.section("Latency")
        f.add(f.paint(dim, col("", 12)+right("count", 8)+right("p50", 10)+right("p90", 10)+right("p99", 10)+right("max", 10)+right("jitter", 10)))
        for _, r := range latencyRows {
                st, ok := s.Latency[r.key]
                if !ok {
                        f.add(col(r.label, 12) + right("-", 8))
                        continue
                }
                f.add(col(r.label, 12) + right(Count(st.Count), 8) + right(Micros(st.P50), 10) + right(Micros(st.P90), 10) + right(Micros(st.P99), 10) + right(Micros(st.Max), 10) + right(Micros(st.Jitter), 10))
        }
}

func (f *frame) probes(s observe.Snapshot) {
        f.section("Probes")
        var parts []string
        for _, p := range s.Probes {
                mark := f.paint(green, "ok")
                if !p.OK {
                        mark = f.paint(red, "FAIL")
                }
                parts = append(parts, fmt.Sprintf("%s %s %s", Clean(p.Name), mark, Micros(p.LatencyUs)))
        }
        f.add(strings.Join(parts, "   "))
        for _, p := range s.Probes {
                if !p.OK {
                        f.add(f.paint(red, "  "+Clean(p.Name)+": "+cut(Clean(p.Detail), max(f.o.Width-len(p.Name)-4, 10))))
                }
        }
}

func (f *frame) usageLine(s observe.Snapshot) {
        u := s.Usage
        f.section("Usage")
        line := fmt.Sprintf("tokens %s   spent %s", Count(u.Tokens), Money(u.Spent))
        if u.Budgeted > 0 {
                line += "   budgeted " + Money(u.Budgeted)
        }
        if u.OverBudget > 0 {
                line += "   " + f.paint(red, fmt.Sprintf("%d over budget", u.OverBudget))
        }
        f.add(line)
}

func opt(ms *int64) string {
        if ms == nil {
                return "-"
        }
        return Millis(*ms)
}

func (f *frame) healthWord(h string) string {
        switch h {
        case observe.HealthOK:
                return f.paint(green, col("ok", 7))
        case observe.HealthAtRisk:
                return f.paint(yellow, col("at risk", 7))
        case observe.HealthExpired:
                return f.paint(red, col("expired", 7))
        }
        return f.paint(dim, col("-", 7))
}

func (f *frame) tasks(s observe.Snapshot, room, scroll int) {
        f.section(fmt.Sprintf("Tasks with work in progress or problems: %d", len(s.Tasks)+s.Truncated))
        title := max(f.o.Width-68, 8)
        f.add(f.paint(dim, col("HEALTH", 8)+col("STATE", 9)+col("T", 2)+col("ID", 16)+col("OWNER", 14)+right("LEASE", 7)+right("PROG", 7)+"  "+col("TITLE", title)))
        if len(s.Tasks) == 0 {
                f.add(f.paint(dim, "none"))
                return
        }
        rows := s.Tasks[min(max(scroll, 0), len(s.Tasks)-1):]
        room -= 2
        for i, t := range rows {
                if i >= room-1 && len(rows) > room {
                        f.add(f.paint(dim, fmt.Sprintf("… %d more", len(rows)-i+s.Truncated)))
                        return
                }
                f.add(f.healthWord(t.Health) + " " + col(t.State, 9) + col(fmt.Sprint(t.Tier), 2) + col(t.ID, 16) + col(t.Owner, 14) + right(opt(t.LeaseRemainingMs), 7) + right(opt(t.ProgressRemaining), 7) + "  " + col(rowTitle(t), title))
        }
        if s.Truncated > 0 {
                f.add(f.paint(dim, fmt.Sprintf("… %d more not sent by the server", s.Truncated)))
        }
}

func rowTitle(t observe.TaskLive) string {
        if t.State == "parked" || t.State == "failed" {
                return t.Title + " [" + t.Reason + "]"
        }
        return t.Title
}

func (f *frame) agents(s observe.Snapshot, room, scroll int) {
        f.section(fmt.Sprintf("Agents: %d", len(s.Agents)))
        f.add(f.paint(dim, col("AGENT", 20)+col("T", 2)+col("STATE", 9)+col("TASK", 16)+right("SEEN", 8)+right("TOKENS", 8)+right("COST", 9)+right("DONE", 6)+right("FAIL", 6)))
        if len(s.Agents) == 0 {
                f.add(f.paint(dim, "none yet. Join with: aiculator work join, or see aiculator join"))
                return
        }
        rows := s.Agents[min(max(scroll, 0), len(s.Agents)-1):]
        room -= 2
        for i, a := range rows {
                if i >= room-1 && len(rows) > room {
                        f.add(f.paint(dim, fmt.Sprintf("… %d more", len(rows)-i)))
                        return
                }
                state := col(a.State, 9)
                switch a.State {
                case "working":
                        state = f.paint(green, state)
                case "gone":
                        state = f.paint(dim, state)
                }
                f.add(col(a.ID, 20) + col(fmt.Sprint(a.Tier), 2) + state + col(a.Task, 16) + right(Millis(a.SeenAgoMs), 8) + right(Count(a.Tokens), 8) + right(Money(a.Cost), 9) + right(Count(a.Done), 6) + right(Count(a.Failed), 6))
        }
}

func (f *frame) flow(s observe.Snapshot) {
        f.section("Tasks by state")
        f.stateLine(s)
        f.add("")
        f.section("Moves between states, since the server started")
        if len(s.Flow) == 0 {
                f.add(f.paint(dim, "none yet"))
                return
        }
        var peak int64
        for _, e := range s.Flow {
                peak = max(peak, e.Count)
        }
        barMax := max(f.o.Width-34, 5)
        for _, e := range slices.Clone(s.Flow) {
                bar := strings.Repeat("█", max(int(e.Count*int64(barMax)/peak), 1))
                f.add(col(e.From, 9) + "→ " + col(e.To, 9) + right(Count(e.Count), 8) + "  " + f.paint(cyan, bar))
        }
}

func (f *frame) usage(s observe.Snapshot) {
        f.usageLine(s)
        f.add("")
        f.section("By tier")
        f.add(f.paint(dim, col("TIER", 6)+right("TASKS", 8)+right("TOKENS", 10)+right("SPENT", 10)+right("BUDGET", 10)))
        for _, t := range s.Usage.ByTier {
                f.add(col(fmt.Sprint(t.Tier), 6) + right(Count(int64(t.Tasks)), 8) + right(Count(t.Tokens), 10) + right(Money(t.Spent), 10) + right(Money(t.Budget), 10))
        }
        f.add("")
        f.section("Tightest budgets")
        if len(s.Usage.Tightest) == 0 {
                f.add(f.paint(dim, "no budgeted task has spent anything yet"))
        } else {
                barW := 20
                for _, b := range s.Usage.Tightest {
                        fill := min(int(b.Spent*int64(barW)/max(b.Budget, 1)), barW)
                        bar := strings.Repeat("█", fill) + strings.Repeat("░", barW-fill)
                        code := green
                        if b.Spent*4 >= b.Budget*3 {
                                code = yellow
                        }
                        if b.Spent >= b.Budget {
                                code = red
                        }
                        f.add(col(b.ID, 16) + f.paint(code, bar) + " " + right(Money(b.Spent), 9) + " of " + Money(b.Budget) + "  " + Clean(b.State))
                }
        }
        f.add("")
        f.section("By agent, since the server started")
        f.add(f.paint(dim, col("AGENT", 24)+right("TOKENS", 10)+right("COST", 10)+right("DONE", 7)+right("FAIL", 7)))
        for _, a := range s.Agents {
                f.add(col(a.ID, 24) + right(Count(a.Tokens), 10) + right(Money(a.Cost), 10) + right(Count(a.Done), 7) + right(Count(a.Failed), 7))
        }
}

package tui

import (
        "context"
        "fmt"
        "io"
        "os"
        "regexp"
        "strings"
        "time"

        "golang.org/x/term"

        "github.com/Grano22/aiculator/pkg/observe"
)

// Fetch gets the latest snapshot.
type Fetch func(ctx context.Context) (observe.Snapshot, error)

var ansiSeq = regexp.MustCompile("\x1b\\[[0-9;]*m")

// fit cuts a painted line to the terminal width, counting only visible characters, so a
// long line cannot wrap and throw off the whole screen.
func fit(line string, width int) string {
        if len([]rune(ansiSeq.ReplaceAllString(line, ""))) <= width {
                return line
        }
        var b strings.Builder
        seen := 0
        for i := 0; i < len(line); {
                if loc := ansiSeq.FindStringIndex(line[i:]); loc != nil && loc[0] == 0 {
                        b.WriteString(line[i : i+loc[1]])
                        i += loc[1]
                        continue
                }
                r := []rune(line[i:])[0]
                if seen < width {
                        b.WriteRune(r)
                        seen++
                }
                i += len(string(r))
        }
        b.WriteString("\x1b[0m")
        return b.String()
}

func draw(out io.Writer, text string, width int) {
        var b strings.Builder
        b.WriteString("\x1b[H")
        for i, line := range strings.Split(text, "\n") {
                if i > 0 {
                        b.WriteString("\r\n")
                }
                b.WriteString(fit(line, width))
                b.WriteString("\x1b[K") // Clear what the last frame left to the right.
        }
        b.WriteString("\x1b[J")
        _, _ = io.WriteString(out, b.String())
}

// Run shows the dashboard until the user quits or ctx ends. It needs a real terminal.
func Run(ctx context.Context, fetch Fetch, interval time.Duration, color bool) error {
        var snap observe.Snapshot
        return loop(ctx, interval, color, func(c context.Context) error {
                got, err := fetch(c)
                if err == nil {
                        snap = got
                }
                return err
        }, func(o Options) string { return Render(snap, o) })
}

// RunFleet shows every realm until the user quits or ctx ends.
func RunFleet(ctx context.Context, fetch FleetFetch, interval time.Duration, color bool) error {
        var rows []FleetRow
        return loop(ctx, interval, color, func(c context.Context) error {
                got, err := fetch(c)
                if err == nil {
                        rows = got
                }
                return err
        }, func(o Options) string { return RenderFleet(rows, o) })
}

func loop(ctx context.Context, interval time.Duration, color bool, fetch func(context.Context) error, render func(Options) string) error {
        fd := int(os.Stdin.Fd())
        old, err := term.MakeRaw(fd)
        if err != nil {
                return fmt.Errorf("the dashboard needs a terminal; use --once or --json: %w", err)
        }
        // However this ends, the terminal goes back to how it was.
        defer func() { _ = term.Restore(fd, old) }()
        out := os.Stdout
        _, _ = io.WriteString(out, "\x1b[?1049h\x1b[?25l")
        defer func() { _, _ = io.WriteString(out, "\x1b[?25h\x1b[?1049l") }()

        keys := make(chan string, 16)
        go readKeys(os.Stdin, keys)

        o := Options{Color: color}
        refresh := func() {
                c, cancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, 3*time.Second)
                defer cancel()
                if err := fetch(c); err != nil {
                        o.Stale = err.Error()
                        return
                }
                o.Stale = ""
        }
        paint := func() {
                o.Width, o.Height = ScreenSize(term.GetSize(int(out.Fd())))
                draw(out, render(o), o.Width)
        }
        refresh()
        paint()
        tick := time.NewTicker(interval)
        defer tick.Stop()
        for {
                select {
                case <-ctx.Done():
                        return nil
                case <-tick.C:
                        if !o.Paused {
                                refresh()
                        }
                        paint()
                case k, ok := <-keys:
                        if !ok {
                                return nil
                        }
                        if handleKey(k, &o) {
                                return nil
                        }
                        paint()
                }
        }
}

// ScreenSize falls back to a usable size. Some terminals report 0x0 with no error, which
// taken at face value would cut every line to nothing and draw a blank screen.
func ScreenSize(w, h int, err error) (int, int) {
        if err != nil || w <= 0 || h <= 0 {
                return 100, 40
        }
        return w, h
}

// handleKey applies one key and reports whether to quit. In raw mode Ctrl-C arrives as
// a byte rather than a signal, so it has to be handled here.
func handleKey(k string, o *Options) (quit bool) {
        switch k {
        case "q", "Q", "\x03", "\x04":
                return true
        case "1", "2", "3", "4", "5":
                o.View, o.Scroll = View(k[0]-'1'), 0
        case "\t", "l", "\x1b[C":
                o.View, o.Scroll = (o.View+1)%View(len(viewNames)), 0
        case "\x1b[Z", "h", "\x1b[D":
                o.View, o.Scroll = (o.View+View(len(viewNames))-1)%View(len(viewNames)), 0
        case "j", "\x1b[B":
                o.Scroll++
        case "k", "\x1b[A":
                o.Scroll = max(o.Scroll-1, 0)
        case "p", " ":
                o.Paused = !o.Paused
        }
        return false
}

func readKeys(in io.Reader, keys chan<- string) {
        defer close(keys)
        buf := make([]byte, 16)
        for {
                n, err := in.Read(buf)
                if err != nil {
                        return
                }
                select {
                case keys <- string(buf[:n]):
                default: // Nobody is reading; a dropped key does no harm.
                }
        }
}

package vlog

import (
        "bytes"
        "encoding/json"
        "fmt"
        "net/http"
        "slices"
        "strings"
)

const (
        truncatedBody = 1 << 10
        fullBody      = 1 << 20
)

// HTTPLimit is how much of a body to keep at the current level; 0 means none.
func HTTPLimit(component string) int {
        switch n := ComponentLevel(component); {
        case n >= LevelFull:
                return fullBody
        case n >= LevelBodies:
                return truncatedBody
        }
        return 0
}

// Headers renders headers with credentials removed, in a stable order.
func Headers(h http.Header) string {
        names := make([]string, 0, len(h))
        for k := range h {
                names = append(names, k)
        }
        slices.Sort(names)
        var b strings.Builder
        for i, k := range names {
                if i > 0 {
                        b.WriteString("; ")
                }
                v := strings.Join(h[k], ",")
                if IsSecretName(k) {
                        v = Redacted
                }
                fmt.Fprintf(&b, "%s: %s", k, Scrub(v))
        }
        return b.String()
}

// Body renders a body for the log: credentials removed, and cut to limit bytes.
func Body(raw []byte, limit int) string {
        if limit <= 0 || len(raw) == 0 {
                return ""
        }
        clean := raw
        var doc any
        // Field names are the reliable signal, so use them whenever the body is JSON.
        if json.Unmarshal(raw, &doc) == nil {
                if out, err := json.Marshal(scrubJSON(doc)); err == nil {
                        clean = out
                }
        } else {
                clean = []byte(Scrub(string(raw)))
        }
        if len(clean) > limit {
                return fmt.Sprintf("%s [truncated %d bytes]", clean[:limit], len(clean)-limit)
        }
        return string(clean)
}

func scrubJSON(v any) any {
        switch x := v.(type) {
        case map[string]any:
                for k, val := range x {
                        if IsSecretName(k) {
                                if _, isNumber := val.(float64); !isNumber {
                                        x[k] = Redacted
                                        continue
                                }
                        }
                        x[k] = scrubJSON(val)
                }
                return x
        case []any:
                for i := range x {
                        x[i] = scrubJSON(x[i])
                }
                return x
        case string:
                return Scrub(x)
        }
        return v
}

// Capture records what a handler writes, up to a limit, while still streaming it.
type Capture struct {
        http.ResponseWriter
        Status int
        Bytes  int64
        body   bytes.Buffer
        limit  int
}

// NewCapture wraps a response writer. A limit of 0 records no body.
func NewCapture(w http.ResponseWriter, limit int) *Capture {
        return &Capture{ResponseWriter: w, Status: http.StatusOK, limit: limit}
}

// WriteHeader implements http.ResponseWriter.
func (c *Capture) WriteHeader(code int) {
        c.Status = code
        c.ResponseWriter.WriteHeader(code)
}

// Write implements http.ResponseWriter.
func (c *Capture) Write(p []byte) (int, error) {
        if left := c.limit - c.body.Len(); left > 0 {
                c.body.Write(p[:min(left, len(p))])
        }
        n, err := c.ResponseWriter.Write(p)
        c.Bytes += int64(n)
        return n, err
}

// Flush keeps streaming responses working.
func (c *Capture) Flush() {
        if f, ok := c.ResponseWriter.(http.Flusher); ok {
                f.Flush()
        }
}

// Unwrap lets http.ResponseController reach the real writer.
func (c *Capture) Unwrap() http.ResponseWriter { return c.ResponseWriter }

// Recorded returns the body kept so far.
func (c *Capture) Recorded() []byte { return c.body.Bytes() }

// Package vlog is leveled logging in the style of Kubernetes: -v=0 to -v=9, with
// --vmodule to raise one component alone. The levels mean what they mean in kubectl, so
// the habit carries over: 2 is the steady state for a server, 4 is debug, 5 is trace, and
// 6 to 9 show HTTP traffic in growing detail.
//
// A disabled call costs one atomic load and allocates nothing, so logging can stay in hot
// paths. Secrets are removed at the handler, so no call site can leak one by mistake.
package vlog

import (
        "context"
        "fmt"
        "io"
        "log/slog"
        "os"
        "path"
        "regexp"
        "strconv"
        "strings"
        "sync"
        "sync/atomic"
        "time"
)

// Levels, with the meanings kubectl documents. Levels 1 to 5 are general and 6 to 9
// are HTTP traffic.
const (
        LevelAlways   = 0 // Always useful to an operator.
        LevelDefault  = 1 // A quiet default.
        LevelSteady   = 2 // Steady state: the recommended level for a server.
        LevelChanges  = 3 // Extended information about changes.
        LevelDebug    = 4 // Debug.
        LevelTrace    = 5 // Trace.
        LevelRequests = 6 // Requested resources.
        LevelHeaders  = 7 // Request and response headers.
        LevelBodies   = 8 // Bodies, truncated.
        LevelFull     = 9 // Bodies, not truncated.
        MaxLevel      = LevelFull
)

// Descriptions explains each level for help text and docs.
var Descriptions = []string{
        "Always visible: errors, and what an operator must see",
        "A quiet default: server start and stop, plugins, serious warnings",
        "Steady state, the server's default: task transitions, plans, tool calls, session starts",
        "Changes: every commit and grant, rejected commands, permission decisions, checks",
        "Debug: why an agent was told to wait, worktrees, check output, sandbox commands",
        "Trace: every git command, dispatch rejections, compare-and-swap revisions",
        "Requests: method, URL, status and time for each HTTP call",
        "Headers: also HTTP headers, with credentials removed",
        "Bodies: also HTTP bodies, cut to 1 KiB, with credentials removed",
        "Full: also HTTP bodies up to 1 MiB, with credentials removed",
}

type rule struct {
        pattern string
        level   int32
}

var (
        level   atomic.Int32
        rules   atomic.Pointer[[]rule]
        handler atomic.Pointer[slog.Logger]

        tempMu    sync.Mutex
        tempTimer *time.Timer
        tempUntil time.Time
        base      struct {
                level   int32
                vmodule string
        }
        vmoduleText atomic.Pointer[string]
)

func init() {
        handler.Store(slog.New(newHandler(os.Stderr, "text")))
}

func newHandler(w io.Writer, format string) slog.Handler {
        opts := &slog.HandlerOptions{ReplaceAttr: scrubAttr}
        if format == "json" {
                return slog.NewJSONHandler(w, opts)
        }
        return slog.NewTextHandler(w, opts)
}

// Options configures logging.
type Options struct {
        Level   int
        VModule string
        Format  string // "text" or "json".
        Output  io.Writer
}

// Setup applies options and makes this the default for slog as well, so that anything
// logging through slog gets the same format and redaction.
func Setup(o Options) error {
        if o.Format != "" && o.Format != "text" && o.Format != "json" {
                return fmt.Errorf("log format %q: use text or json", o.Format)
        }
        if err := SetLevel(o.Level); err != nil {
                return err
        }
        if err := SetVModule(o.VModule); err != nil {
                return err
        }
        w := o.Output
        if w == nil {
                w = os.Stderr
        }
        l := slog.New(newHandler(w, o.Format))
        handler.Store(l)
        slog.SetDefault(l)
        return nil
}

// SetOutput keeps the format simple for callers that only move the stream, such as the
// terminal dashboard, whose screen a log line would corrupt.
func SetOutput(w io.Writer, format string) {
        l := slog.New(newHandler(w, format))
        handler.Store(l)
        slog.SetDefault(l)
}

// SetLevel changes the global level at once. It is safe at any time.
func SetLevel(n int) error {
        if n < 0 || n > MaxLevel {
                return fmt.Errorf("verbosity %d: use 0 to %d", n, MaxLevel)
        }
        level.Store(int32(n))
        return nil
}

// Level returns the global level.
func Level() int { return int(level.Load()) }

// ParseVModule reads a list such as "engine=5,driver=3,http*=7".
func parseVModule(s string) ([]rule, error) {
        if strings.TrimSpace(s) == "" {
                return nil, nil
        }
        var out []rule
        for _, part := range strings.Split(s, ",") {
                name, val, ok := strings.Cut(strings.TrimSpace(part), "=")
                if !ok || name == "" {
                        return nil, fmt.Errorf("vmodule %q: want component=level", part)
                }
                n, err := strconv.Atoi(val)
                if err != nil || n < 0 || n > MaxLevel {
                        return nil, fmt.Errorf("vmodule %q: level must be 0 to %d", part, MaxLevel)
                }
                if _, err := path.Match(name, ""); err != nil {
                        return nil, fmt.Errorf("vmodule %q: %w", part, err)
                }
                out = append(out, rule{name, int32(n)})
        }
        return out, nil
}

// SetVModule sets per-component levels. An empty string clears them.
func SetVModule(s string) error {
        parsed, err := parseVModule(s)
        if err != nil {
                return err
        }
        if parsed == nil {
                rules.Store(nil)
        } else {
                rules.Store(&parsed)
        }
        vmoduleText.Store(&s)
        return nil
}

// VModule returns the current per-component levels.
func VModule() string {
        if p := vmoduleText.Load(); p != nil {
                return *p
        }
        return ""
}

// SetFor changes levels until d has passed, then restores the previous ones, so that a
// debugging session cannot leave a server at -v=9 for good. d of 0 makes it permanent.
func SetFor(n int, vmodule string, d time.Duration) error {
        if n < 0 || n > MaxLevel {
                return fmt.Errorf("verbosity %d: use 0 to %d", n, MaxLevel)
        }
        if _, err := parseVModule(vmodule); err != nil {
                return err
        }
        tempMu.Lock()
        defer tempMu.Unlock()
        if tempTimer != nil {
                tempTimer.Stop()
                tempTimer = nil
        } else {
                // A temporary change on top of another keeps the original to return to.
                base.level, base.vmodule = level.Load(), VModule()
        }
        tempUntil = time.Time{}
        _ = SetLevel(n)
        _ = SetVModule(vmodule)
        if d > 0 {
                tempUntil = time.Now().Add(d)
                tempTimer = time.AfterFunc(d, restore)
        } else {
                base.level, base.vmodule = int32(n), vmodule
        }
        return nil
}

func restore() {
        tempMu.Lock()
        defer tempMu.Unlock()
        tempTimer = nil
        tempUntil = time.Time{}
        _ = SetLevel(int(base.level))
        _ = SetVModule(base.vmodule)
}

// RevertsAt says when a temporary change ends; zero means it is permanent.
func RevertsAt() time.Time {
        tempMu.Lock()
        defer tempMu.Unlock()
        return tempUntil
}

// ComponentLevel is the level in force for one component.
func ComponentLevel(component string) int {
        if r := rules.Load(); r != nil {
                for _, x := range *r {
                        if ok, _ := path.Match(x.pattern, component); ok {
                                return int(x.level)
                        }
                }
        }
        return int(level.Load())
}

// Logger logs for one component.
type Logger struct{ component string }

// For returns the logger for a component.
func For(component string) Logger { return Logger{component} }

// Verbose is the result of a level check.
type Verbose struct {
        component string
        level     int
        on        bool
}

// V checks a level. It allocates nothing, so a disabled call is nearly free. Build costly
// arguments only inside: if v := log.V(4); v.Enabled() { v.Info(...) }.
func (l Logger) V(n int) Verbose {
        if r := rules.Load(); r == nil {
                return Verbose{l.component, n, int32(n) <= level.Load()}
        }
        return Verbose{l.component, n, n <= ComponentLevel(l.component)}
}

// Enabled reports whether this level is on.
func (v Verbose) Enabled() bool { return v.on }

// Info writes one line if this level is on.
func (v Verbose) Info(msg string, kv ...any) {
        if !v.on {
                return
        }
        write(slog.LevelInfo, v.component, v.level, msg, kv)
}

// Warn writes one warning if this level is on.
func (v Verbose) Warn(msg string, kv ...any) {
        if !v.on {
                return
        }
        write(slog.LevelWarn, v.component, v.level, msg, kv)
}

// Error always writes, at any verbosity.
func (l Logger) Error(msg string, kv ...any) {
        write(slog.LevelError, l.component, 0, msg, kv)
}

func write(lv slog.Level, component string, v int, msg string, kv []any) {
        attrs := make([]any, 0, len(kv)+4)
        attrs = append(attrs, "v", v, "component", component)
        attrs = append(attrs, kv...)
        handler.Load().Log(context.Background(), lv, msg, attrs...)
}

// Slog returns a standard logger for a component, for code that takes one.
func Slog(component string) *slog.Logger {
        return handler.Load().With("component", component)
}

var (
        // Agent tokens are base64url JSON, then a dot, then a base64url signature.
        tokenShape = regexp.MustCompile(`eyJ[A-Za-z0-9_-]{8,}\.[A-Za-z0-9_-]{16,}`)
        bearer     = regexp.MustCompile(`(?i)\b(bearer|basic)\s+[A-Za-z0-9._~+/=-]+`)
        secretName = regexp.MustCompile(`(?i)(token|authorization|password|passwd|secret|api[_-]?key|cookie|credential|private[_-]?key)`)
)

// Redacted replaces every secret value.
const Redacted = "[redacted]"

// IsSecretName reports whether a key or header name holds a credential.
func IsSecretName(name string) bool {
        // A count of tokens used is not a credential.
        switch strings.ToLower(name) {
        case "tokens", "input_tokens", "output_tokens", "total_tokens":
                return false
        }
        return secretName.MatchString(name)
}

// Scrub removes anything shaped like a credential from text.
func Scrub(s string) string {
        s = bearer.ReplaceAllString(s, "$1 "+Redacted)
        return tokenShape.ReplaceAllString(s, Redacted)
}

// scrubAttr runs on every attribute of every line, so a credential is removed whichever
// call site logged it, and under whichever name.
func scrubAttr(_ []string, a slog.Attr) slog.Attr {
        if a.Value.Kind() == slog.KindGroup {
                return a
        }
        if a.Key == slog.TimeKey || a.Key == slog.LevelKey {
                return a
        }
        if IsSecretName(a.Key) {
                a.Value = slog.StringValue(Redacted)
                return a
        }
        switch a.Value.Kind() {
        case slog.KindString:
                a.Value = slog.StringValue(Scrub(a.Value.String()))
        case slog.KindAny:
                // Errors and other values reach the log as text, so scrub that text too.
                a.Value = slog.StringValue(Scrub(fmt.Sprint(a.Value.Any())))
        }
        return a
}

// Package work isolates each task in its own git worktree, saves work-in-progress
// commits under refs/swarm/, runs acceptance checks in a clean checkout, and merges
// verified work one at a time. It calls the git command itself, and it never
// touches the user's own branches: finished work lands on an integration branch.
package work

import (
        "bytes"
        "context"
        "errors"
        "fmt"
        "maps"
        "os"
        "os/exec"
        "path/filepath"
        "regexp"
        "slices"
        "strings"
        "sync"
        "time"

        "github.com/Grano22/aiculator/internal/core"
        "github.com/Grano22/aiculator/internal/sandbox"
        "github.com/Grano22/aiculator/internal/vlog"
)

var log = vlog.For("work")

// DefaultBranch is where merged work lands.
const DefaultBranch = "swarm/integration"

// Manager owns the worktrees for one repository.
type Manager struct {
        repo         string
        root         string
        branch       string
        sb           sandbox.Sandbox
        checkTimeout time.Duration
        hide         []string
        mergeMu      sync.Mutex
        gitMu        sync.Mutex // Serializes commands that change worktree metadata.
}

// Options configures a Manager.
type Options struct {
        Repo         string
        Root         string // Directory for worktrees.
        Branch       string
        Sandbox      sandbox.Sandbox
        CheckTimeout time.Duration
        Hide         []string // Paths checks may not read, such as the swarm's secrets.
}

// New prepares the repository and creates the integration branch if needed.
func New(ctx context.Context, o Options) (*Manager, error) {
        if o.Branch == "" {
                o.Branch = DefaultBranch
        }
        if o.CheckTimeout == 0 {
                o.CheckTimeout = 10 * time.Minute
        }
        if o.Sandbox == nil {
                return nil, errors.New("work: a sandbox is required")
        }
        root, err := filepath.Abs(o.Root)
        if err != nil {
                return nil, err
        }
        if err := os.MkdirAll(root, 0o755); err != nil {
                return nil, err
        }
        m := &Manager{repo: o.Repo, root: root, branch: o.Branch, sb: o.Sandbox, checkTimeout: o.CheckTimeout, hide: o.Hide}
        if _, err := m.git(ctx, m.repo, "rev-parse", "--verify", "HEAD"); err != nil {
                return nil, fmt.Errorf("repository needs at least one commit: %w", err)
        }
        if _, err := m.git(ctx, m.repo, "rev-parse", "--verify", "refs/heads/"+m.branch); err != nil {
                if _, err := m.git(ctx, m.repo, "branch", m.branch, "HEAD"); err != nil {
                        return nil, err
                }
        }
        return m, nil
}

// git runs one git command with a controlled environment. Repository hooks are
// disabled, so a task's commits cannot execute code from an agent-written hook.
func (m *Manager) git(ctx context.Context, dir string, args ...string) (string, error) {
        return m.gitEnv(ctx, dir, nil, args...)
}

func (m *Manager) gitEnv(ctx context.Context, dir string, env []string, args ...string) (string, error) {
        full := append([]string{
                "-c", "user.name=swarm", "-c", "user.email=swarm@localhost",
                "-c", "core.hooksPath=/dev/null", "-c", "commit.gpgsign=false",
        }, args...)
        cmd := exec.CommandContext(ctx, "git", full...)
        cmd.Dir = dir
        cmd.Env = append(os.Environ(), env...)
        var out, errb bytes.Buffer
        cmd.Stdout, cmd.Stderr = &out, &errb
        began := time.Now()
        err := cmd.Run()
        if v := log.V(vlog.LevelTrace); v.Enabled() {
                v.Info("git", "args", strings.Join(args, " "), "dir", dir, "took", time.Since(began), "err", err)
        }
        if err != nil {
                detail := strings.TrimSpace(errb.String() + "\n" + out.String())
                return "", fmt.Errorf("git %s: %w: %s", strings.Join(args, " "), err, detail)
        }
        return strings.TrimSpace(out.String()), nil
}

var safeID = regexp.MustCompile(`^[A-Za-z0-9_-]+$`)

func (m *Manager) path(kind, id string, attempt int) (string, error) {
        if !safeID.MatchString(id) {
                return "", fmt.Errorf("unsafe task id %q", id)
        }
        return filepath.Join(m.root, fmt.Sprintf("%s-%s-%d", kind, id, attempt)), nil
}

// LatestRef is the ref holding a task's newest saved work, across all attempts.
func LatestRef(id string) string { return "refs/swarm/" + id + "/latest" }

// Prepare creates the worktree for an attempt. If an earlier attempt saved work,
// the new one starts from it: that is what makes handoff and escalation lose
// nothing. Calling it twice returns the same directory.
func (m *Manager) Prepare(ctx context.Context, t core.Task) (string, error) {
        dir, err := m.path("wt", t.ID, t.Attempt)
        if err != nil {
                return "", err
        }
        if _, err := os.Stat(filepath.Join(dir, ".git")); err == nil {
                return dir, nil
        }
        m.salvage(ctx, t)
        branchRef := "refs/heads/" + m.branch
        start, resumed := branchRef, false
        if _, err := m.git(ctx, m.repo, "rev-parse", "--verify", LatestRef(t.ID)); err == nil {
                start, resumed = LatestRef(t.ID), true
        }
        m.gitMu.Lock()
        _, _ = m.git(ctx, m.repo, "worktree", "prune")
        _, err = m.git(ctx, m.repo, "worktree", "add", "--detach", "--force", dir, start)
        m.gitMu.Unlock()
        if err != nil {
                return "", err
        }
        if resumed {
                // Bring in what landed since the earlier attempt. Otherwise work that hit a
                // merge conflict would restart from the same stale base and conflict again.
                // A real conflict is left in the files for this attempt's agent to resolve.
                _, _ = m.git(ctx, dir, "merge", "--no-edit", "-m", "swarm: update from integration", branchRef)
        }
        if v := log.V(vlog.LevelDebug); v.Enabled() {
                v.Info("worktree ready", "task", t.ID, "attempt", t.Attempt, "dir", dir, "resumed", resumed)
        }
        return dir, nil
}

// salvage saves whatever earlier attempts left in their worktrees, including work
// that was never reported. A crashed or zombie agent therefore loses nothing.
func (m *Manager) salvage(ctx context.Context, t core.Task) {
        for a := 1; a < t.Attempt; a++ {
                prev := t.Clone()
                prev.Attempt = a
                if _, _, err := m.Snapshot(ctx, prev, "salvaged by the swarm"); err == nil {
                        continue
                }
        }
}

// PrepareReview creates a clean checkout of submitted work for a reviewer.
func (m *Manager) PrepareReview(ctx context.Context, t core.Task) (string, error) {
        dir, err := m.path("review", t.ID, int(t.LeaseEpoch))
        if err != nil {
                return "", err
        }
        if _, err := os.Stat(filepath.Join(dir, ".git")); err == nil {
                return dir, nil
        }
        if t.Ref == "" {
                return "", fmt.Errorf("task %s has no submitted ref", t.ID)
        }
        m.gitMu.Lock()
        defer m.gitMu.Unlock()
        if _, err := m.git(ctx, m.repo, "worktree", "add", "--detach", "--force", dir, t.Ref); err != nil {
                return "", err
        }
        return dir, nil
}

// Snapshot saves the worktree as a commit without disturbing the agent: it uses a
// private index, so whatever the agent has staged stays as it was. It returns the
// tree hash, which is the evidence of progress. An agent cannot fake this, because
// the swarm computes it from the actual files.
func (m *Manager) Snapshot(ctx context.Context, t core.Task, note string) (tree, ref string, err error) {
        dir, err := m.path("wt", t.ID, t.Attempt)
        if err != nil {
                return "", "", err
        }
        if _, err := os.Stat(dir); err != nil {
                return "", "", fmt.Errorf("worktree for %s: %w", t.ID, err)
        }
        idx, err := os.CreateTemp(m.root, "index-*")
        if err != nil {
                return "", "", err
        }
        idxPath := idx.Name()
        idx.Close()
        os.Remove(idxPath) // Git must create this itself.
        defer os.Remove(idxPath)
        env := []string{"GIT_INDEX_FILE=" + idxPath}
        if _, err := m.gitEnv(ctx, dir, env, "add", "-A"); err != nil {
                return "", "", err
        }
        if tree, err = m.gitEnv(ctx, dir, env, "write-tree"); err != nil {
                return "", "", err
        }
        parent, err := m.git(ctx, dir, "rev-parse", "HEAD")
        if err != nil {
                return "", "", err
        }
        attemptRef := fmt.Sprintf("refs/swarm/%s/%d", t.ID, t.Attempt)
        parents := []string{parent}
        if prev, err := m.git(ctx, m.repo, "rev-parse", "--verify", attemptRef); err == nil {
                parent = prev
                parents = []string{prev}
        } else if mh, err := m.git(ctx, dir, "rev-parse", "-q", "--verify", "MERGE_HEAD"); err == nil {
                // Recording the merge as a parent is what lets this work land cleanly later.
                parents = append(parents, mh)
        }
        if parentTree, err := m.git(ctx, m.repo, "rev-parse", parent+"^{tree}"); err == nil && parentTree == tree && len(parents) == 1 {
                // Nothing new. Still point the refs at it, so the ref is always usable.
                if _, err := m.git(ctx, m.repo, "update-ref", attemptRef, parent); err != nil {
                        return "", "", err
                }
                if _, err := m.git(ctx, m.repo, "update-ref", LatestRef(t.ID), parent); err != nil {
                        return "", "", err
                }
                return tree, attemptRef, nil
        }
        if note == "" {
                note = "work in progress"
        }
        msg := fmt.Sprintf("swarm wip: %s attempt %d\n\n%s", t.ID, t.Attempt, note)
        args := []string{"commit-tree", tree, "-m", msg}
        for _, p := range parents {
                args = append(args, "-p", p)
        }
        commit, err := m.git(ctx, m.repo, args...)
        if err != nil {
                return "", "", err
        }
        for _, r := range []string{attemptRef, LatestRef(t.ID)} {
                if _, err := m.git(ctx, m.repo, "update-ref", r, commit); err != nil {
                        return "", "", err
                }
        }
        return tree, attemptRef, nil
}

// CheckResult is the outcome of the machine checks.
type CheckResult struct {
        Pass   bool
        Detail string
}

const maxDetail = 4000

func tail(b []byte) string {
        if len(b) > maxDetail {
                b = b[len(b)-maxDetail:]
        }
        return string(b)
}

// RunChecks tests the submitted commit in a fresh checkout, inside the sandbox.
// Files the agent left outside the commit cannot influence the result, and an
// agent saying "done" has no effect on it at all.
func (m *Manager) RunChecks(ctx context.Context, t core.Task) (CheckResult, error) {
        if t.Ref == "" {
                return CheckResult{Detail: "no work was submitted"}, nil
        }
        if !t.AllowEmpty {
                same, err := m.sameTree(ctx, t.Ref, "refs/heads/"+m.branch)
                if err != nil {
                        return CheckResult{}, err
                }
                if same {
                        return CheckResult{Detail: "submission changes nothing compared to the base"}, nil
                }
        }
        if files := m.newConflictMarkers(ctx, t.Ref); files != "" {
                return CheckResult{Detail: "unresolved conflict markers in: " + files}, nil
        }
        dir, err := m.path("check", t.ID, t.Attempt)
        if err != nil {
                return CheckResult{}, err
        }
        defer m.removeWorktree(context.WithoutCancel(ctx), dir)
        m.removeWorktree(ctx, dir)
        m.gitMu.Lock()
        _, err = m.git(ctx, m.repo, "worktree", "add", "--detach", "--force", dir, t.Ref)
        m.gitMu.Unlock()
        if err != nil {
                return CheckResult{}, err
        }
        return m.runIn(ctx, dir, t.Checks), nil
}

// newConflictMarkers lists files holding conflict markers that the integration
// branch does not already have, so that a file which legitimately documents
// markers is not blamed on this task.
func (m *Manager) newConflictMarkers(ctx context.Context, ref string) string {
        grep := func(rev string) []string {
                out, err := m.git(ctx, m.repo, "grep", "-lE", "^(<<<<<<<|>>>>>>>) ", rev)
                if err != nil || out == "" {
                        return nil
                }
                var files []string
                for _, l := range strings.Split(out, "\n") {
                        files = append(files, strings.TrimPrefix(l, rev+":"))
                }
                return files
        }
        known := grep("refs/heads/" + m.branch)
        var fresh []string
        for _, f := range grep(ref) {
                if !slices.Contains(known, f) {
                        fresh = append(fresh, f)
                }
        }
        return strings.Join(fresh, ", ")
}

func (m *Manager) sameTree(ctx context.Context, a, b string) (bool, error) {
        ta, err := m.git(ctx, m.repo, "rev-parse", a+"^{tree}")
        if err != nil {
                return false, err
        }
        tb, err := m.git(ctx, m.repo, "rev-parse", b+"^{tree}")
        if err != nil {
                return false, err
        }
        return ta == tb, nil
}

func (m *Manager) runIn(ctx context.Context, dir string, checks []string) CheckResult {
        for _, check := range checks {
                cctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, m.checkTimeout)
                home := filepath.Join(dir, ".swarm-home")
                _ = os.MkdirAll(filepath.Join(home, ".tmp"), 0o755)
                cmd, err := m.sb.Command(cctx, sandbox.Spec{
                        Dir: dir, Argv: []string{"sh", "-c", check}, Env: sandbox.BaseEnv(home), Hide: m.hide,
                })
                if err != nil {
                        cancel()
                        return CheckResult{Detail: fmt.Sprintf("%s: %v", check, err)}
                }
                if v := log.V(vlog.LevelChanges); v.Enabled() {
                        v.Info("running check", "check", check, "sandbox", m.sb.Name(), "dir", dir)
                }
                out, err := cmd.CombinedOutput()
                cancel()
                _ = os.RemoveAll(home)
                if v := log.V(vlog.LevelDebug); v.Enabled() {
                        v.Info("check output", "check", check, "err", err, "output", tail(out))
                }
                if err != nil {
                        return CheckResult{Detail: fmt.Sprintf("check failed: %s: %v\n%s", check, err, tail(out))}
                }
        }
        return CheckResult{Pass: true, Detail: fmt.Sprintf("%d checks passed", len(checks))}
}

// ErrMergeConflict means the work no longer applies on top of the integration branch.
var ErrMergeConflict = errors.New("merge conflict")

// Merge lands a verified task on the integration branch, one task at a time. It
// re-runs the checks on the merged result, because each change can pass alone
// and still fail combined. It is safe to repeat: work that has already landed is
// recognized, which covers a crash between the merge and recording it.
func (m *Manager) Merge(ctx context.Context, t core.Task) (string, error) {
        m.mergeMu.Lock()
        defer m.mergeMu.Unlock()
        branchRef := "refs/heads/" + m.branch
        if _, err := m.git(ctx, m.repo, "merge-base", "--is-ancestor", t.Ref, branchRef); err == nil {
                return m.git(ctx, m.repo, "rev-parse", branchRef)
        }
        head, err := m.git(ctx, m.repo, "rev-parse", branchRef)
        if err != nil {
                return "", err
        }
        dir, err := m.path("merge", t.ID, t.Attempt)
        if err != nil {
                return "", err
        }
        defer m.removeWorktree(context.WithoutCancel(ctx), dir)
        m.removeWorktree(ctx, dir)
        m.gitMu.Lock()
        _, err = m.git(ctx, m.repo, "worktree", "add", "--detach", "--force", dir, head)
        m.gitMu.Unlock()
        if err != nil {
                return "", err
        }
        msg := fmt.Sprintf("swarm: %s\n\ntask %s attempt %d, verified by %s", t.Title, t.ID, t.Attempt, t.Verifier)
        if _, err := m.git(ctx, dir, "merge", "--no-ff", "--no-edit", "-m", msg, t.Ref); err != nil {
                return "", fmt.Errorf("%w: %v", ErrMergeConflict, err)
        }
        if r := m.runIn(ctx, dir, t.Checks); !r.Pass {
                return "", fmt.Errorf("%w: merged result fails: %s", ErrMergeConflict, r.Detail)
        }
        merged, err := m.git(ctx, dir, "rev-parse", "HEAD")
        if err != nil {
                return "", err
        }
        // Compare-and-swap on the branch, so nothing else's commit can be overwritten.
        if _, err := m.git(ctx, m.repo, "update-ref", branchRef, merged, head); err != nil {
                return "", err
        }
        if v := log.V(vlog.LevelSteady); v.Enabled() {
                v.Info("merged", "task", t.ID, "branch", m.branch, "commit", merged)
        }
        return merged, nil
}

func (m *Manager) removeWorktree(ctx context.Context, dir string) {
        m.gitMu.Lock()
        defer m.gitMu.Unlock()
        _, _ = m.git(ctx, m.repo, "worktree", "remove", "--force", dir)
        _ = os.RemoveAll(dir)
}

var worktreeName = regexp.MustCompile(`^(wt|review|check|merge)-(.+)-(\d+)$`)

// WorktreeTasks lists the tasks that have a worktree on disk, from the folder names.
func (m *Manager) WorktreeTasks() ([]string, error) {
        entries, err := os.ReadDir(m.root)
        if errors.Is(err, os.ErrNotExist) {
                return nil, nil
        }
        if err != nil {
                return nil, err
        }
        seen := map[string]bool{}
        for _, e := range entries {
                if m := worktreeName.FindStringSubmatch(e.Name()); m != nil && e.IsDir() {
                        seen[m[2]] = true
                }
        }
        return slices.Sorted(maps.Keys(seen)), nil
}

// Prune lets git forget worktrees whose folders are gone.
func (m *Manager) Prune(ctx context.Context) error {
        m.gitMu.Lock()
        defer m.gitMu.Unlock()
        _, err := m.git(ctx, m.repo, "worktree", "prune")
        return err
}

// Cleanup removes a finished task's worktrees. Its refs stay, as the audit trail.
func (m *Manager) Cleanup(ctx context.Context, id string) {
        if !safeID.MatchString(id) {
                return
        }
        for _, kind := range []string{"wt", "review", "check", "merge"} {
                matches, _ := filepath.Glob(filepath.Join(m.root, kind+"-"+id+"-*"))
                for _, d := range matches {
                        m.removeWorktree(ctx, d)
                }
        }
}

// Probe checks that the repository and integration branch are readable.
func (m *Manager) Probe(ctx context.Context) error {
        _, err := m.git(ctx, m.repo, "rev-parse", "--verify", "refs/heads/"+m.branch)
        return err
}

// SandboxName says which sandbox checks run in.
func (m *Manager) SandboxName() string { return m.sb.Name() }

// Branch returns the integration branch name.
func (m *Manager) Branch() string { return m.branch }

package observe

import (
        "cmp"
        "regexp"
        "slices"
        "strings"
        "sync"
        "time"
)

// The flow analytics: how tasks move through the states, why they fall out, how many tries
// they take, and how many sat in each state over time. They are computed from the durable
// event log, so they survive restarts, unlike the rates above.

// Pipeline is the path a task takes when all goes well.
var Pipeline = []string{"draft", "ready", "claimed", "running", "review", "merging", "done"}

// Exits are the states a task leaves the path for.
var Exits = []string{"failed", "parked", "canceled"}

// Revision is what the index needs of one committed task revision.
type Revision struct {
        ID      string
        State   string
        Tier    int
        Attempt int
        Reason  string
        Labels  map[string]string
        At      time.Time
}

type move struct {
        at      int64 // Unix milliseconds.
        state   uint8
        attempt uint16
        reason  uint16
}

type taskHistory struct {
        tier   int
        labels map[string]string
        moves  []move
}

// FlowIndex keeps each task's state changes, compactly, for the analytics. A heartbeat or
// any other revision that leaves the state and attempt as they were adds nothing.
type FlowIndex struct {
        mu      sync.RWMutex
        tasks   map[string]*taskHistory
        states  []string
        stateID map[string]uint8
        reasons []string
        reasonI map[string]uint16
        moves   int
        ready   bool
        // Per state: whether it leaves the path, and where on the path it is.
        exit [256]bool
        rank [256]uint8
}

// NewFlowIndex returns an empty index.
func NewFlowIndex() *FlowIndex {
        x := &FlowIndex{tasks: map[string]*taskHistory{}, stateID: map[string]uint8{}, reasonI: map[string]uint16{"": 0}, reasons: []string{""}}
        for _, s := range append(slices.Clone(Pipeline), Exits...) {
                x.state(s)
        }
        return x
}

func (x *FlowIndex) state(s string) uint8 {
        if i, ok := x.stateID[s]; ok {
                return i
        }
        if len(x.states) >= 255 {
                return 0
        }
        i := uint8(len(x.states))
        x.states = append(x.states, s)
        x.stateID[s] = i
        x.exit[i] = slices.Contains(Exits, s)
        x.rank[i] = uint8(len(Pipeline))
        if r := slices.Index(Pipeline, s); r >= 0 {
                x.rank[i] = uint8(r)
        }
        return i
}

func (x *FlowIndex) reason(r string) uint16 {
        r = ReasonCode(r)
        if i, ok := x.reasonI[r]; ok {
                return i
        }
        if len(x.reasons) >= 65535 {
                return 0
        }
        i := uint16(len(x.reasons))
        x.reasons = append(x.reasons, r)
        x.reasonI[r] = i
        return i
}

var codeRE = regexp.MustCompile(`^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,39}$`)

// ReasonCode turns a reason into a short code for charts. The swarm's own reasons are codes
// already. A note an agent wrote when it gave up is free text, which could hold anything, so
// it becomes "agent_note" instead of a category of its own.
func ReasonCode(r string) string {
        r = strings.TrimSpace(r)
        if r == "" {
                return ""
        }
        if code, _, ok := strings.Cut(r, ":"); ok && codeRE.MatchString(code) {
                return code
        }
        if codeRE.MatchString(r) {
                return r
        }
        low := strings.ToLower(r)
        switch {
